30/// A runtime context for a semantic math parser action
31/// Ideally, these are all immutable borrows of various `Core` data.
32pub struct ActionContext<'a> {
33  /// The original XML nodes involved in this parse request
34  pub nodes:    &'a [XMLNode],
35  /// The owner document of the parsed nodes
36  pub document: &'a mut Document,
37}
38pub type ActionClosure = Rc<
39  dyn Fn(
40    i32,
41    Vec<Option<XM>>,
42    &[ValidationPragmatics],
43    ActionContext,
44  ) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>>,
45>;
46
47#[derive(Default)]
48pub struct Actions {
49  dispatch: HashMap<i32, ActionClosure>,
50}
51
52impl Actions {
53  pub fn register(&mut self, id: i32, closure: ActionClosure) { self.dispatch.insert(id, closure); }
54  /// Whether a rule has a registered semantic action. Used by the
55  /// ASF traverser to discriminate "structural/literal" rules (treat
56  /// as transparent byte-passthrough — match legacy `rollup_token_rec`)
57  /// from "semantic" rules (call `action_on`).
58  pub fn has_action(&self, id: i32) -> bool { self.dispatch.contains_key(&id) }
59  pub fn action_on(
60    &self,
61    id: i32,
62    mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
63    pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
64    ctxt: ActionContext,
65  ) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
66    if let Some(action) = self.dispatch.get(&id) {
67      action(id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
68    } else {
69      match args.len() {
70        0 => Ok(None),
71        1 => Ok(args.remove(0)),
72        more => {
73          // No registered action for this rule id with multiple children — the
74          // ambiguous grammar's fallback keeps the first parse (the "aggressively
75          // prune" design). Route it through the math-parser diagnostic path
76          // (`Info:` — captured in the log floor, `--quiet`-gated on stderr, and
77          // NOT inflating the warning verdict) instead of a raw `eprintln!` that
78          // bypassed the logger and printed unconditionally.
79          log_math_info!(
80            "ambiguous",
81            "action",
82            format!("rule {id:?}: returning first of {more} children; dropped {args:?}")
83          );
84          Ok(args.remove(0))
85        },
86      }
87    }
88  }
89
90  pub fn get_tree(
91    &self,
92    b: TreeBuilder,
93    v: Value,
94    pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
95    ctxt: ActionContext,
96  ) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
97    let handle = proc_value(b, v);
98    self.translate_node(&handle, pragmas, ctxt)
99  }
100
101  pub fn translate_node<T: Token>(
102    &self,
103    n: &Handle<T>,
104    pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
105    ctxt: ActionContext,
106  ) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
107    match *n.borrow() {
108      Node::Tree(ref rule, ref children) => {
109        let mut translated_children = Vec::with_capacity(children.len());
110        for child in children.iter() {
111          let translated = self.translate_node(child, pragmas, ActionContext {
112            nodes:    ctxt.nodes,
113            document: ctxt.document,
114          })?;
115          translated_children.push(translated);
116        }
117        self.action_on(*rule, translated_children, pragmas, ctxt)
118      },
119      Node::Rule(ref rule, ref children) => {
120        let mut translated_children = Vec::with_capacity(children.len());
121        for child in children.iter() {
122          translated_children.push(self.translate_node(child, pragmas, ActionContext {
123            nodes:    ctxt.nodes,
124            document: ctxt.document,
125          })?);
126        }
127        self.action_on(*rule, translated_children, pragmas, ctxt)
128      },
129      Node::Token(_ty, ref val) => {
130        let token_str = ::std::str::from_utf8(val).unwrap_or("malformed-utf8");
131        Ok(Some(
132          XM::Lexeme(Rc::from(token_str), Meta::default()).specialize(Meta::default(), pragmas)?,
133        ))
134      },
135      Node::Leaf(ref tok) => Ok(Some(XM::Lexeme(
136        Rc::from(tok.to_string().as_str()),
137        Meta::default(),
138      ))),
139      Node::Null(_) => {
140        // e.g.* argument failed nothing, just skip.
141        Ok(None)
142        // XM::Lexeme("null".into())
143      },
144    }
145  }
146}

148/// standard infix application of an operator
149pub fn infix_apply(
150  _rule_id: i32,
151  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
152  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
153  _: ActionContext,
154) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
155  unp!(args => arg1, infixop, arg2);
156  // Composition (meaning="compose") requires function-level operands.
157  // Prune parses where an operand is an applied function (ground term).
158  // f∘sin x → prefer (f∘sin)(x), not f∘(sin(x))
159  if let Some(XM::Lexeme(ref lex, _)) = infixop
160    && lex.contains(":compose:")
161  {
162    // Check that operands are function-level (not applied/ground)
163    if is_applied_function(&arg1) || is_applied_function(&arg2) {
164      return Err(
165        "infix_apply: compose requires function-level operands, not applied functions".into(),
166      );
167    }
168    // Compose left-associativity: reject right-nested form `f ∘ (g ∘ h)`.
169    // The grammar admits both `(f ∘ g) ∘ h` and `f ∘ (g ∘ h)` for chains
170    // like `f * g * h`. Math convention is to left-associate composition,
171    // so canonicalize by dropping the right-nested form here; Marpa's
172    // alternative parse with the left-nested form survives.
173    if let Some(XM::Apply(Operator(ref rhs_op), ..)) = arg2 {
174      let rhs_is_compose = match &**rhs_op {
175        XM::Lexeme(rl, _) => rl.contains(":compose:"),
176        XM::Token(p, _) => p.meaning.as_deref() == Some("compose"),
177        _ => false,
178      };
179      if rhs_is_compose {
180        return Err(
181          "infix_apply: compose is left-associative — reject right-nested f ∘ (g ∘ h)".into(),
182        );
183      }
184    }
185  }
186  let apply_tree = XM::Apply(
187    infixop.into(),
188    Args(vec![arg1, arg2]),
189    XProps::default(),
190    Meta::default(),
191  );
192  Ok(Some(apply_tree))
193}

195/// Check if an XM node is an applied function (curry level 1 / ground term).
196/// Applied functions are Apply(function, args...) — the function has been applied to arguments.
197fn is_applied_function(xm: &Option<XM>) -> bool {
198  if let Some(XM::Apply(op, args, ..)) = xm {
199    // An Apply with a function/trigfunction/opfunction operator that has arguments
200    // is a ground-level application, not a function value.
201    if !args.0.is_empty()
202      && let XM::Lexeme(ref lex, _) = *op.0
203    {
204      return lex.starts_with("TRIGFUNCTION:")
205        || lex.starts_with("OPFUNCTION:")
206        || lex.starts_with("EXPECTATION:")
207        || lex.starts_with("FUNCTION:");
208    }
209  }
210  false
211}

213/// Perl MathGrammar: Anything : Statement PUNCT <leftop: Statement PUNCT Statement>
214/// Creates a list@(...) or formulae@(...) XMDual: content arm is Apply(meaning=list/formulae,
215/// refs...), presentation arm is Wrap(items with separators).
216/// Left-recursive: first call creates a 2-item list, subsequent calls extend it.
217/// Perl distinction: comma-separated relational formulas at top level → "formulae",
218/// comma-separated plain expressions → "list".
219pub fn list_apply(
220  _rule_id: i32,
221  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
222  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
223  ctxt: ActionContext,
224) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
225  // Grammar is left-recursive: `statements punct statement => list_apply`
226  // so `left` is the accumulated structure and `right` is the new item.
227  unp!(args => left, sep, right);
228  let right = right.unwrap();
229  let sep = sep.unwrap();
230
231  // The separator decides the wrapper:
232  //  * `\quad` (WIDE_PUNCT) separates whole FORMULAS at the top level — a
233  //    `\quad`-list is a flat `formulae@(…)` whose items may be of ANY kind
234  //    (relational or not), e.g. `a\op b \quad a\rel b \quad …`. (Perl emits a
235  //    right-NESTED `formulae@(a, formulae@(b, …))`; we keep it FLAT — an
236  //    intentional, user-directed divergence; see docs/parity/KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS.md.)
237  //  * a plain comma separates a `list@(…)`. A MIXED comma-list — a relational
238  //    item plus plain items — IS a valid list: a bare (unparenthesized)
239  //    comma-list is a top-level list, and a relation is a legitimate item. So
240  //    `0 < x, y` → `list(0<x, y)` and `a = b, c, d` → `list(a=b, c, d)`, NOT
241  //    `lt(0, list(x,y))` / `eq(a, list(b,c,d))` (also an intentional divergence
242  //    from Perl, which wrongly reads the comma-list as a single bare relation
243  //    operand). The grammar's deleted `formula relop formula_list` rule used to
244  //    manufacture that bogus reading.
245  let is_quad = is_quad_separator(&sep);
246  let left_rel = left.as_ref().is_some_and(is_relational_item);
247  let right_rel = is_relational_item(&right);
248  // For a COMMA list, an all-relational pair (`a=b, c=d`) is a `formulae@`, not a
249  // list — defer to `formulae_apply`. `\quad` accepts relational pairs directly
250  // (it builds `formulae@` itself). A comma list with exactly one relational item
251  // (mixed) is accepted here as a `list@`.
252  if !is_quad && left_rel && right_rel {
253    return Err("list_apply: both items relational in a comma list, use formulae_apply".into());
254  }
255  // Rule 3: an `absent` relop operand marks an equation FRAGMENT — a leading or
256  // trailing relop whose other operand lives on a different align line. How
257  // strictly a fragment disqualifies an item depends on the separator:
258  //
259  //  * `\quad` (WIDE_PUNCT): reject if EITHER item is a fragment. A
260  //    `\quad`-separated run of align continuations is one broken-up equation,
261  //    not a list, and admitting it produces actively WRONG trees — the pinned
262  //    `tests/math/sampler` case `\displaystyle=f(x)+\phantom{g(x)}+h(x)`
263  //    (`\phantom` lexes as WIDE_PUNCT) parses to
264  //    `fragments@(absent = limit-from@(f@(x), +), + h@(x))`, which mis-groups
265  //    the `+`. `ltx_math_unparsed` is the honest outcome there.
266  //  * comma: reject only when BOTH items are fragments. This mirrors the
267  //    relaxation `formulae_apply` already carries below ("the earlier strict
268  //    rule (reject if EITHER is a fragment) was correct only for inner
269  //    contexts … at the top level these pairings are well-formed and need to
270  //    survive pragmatic prune").
271  //
272  // The comma half matters because `list_apply` kept the strict form for both,
273  // and with the `formula relop formula_list` rule deliberately gone
274  // (KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #37) a leading-relop item followed by a comma then had NO
275  // derivation at all: `$>50,000$` fell out as `ltx_math_unparsed` even though
276  // both halves parse alone (`>x` ✓, `a,b` ✓, `a>50,000` ✓). Pragmas prune; they
277  // must not empty the forest. With this split, `>50,000` reaches the #37 reading
278  // `list@(absent>50, 000)` — the same shape `a>50,000` already produced as
279  // `list@(a>50, 000)`. (Perl instead builds `>(absent, list(50,000))` via the
280  // rule #37 removed; ours is the intended divergence.) Witness: arXiv 2605.17646.
281  let left_fragment = left.as_ref().is_some_and(has_absent_relop_operand);
282  let right_fragment = has_absent_relop_operand(&right);
283  let fragment_reject = if is_quad {
284    left_fragment || right_fragment
285  } else {
286    left_fragment && right_fragment
287  };
288  if fragment_reject {
289    return Err("list_apply: fragment item (absent relop operand) in this list".into());
290  }
291  // Rule 4: Reject when an item is a BARE `conditional@(...)` Apply
292  // — `|` (conditional / MODIFIEROP) binds LOOSER than `,` (list
293  // separator) when unfenced, so the conditional should wrap the
294  // list. For `x|y, z, t`, prefer `conditional@(x, list@(y, z, t))`.
295  //
296  // **Exception**: when the conditional IS inside a parens-fenced
297  // group (e.g. `(a|b), (a|b)`), each `(a|b)` is a complete
298  // `Dual(conditional(a,b), Wrap[(, a, |, b, )])` unit, which CAN
299  // legitimately be a list item. Detect this by checking whether
300  // the Dual's presentation Wrap starts with OPEN paren.
301  let bare_conditional = |item: &XM| -> bool {
302    match item {
303      // Naked Apply(conditional, ...): always bare.
304      XM::Apply(Operator(op), ..) => {
305        let meaning = match &**op {
306          XM::Token(p, _) | XM::Ref(p) => p.meaning.as_deref(),
307          XM::Lexeme(name, _) => Some(&**name),
308          _ => None,
309        };
310        meaning == Some("conditional")
311      },
312      // Dual wrapping conditional: bare only if presentation is NOT
313      // parens-fenced.
314      XM::Dual(content, pres, ..) => {
315        let inner_is_conditional = if let XM::Apply(Operator(ref op), ..) = **content {
316          let meaning = match &**op {
317            XM::Token(p, _) => p.meaning.as_deref(),
318            XM::Lexeme(name, _) => Some(&**name),
319            _ => None,
320          };
321          meaning == Some("conditional")
322        } else {
323          false
324        };
325        if !inner_is_conditional {
326          return false;
327        }
328        // Check presentation for parens fence.
329        let presentation_is_parens_fenced = if let XM::Wrap(ref items, ..) = **pres {
330          (matches!(items.first(),
331            Some(XM::Token(p, _))
332              if p.role.as_deref() == Some("OPEN")
333                && p.content.as_deref() == Some("("))
334            || matches!(items.first(),
335              Some(XM::Lexeme(name, _)) if name.starts_with("OPEN:(:")))
336        } else {
337          false
338        };
339        !presentation_is_parens_fenced
340      },
341      _ => false,
342    }
343  };
344  if left.as_ref().is_some_and(bare_conditional) || bare_conditional(&right) {
345    return Err(
346      "list_apply: child is BARE `conditional@` at root — conditional/MODIFIEROP binds \
347       looser than comma, so the bare conditional should wrap the list (the parens-fenced \
348       case is allowed)."
349        .into(),
350    );
351  }
352  // `\quad` (WIDE_PUNCT) separates top-level FRAGMENTS — heterogeneous content
353  // that needn't be formulas — so it gets its own flat `fragments@` class,
354  // distinct from comma's `list@`/`formulae@`. A plain comma builds `list@`
355  // (all-relational comma pairs were already routed to `formulae_apply` above).
356  list_apply_core(left, sep, right, ctxt)
357}

359/// Does a list Dual's presentation hold its `items` alone — `[item, separator, item, …]`, `2n - 1`
360/// nodes? A list fenced with its own delimiters (a bracket or brace list since 57au, Perl's `Fence`:
361/// `[open, item, separator, …, close]`) does not: it is one closed item, which a comma after it does
362/// not extend, a relation after it does not split, and parens around it do not rename or unpack —
363/// each read it as a bare run and lost or unparsed the formula (`\left([a;b]\right)`
364/// `vector@([, ;, ])`, 57aw; `W=[w_1,\ldots,w_d]\in\mathbb{R}^d` unparsed, 233 formulas of the 57ax
365/// train A/B, 2605.03399, 2605.29816).
366fn presents_its_items_alone(presentation: &XM, items: usize) -> bool {
367  matches!(presentation, XM::Wrap(wrapped, ..) if items > 0 && wrapped.len() == 2 * items - 1)
368}
369
370/// Core list/fragments construction for `list_apply`, AFTER its admission
371/// checks (relational pairs, absent-relop, Rule-4 bare-conditional). Extracted
372/// so `vertbar_modifier_listlhs` can append a conditional as the LAST list item
373/// WITHOUT Rule-4's rejection: in the bar-after-comma context (`a,b | c`) the
374/// conditional `b|c` IS a legitimate item (Perl `list@(a, conditional@(b,c))`),
375/// unlike the bar-first `x|y,z` wrap case (`conditional@(x, list@(y,z))`) that
376/// Rule 4 guards against. `list_apply` itself runs the checks then calls this.
377fn list_apply_core(
378  mut left: Option<XM>,
379  sep: XM,
380  mut right: XM,
381  ctxt: ActionContext,
382) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
383  let is_quad = is_quad_separator(&sep);
384  let meaning = if is_quad { "fragments" } else { "list" };
385
386  // If left is already a list/formulae/fragments Dual without its own delimiters, extend it (flat
387  // accumulation — all three classes are kept flat; `presents_its_items_alone`). A
388  // `distribute_list_relation` dual has `formulae` content but a relation-Apply presentation, and
389  // extending it here would strand a keyless bare ref (see the matching guard + rationale in
390  // `formulae_apply`, EXPECTED_ID_XMREF_DESIGN 26v); a fenced list is one closed item, which a comma
391  // after it does not extend (`[a,b,c],d`, 57ay; 2605.03399).
392  if let Some(XM::Dual(ref mut content, ref mut pres, ..)) = left
393    && let XM::Apply(ref op, ref mut op_args, ..) = **content
394    && presents_its_items_alone(pres, op_args.0.len())
395    && let XM::Token(ref props, _) = *op.0
396    && matches!(
397      props.meaning.as_deref(),
398      Some("list") | Some("formulae") | Some("fragments")
399    )
400  {
401    // Extend: add ref for new item to content args
402    let new_ref = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut right], ctxt)?;
403    op_args.0.extend(new_ref.into_iter().map(Some));
404    // Add separator and new item to presentation wrap
405    if let XM::Wrap(ref mut items, ..) = **pres {
406      items.push(sep);
407      items.push(right);
408    }
409    return Ok(left);
410  }
411
412  list_or_formulae_create(left.unwrap(), sep, right, meaning, ctxt)
413}
414
415/// ASF migration item 5 (Option A): build a comma-list of
416/// `modified_term` items. Mirrors `list_apply` but explicitly
417/// ACCEPTS relational items — that's the whole point. Used for
418/// function argument lists where each argument carries its own
419/// single-relop expression, e.g. `P(x=0, y<0)`.
420///
421/// Rejects the same non-relop pathologies `list_apply` rejects
422/// (bare conditional, etc.) but does NOT force formulae_apply on
423/// relations. The grammar rules that route to this action
424/// (`formula_list += modified_term punct …`) only fire when at
425/// least one side is a `modified_term`, so the relation case is
426/// the expected one.
427pub fn modified_list_apply(
428  _rule_id: i32,
429  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
430  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
431  ctxt: ActionContext,
432) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
433  unp!(args => left, sep, right);
434  let mut left = left;
435  let mut right = right.unwrap();
436  let sep = sep.unwrap();
437  let meaning = "list";
438
439  // If left is already a list/formulae Dual, extend it (mirrors the
440  // flat-accumulation behaviour at the end of `list_apply`).
441  if let Some(XM::Dual(ref mut content, ref mut pres, ..)) = left
442    && let XM::Apply(ref op, ref mut op_args, ..) = **content
443    && presents_its_items_alone(pres, op_args.0.len())
444    && let XM::Token(ref props, _) = *op.0
445    && (props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("list") || props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("formulae"))
446  {
447    let new_ref = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut right], ctxt)?;
448    op_args.0.extend(new_ref.into_iter().map(Some));
449    if let XM::Wrap(ref mut items, ..) = **pres {
450      items.push(sep);
451      items.push(right);
452    }
453    return Ok(left);
454  }
455
456  list_or_formulae_create(left.unwrap(), sep, right, meaning, ctxt)
457}

459/// Perl: within a Formula, comma-separated expressions after a relop form a list RHS.
460/// Like list_apply but rejects items that contain relations (those should go to statement level).
461/// This prevents `1<x<10,2<y<20` from being parsed as `1 < x < list(10,2) < y < ...`.
462pub fn formula_list_apply(
463  rule_id: i32,
464  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
465  p: &[ValidationPragmatics],
466  ctxt: ActionContext,
467) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
468  // Check if ANY of the items contain relations — if so, reject this parse
469  // so Marpa falls back to the statement-level comma separation.
470  let has_relational = args
471    .iter()
472    .any(|a| a.as_ref().is_some_and(is_relational_item));
473  if has_relational {
474    return Err("formula_list_apply: items contain relations, use statement-level list".into());
475  }
476  // Also check if the left side is already a list Dual containing relational items
477  if let Some(Some(XM::Dual(content, ..))) = args.first()
478    && let XM::Apply(ref op, ref op_args, ..) = **content
479    && let XM::Token(ref props, _) = *op.0
480    && props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("list")
481  {
482    // Check if any list item is relational
483    for arg in &op_args.0 {
484      if arg.as_ref().is_some_and(is_relational_item) {
485        return Err("formula_list_apply: list contains relational items".into());
486      }
487    }
488  }
489  list_apply(rule_id, args, p, ctxt)
490}
491
492/// Check if an XM tree contains `absent` as a direct operand of a relop.
493/// Absent operands are valid at the top level (equation fragments like `= f(x)`)
494/// but should be pruned when inside inner rules (lists, fenced expressions, function args).
495fn has_absent_relop_operand(xm: &XM) -> bool {
496  if let XM::Apply(op, args, ..) = xm
497    && (is_multirelation(&op.0) || is_relational_op(&op.0))
498  {
499    for arg in &args.0 {
500      if let Some(XM::Token(props, _)) = arg
501        && props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("absent")
502      {
503        return true;
504      }
505    }
506  }
507  false
508}
509
510/// Check if an XM tree is a relational formula (contains RELOP or multirelation).
511/// Used to distinguish Perl's "formulae" (comma-separated relations at top level)
512/// from "list" (comma-separated plain expressions).
513pub(crate) fn is_relational_item(xm: &XM) -> bool {
514  match xm {
515    XM::Apply(op, ..) => is_multirelation(&op.0) || is_relational_op(&op.0),
516    // A formulae XMDual is inherently relational (it wraps relational items)
517    XM::Dual(content, ..) => {
518      if let XM::Apply(ref op, ..) = **content
519        && let XM::Token(ref props, _) = *op.0
520      {
521        return props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("formulae");
522      }
523      false
524    },
525    _ => false,
526  }
527}
528
529/// The #37 hole: a comma list that opens with two relations and goes on with a plain item
530/// (`x=0, y=1, z`; `x_i\ge 0,\ i=1,\ldots,n`). The relational pair can only be a `formulae`
531/// (`list_apply` refuses a comma pair of two relations), and `formulae_apply` refuses a plain item
532/// after relations, so the list had no derivation (unparsed; Perl reads it). A flat `formulae`
533/// container followed by a plain item after a comma (a WIDE_PUNCT comma too) is extended as a list is —
534/// `list_apply`'s checks — and made a `list@(x = 0, y = 1, z)` (#37).
535/// `attach_enumerations` then attaches an enumeration to its relation. A relational item after it
536/// is `formulae_apply`'s; a non-flat formulae (`distribute_list_relation`'s) is refused, as
537/// `list_apply_core` refuses to extend it. Its grammar rule takes `relation_pairs` and a plain
538/// expression only, so no other comma list gets a derivation. Witnesses 2605.00467, 2605.24797.
539pub fn formulae_then_item_apply(
540  rule_id: i32,
541  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
542  pragmatics: &[ValidationPragmatics],
543  ctxt: ActionContext,
544) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
545  let flat_formulae = matches!(args.first(), Some(Some(XM::Dual(content, pres, ..)))
546    if matches!(&**content, XM::Apply(op, items, ..)
547      if matches!(&*op.0, XM::Token(props, _) if props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("formulae"))
548        && presents_its_items_alone(pres, items.0.len())));
549  if !flat_formulae {
550    return Err("formulae_then_item_apply: not a flat formulae container".into());
551  }
552  if args
553    .get(2)
554    .and_then(Option::as_ref)
555    .is_none_or(is_relational_item)
556  {
557    return Err("formulae_then_item_apply: a relation after formulae is formulae_apply's".into());
558  }
559  // A comma only (a WIDE_PUNCT comma too): a `\quad`-list reads as fragments already, and a second
560  // derivation for it would make its reading depend on enumeration order.
561  if !args.get(1).and_then(Option::as_ref).is_some_and(|sep| {
562    !is_quad_separator(sep) && realized_value(sep, &ctxt).is_ok_and(|v| v == ",")
563  }) {
564    return Err("formulae_then_item_apply: a comma list only".into());
565  }
566  let mut out = list_apply(rule_id, args, pragmatics, ctxt)?;
567  if let Some(XM::Dual(content, ..)) = out.as_mut()
568    && let XM::Apply(op, ..) = &mut **content
569    && let XM::Token(props, _) = &mut *op.0
570    && props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("formulae")
571  {
572    props.meaning = Some(Cow::Borrowed("list"));
573  }
574  Ok(out)
575}
576
577/// Perl: NewFormulae — punct-separated formulas at top level → meaning="formulae".
578/// This action is used by `formula_list` (the top-level rule that competes with
579/// `statements` via `list_apply`). It ALWAYS produces meaning="formulae", but
580/// REJECTS the parse (returns Err) if no items are relational — causing Marpa
581/// to fall back to the `statements` parse which produces "list".
582pub fn formulae_apply(
583  _rule_id: i32,
584  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
585  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
586  ctxt: ActionContext,
587) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
588  unp!(args => left, sep, right);
589  let mut left = left;
590  let mut right = right.unwrap();
591  let sep = sep.unwrap();
592
593  // Check if ANY item is relational — if not, reject this parse.
594  // This forces Marpa to use the `statements` rule (list_apply) instead.
595  let left_rel = left.as_ref().is_some_and(is_relational_item);
596  let right_rel = is_relational_item(&right);
597
598  // Reject when BOTH items are fragments (have `absent` as a relop operand).
599  // A fragment + a complete formula is a common arXiv pattern: align'd
600  // equation continuations followed by a side-condition, e.g.
601  //   `\lesssim T(r,f) + \log r, \quad r \notin E_3`
602  // where the LEFT (`\lesssim ...`) has an absent LHS because the
603  // original LHS is on a previous line of an align block, and the RIGHT
604  // (`r \notin E_3`) is the trailing condition annotation. The earlier
605  // strict rule (reject if EITHER is a fragment) was correct only for
606  // inner contexts (fenced lists, function args); at the top level
607  // these pairings are well-formed and need to survive pragmatic prune.
608  // True inner-context fragment cases are still pruned because BOTH
609  // sides are typically fragments (or one is a single bare token).
610  if left.as_ref().is_some_and(has_absent_relop_operand) && has_absent_relop_operand(&right) {
611    return Err("formulae_apply: both operands are fragments (not complete formulae)".into());
612  }
613  // Also check inside an existing formulae Dual being extended
614  if let Some(XM::Dual(ref content, ..)) = left
615    && let XM::Apply(_, ref args, ..) = **content
616  {
617    for arg in &args.0 {
618      if arg.as_ref().is_some_and(has_absent_relop_operand) {
619        return Err("formulae_apply: formulae contains fragment with absent".into());
620      }
621    }
622  }
623  // Period separator always creates formulae (it's a hard formula boundary).
624  // Comma separator requires at least one relational item.
625  // The separator's value read through an XMRef, as a gathered/split row's content branch holds it.
626  let sep_is_period = realized_value(&sep, &ctxt).is_ok_and(|v| v == ".");
627  if !left_rel && !right_rel && !sep_is_period {
628    return Err("formulae_apply: no relational items, use list_apply instead".into());
629  }
630
631  // Reject when right is non-relational and left is relational, BUT only for
632  // comma separators. Period is a hard formula boundary and should NOT trigger
633  // list grouping. This forces `a=b, c` via `formula relop formula_list`
634  // (producing `a = list(b,c)`) but allows `a=b. c` to produce `formulae(a=b, c)`.
635  let sep_is_period = match &sep {
636    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lex.starts_with("PERIOD:"),
637    XM::Token(props, _) => props.role.as_deref() == Some("PERIOD"),
638    _ => false,
639  };
640  if left_rel && !right_rel && !sep_is_period {
641    return Err(
642      "formulae_apply: non-relational right after relational left — a list (formulae_then_item_apply)".into(),
643    );
644  }
645
646  let meaning = "formulae"; // always
647
648  // If left is already a formulae Dual, extend it — BUT only when its
649  // presentation holds its items alone (`presents_its_items_alone`: the flat-list `XMWrap`
650  // without delimiters of its own, which a fenced list has, 57ay). A
651  // `distribute_list_relation` dual ALSO has `meaning="formulae"` content yet a
652  // RELATION-`Apply` presentation (`(a,b)=c`), not a Wrap; extending that here
653  // would push a content ref but silently skip the presentation update (the
654  // `if let XM::Wrap` below fails), stranding the ref as a keyless bare `<XMRef/>`
655  // → the dominant `expected:id` "Missing idref" cluster (370 papers; witness
656  // `0704.2334`, `a,\quad b=c,\quad d=e`). Requiring a Wrap presentation makes
657  // such a left fall through to `list_or_formulae_create`, which builds a fresh
658  // dual whose content refs BOTH resolve. See EXPECTED_ID_XMREF_DESIGN 2026-06-26v.
659  if let Some(XM::Dual(ref mut content, ref mut pres, ..)) = left
660    && let XM::Apply(ref op, ref mut op_args, ..) = **content
661    && presents_its_items_alone(pres, op_args.0.len())
662    && let XM::Token(ref props, _) = *op.0
663    && props.meaning.as_deref() == Some(meaning)
664  {
665    let new_ref = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut right], ctxt)?;
666    op_args.0.extend(new_ref.into_iter().map(Some));
667    if let XM::Wrap(ref mut items, ..) = **pres {
668      items.push(sep);
669      items.push(right);
670    }
671    return Ok(left);
672  }
673  // Comma-list LEFT of a relation: `a,b \in A` / `x,y \le z`. The grammar reaches
674  // here with `left` a bare (non-relational) item and `right` a binary RELOP
675  // relation `Apply(∈,[b,A])`. The plain `formulae@(a, b∈A)` is semantically wrong
676  // (∈ binds only `b`, splitting `a` off). Build the user-specified XMDual
677  // (2026-06-22): content DISTRIBUTES the relation over the list, presentation
678  // wraps the list as the relation's LHS. (List-RIGHT `0<x,y` is the separate
679  // `formula relop formula_list` path → `list(0<x,y)`, untouched.)
680  // Not over a factor-level conditional, whose condition binds the last item only (`a,b\mid c\sim d`,
681  // `\Delta;\Gamma\mid\Phi\vdash P`), nor from a text label beside math (`\text{Poisson:}\quad
682  // y\mid\lambda\sim…`, `\text{where}\quad G=W\times A`, 2605.01549; 57cc review): an item holding text
683  // distributes only over a relation whose left operand holds text too, its kin (`\textbf{A},\textbf{B}
684  // \in\mathbb{R}^n` 2605.12082, `\mbox{det}\,G,\mbox{det}\,G_h\geq c_0`; 57cc's A/B).
685  let kin = |l: &XM| {
686    !holds_text(l, &ctxt)
687      || matches!(&right, XM::Apply(_, Args(a), ..)
688        if a.first().and_then(Option::as_ref).is_some_and(|lhs| holds_text(lhs, &ctxt)))
689  };
690  if !left_rel
691    && !sep_is_period
692    && left
693      .as_ref()
694      .is_some_and(|l| !matches!(l, XM::Dual(..)) && kin(l))
695    && matches!(&right, XM::Apply(op, Args(a), ..) if a.len() == 2 && op_is_relop(op))
696    && !relates_a_conditional(&right)
697  {
698    return Ok(Some(distribute_list_relation(
699      left.unwrap(),
700      sep,
701      right,
702      ctxt,
703    )?));
704  }
705  list_or_formulae_create(left.unwrap(), sep, right, meaning, ctxt)
706}
707
708/// True iff `op` is a binary RELOP operator (`∈`, `≤`, `=`, …) — NOT a
709/// `multirelation` chain. Used to gate `distribute_list_relation`.
710fn op_is_relop(op: &Operator) -> bool {
711  !is_multirelation(&op.0) && operator_category(&op.0).is_some_and(|r| r.contains("RELOP"))
712}
713
714/// `a,b \in A` → the user-specified XMDual (2026-06-22, surpass-Perl): the content
715/// branch DISTRIBUTES the relation over each list element —
716/// `formulae@(∈(a,A), ∈(b,A))`, sharing XMRefs to the relop (∈) and RHS (A) — while
717/// the presentation branch wraps the list `a,b` in an `<XMWrap>` as the relation's
718/// LHS — `Apply(∈, XMWrap(a,',',b), A)`. `right` MUST be a binary RELOP relation
719/// (caller guarantees via `op_is_relop`).
720fn distribute_list_relation(
721  mut left: XM,
722  sep: XM,
723  right: XM,
724  ctxt: ActionContext,
725) -> Result<XM, Box<dyn Error>> {
726  let XM::Apply(Operator(r_op_box), Args(mut r_args), ..) = right else {
727    unreachable!("distribute_list_relation: caller guarantees a binary relation")
728  };
729  let mut rhs = r_args.pop().flatten().unwrap();
730  let mut lhs = r_args.pop().flatten().unwrap();
731  let mut r_op = *r_op_box;
732  // Ref the four presentation nodes (left, lhs, rhs, relop); rhs and relop are
733  // shared across the two distributed content relations.
734  let refs = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut left, &mut lhs, &mut rhs, &mut r_op], ctxt)?;
735  let mut it = refs.into_iter();
736  let ref_left = it.next().unwrap();
737  let ref_lhs = it.next().unwrap();
738  let ref_rhs = it.next().unwrap();
739  let ref_rop = it.next().unwrap();
740  let mk_rel = |op: XM, l: XM, r: XM| {
741    XM::Apply(
742      Operator(Box::new(op)),
743      Args(vec![Some(l), Some(r)]),
744      XProps::default(),
745      Meta::default(),
746    )
747  };
748  // content: formulae@(∈(a,A), ∈(b,A))
749  let rel1 = mk_rel(ref_rop.clone(), ref_left, ref_rhs.clone());
750  let rel2 = mk_rel(ref_rop, ref_lhs, ref_rhs);
751  let formulae_op: XM = XProps {
752    meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("formulae")),
753    ..XProps::default()
754  }
755  .into();
756  let content = XM::Apply(
757    Operator(Box::new(formulae_op)),
758    Args(vec![Some(rel1), Some(rel2)]),
759    XProps::default(),
760    Meta::default(),
761  );
762  // presentation: ∈(XMWrap(a,',',b), A)
763  let pres_wrap = XM::Wrap(vec![left, sep, lhs], XProps::default(), Meta::default());
764  let pres = XM::Apply(
765    Operator(Box::new(r_op)),
766    Args(vec![Some(pres_wrap), Some(rhs)]),
767    XProps::default(),
768    Meta::default(),
769  );
770  Ok(XM::Dual(
771    Box::new(content),
772    Box::new(pres),
773    XProps::default(),
774    Meta::default(),
775  ))
776}
777
778fn list_or_formulae_create(
779  mut left: XM,
780  sep: XM,
781  mut right: XM,
782  meaning: &'static str,
783  ctxt: ActionContext,
784) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
785  let op = XProps {
786    meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed(meaning)),
787    ..XProps::default()
788  };
789  let ref_args = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut left, &mut right], ctxt)?;
790  Ok(Some(XM::Dual(
791    Box::new(XM::Apply(
792      op.into(),
793      Args(ref_args.into_iter().map(Some).collect()),
794      XProps::default(),
795      Meta::default(),
796    )),
797    Box::new(XM::Wrap(
798      vec![left, sep, right],
799      XProps::default(),
800      Meta::default(),
801    )),
802    XProps::default(),
803    Meta::default(),
804  )))
805}
806
807/// Restructure flat formulae with \quad separators into right-recursive nesting.
808/// Perl's moreRHS/maybeColRHS builds right-recursive formulae@(f1, formulae@(f2, formulae@(f3,
809/// f4))) for \quad-separated relational expressions. The left-recursive Marpa grammar produces flat
810/// formulae@(f1, f2, f3, f4). This function converts flat to right-recursive after parsing.
811///
812/// The XMWrap items alternate: [item, sep, item, sep, item, ...]
813/// Only restructures when ALL separators are \quad-type (have name containing "uad").
814pub fn restructure_formulae_right(xm: &mut XM) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
815  // Recurse into children first (bottom-up)
816  match xm {
817    XM::Apply(_, args, ..) => {
818      for arg in args.0.iter_mut().flatten() {
819        restructure_formulae_right(arg)?;
820      }
821    },
822    XM::Wrap(items, ..) => {
823      for item in items.iter_mut() {
824        restructure_formulae_right(item)?;
825      }
826    },
827    XM::Dual(content, pres, ..) => {
828      restructure_formulae_right(content)?;
829      restructure_formulae_right(pres)?;
830      // NOTE: `\quad`-separated `formulae@(…)` are kept FLAT. We used to
831      // right-nest them here (`formulae@(f1, formulae@(f2, …))`) to mirror
832      // Perl's `moreRHS`/`maybeColRHS`, but a flat `formulae@(f1, f2, …)` is the
833      // correct shape — an intentional, user-directed divergence from Perl (see
834      // docs/parity/KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS.md).
835    },
836    XM::Choices(choices) => {
837      for choice in choices.iter_mut() {
838        restructure_formulae_right(choice)?;
839      }
840    },
841    XM::Arg(items) => {
842      for item in items.iter_mut() {
843        restructure_formulae_right(item)?;
844      }
845    },
846    _ => {},
847  }
848  Ok(())
849}
850
851/// The names of the ellipsis tokens: `\ldots` (and `\hdots`, `...`), `\dots` and amsmath's
852/// `\dotsc`/`\dotsb`/`\dotsm`/`\dotsi`/`\dotso`, `\cdots`.
853const ELLIPSIS_NAMES: [&str; 8] = [
854  "ldots", "dots", "dotsc", "dotsb", "dotsm", "dotsi", "dotso", "cdots",
855];
856
857/// An ellipsis item: an ELIDEOP (`\cdots`), or a token named as an ellipsis (`\ldots` and `\dots`
858/// are IDs, math_common.rs), read through an XMRef.
859pub(crate) fn is_ellipsis(xm: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
860  if operator_category(xm) == Some("ELIDEOP") {
861    return true;
862  }
863  match xm {
864    XM::Token(props, _) => props
865      .name
866      .as_deref()
867      .is_some_and(|name| ELLIPSIS_NAMES.contains(&name)),
868    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes).ok().is_some_and(|node| {
869      let node = crate::data::resolve_xmref(node).unwrap_or_else(|| node.clone());
870      node.get_name() == "XMTok"
871        && (node.get_attribute("role").as_deref() == Some("ELIDEOP")
872          || node
873            .get_attribute("name")
874            .is_some_and(|name| ELLIPSIS_NAMES.contains(&name.as_str())))
875    }),
876    _ => false,
877  }
878}
879
880/// A separator that ends a segment of a comma container: `\quad`-spaced punctuation (a `\quad`
881/// hint, or a comma the lexer read as WIDE_PUNCT for its `rpadding`), `;`, a period.
882fn ends_a_segment(sep: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
883  is_quad_separator(sep)
884    || matches!(operator_category(sep), Some("WIDE_PUNCT" | "PERIOD"))
885    || realized_value(sep, ctxt).is_ok_and(|value| value == ";" || value == ".")
886}
887
888/// A missing comma beside an ellipsis (user ruling 2026-09-29: split it off; Perl, and the parse,
889/// read `\{l_1,\cdots l_k\}` as `set@(l _ 1, cdots * l _ k)`): in a comma container, an item whose
890/// first-argument spine — through unfenced invisible products, sums and relations — reaches an
891/// invisible product that starts with an ellipsis gives the ellipsis up as an item of its own before
892/// it (`set@(l _ 1, cdots, l _ k)`, `k=0,1,\cdots L-1` `list@(k = 0, 1, cdots, L - 1)`); an item
893/// ending in one, before a comma, gives it up after it (`\{30,40\ldots,80\}`). The item as it would
894/// read with the comma typed, an invisible comma (U+2063) between — the separator Perl supplies for
895/// a missing one (`InvisibleComma`, MathParser.pm:1182-1183) — so `attach_enumerations`, which runs
896/// next, reads it as it reads the comma'd list. A post-pass like it: a grammar rule would need an
897/// ellipsis-item twin of every list action. Not an ellipsis before a visible operator (`x_1,\cdots
898/// +x_n` elides a sum), nor a decimal's trailing dots in a relation (`x=0.325\ldots`).
899/// Witnesses 2605.12837, 2605.12555, 2605.02211, 2605.00390, 2605.25695.
900pub fn separate_ellipsis_items(
901  xm: &mut XM,
902  ctxt: &mut ActionContext,
903) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
904  match xm {
905    XM::Apply(op, args, ..) => {
906      separate_ellipsis_items(&mut op.0, ctxt)?;
907      for arg in args.0.iter_mut().flatten() {
908        separate_ellipsis_items(arg, ctxt)?;
909      }
910    },
911    XM::Dual(content, pres, ..) => {
912      separate_ellipsis_items(content, ctxt)?;
913      separate_ellipsis_items(pres, ctxt)?;
914    },
915    XM::Wrap(items, ..) | XM::Arg(items) | XM::Choices(items) => {
916      for item in items.iter_mut() {
917        separate_ellipsis_items(item, ctxt)?;
918      }
919    },
920    _ => {},
921  }
922  separate_in_container(xm, ctxt)
923}
924
925/// The meanings of a comma container the split reads: a bare list or formulae, or a Fence-named one
926/// (`\{l_1,\cdots l_k\}` is `set@` already, `(a,\cdots b)` a pair).
927const COMMA_CONTAINERS: [&str; 8] = [
928  "list",
929  "formulae",
930  "set",
931  "vector",
932  "open-interval",
933  "closed-interval",
934  "open-closed-interval",
935  "closed-open-interval",
936];
937
938fn separate_in_container(xm: &mut XM, ctxt: &mut ActionContext) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
939  let XM::Dual(content, pres, _, dual_meta) = xm else {
940    return Ok(());
941  };
942  let XM::Apply(op, refs, ..) = &mut **content else {
943    return Ok(());
944  };
945  match (&mut *op.0, &mut **pres) {
946    // A comma container: `list@(…)` and its kin, presented as its items.
947    (XM::Token(op_props, _), XM::Wrap(wrapped, ..))
948      if op_props
949        .meaning
950        .as_deref()
951        .is_some_and(|m| COMMA_CONTAINERS.contains(&m)) =>
952    {
953      if separate_items(&mut refs.0, wrapped, ctxt)? {
954        match op_props.meaning.as_deref() {
955          // A comma formulae that gains a plain ellipsis item is named once the enumerations are
956          // attached (`name_an_elided_formulae`), as its comma'd twin reads.
957          Some("formulae") => dual_meta.elided_formulae = true,
958          // A pair that became three items is named as Perl's Fence names three (`encloseN`,
959          // MathParser.pm:1368-1377): between parentheses a vector, else a list.
960          Some(
961            "vector"
962            | "open-interval"
963            | "closed-interval"
964            | "open-closed-interval"
965            | "closed-open-interval",
966          ) => {
967            let parens = matches!((wrapped.first(), wrapped.last()), (Some(open), Some(close))
968              if realized_value(open, ctxt).is_ok_and(|v| v == "(") && realized_value(close, ctxt).is_ok_and(|v| v == ")"));
969            op_props.meaning = Some(Cow::Borrowed(if parens { "vector" } else { "list" }));
970          },
971          _ => {},
972        }
973      }
974    },
975    // A head applied to its arguments between delimiters (`\max(a_1,\ldots a_n)`): the content
976    // applies the head's ref to the argument refs, the presentation the head to the fenced wrap.
977    (XM::Ref(_), XM::Apply(_, pres_args, ..)) => {
978      if let [Some(XM::Wrap(wrapped, ..))] = pres_args.0.as_mut_slice()
979        && wrapped.len() == 2 * refs.0.len() + 1
980      {
981        separate_items(&mut refs.0, wrapped, ctxt)?;
982      }
983    },
984    _ => {},
985  }
986  Ok(())
987}
988
989/// Split the ellipses off the items of one comma container: its item refs and its presentation, the
990/// items with their separators, bare or between delimiters. Whether any item gave one up.
991fn separate_items(
992  refs: &mut Vec<Option<XM>>,
993  wrapped: &mut Vec<XM>,
994  ctxt: &mut ActionContext,
995) -> Result<bool, Box<dyn Error>> {
996  let n = refs.len();
997  if n < 2 || refs.iter().any(Option::is_none) {
998    return Ok(false);
999  }
1000  let fenced = wrapped.len() == 2 * n + 1;
1001  if !fenced && wrapped.len() != 2 * n - 1 {
1002    return Ok(false);
1003  }
1004  let offset = usize::from(fenced);
1005  let is_comma =
1006    |sep: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext| realized_value(sep, ctxt).is_ok_and(|value| value == ",");
1007  // Item k, with the ellipses it gives up before and after it.
1008  let mut new_wrapped: Vec<XM> = Vec::with_capacity(wrapped.len() + 4);
1009  let mut new_refs: Vec<Option<XM>> = Vec::with_capacity(n + 2);
1010  let old = std::mem::take(wrapped);
1011  let mut old_refs = std::mem::take(refs);
1012  let mut changed = false;
1013  let mut items: Vec<Option<XM>> = Vec::with_capacity(n);
1014  let mut separators: Vec<XM> = Vec::with_capacity(n);
1015  let (mut open, mut close) = (None, None);
1016  for (i, node) in old.into_iter().enumerate() {
1017    if fenced && i == 0 {
1018      open = Some(node);
1019    } else if fenced && i == 2 * n {
1020      close = Some(node);
1021    } else if (i - offset) % 2 == 0 {
1022      items.push(Some(node));
1023    } else {
1024      separators.push(node);
1025    }
1026  }
1027  let comma_before: Vec<bool> = (0..n)
1028    .map(|k| k > 0 && is_comma(&separators[k - 1], ctxt))
1029    .collect();
1030  let comma_after: Vec<bool> = (0..n)
1031    .map(|k| k + 1 < n && is_comma(&separators[k], ctxt))
1032    .collect();
1033  if let Some(open) = open {
1034    new_wrapped.push(open);
1035  }
1036  for k in 0..n {
1037    if k > 0 {
1038      new_wrapped.push(separators[k - 1].clone());
1039    }
1040    let mut item = items[k]
1041      .take()
1042      .ok_or("separate_ellipsis_items: item taken twice")?;
1043    let mut item_ref = old_refs[k].take();
1044    let leading = if comma_before[k] || (k == 0 && comma_after[k]) {
1045      take_edge_ellipsis(&mut item, true, true, ctxt)
1046    } else {
1047      None
1048    };
1049    let trailing = if comma_after[k] || (k + 1 == n && comma_before[k]) {
1050      take_edge_ellipsis(&mut item, false, true, ctxt)
1051    } else {
1052      None
1053    };
1054    if leading.is_some() || trailing.is_some() {
1055      changed = true;
1056      // The item may have collapsed to one factor: point its ref at what stands now (the item's own
1057      // key or id where it kept one).
1058      item_ref = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut item], ActionContext {
1059        nodes:    ctxt.nodes,
1060        document: &mut *ctxt.document,
1061      })?
1062      .into_iter()
1063      .next();
1064    }
1065    if let Some(mut ellipsis) = leading {
1066      let ellipsis_ref = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut ellipsis], ActionContext {
1067        nodes:    ctxt.nodes,
1068        document: &mut *ctxt.document,
1069      })?;
1070      new_wrapped.push(ellipsis);
1071      new_wrapped.push(XM::Token(invisible_comma(), Meta::default()));
1072      new_refs.extend(ellipsis_ref.into_iter().map(Some));
1073    }
1074    new_wrapped.push(item);
1075    new_refs.push(item_ref);
1076    if let Some(mut ellipsis) = trailing {
1077      let ellipsis_ref = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut ellipsis], ActionContext {
1078        nodes:    ctxt.nodes,
1079        document: &mut *ctxt.document,
1080      })?;
1081      new_wrapped.push(XM::Token(invisible_comma(), Meta::default()));
1082      new_wrapped.push(ellipsis);
1083      new_refs.extend(ellipsis_ref.into_iter().map(Some));
1084    }
1085  }
1086  if let Some(close) = close {
1087    new_wrapped.push(close);
1088  }
1089  *wrapped = new_wrapped;
1090  *refs = new_refs;
1091  Ok(changed)
1092}
1093
1094/// Take the ellipsis at the leading (or trailing) edge of `xm`'s spine: through unfenced invisible
1095/// products, sums and relations, to an invisible product of two or more factors whose edge factor is
1096/// an ellipsis. Stops at anything else — a fence, a Dual, a script, a node with its own key below the
1097/// root (another ref points at it). A product left with one factor is that factor.
1098fn take_edge_ellipsis(xm: &mut XM, leading: bool, root: bool, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> Option<XM> {
1099  let XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), props, meta) = xm else {
1100    return None;
1101  };
1102  if meta.fenced.is_some() || (!root && (props.xmkey.is_some() || props.id.is_some())) {
1103    return None;
1104  }
1105  let edge = if leading {
1106    args.iter().position(Option::is_some)?
1107  } else {
1108    args.iter().rposition(Option::is_some)?
1109  };
1110  let invisible_product = matches!(&**op, XM::Token(p, _) if p.content.as_deref() == Some("\u{2062}"))
1111    || is_invisible_times_lexeme(op);
1112  if invisible_product && args.iter().flatten().count() >= 2 {
1113    let is_edge_ellipsis = args[edge]
1114      .as_ref()
1115      .is_some_and(|factor| is_ellipsis(factor, ctxt));
1116    if !is_edge_ellipsis {
1117      return take_edge_ellipsis(args[edge].as_mut()?, leading, false, ctxt);
1118    }
1119    // A trailing ellipsis leaves one factor only (`40\ldots,80`): after a longer product it elides the
1120    // product (`p_1p_2\cdots, q`), and after a decimal it elides digits (`x=0.325\ldots`).
1121    if !leading && (args.iter().flatten().count() != 2 || ends_in_a_decimal(args, edge, ctxt)) {
1122      return None;
1123    }
1124    let ellipsis = args.remove(edge)?;
1125    if args.iter().flatten().count() == 1 {
1126      // The one factor left is the item; the caller makes its ref anew (the root's key is orphaned,
1127      // which `resolve_xmkeys` drops).
1128      *xm = args.iter_mut().find_map(Option::take)?;
1129    }
1130    return Some(ellipsis);
1131  }
1132  if matches!(operator_category(op), Some("ADDOP" | "BINOP")) || is_relational_op(op) {
1133    return take_edge_ellipsis(args[edge].as_mut()?, leading, false, ctxt);
1134  }
1135  None
1136}
1137
1138/// `x=0.325\ldots`, `x, 0.3\ldots`: the factor before a trailing ellipsis is a decimal — digit
1139/// elision, not a missing comma.
1140fn ends_in_a_decimal(args: &[Option<XM>], edge: usize, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
1141  edge > 0
1142    && args[..edge]
1143      .iter()
1144      .rev()
1145      .flatten()
1146      .next()
1147      .is_some_and(|before| {
1148        operator_category(before) == Some("NUMBER")
1149          && realized_value(before, ctxt).is_ok_and(|v| v.contains('.'))
1150      })
1151}
1152
1153fn is_invisible_times_lexeme(op: &XM) -> bool {
1154  matches!(op, XM::Lexeme(lex, _) if lex.starts_with("MULOP:") && lex.contains('\u{2062}'))
1155}
1156
1157/// The #37 ellipsis exception (user ruling 2026-09-29): an enumeration attaches to its relation. A
1158/// run of plain comma items holding an ellipsis is one operand, as Perl reads it (`maybeColRHS`,
1159/// `maybeRHS`, MathGrammar:146-170): the right operand of the relation before it when the run
1160/// reaches the end of its segment or ends in an item (`i=1,\ldots,n` `i = list@(1, ldots, n)`,
1161/// `i=1,\ldots,n, j=1,\ldots,m`), the left operand of the relation after it when it opens its
1162/// segment (`x_1,\ldots,x_n\in X` `list@(x _ 1, ldots, x _ n) element-of X`); a run ending in its
1163/// ellipsis between two relations stays (relation elision, `a_1=0,\ldots,a_n=0`; a bridging chain,
1164/// `G=G_0,G_1,\dots,G_L=G'`). Segments end at `\quad`, `;` and a period
1165/// (`\beta\in\mathbb{Q},\qquad\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_L\in\mathbb{C}`). A post-pass on the chosen
1166/// parse, like `rename_fenced_lists`: no parse trees are added (a grammar rule would need the whole
1167/// segment for its choice, and #37's over-parse would come back). The run items keep their keys —
1168/// their refs move from the container to the enumeration; a container left with one relation is
1169/// that relation, which takes the container's key. Plain lists keep #37 (`a=b,c,d`, `i=1,2`).
1170/// Where the run is plainly not the relation's operand it stays an item (57bv.1, the guards in
1171/// `attach_in_container`): a tuple component's equation between delimiters, a left operand past a
1172/// text, a run after a scripted member (`P_0=I,P_1,\dots`), bridging to one, or after a relation that
1173/// closes an elided run of relations, and "and so on" before a repeated statement.
1174/// Witnesses 2605.12085, 2605.00329 (left), 2605.00515 (set-builder), 2605.21039 (43 formulas).
1175pub fn attach_enumerations(xm: &mut XM, ctxt: &mut ActionContext) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
1176  attach_enumerations_in(xm, ctxt, false)
1177}
1178
1179/// `attach_enumerations` on `xm`, which stands between delimiters of its own when `delimited` (the
1180/// middle of a fence's `Wrap(open, xm, close)`, `fenced`).
1181fn attach_enumerations_in(
1182  xm: &mut XM,
1183  ctxt: &mut ActionContext,
1184  delimited: bool,
1185) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
1186  match xm {
1187    XM::Apply(op, args, ..) => {
1188      attach_enumerations_in(&mut op.0, ctxt, false)?;
1189      for arg in args.0.iter_mut().flatten() {
1190        attach_enumerations_in(arg, ctxt, false)?;
1191      }
1192    },
1193    XM::Dual(content, pres, ..) => {
1194      attach_enumerations_in(content, ctxt, false)?;
1195      attach_enumerations_in(pres, ctxt, false)?;
1196    },
1197    XM::Wrap(items, ..) => {
1198      let fence = items.len() == 3
1199        && operator_category(&items[0]) == Some("OPEN")
1200        && operator_category(&items[2]) == Some("CLOSE");
1201      for (k, item) in items.iter_mut().enumerate() {
1202        attach_enumerations_in(item, ctxt, fence && k == 1)?;
1203      }
1204    },
1205    XM::Arg(items) | XM::Choices(items) => {
1206      for item in items.iter_mut() {
1207        attach_enumerations_in(item, ctxt, false)?;
1208      }
1209    },
1210    _ => {},
1211  }
1212  if let Some(relation) = attach_in_container(xm, ctxt, delimited)? {
1213    *xm = relation;
1214  } else {
1215    name_an_elided_formulae(xm, ctxt);
1216  }
1217  Ok(())
1218}
1219
1220/// A comma formulae that `separate_ellipsis_items` gave a plain ellipsis item (`Meta::elided_formulae`)
1221/// and that still holds one, once the enumerations are attached, is a list, as its comma'd twin reads
1222/// (`x_{1}=0,\dots x_{n}=0` as `a_1=0,\ldots,a_n=0`); one whose ellipsis a relation took stays
1223/// formulae (`\{\epsilon_i, i=1, 2,\ldots n\}` as its twin set@(formulae@(ε_i, i = list@(1, 2, ldots,
1224/// n))); 57bv A/B, 2605.00514). A formulae the grammar built keeps its name.
1225fn name_an_elided_formulae(xm: &mut XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) {
1226  if let XM::Dual(content, pres, _, meta) = xm
1227    && meta.elided_formulae
1228    && let XM::Apply(op, ..) = &mut **content
1229    && let XM::Token(op_props, _) = &mut *op.0
1230    && op_props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("formulae")
1231    && let XM::Wrap(wrapped, ..) = &**pres
1232    && wrapped.iter().any(|item| is_ellipsis(item, ctxt))
1233  {
1234    op_props.meaning = Some(Cow::Borrowed("list"));
1235  }
1236}
1237
1238/// One block of a rebuilt container: an item kept as it stood, or a relation with the enumeration
1239/// runs it takes (item indices), left and right.
1240struct EnumerationBlock {
1241  item:  usize,
1242  left:  Vec<usize>,
1243  right: Vec<usize>,
1244}
1245
1246fn attach_in_container(
1247  xm: &mut XM,
1248  ctxt: &mut ActionContext,
1249  delimited: bool,
1250) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
1251  let XM::Dual(content, pres, dual_props, _) = xm else {
1252    return Ok(None);
1253  };
1254  let XM::Apply(op, refs, ..) = &mut **content else {
1255    return Ok(None);
1256  };
1257  let XM::Token(op_props, _) = &mut *op.0 else {
1258    return Ok(None);
1259  };
1260  if !matches!(
1261    op_props.meaning.as_deref(),
1262    Some("list" | "formulae" | "fragments")
1263  ) {
1264    return Ok(None);
1265  }
1266  let XM::Wrap(wrapped, ..) = &mut **pres else {
1267    return Ok(None);
1268  };
1269  let n = refs.0.len();
1270  if n < 2 || refs.0.iter().any(Option::is_none) {
1271    return Ok(None);
1272  }
1273  let fenced = wrapped.len() == 2 * n + 1;
1274  if !fenced && wrapped.len() != 2 * n - 1 {
1275    return Ok(None);
1276  }
1277  let offset = usize::from(fenced);
1278  let item = |k: usize| &wrapped[offset + 2 * k];
1279  let separator = |k: usize| &wrapped[offset + 2 * k + 1];
1280  let relational: Vec<bool> = (0..n)
1281    .map(|k| {
1282      matches!(item(k), XM::Apply(_, args, ..) if args.0.len() >= 2) && is_relational_item(item(k))
1283    })
1284    .collect();
1285  let ellipsis: Vec<bool> = (0..n).map(|k| is_ellipsis(item(k), ctxt)).collect();
1286  if !ellipsis.iter().any(|e| *e) || !relational.iter().any(|r| *r) {
1287    return Ok(None);
1288  }
1289  // A run: maximal plain items holding an ellipsis, within a segment.
1290  let mut owner: Vec<Option<(usize, bool)>> = vec![None; n]; // (relation, attached on its right)
1291  // A relation whose left run is refused (`takes_left`): a tuple component, which takes no run on its
1292  // right either (`(0,\ldots,0,k_\ell=k,0,\ldots,0)`, 2605.09683).
1293  let mut stranded = vec![false; n];
1294  // A plain run (no ellipsis) beside an attached enumeration: `i=1,\ldots,4,\,j=0,1,2` and
1295  // `d=0,1,\,k=1,\ldots,K` (2605.18167) attach it too (user ruling 2026-09-29, both directions;
1296  // `plain_runs` below, divergence #378), as Perl's `maybeColRHS` attaches every run (MathGrammar:165-172).
1297  let mut ranged = vec![false; n];
1298  let mut plain_runs: Vec<(usize, usize, usize)> = Vec::new(); // (first, last, relation)
1299  let mut start = 0;
1300  while start < n {
1301    let mut end = start;
1302    while end + 1 < n && !ends_a_segment(separator(end), ctxt) {
1303      end += 1;
1304    }
1305    let mut k = start;
1306    while k <= end {
1307      if relational[k] {
1308        k += 1;
1309        continue;
1310      }
1311      let first = k;
1312      while k <= end && !relational[k] {
1313        k += 1;
1314      }
1315      let last = k - 1;
1316      let plain = !(first..=last).any(|j| ellipsis[j]);
1317      let before = (first > start && relational[first - 1]).then(|| first - 1);
1318      let after = (last < end && relational[last + 1]).then_some(last + 1);
1319      // A lone ellipsis after a chain of relations is "and so on" (`x=0, y=1, \ldots`), not the last
1320      // relation's value (57bv review); after one relation it is (`i=1,\ldots`).
1321      // So is one before a break whose next relation repeats the last one's left operand — the
1322      // statements go on (`f(v_1)=f(v_2),\dots,\quad f(v_{k-1})=f(v_k)`, 2605.00553;
1323      // `p\leftarrow…,\ \cdots,\quad p\leftarrow…`, 2605.09708).
1324      let repeats_its_statement = |relation: usize| {
1325        end + 1 < n
1326          && relational[end + 1]
1327          && same_progression(
1328            relation_operands(item(relation)).0,
1329            relation_operands(item(end + 1)).0,
1330            ctxt,
1331          )
1332      };
1333      let lone_and_so_on = first == last
1334        && ellipsis[first]
1335        && before.is_some_and(|relation| {
1336          relation > start && relational[relation - 1] || repeats_its_statement(relation)
1337        });
1338      let run: Vec<&XM> = (first..=last).filter(|&j| !ellipsis[j]).map(item).collect();
1339      // A relation takes the run on its right when it opens it: not when it closes an elided run of
1340      // relations (`A_1\lhd B_1,\ldots,A_n\lhd B_n,C_1,\ldots`, 2605.14476), nor when its left operand
1341      // is a scripted member of the run — its letter a scripted run item's — and its right is none
1342      // (`P_0=I,P_1,\dots,P_n`, 2605.23874; `i=1,\ldots,i_{\max}`, `l''=l,\ldots,l'`, `T_{train}\subseteq
1343      // 1,\ldots,T` attach, 2605.24906), nor after a stranded run.
1344      let takes_right = |relation: usize| {
1345        let (left, right) = relation_operands(item(relation));
1346        let closes_an_elided_run =
1347          relation >= start + 2 && ellipsis[relation - 1] && relational[relation - 2];
1348        let scripted_run: Vec<&XM> = run
1349          .iter()
1350          .copied()
1351          .filter(|item| script_base(item).is_some())
1352          .collect();
1353        let member_left = left.is_some_and(|left| script_base(left).is_some())
1354          && shares_progression(left, &scripted_run, ctxt)
1355          && !shares_progression(right, &run, ctxt);
1356        !closes_an_elided_run && !member_left && !stranded[relation]
1357      };
1358      // A relation takes the run on its left (Perl's `maybeRHS`, MathGrammar:146-150), except past a
1359      // text (`\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_k\text{ s.t. gaps }\geq\delta`, 2605.23087) and except a tuple
1360      // component's equation: between delimiters, an `=` whose left operand does not continue the run
1361      // or whose right is one of it (`(j_1,\ldots,j_L,j_{L+1}=j_1)`, `\{v_1,\ldots,u=\{v_0,v_k\}\}`,
1362      // `(0,\ldots,0,k_\ell=k,0,\ldots,0)`; 2605.18633, 2605.24348, 2605.09683).
1363      let takes_left = |relation: usize| {
1364        let (left, right) = relation_operands(item(relation));
1365        let component = (fenced || delimited)
1366          && matches!(item(relation), XM::Apply(Operator(op), ..)
1367            if realized_meaning(op, ctxt).as_deref() == Some("equals"))
1368          && (!continues_progression(left, &run, ctxt) || shares_progression(right, &run, ctxt));
1369        !left.is_some_and(|left| holds_text(left, ctxt)) && !component
1370      };
1371      // A run between two relations is the first one's value unless it bridges a chain to the next,
1372      // whose left operand is a scripted member (`a=a_0,a_1,\dots,a_{n-1},a_n=b` as
1373      // `G=G_0,G_1,\dots,G_L=G'`; 2605.24348, 2605.17185; `i=1,\ldots,n,\ n\geq 2` attaches).
1374      let bridges = |next: usize| {
1375        let left = relation_operands(item(next)).0;
1376        left.is_some_and(|left| script_base(left).is_some()) && shares_progression(left, &run, ctxt)
1377      };
1378      // A plain run continues the relation before it in its own segment — each item of its right
1379      // operand's progression, a number after a number, the same letter under scripts, a plain letter
1380      // after plain letters — and bridges no chain to the next (`i=1,\ldots,n,\ x=0, y`,
1381      // `x_1,\dots,x_n=0, y` keep theirs as items); attached after the segment loop, if another
1382      // relation of the container took an enumeration on its right.
1383      if plain {
1384        if let Some(relation) = before
1385          && takes_right(relation)
1386          && after.is_none_or(|next| !bridges(next))
1387          && let (_, Some(value)) = relation_operands(item(relation))
1388          && (first..=last).all(|j| continues_progression(Some(item(j)), &[value], ctxt))
1389        {
1390          plain_runs.push((first, last, relation));
1391        }
1392        continue;
1393      }
1394      let target = match (before, after) {
1395        (Some(_), None) if lone_and_so_on => None,
1396        (Some(relation), None) if takes_right(relation) => Some((relation, true)),
1397        (Some(relation), Some(next))
1398          if !ellipsis[last] && !bridges(next) && takes_right(relation) =>
1399        {
1400          Some((relation, true))
1401        },
1402        (None, Some(relation)) if first == start => {
1403          if takes_left(relation) {
1404            Some((relation, false))
1405          } else {
1406            stranded[relation] = true;
1407            None
1408          }
1409        },
1410        _ => None,
1411      };
1412      if let Some(target) = target {
1413        if target.1 {
1414          ranged[target.0] = true;
1415        }
1416        for slot in owner.iter_mut().take(last + 1).skip(first) {
1417          *slot = Some(target);
1418        }
1419      }
1420    }
1421    start = end + 1;
1422  }
1423  for (first, last, relation) in plain_runs {
1424    if ranged
1425      .iter()
1426      .enumerate()
1427      .any(|(other, &ranged)| ranged && other != relation)
1428    {
1429      for slot in owner.iter_mut().take(last + 1).skip(first) {
1430        *slot = Some((relation, true));
1431      }
1432    }
1433  }
1434  if owner.iter().all(Option::is_none) {
1435    return Ok(None);
1436  }
1437  // Blocks in source order: each relation with its runs, each other item alone.
1438  let mut blocks: Vec<EnumerationBlock> = Vec::new();
1439  for (k, slot) in owner.iter().enumerate() {
1440    match *slot {
1441      Some((relation, right)) => {
1442        let index = blocks.iter().position(|b| b.item == relation);
1443        let block = match index {
1444          Some(i) => &mut blocks[i],
1445          None => {
1446            blocks.push(EnumerationBlock {
1447              item:  relation,
1448              left:  Vec::new(),
1449              right: Vec::new(),
1450            });
1451            blocks.last_mut().unwrap()
1452          },
1453        };
1454        if right {
1455          block.right.push(k);
1456        } else {
1457          block.left.push(k);
1458        }
1459      },
1460      None if blocks.iter().any(|b| b.item == k) => {},
1461      None => blocks.push(EnumerationBlock {
1462        item:  k,
1463        left:  Vec::new(),
1464        right: Vec::new(),
1465      }),
1466    }
1467  }
1468  let block_start = |b: &EnumerationBlock| b.left.first().copied().unwrap_or(b.item);
1469  // Take the pieces out of the container.
1470  let mut items: Vec<Option<XM>> = Vec::with_capacity(n);
1471  let mut separators: Vec<Option<XM>> = Vec::with_capacity(n);
1472  let old = std::mem::take(wrapped);
1473  let (open, close) = if fenced {
1474    (old.first().cloned(), old.last().cloned())
1475  } else {
1476    (None, None)
1477  };
1478  for (i, node) in old.into_iter().enumerate() {
1479    if fenced && (i == 0 || i == 2 * n) {
1480      continue;
1481    }
1482    if (i - offset) % 2 == 0 {
1483      items.push(Some(node));
1484    } else {
1485      separators.push(Some(node));
1486    }
1487  }
1488  let mut item_refs: Vec<Option<XM>> = std::mem::take(&mut refs.0);
1489  let mut new_wrapped: Vec<XM> = Vec::with_capacity(2 * blocks.len() + 1);
1490  let mut new_refs: Vec<Option<XM>> = Vec::with_capacity(blocks.len());
1491  if let Some(open) = open {
1492    new_wrapped.push(open);
1493  }
1494  let mut all_relational = true;
1495  for (b, block) in blocks.iter().enumerate() {
1496    if b > 0
1497      && let Some(sep) = separators[block_start(block) - 1].take()
1498    {
1499      new_wrapped.push(sep);
1500    }
1501    let mut node = items[block.item]
1502      .take()
1503      .ok_or("attach_enumerations: item taken twice")?;
1504    if !block.left.is_empty() || !block.right.is_empty() {
1505      let XM::Apply(_, args, ..) = &mut node else {
1506        return Err("attach_enumerations: relation is not an application".into());
1507      };
1508      if !block.left.is_empty()
1509        && let Some(slot) = args.0.iter_mut().find(|a| a.is_some())
1510      {
1511        let mut operand = slot.take().ok_or("attach_enumerations: no left operand")?;
1512        let operand_ref = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut operand], ActionContext {
1513          nodes:    ctxt.nodes,
1514          document: &mut *ctxt.document,
1515        })?;
1516        let mut wrap = Vec::new();
1517        let mut run_refs = Vec::new();
1518        for &k in &block.left {
1519          wrap.push(
1520            items[k]
1521              .take()
1522              .ok_or("attach_enumerations: run item taken twice")?,
1523          );
1524          wrap.push(
1525            separators[k]
1526              .take()
1527              .ok_or("attach_enumerations: run separator taken twice")?,
1528          );
1529          run_refs.push(item_refs[k].take());
1530        }
1531        wrap.push(operand);
1532        run_refs.extend(operand_ref.into_iter().map(Some));
1533        *slot = Some(enumeration(run_refs, wrap));
1534      }
1535      if !block.right.is_empty()
1536        && let Some(slot) = args.0.iter_mut().rev().find(|a| a.is_some())
1537      {
1538        let mut operand = slot.take().ok_or("attach_enumerations: no right operand")?;
1539        let operand_ref = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut operand], ActionContext {
1540          nodes:    ctxt.nodes,
1541          document: &mut *ctxt.document,
1542        })?;
1543        let mut wrap = vec![operand];
1544        let mut run_refs: Vec<Option<XM>> = operand_ref.into_iter().map(Some).collect();
1545        let mut previous = block.item;
1546        for &k in &block.right {
1547          wrap.push(
1548            separators[previous]
1549              .take()
1550              .ok_or("attach_enumerations: run separator taken twice")?,
1551          );
1552          wrap.push(
1553            items[k]
1554              .take()
1555              .ok_or("attach_enumerations: run item taken twice")?,
1556          );
1557          run_refs.push(item_refs[k].take());
1558          previous = k;
1559        }
1560        *slot = Some(enumeration(run_refs, wrap));
1561      }
1562    } else {
1563      all_relational &= relational[block.item];
1564    }
1565    new_wrapped.push(node);
1566    new_refs.push(item_refs[block.item].take());
1567  }
1568  if let Some(close) = close {
1569    new_wrapped.push(close);
1570  }
1571  if new_refs.len() == 1 && !fenced {
1572    // One relation left: it is the formula, under the container's key.
1573    let mut relation = new_wrapped
1574      .pop()
1575      .ok_or("attach_enumerations: empty container")?;
1576    // Its own key was the container's ref to it, now gone: it takes the container's (an outer ref's
1577    // target), or none, so no orphan id is minted.
1578    if let XM::Apply(_, _, props, _) = &mut relation {
1579      props.xmkey = dual_props.xmkey.clone();
1580      if dual_props.id.is_some() {
1581        props.id = dual_props.id.clone();
1582      }
1583    }
1584    return Ok(Some(relation));
1585  }
1586  *wrapped = new_wrapped;
1587  refs.0 = new_refs;
1588  if all_relational && op_props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("list") {
1589    op_props.meaning = Some(Cow::Borrowed("formulae"));
1590  }
1591  Ok(None)
1592}
1593
1594/// A comma container of statements a bare condition cannot hold: two relations then an index range —
1595/// an ellipsis with an item after the last relation (`\theta_i\sim P,\ i=1,\ldots,n`) — or a relation and a
1596/// `\quad`-spaced separator (`,\quad`). An elided run of relations (`X_n=i,\ldots,X_0=i_0`), "and so on"
1597/// after them (`X_n=i_n,X_{n-1}=i_{n-1},\ldots`), one relation's range (`\sum_{j|j=1,\ldots,n}`) and a `;`
1598/// (`y|x=1;\theta`) stay conditions.
1599fn is_statement_list(xm: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
1600  let XM::Dual(content, pres, ..) = xm else {
1601    return false;
1602  };
1603  let XM::Apply(op, refs, ..) = &**content else {
1604    return false;
1605  };
1606  if !matches!(&*op.0, XM::Token(props, _)
1607    if matches!(props.meaning.as_deref(), Some("list" | "formulae" | "fragments")))
1608  {
1609    return false;
1610  }
1611  let XM::Wrap(wrapped, ..) = &**pres else {
1612    return false;
1613  };
1614  let n = refs.0.len();
1615  let fenced = wrapped.len() == 2 * n + 1;
1616  if n < 2 || !fenced && wrapped.len() != 2 * n - 1 {
1617    return false;
1618  }
1619  let offset = usize::from(fenced);
1620  let items: Vec<&XM> = (0..n).map(|k| &wrapped[offset + 2 * k]).collect();
1621  let relations: Vec<usize> = (0..n)
1622    .filter(|&k| {
1623      matches!(items[k], XM::Apply(_, args, ..) if args.0.len() >= 2)
1624        && is_relational_item(items[k])
1625    })
1626    .collect();
1627  let Some(&last_relation) = relations.last() else {
1628    return false;
1629  };
1630  let tail = &items[last_relation + 1..];
1631  let index_range = relations.len() >= 2
1632    && tail.iter().any(|item| is_ellipsis(item, ctxt))
1633    && tail.iter().any(|item| !is_ellipsis(item, ctxt));
1634  let crosses_a_segment = (0..n - 1).any(|k| {
1635    let separator = &wrapped[offset + 2 * k + 1];
1636    is_quad_separator(separator) || operator_category(separator) == Some("WIDE_PUNCT")
1637  });
1638  index_range || crosses_a_segment
1639}
1640
1641/// A relation's outer operands: its first and last (`x_n\in X` → `x_n`, `X`).
1642fn relation_operands(relation: &XM) -> (Option<&XM>, Option<&XM>) {
1643  match relation {
1644    XM::Apply(_, Args(args), ..) => (
1645      args.iter().flatten().next(),
1646      args.iter().flatten().next_back(),
1647    ),
1648    _ => (None, None),
1649  }
1650}
1651
1652/// What makes an item a member of an enumeration's progression: its letter under its scripts
1653/// (`x_1`, `x^{(n)}`, `l''` → x, x, l), a number, or an applied letter (`f(x_1)` → f).
1654fn progression_key(xm: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> Option<String> {
1655  let nucleus = script_nucleus(xm);
1656  match nucleus {
1657    XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..) => {
1658      if operator_category(nucleus) == Some("NUMBER") {
1659        Some("#".to_string())
1660      } else {
1661        realized_value(nucleus, ctxt)
1662          .ok()
1663          .filter(|v| !v.is_empty())
1664          .map(|v| v.into_owned())
1665      }
1666    },
1667    XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(args), ..)
1668      if args.len() == 1
1669        && matches!(**head, XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..))
1670        && matches!(operator_category(head), Some("UNKNOWN" | "FUNCTION")) =>
1671    {
1672      realized_value(head, ctxt).ok().map(|v| format!("@{v}"))
1673    },
1674    // a signed number is a number: `j=-1,0,1` (57cc review; `\mathcal J\in\{-1,0,1\}^d` shapes)
1675    XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(args), ..)
1676      if operator_category(head) == Some("ADDOP")
1677        && matches!(args.as_slice(), [Some(number)] if operator_category(number) == Some("NUMBER")) =>
1678    {
1679      Some("#".to_string())
1680    },
1681    _ => None,
1682  }
1683}
1684
1685/// Do two operands share a progression key (`f(v_1)`, `f(v_{k-1})`)?
1686fn same_progression(a: Option<&XM>, b: Option<&XM>, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
1687  let key = |xm: Option<&XM>| xm.and_then(|xm| progression_key(xm, ctxt));
1688  key(a).is_some_and(|a| key(b).as_ref() == Some(&a))
1689}
1690
1691/// Does `xm` hold a text (an `XMText` lexeme) outside its scripts? A scripted item is its base
1692/// (`x_{\text{out}}`, `\underbrace{…}_{\textrm{…}}` hold none; 57bv.1 review, 2605.11818, 2605.01053).
1693fn holds_text(xm: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
1694  if let Some(base) = script_base(xm) {
1695    return holds_text(base, ctxt);
1696  }
1697  match xm {
1698    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => {
1699      lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes).is_ok_and(|node| node.get_name() == "XMText")
1700    },
1701    XM::Apply(op, args, ..) => {
1702      holds_text(&op.0, ctxt) || args.0.iter().flatten().any(|arg| holds_text(arg, ctxt))
1703    },
1704    XM::Dual(_, pres, ..) => holds_text(pres, ctxt),
1705    XM::Wrap(items, ..) | XM::Arg(items) => items.iter().any(|item| holds_text(item, ctxt)),
1706    _ => false,
1707  }
1708}
1709
1710/// Does `operand` share a progression key with an item of the run?
1711fn shares_progression(operand: Option<&XM>, run: &[&XM], ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
1712  operand
1713    .and_then(|operand| progression_key(operand, ctxt))
1714    .is_some_and(|key| {
1715      run
1716        .iter()
1717        .any(|item| progression_key(item, ctxt).as_ref() == Some(&key))
1718    })
1719}
1720
1721/// Does `operand` continue the run: of its progression, or a plain letter after plain letters
1722/// (`x,y,\ldots,z`)?
1723fn continues_progression(operand: Option<&XM>, run: &[&XM], ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
1724  let plain_letter = |xm: &XM| {
1725    matches!(xm, XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..))
1726      && operator_category(xm) == Some("UNKNOWN")
1727      && realized_value(xm, ctxt).is_ok_and(|v| v.chars().count() == 1)
1728  };
1729  shares_progression(operand, run, ctxt)
1730    || operand
1731      .is_some_and(|operand| plain_letter(operand) && run.iter().any(|item| plain_letter(item)))
1732}
1733
1734/// An enumeration: a flat `list@(…)` whose presentation holds the items as written.
1735fn enumeration(refs: Vec<Option<XM>>, wrapped: Vec<XM>) -> XM {
1736  let op = XProps {
1737    meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("list")),
1738    ..XProps::default()
1739  };
1740  XM::Dual(
1741    Box::new(XM::Apply(
1742      op.into(),
1743      Args(refs),
1744      XProps::default(),
1745      Meta::default(),
1746    )),
1747    Box::new(XM::Wrap(wrapped, XProps::default(), Meta::default())),
1748    XProps::default(),
1749    Meta::default(),
1750  )
1751}
1752
1753/// Check if an XM node is a \quad-type separator (XMHint PUNCT with name containing "uad").
1754fn is_quad_separator(xm: &XM) -> bool {
1755  match xm {
1756    XM::Token(props, _) => props.name.as_deref().is_some_and(|n| n.contains("uad")),
1757    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lex.split(':').nth(1).is_some_and(|t| t.contains("uad")),
1758    _ => false,
1759  }
1760}
1761
1762/// Post-processing: name the fenced lists and paren pairs of the chosen parse.
1763/// Perl's Fence receives flat (open, item, punct, ..., close) and uses encloseN tables.
1764/// Our grammar builds `list` via `list_apply` before fencing can see the items, so a list Dual whose
1765/// presentation XMWrap starts with OPEN and ends with CLOSE takes the encloseN meaning here; and a
1766/// two-item comma pair between parentheses is named by the slot it fills (`paren_pair_meaning`), once,
1767/// on the parse already chosen, so its name no longer depends on which derivation Marpa enumerated
1768/// first (`interval_term`'s open-interval, `fenced`'s vector).
1769pub fn rename_fenced_lists(xm: &mut XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
1770  name_fenced_lists(xm, PairSlot::Other, ctxt)
1771}
1772
1773/// The slot a paren pair fills (`operand_slots`): one that holds a set (`x\in(0,1)`), a function's
1774/// argument group (`f(a,b)`, `u(x,\infty)`), or any other.
1775#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
1776enum PairSlot {
1777  Set,
1778  Argument,
1779  Other,
1780}
1781
1782fn name_fenced_lists(
1783  xm: &mut XM,
1784  slot: PairSlot,
1785  ctxt: &ActionContext,
1786) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
1787  match xm {
1788    XM::Apply(op, args, ..) => {
1789      let slots = operand_slots(&op.0, &args.0, slot, ctxt);
1790      for (arg, slot) in args.0.iter_mut().zip(slots) {
1791        if let Some(arg) = arg {
1792          name_fenced_lists(arg, slot, ctxt)?;
1793        }
1794      }
1795    },
1796    XM::Wrap(items, ..) => {
1797      // A single item between parentheses is transparent to a set slot: `\subset((-0.28,0))`
1798      // (2605.01702); an argument group's inner pair is an item of its own (`\mu((x,\infty))`).
1799      let transparent = items.len() == 3 && is_paren_wrap(items, ctxt);
1800      for (i, item) in items.iter_mut().enumerate() {
1801        let inner = if slot == PairSlot::Set && transparent && i == 1 {
1802          PairSlot::Set
1803        } else {
1804          PairSlot::Other
1805        };
1806        name_fenced_lists(item, inner, ctxt)?;
1807      }
1808      // Check if this Wrap is exactly [OPEN, list_Dual, CLOSE] — rename list meaning
1809      // Handles script content like ^{(1+,0+,1-,0-)} where OPEN/CLOSE are siblings
1810      // of the list Dual in the script's presentation Wrap. Only then: a list among other items
1811      // is not the delimiters' own — `p(x|y,z)`'s `y,z` is the conditional's condition, not an
1812      // open interval (57bd; ≤3,964 formulas in 511 papers of the 57bb A/B, 2605.00161
1813      // `q(x_s\mid x_t,x_0)`; Perl `conditional@(x, list@(y, z))`).
1814      if items.len() == 3 {
1815        let first_role = get_xm_role(&items[0]);
1816        let last_role = get_xm_role(items.last().unwrap());
1817        if first_role.as_deref() == Some("OPEN") && last_role.as_deref() == Some("CLOSE") {
1818          let o_val: String = realized_value(&items[0], ctxt)?.into_owned();
