1819          let c_val: String = realized_value(items.last().unwrap(), ctxt)?.into_owned();
1820          // Rename the list Dual between the delimiters (the wrap's one inner item)
1821          if let Some(item) = items.get_mut(1) {
1822            // A bare list only (its presentation `[item, separator, item, …]`): a list that carries
1823            // its own delimiters is fenced already (`\left([a;b]\right)`: `list@(a, b)`, not the
1824            // parens' `open-interval`; 57av train A/B, 2605.08815).
1825            // And a comma list only: Perl's enclose tables are keyed by the first separator and name
1826            // comma lists alone (MathParser.pm:1368-1377), `x^{(a;b)}` `x ^ (list@(a, b))` (57ay review).
1827            if let XM::Dual(content, presentation, ..) = item
1828              && let XM::Apply(ref mut op, ref args, ..) = **content
1829              && let XM::Token(ref mut props, _) = *op.0
1830              && props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("list")
1831              && presents_its_items_alone(presentation, args.0.len())
1832              && let XM::Wrap(ref separated, ..) = **presentation
1833              && separated
1834                .iter()
1835                .skip(1)
1836                .step_by(2)
1837                .map(|separator| realized_value(separator, ctxt))
1838                .find(|value| !value.as_deref().is_ok_and(|v| v == "\u{2063}"))
1839                .is_some_and(|value| value.is_ok_and(|v| v == ","))
1840            {
1841              let n = args.0.len();
1842              let new_meaning = match (o_val.as_ref(), c_val.as_ref()) {
1843                ("(", ")") if n == 2 => {
1844                  Some(paren_pair_meaning(slot, &separated[0], &separated[2], ctxt))
1845                },
1846                ("[", "]") if n == 2 => Some("closed-interval"),
1847                ("(", "]") if n == 2 => Some("open-closed-interval"),
1848                ("[", ")") if n == 2 => Some("closed-open-interval"),
1849                ("{", "}") => Some("set"),
1850                ("(", ")") => Some("vector"), // n >= 3
1851                _ => None,
1852              };
1853              if let Some(m) = new_meaning {
1854                props.meaning = Some(Cow::Borrowed(m));
1855              }
1856            }
1857          }
1858        }
1859      }
1860    },
1861    XM::Dual(content, pres, ..) => {
1862      if is_paren_pair(content, pres, ctxt) {
1863        if let XM::Wrap(ref wrapped, ..) = **pres
1864          && let XM::Apply(ref mut op, ..) = **content
1865          && let XM::Token(ref mut props, _) = *op.0
1866        {
1867          props.meaning = Some(Cow::Borrowed(paren_pair_meaning(
1868            slot,
1869            &wrapped[1],
1870            &wrapped[3],
1871            ctxt,
1872          )));
1873        }
1874        name_fenced_lists(content, PairSlot::Other, ctxt)?;
1875        name_fenced_lists(pres, PairSlot::Other, ctxt)?;
1876      } else {
1877        name_fenced_lists(content, slot, ctxt)?;
1878        name_fenced_lists(pres, slot, ctxt)?;
1879      }
1880    },
1881    XM::Choices(trees) => {
1882      for tree in trees.iter_mut() {
1883        name_fenced_lists(tree, slot, ctxt)?;
1884      }
1885    },
1886    XM::Arg(items) => {
1887      for item in items.iter_mut() {
1888        name_fenced_lists(item, PairSlot::Other, ctxt)?;
1889      }
1890    },
1891    _ => {},
1892  }
1893  Ok(())
1894}
1895
1896/// A two-item comma pair between parentheses: a Dual applying `vector` or `open-interval` to two items,
1897/// presented `( a , b )`.
1898fn is_paren_pair(content: &XM, presentation: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
1899  matches!(content, XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..)
1900    if args.len() == 2
1901      && matches!(&**op, XM::Token(props, _)
1902        if matches!(props.meaning.as_deref(), Some("vector" | "open-interval"))))
1903    && matches!(presentation, XM::Wrap(wrapped, ..)
1904      if wrapped.len() == 5
1905        && is_paren_wrap(wrapped, ctxt)
1906        && realized_value(&wrapped[2], ctxt).is_ok_and(|v| v == ","))
1907}
1908
1909/// A two-item comma pair between parentheses is an open interval where the slot holds a set, a vector
1910/// — a pair, a point — elsewhere (user ruling 2026-09-29, divergence #371; Perl names every one
1911/// `open-interval`, `%enclose2` MathParser.pm:1369). Outside a set or argument slot an infinite
1912/// endpoint on its own side makes an interval (`(0,\infty)`, `(-\infty,0]`, `C^1((0,\infty))`,
1913/// 2605.00581); a function's argument pair stays a vector (`u(x,\infty)`, `\Pi(M^2,\infty)`,
1914/// 2605.28015) unless it runs from −∞ to ∞ or to a number (`S(-\infty,\infty)`, 57bx), and so does
1915/// `(\infty,1)` (higher categories, 2605.30648).
1916fn paren_pair_meaning(
1917  slot: PairSlot,
1918  first: &XM,
1919  second: &XM,
1920  ctxt: &ActionContext,
1921) -> &'static str {
1922  let interval = match slot {
1923    PairSlot::Set => true,
1924    // A function's argument pair is a pair (`u(x,\infty)`, `\Pi(M^2,\infty)`), unless it runs from −∞
1925    // to ∞ or to a single-token number — an interval the function takes (`S(-\infty,\infty)`,
1926    // `f(-\infty,-3)`, 57bx; 2605.16086, 2605.01702; `u(-\infty,t)`, `f(\pm\infty,0)` stay pairs).
1927    PairSlot::Argument => {
1928      infinity_sign(first, ctxt).is_some_and(|sign| matches!(sign, '-' | '\u{2212}'))
1929        && (infinity_sign(second, ctxt)
1930          .is_some_and(|sign| matches!(sign, ' ' | '+' | '\u{B1}' | '\u{2213}'))
1931          || is_signed_number(second))
1932    },
1933    PairSlot::Other => {
1934      infinity_sign(first, ctxt)
1935        .is_some_and(|sign| matches!(sign, '-' | '\u{2212}' | '\u{B1}' | '\u{2213}'))
1936        || infinity_sign(second, ctxt)
1937          .is_some_and(|sign| matches!(sign, ' ' | '+' | '\u{B1}' | '\u{2213}'))
1938    },
1939  };
1940  if interval { "open-interval" } else { "vector" }
1941}
1942
1943/// A number, signed or not (`3`, `-3`).
1944fn is_signed_number(xm: &XM) -> bool {
1945  match xm {
1946    XM::Apply(op, args, ..) if args.0.len() == 1 && operator_category(&op.0) == Some("ADDOP") => {
1947      args.0[0].as_ref().is_some_and(is_signed_number)
1948    },
1949    XM::Dual(_, pres, ..) => is_signed_number(pres),
1950    XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..) => operator_category(xm) == Some("NUMBER"),
1951    _ => false,
1952  }
1953}
1954
1955/// The sign of an infinite endpoint: `∞` (`' '`), or `∞` under a sign (`-\infty`, `+\infty`,
1956/// `\pm\infty`, `\mp\infty`).
1957fn infinity_sign(xm: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> Option<char> {
1958  match xm {
1959    XM::Apply(op, args, ..) if args.0.len() == 1 && operator_category(&op.0) == Some("ADDOP") => {
1960      let sign = realized_value(&op.0, ctxt).ok()?.chars().next()?;
1961      args.0[0]
1962        .as_ref()
1963        .and_then(|arg| infinity_sign(arg, ctxt))
1964        .filter(|inner| *inner == ' ')
1965        .map(|_| sign)
1966    },
1967    XM::Dual(_, pres, ..) => infinity_sign(pres, ctxt),
1968    XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..) => realized_value(xm, ctxt)
1969      .is_ok_and(|v| v == "\u{221E}")
1970      .then_some(' '),
1971    _ => None,
1972  }
1973}
1974
1975/// A wrap between a `(` and a `)`, each read through the node it names.
1976fn is_paren_wrap(items: &[XM], ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
1977  let (Some(open), Some(close)) = (items.first(), items.last()) else {
1978    return false;
1979  };
1980  realized_value(open, ctxt).is_ok_and(|v| v == "(")
1981    && realized_value(close, ctxt).is_ok_and(|v| v == ")")
1982}
1983
1984/// The slots an application's operands fill: a set — the right of `∈`/`∉` (unless both sides of
1985/// the `∈` are paren pairs, a componentwise membership: `(x,a)\in(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)`,
1986/// 2605.06977, 2605.09849; a pair left of a set product keeps the set slot,
1987/// `(t,x)\in(0,T)\times\Omega`, 2605.25978), the left of `∋`, both of a subset or superset relation; in a multirelation an operand
1988/// whose neighbouring relation asks for a set on its side; and every operand of a set operator (`×`
1989/// as written, `∪`, `∩`, `∖`, big or scripted: `\bigcup_n`) or the base of a power, when the
1990/// application itself fills a set slot (`x\in(0,1)^d`, `t\in(-\delta,\delta)\setminus\{0\}`,
1991/// 2605.01633); a function's argument group (`f(a,b)`, `\Pi(M^2,\infty)`; a scripted or accented head
1992/// parses as a product, so `\Pi_1(a,b)` does not reach here); else none.
1993fn operand_slots(
1994  op: &XM,
1995  args: &[Option<XM>],
1996  slot: PairSlot,
1997  ctxt: &ActionContext,
1998) -> Vec<PairSlot> {
1999  let n = args.len();
2000  let set_if = |set: bool| if set { PairSlot::Set } else { PairSlot::Other };
2001  if is_multirelation(op) {
2002    let sides = |i: usize| {
2003      args
2004        .get(i)
2005        .and_then(Option::as_ref)
2006        .map_or((false, false), |relation| {
2007          relation_set_sides(relation, ctxt)
2008        })
2009    };
2010    return (0..n)
2011      .map(|i| set_if(i % 2 == 0 && ((i > 0 && sides(i - 1).1) || sides(i + 1).0)))
2012      .collect();
2013  }
2014  let (left, right) = relation_set_sides(op, ctxt);
2015  if (left || right) && n == 2 {
2016    // A pair right of a pair is componentwise membership, `(x,a)\in(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)`: only that
2017    // right-hand pair stays a vector; `(t,x)\in(0,T)\times\Omega` keeps its set slot (57br re-review;
2018    // 2605.25978, 2605.01547 `(r,t)\in(0,5)\times\mathbb R`, 2605.26054).
2019    let is_pair = |arg: &Option<XM>| match arg {
2020      Some(XM::Dual(content, pres, ..)) => is_paren_pair(content, pres, ctxt),
2021      _ => false,
2022    };
2023    let componentwise = !left && is_pair(&args[0]) && is_pair(&args[1]);
2024    return vec![set_if(left), set_if(right && !componentwise)];
2025  }
2026  if slot == PairSlot::Set {
2027    if operator_role(op, ctxt.nodes).as_deref() == Some("SUPERSCRIPTOP") {
2028      return (0..n).map(|i| set_if(i == 0)).collect();
2029    }
2030    let passes_the_slot = match realized_meaning(op, ctxt).as_deref() {
2031      Some("union" | "intersection" | "set-minus") => true,
2032      Some("times") => realized_value(op, ctxt).is_ok_and(|v| v == "\u{D7}"),
2033      _ => false,
2034    };
2035    if passes_the_slot {
2036      return vec![PairSlot::Set; n];
2037    }
2038  }
2039  if matches!(
2040    operator_category(script_nucleus(op)),
2041    Some("FUNCTION" | "UNKNOWN" | "ID" | "OPFUNCTION" | "TRIGFUNCTION" | "OPERATOR" | "ATOM")
2042  ) {
2043    return vec![PairSlot::Argument; n];
2044  }
2045  vec![PairSlot::Other; n]
2046}
2047
2048/// Which sides of a relation hold sets: `(left, right)`.
2049fn relation_set_sides(relation: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> (bool, bool) {
2050  let Some(meaning) = realized_meaning(relation, ctxt) else {
2051    return (false, false);
2052  };
2053  if meaning.starts_with("element-of") || meaning.starts_with("not-element-of") {
2054    (false, true)
2055  } else if matches!(
2056    meaning.as_str(),
2057    "contains" | "not-contains" | "not-contains-nor-equals"
2058  ) {
2059    (true, false)
2060  } else if meaning.contains("subset") || meaning.contains("superset") {
2061    (true, true)
2062  } else {
2063    (false, false)
2064  }
2065}
2066
2067/// Perl `p_getTokenMeaning(realizeXMNode($x))` (MathParser.pm:1090, :135-150): a token's meaning, a
2068/// lexeme's node's read through an XMRef, as a gathered/split row's content branch holds them
2069/// (2605.00284); a scripted or decorated operator's, its base's (`\bigcup_n`, `\in_{\mathcal A}`).
2070fn realized_meaning(xm: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> Option<String> {
2071  if let Some(base) = script_base(xm) {
2072    return realized_meaning(base, ctxt);
2073  }
2074  match xm {
2075    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => {
2076      let node = lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes).ok()?;
2077      realize_xmnode(node, ctxt.document).get_attribute("meaning")
2078    },
2079    XM::Token(props, _) | XM::Ref(props) => props.meaning.as_deref().map(String::from),
2080    _ => None,
2081  }
2082}
2083
2084/// Post-processing: combine adjacent SUPOP tokens in script content.
2085/// Perl MathGrammar L720-723: supops = SUPOP(s) → prime2, prime3, etc.
2086/// Marpa often parses `\prime\prime` as `list@(prime, prime)` or `times(prime, prime)`
2087/// instead of using the `supops` grammar rule. This pass detects these patterns
2088/// and replaces them with combined `prime{N}` tokens.
2089pub fn combine_supop_post(xm: &mut XM, nodes: &[libxml::tree::Node]) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
2090  match xm {
2091    XM::Apply(_, args, ..) => {
2092      for arg in args.0.iter_mut().flatten() {
2093        combine_supop_post(arg, nodes)?;
2094      }
2095    },
2096    XM::Wrap(items, ..) => {
2097      for item in items.iter_mut() {
2098        combine_supop_post(item, nodes)?;
2099      }
2100    },
2101    XM::Dual(content, pres, ..) => {
2102      combine_supop_post(content, nodes)?;
2103      combine_supop_post(pres, nodes)?;
2104      // Check if content is Apply(list/times, args) where pres Wrap has all SUPOP items
2105      if let XM::Apply(ref op, ref args, ..) = **content {
2106        let is_list_or_times = if let XM::Token(ref props, _) = *op.0 {
2107          props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("list") || props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("times")
2108        } else {
2109          false
2110        };
2111        if is_list_or_times && args.0.len() >= 2 {
2112          // Check presentation Wrap: all non-separator items should be SUPOP
2113          if let XM::Wrap(ref items, ..) = **pres {
2114            // Items at even indices (0, 2, 4, ...) are the actual tokens
2115            // Items at odd indices (1, 3, ...) are separators (PUNCT, MULOP)
2116            let all_supop = items
2117              .iter()
2118              .enumerate()
2119              .filter(|(i, _)| i % 2 == 0) // actual items at even positions
2120              .all(|(_, item)| get_xm_role(item).as_deref() == Some("SUPOP"));
2121            if all_supop {
2122              let count = args.0.len();
2123              let text: String = items
2124                .iter()
2125                .enumerate()
2126                .filter(|(i, _)| i % 2 == 0)
2127                .map(|(_, item)| {
2128                  item
2129                    .get_value(nodes)
2130                    .unwrap_or(Cow::Borrowed("′"))
2131                    .into_owned()
2132                })
2133                .collect();
2134              // Replace the Dual with a single combined SUPOP Token
2135              *xm = XM::Token(
2136                XProps {
2137                  role: Some(Cow::Borrowed("SUPOP")),
2138                  name: Some(Cow::Owned(format!("prime{count}"))),
2139                  content: Some(Cow::Owned(text)),
2140                  ..XProps::default()
2141                },
2142                Meta::default(),
2143              );
2144              return Ok(());
2145            }
2146          }
2147        }
2148      }
2149    },
2150    XM::Choices(trees) => {
2151      for tree in trees.iter_mut() {
2152        combine_supop_post(tree, nodes)?;
2153      }
2154    },
2155    _ => {},
2156  }
2157  Ok(())
2158}
2159
2160fn get_xm_role(xm: &XM) -> Option<String> {
2161  match xm {
2162    XM::Lexeme(l, _) => l.split(':').next().map(|s| s.to_string()),
2163    XM::Token(p, _) => p.role.as_ref().map(|r| r.to_string()),
2164    _ => None,
2165  }
2166}
2167
2168/// application with trailing elision, as in `x \cdot y \cdot\cdot\cdot`
2169///
2170/// Not after a head or its bare application (`reaches_a_following_ellipsis`), whose argument the ellipsis opens or goes
2171/// on (a trig function's `trig_ellipses`, an OPFUNCTION's or operator's `op_bare_base`, a big operator's operand) or
2172/// which it multiplies: `a+\cos\cdots` is a + cos@(⋯), `\sin\cdots-\cos\cdots` sin@(⋯) − cos@(⋯), `a+2\log\cdots`,
2173/// `a+\nabla\cdots` (57cj.12 review), `a+\sum\cdots` a + ∑@(⋯), `a+\sum_n\cdots`, `a+\int\cdots`, `a+\lim\cdots`,
2174/// `\sin\cdots+\det\cdots`, `a+\partial_x\cdots` (57cj.13 review), `a+\cos\cdots\cdots` a + cos@(⋯·⋯), `a+\det A\cdots`
2175/// a + det@(A·⋯), `a+\log x\cdots`, `a+\sin x\cdots` a + sin@(x)·⋯ (a trailing ellipsis leaves a trig argument, user ruling
2176/// 2026-09-29: `\sin x\cdots` sin@(x)·⋯; between two items it stays inside, `trig_elided`), as Perl or its product, where an elided sum read a + cos + ⋯ and showed a `+` the source
2177/// does not have (latent, no corpus witness in the 3,003 A/B sources). A closed factor keeps the elision reading
2178/// (`a+b\cdots` a + b + ⋯, `a+\sin(x)\cdots`: SYNC_STATUS "Math-parse residuals of the 57cj train" (9)).
2179pub fn infix_apply_and_elide(
2180  rule_id: i32,
2181  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
2182  p: &[ValidationPragmatics],
2183  ctxt: ActionContext,
2184) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
2185  unp!(args => arg1, infixop, arg2, elision);
2186  if arg2
2187    .as_ref()
2188    .is_some_and(|arg2| reaches_a_following_ellipsis(product_end(arg2, true)))
2189  {
2190    return Err(
2191      "infix_apply_and_elide: the ellipsis belongs to the head before it or its argument".into(),
2192    );
2193  }
2194  // … and one after another continues their run (`ends_an_elided_run`): `a+x\cdots\cdots` is a + x·⋯·⋯
2195  if arg2
2196    .as_ref()
2197    .is_some_and(|arg2| ends_an_elided_run(arg2, &ctxt))
2198  {
2199    return Err("infix_apply_and_elide: the ellipsis continues the run before it".into());
2200  }
2201  // check if "left" is already an application of infix op, in which case we can do n-ary apply.
2202  if let Some(XM::Apply(new_op, mut new_args, props, meta)) =
2203    infix_apply_nary(rule_id, vec![arg1, infixop, arg2], p, ctxt)?
2204  {
2205    new_args.0.push(elision);
2206    Ok(Some(XM::Apply(new_op, new_args, props, meta)))
2207  } else {
2208    Ok(None)
2209  }
2210}
2211
2212// infix_apply in the base case,
2213// but when chained, using the flat "multirelation" behavior of latexml
2214pub fn infix_relation(
2215  _rule_id: i32,
2216  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
2217  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
2218  _: ActionContext,
2219) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
2220  unp!(args => left, infixop, right);
2221  // Reject `relop` applied to a comma-list whose items include a
2222  // relation (single-relop modified_term). For `P(x = 0, y < 0)`
2223  // both grammar paths reach the action:
2224  //   * Path A (current): `formula = formula relop formula_list` → `x = list(0, y<0)` (this branch)
2225  //   * Path B (new): `formula_list = modified_term punct modified_term` → `list(x=0, y<0)` wrapped
2226  //     by fenced+function-app
2227  //
2228  // Path B is the surpass-Perl interpretation (math convention: a
2229  // comma-list of relations inside a function-arg group). Rejecting
2230  // Path A here forces Marpa to commit to Path B. ASF migration
2231  // item 5 (Option A), 2026-05-19.
2232  fn list_has_relation(xm: &XM) -> bool {
2233    // Returns true when `xm` is a `list@(...)` (XMApp directly, or
2234    // XMDual wrapping one) and any presentation item is a relation
2235    // Apply. We check the presentation wrap (not the content args)
2236    // because list-Apply args are XMRefs after `create_xmrefs`; the
2237    // actual relation Applies live in the presentation branch.
2238    let (content_args, pres_items) = match xm {
2239      XM::Apply(op, args, ..) => {
2240        if let XM::Token(ref props, _) = *op.0 {
2241          if props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("list") {
2242            (Some(args), None)
2243          } else {
2244            (None, None)
2245          }
2246        } else {
2247          (None, None)
2248        }
2249      },
2250      XM::Dual(content, pres, ..) => {
2251        if let XM::Apply(ref op, ref args, ..) = **content {
2252          if let XM::Token(ref props, _) = *op.0 {
2253            if props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("list") {
2254              // Only a bare list's presentation is its items; a fenced list is one closed item (57ay).
2255              let pres_items = match **pres {
2256                XM::Wrap(ref items, ..) if presents_its_items_alone(pres, args.0.len()) => {
2257                  Some(items)
2258                },
2259                _ => None,
2260              };
2261              (Some(args), pres_items)
2262            } else {
2263              (None, None)
2264            }
2265          } else {
2266            (None, None)
2267          }
2268        } else {
2269          (None, None)
2270        }
2271      },
2272      _ => (None, None),
2273    };
2274    if let Some(args) = content_args
2275      && args
2276        .0
2277        .iter()
2278        .any(|a| a.as_ref().is_some_and(is_relational_item))
2279    {
2280      return true;
2281    }
2282    if let Some(items) = pres_items
2283      && items.iter().any(is_relational_item)
2284    {
2285      return true;
2286    }
2287    false
2288  }
2289  if let Some(ref right_xm) = right
2290    && list_has_relation(right_xm)
2291  {
2292    return Err(
2293      "infix_relation: right is list@ containing relations — prefer list-of-modified_terms path"
2294        .into(),
2295    );
2296  }
2297  // Reject multirelation when the left formula's last operand is a list Dual without delimiters of
2298  // its own (`presents_its_items_alone`). For `a = b, c = d`: the wrong parse creates `a = list(b,c)`
2299  // then tries to extend with `= d`. If the left formula has a bare list as its last arg, the comma
2300  // should have been a formula boundary, not an expression list. Rejecting here forces Marpa to use
2301  // formula_list instead. A fenced list is one closed item and splits nothing: `x=[a,b,c]=y` (57ay;
2302  // 2605.03399, 2605.29816).
2303  if let Some(ref left_xm) = left {
2304    fn last_arg_is_list(xm: &XM) -> bool {
2305      match xm {
2306        XM::Apply(op, args, ..) => {
2307          // Check if this is a relational Apply (has RELOP/ARROW operator)
2308          let is_rel = is_multirelation(&op.0) || is_relational_op(&op.0);
2309          if is_rel {
2310            // Check last argument
2311            if let Some(Some(XM::Dual(content, presentation, ..))) = args.0.last()
2312              && let XM::Apply(ref inner_op, ref inner_args, ..) = **content
2313              && let XM::Token(ref props, _) = *inner_op.0
2314            {
2315              return props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("list")
2316                && presents_its_items_alone(presentation, inner_args.0.len());
2317            }
2318          }
2319          false
2320        },
2321        _ => false,
2322      }
2323    }
2324    if last_arg_is_list(left_xm) {
2325      return Err(
2326        "infix_relation: left formula ends with list (comma should be formula boundary)".into(),
2327      );
2328    }
2329  }
2330  // if left has a "multirelation" already, add right in.
2331  // if left applies a relation, flatten it out to infix form.
2332  // base case - build a simple infix apply
2333  Ok(Some(chain_relation(left, infixop, right)))
2334}
2335
2336pub fn infix_apply_nary(
2337  _rule_id: i32,
2338  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
2339  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
2340  ctxt: ActionContext,
2341) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
2342  unp!(args => left, infixop, right);
2343  let mut left = left;
2344  // `a\cdot b\cdots` elides the operation (`infix_apply_and_elide`: a cdot b cdot cdots); a product
2345  // ending in a bare ellipsis as a visible operation's right operand is that reading's duplicate once
2346  // an ellipsis is a factor (57bs).
2347  if infixop
2348    .as_ref()
2349    .is_some_and(|op| matches!(operator_category(op), Some("MULOP" | "BINOP" | "ADDOP")))
2350    && right
2351      .as_ref()
2352      .is_some_and(|right| ends_in_a_bare_ellipsis(right, &ctxt))
2353  {
2354    return Err(
2355      "infix_apply_nary: the ellipsis elides the operation (infix_apply_and_elide)".into(),
2356    );
2357  }
2358  // Perl's greedy `barearg` (MathGrammar:321-337) takes a MulOp — a decorated `\otimes_k` too —
2359  // and the bare argument after it into an operator's argument: `\nabla u\cdot v` is ∇@(u·v).
2360  if infixop.as_ref().is_some_and(is_product_operator)
2361    && let (Some(l), Some(r)) = (&left, &right)
2362    && leaves_a_bare_argument(l, r, infixop.as_ref(), &ctxt)
2363  {
2364    return Err("infix_apply_nary: the operator on the left takes this bare argument".into());
2365  }
2366  // … and the trig function a differential operator takes, Perl's greedy `moreTrigBareargs`
2367  // (MathGrammar:351-357; `trig_arg mulop factor_base`): `\partial\sin x\times_i^2 y` is ∂(sin(x ×_i² y)),
2368  // Perl's golden t/parse/artefacts (#374).
2369  // (Not across an operator that ends a trig function's bare argument, `ends_a_trig_bare_argument`: `\partial\sin x\otimes
2370  // y` (∂ sin x)⊗y, `\sin x\otimes y z` (sin x)⊗(y z).)
2371  let continues_a_trig_argument = infixop
2372    .as_ref()
2373    .is_some_and(|op| is_product_operator(op) && !ends_a_trig_bare_argument(op, &ctxt));
2374  if continues_a_trig_argument
2375    && let (Some(l), Some(r)) = (&left, &right)
2376    && is_differential(product_end(l, true))
2377    && leaves_a_trig_bare_argument(l, r, &ctxt)
2378  {
2379    return Err(
2380      "infix_apply_nary: the differential operator's trig function takes this factor".into(),
2381    );
2382  }
2383  // … and any trig function's bare argument a MulOp continues (`trig_arg mulop factor_base`), as Perl's greedy
2384  // `moreTrigBareargs` (`trig_argument_across_a_mulop`) — not a BINOP or a large MULOP (`ends_a_trig_bare_argument`)
2385  if continues_a_trig_argument
2386    && let (Some(l), Some(r)) = (&left, &right)
2387    && trig_argument_across_a_mulop(l, r, &ctxt)
2388  {
2389    return Err("infix_apply_nary: the trig function's bare argument takes this factor".into());
2390  }
2391  // … nor differentiates an operator's bare head before a divergence's or a curl's product (`divergence_or_curl`)
2392  if let (Some(l), Some(op), Some(r)) = (&left, &infixop, &right)
2393    && differentiates_a_divergence_s_head(l, op, r, &ctxt)
2394  {
2395    return Err("infix_apply_nary: the derivative takes the divergence or the curl".into());
2396  }
2397  // Divergence #374: a Leibniz quotient is one derivative (`leibniz_quotient`).
2398  let leibniz = matches!((&left, &infixop, &right), (Some(l), Some(op), Some(r))
2399    if is_divide(op) && is_differential(product_end(r, false)) && holds_a_leibniz_numerator(l));
2400  if leibniz {
2401    let (Some(l), Some(op), Some(r)) = (left, infixop, right) else {
2402      unreachable!()
2403    };
2404    return Ok(Some(leibniz_quotient(l, op, r, &ctxt)));
2405  }
2406  // left-to-right associative:
2407  // 1. if "left" is already an application of "infixop",
2408  // 2. then tuck "right" inside it.
2409  //
2410  // Note (ASF + LOSTNODES): in pure-Tree-iter parsing it would be
2411  // natural to record `ReplacedBy(infixop, left_op)` here so the
2412  // absorbed operator's xml:id is redirected to the kept operator's.
2413  // But this action runs inside the ASF Cartesian-product loop —
2414  // `action_on` fires for every candidate combo, including ones
2415  // ultimately discarded. Recording from action time would pollute
2416  // LOSTNODES with mappings from pruned parses, breaking the
2417  // top-level rewrite walk on the *final* tree. The recording
2418  // therefore lives at `parse_single` (after `into_xmath` +
2419  // `append_tree` commit the chosen tree), via the pre/post-snapshot
2420  // diff against the document idstore.
2421  //
2422  // Perl left-to-right: an explicit MULOP only takes one factor on the right (Perl's `moreFactors`,
2423  // MathGrammar:252-258: `MulOp Factor` and `Factor`, each `ApplyNary` on the product so far).
2424  // a/bc → (a/b)*c, F×G dx → (F×G)*dx — NOT a/(b*c) or F×(G*dx). When an explicit (visible) MULOP
2425  // has a right operand that is an invisible-times application, it takes just the first factor and the
2426  // rest multiply the result: Apply(op, left, Apply(⁢, first, rest...)) → Apply(⁢, Apply(op, left,
2427  // first), rest...). A decorated MULOP (`a\times_k DB` is `(a ×_k D) * B`, as Perl's `MulOp`) is
2428  // visible. A BINOP keeps its juxtaposed operand whole, where Perl's `MulOp : BINOP` (:688) takes one
2429  // factor: a `\mathbin` of unknown meaning is no product, and every reading the one-factor rule gave in
2430  // the corpus was wrong — `KX\mathbin{\|}(I-K)X` ‖(KX, I−K)·X (2605.31129), `[WX_i\mathbin{\|}WX_j]`
2431  // (2605.31315, 2605.08689, 2605.25490, 2605.26237, 2605.30618; 57cj.19.1 A/B km191, divergence #393;
2432  // Q11 extends it to the large MULOPs, below, divergence #396).
2433  //
2434  // A large product operator — ⊗, ⊙ and the circled and boxed family — keeps its juxtaposed operand whole too (user
2435  // ruling Q11, 2026-10-01: juxtaposition binds tighter than a large MULOP; divergence #396): `a\otimes 2b` a⊗(2b),
2436  // `2\Lambda_1\otimes\Lambda_1\otimes 2\Lambda_1\otimes\Lambda_1` (2Λ₁)⊗Λ₁⊗(2Λ₁)⊗Λ₁ (2605.17901), `g\otimes w\otimes\sigma'(\gamma_i)`
2437  // (2605.01702), `P\odot P\odot P_\theta(x|y)` (2605.00423), a decorated one too, `R\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C G` (2605.14864;
2438  // was (a ⊗_k D)·B as Perl's `MulOp`, `a\otimes_k DB`).
2439  let is_explicit_mulop = infixop.as_ref().is_some_and(|op| {
2440    operator_category(op) == Some("MULOP")
2441      && !is_invisible_times_operator(op, &ctxt)
2442      && !is_a_large_mulop(op, &ctxt)
2443  });
2444  // … except before an integral's differentials, which close the integrand: there a BINOP or a large MULOP takes the
2445  // integrand's factors before them, its juxtaposed operand (user rulings Q11 and 2026-10-01, the latter revisiting #393's
2446  // one-factor exception of 57cj.19.3-57cj.19.8): `\int f\otimes g h\,dx` ∫((f⊗(g h))·dx), `\int f\boxast g h\,dx`
2447  // ∫((f⧆(g h))·dx) (was ∫((f⧆g)·h·dx)), as `a\boxast g h` ⧆(a, g h); `\int f\boxast g\,dx` ∫((f⧆g)·dx) (was ∫(⧆(f, g·dx))
2448  // before 57cj.19), `\int_X f\boxast g\,d\mu(x)` ∫((f⧆g)·dμ·x); physics' `\dd x`, `\dd{x}`, `\dd^2 x` too; an operand
2449  // that opens with a differential stays whole (`integrand_split`; latent, the reviews' probes, no corpus witness). The
2450  // integrand closes before the letter `d` of a differential too, the letter twin a differential's reading meets, so
2451  // `LetterDsBeforeVariablesAreDifferentials` decides on the `d` alone (`\int_0^1 f\otimes g h\,dx` read ∫(f⊗(g·h·d·x))
2452  // beside ∫((f⊗(g h))·dx) and the first survived, 57cj.20.Q11 review).
2453  let before_differentials = infixop.as_ref().is_some_and(|op| {
2454    (operator_category(op) == Some("BINOP") || is_a_large_mulop(op, &ctxt))
2455      && integrand_split(&right, &ctxt).is_some()
2456  });
2457  let right = if before_differentials {
2458    integrand_before_differentials(right, &ctxt)
2459  } else {
2460    right
2461  };
2462  let takes_one_juxtaposed_factor =
2463    (is_explicit_mulop || before_differentials) && is_juxtaposed_product(&right, &ctxt);
2464  if let Some(XM::Apply(ref left_op, ref mut left_args, ref left_props, ref _m)) = left
2465    && let XM::Lexeme(left_op_lex, _xmeta) = &*left_op.0
2466    && let Some(ref infix @ XM::Lexeme(ref infix_op_lex, _)) = infixop
2467  {
2468    let left_op_pieces: Vec<_> = left_op_lex.split(':').collect();
2469    let infix_op_pieces: Vec<_> = infix_op_lex.split(':').collect();
2470    if left_op_pieces.len() == 3
2471          && infix_op_pieces.len() == 3
2472          && left_op_pieces[0] == infix_op_pieces[0]
2473          && left_op_pieces[1] == infix_op_pieces[1]
2474          // Perl's `ApplyNary` flattens only the same operator (`isSameExpr`, MathParser.pm:1506,
2475          // :1522-1539: meaning, value and mathstyle) — `a/b\div c` is ÷(/(a,b),c), never one
2476          // n-ary application that drops the ÷ (57cj.19 review).
2477          && same_operator_token(&left_op.0, infix, &ctxt)
2478          // … and never into an application that carries an id (Perl ApplyNary, MathParser.pm:1507-1509;
2479          // a defensive mirror: parse-built applications carry none)
2480          && left_props.id.is_none()
2481          // Perl's LeftRec doesn't flatten prefix applications (1 arg = unary prefix)
2482          // Only flatten when left already has 2+ args (binary or n-ary)
2483          && left_args.0.len() >= 2
2484    {
2485      // … and in an n-ary chain the explicit MulOp takes one factor too: `a\cdot b\cdot c d` is
2486      // (a·b·c)·d and `a/b/c d` ((a/b)/c)·d, as `a\cdot b c` (a·b)·c and as Perl (SYNC residual (14),
2487      // 57cj.19; was a·b·(c d); witnesses 2605.31500 `M\cdot D\cdot si`, 2605.00321
2488      // `\lambda\cdot\beta\cdot\hat{\delta}(\mathbf{p})`, 2605.14476 `12/z/ma`, was 12/z/(m·a)).
2489      if takes_one_juxtaposed_factor
2490        && let Some(XM::Apply(right_op, Args(mut factors), right_props, right_meta)) = right
2491      {
2492        left_args.0.push(factors.remove(0));
2493        let mut new_args = vec![left];
2494        new_args.extend(factors);
2495        return Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
2496          right_op,
2497          Args(new_args),
2498          right_props,
2499          right_meta,
2500        )));
2501      }
2502      left_args.0.push(right);
2503      return Ok(left);
2504    }
2505  }
2506  if takes_one_juxtaposed_factor
2507    && let Some(XM::Apply(right_op, Args(mut factors), right_props, right_meta)) = right
2508  {
2509    let first = factors.remove(0);
2510    // Apply(op, left, first) …
2511    let product = Some(XM::Apply(
2512      infixop.into(),
2513      Args(vec![left, first]),
2514      XProps::default(),
2515      Meta::default(),
2516    ));
2517    // … times the rest: Apply(⁢, product, rest...)
2518    let mut new_args = vec![product];
2519    new_args.extend(factors);
2520    return Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
2521      right_op,
2522      Args(new_args),
2523      right_props,
2524      right_meta,
2525    )));
2526  }
2527
2528  // base case: new apply tree
2529  let apply_tree = XM::Apply(
2530    infixop.into(),
2531    Args(vec![left, right]),
2532    XProps::default(),
2533    Meta::default(),
2534  );
2535  Ok(Some(apply_tree))
2536}
2537
2538/// A large product operator (user ruling Q11, 2026-10-01; divergence #396): ⊗ (`\otimes`, tensor-product), ⊙ (`\odot`,
2539/// direct-product) and the circled and boxed family of the same size, ⊘ `\oslash`, ⊚ `\circledcirc`, ⊛ `\circledast`,
2540/// ⊠ `\boxtimes`, ⊡ `\boxdot`, stmaryrd's ⦸ `\varobslash`; and (the Q11 scope ruling, 2026-10-01) the semidirect products
2541/// ⋉ `\ltimes`, ⋊ `\rtimes`, ⋋ `\leftthreetimes`, ⋌ `\rightthreetimes` (2605.11552, 2605.12221, 2605.15276, 2605.27086),
2542/// the coproduct ∐ `\amalg` (U+2210; `\coprod` shares the glyph as a SUMOP), the circles ○ `\bigcirc` and ◯ `\varbigcirc`, mathabx's box product □
2543/// `\square` and its MULOP ⊕ `\pluscirc` (a MULOP only there: `\oplus` is an ADDOP, amsfonts' `\square` a symbol) — bare
2544/// or decorated (`\otimes_k`). Not `\cdot`, `\times`, `\star`, `\ast`, `\circ`, `/`. A default by glyph with its escape:
2545/// the operator's role, so a document that declares one otherwise reads it so.
2546fn is_a_large_mulop(op: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
2547  operator_category(op) == Some("MULOP")
2548    && realized_value(script_nucleus(op), ctxt).is_ok_and(|value| {
2549      matches!(
2550        value.as_ref(),
2551        "\u{2297}"
2552          | "\u{2299}"
2553          | "\u{2298}"
2554          | "\u{229A}"
2555          | "\u{229B}"
2556          | "\u{22A0}"
2557          | "\u{22A1}"
2558          | "\u{29B8}"
2559          | "\u{22C9}"
2560          | "\u{22CA}"
2561          | "\u{22CB}"
2562          | "\u{22CC}"
2563          | "\u{2210}"
2564          | "\u{25CB}"
2565          | "\u{25EF}"
2566          | "\u{25A1}"
2567          | "\u{2295}"
2568      )
2569    })
2570}
2571
2572/// Regroup an integrand product `g h\,dx\,dy` (`integrand_split`) as its factors before the first
2573/// differential, one juxtaposed product, then the rest: (g h)·dx·dy — what a BINOP or a large MULOP takes is the product's
2574/// first factor (Q11; user ruling 2026-10-01).
2575fn integrand_before_differentials(right: Option<XM>, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> Option<XM> {
2576  let split = integrand_split(&right, ctxt);
2577  let Some(XM::Apply(op, Args(factors), props, meta)) = right else {
2578    return right;
2579  };
2580  match split {
2581    Some(at) if at >= 2 => {
2582      let mut factors = factors;
2583      let rest = factors.split_off(at);
2584      let integrand = XM::Apply(
2585        op.clone(),
2586        Args(factors),
2587        XProps::default(),
2588        Meta::default(),
2589      );
2590      let mut regrouped = vec![Some(integrand)];
2591      regrouped.extend(rest);
2592      Some(XM::Apply(op, Args(regrouped), props, meta))
2593    },
2594    _ => Some(XM::Apply(op, Args(factors), props, meta)),
2595  }
2596}
2597
2598/// Where an unfenced integrand product closes (`integrand_before_differentials`): its first factor after the first that
2599/// is an integral's differential, or the letter `d` before a variable its differential takes (the letter twin,
2600/// `letter_differential_sites`). None when the product opens with a differential — it closes nothing and stays whole
2601/// (#393): `a\mathbin{\#}\dd\omega\,\eta` #(a, dω·η), an exterior derivative, `a\mathbin{\#}\dd x\,\dd y`,
2602/// `\int f\boxast dx\,dy`, `\int f\mathbin{\#}\dd x\,g\,\dd y` (57cj.19.5-57cj.19.7 reviews) — or holds none. A differential is
2603/// a `d`-kind one's application, not a differential operator's (`\partial_t u`): a bare `d` only in an integral's operand
2604/// (`diffop_apply`, `util::in_an_integral_operand`); a bound differential anywhere — iopart's `\rmd`, elsart's `\d` (meaning
2605/// `differential-d`), physics' `\dd`/`\differential` (meaning `differential`, a dual over its symbol), braced too
2606/// (`\dd{x}`, `\dd[3]{x}`: a dual over its application).
2607fn integrand_split(right: &Option<XM>, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> Option<usize> {
2608  let Some(XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(factors), props, meta)) = right else {
2609    return None;
2610  };
2611  if meta.fenced.is_some()
2612    || props.id.is_some()
2613    || factors.len() < 2
2614    || !is_invisible_times_operator(op, ctxt)
2615  {
2616    return None;
2617  }
2618  let is_differential_at = |at: usize| {
2619    factors[at].as_ref().is_some_and(|factor| {
2620      is_an_integral_differential_factor(factor, ctxt)
2621        || is_a_letter_differential_d(factor)
2622          && factors
2623            .get(at + 1)
2624            .and_then(Option::as_ref)
2625            .is_some_and(is_a_differential_variable)
2626    })
2627  };
2628  if is_differential_at(0) {
2629    return None;
2630  }
2631  (1..factors.len()).find(|&at| is_differential_at(at))
2632}
2633
2634/// Is `right` a juxtaposed product — an invisible-times application of two or more factors — whose
2635/// first factor alone an explicit MulOp on its left takes (`infix_apply_nary`) — or, before an integral's differentials,
2636/// a BINOP or a large MULOP (`integrand_before_differentials`)? A visible `×` product is none.
2637fn is_juxtaposed_product(right: &Option<XM>, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
2638  matches!(right, Some(XM::Apply(op, args, ..))
2639    if args.0.len() >= 2 && is_invisible_times_operator(&op.0, ctxt))
2640}
2641
2642/// A factor that is an integral's `d`-kind differential (`integrand_split`): its application or token.
2643fn is_an_integral_differential_factor(factor: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
2644  match factor {
2645    XM::Apply(Operator(head), _, _, factor_meta) => {
2646      factor_meta.differential && is_a_differential(head, ctxt)
2647    },
2648    XM::Lexeme(..) => is_a_differential(factor, ctxt),
2649    _ => false,
2650  }
2651}
2652
2653/// Is `xm` — scripted or not (`\dd^2`) — a `d`-kind differential's token, power, application or dual?
2654fn is_a_differential(xm: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
2655  if let Some(base) = script_base(xm) {
2656    return is_a_differential(base, ctxt);
2657  }
2658  match xm {
2659    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => {
2660      lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes).is_ok_and(|node| node_is_a_differential(node, ctxt.document))
2661    },
2662    other => is_a_differential_meaning(realized_meaning(other, ctxt).as_deref()),
2663  }
2664}
2665
2666/// The meaning of a `d`-kind differential: a `d`'s (`differential-d`) or physics' `\differential` (`differential`)
2667/// — not a variation (`\variation`, δ) or a partial derivative.
2668fn is_a_differential_meaning(meaning: Option<&str>) -> bool {
2669  matches!(meaning, Some("differential-d" | "differential"))
2670}
2671
2672/// Is `node` a `d`-kind differential — its token, its power (`functional-power`), its application, or a dual whose
2673/// content is one of these (physics' `\dd`, `\dd[3]`, `\dd{x}`, `\dd[3]{x}`)?
2674fn node_is_a_differential(node: &libxml::tree::Node, document: &Document) -> bool {
2675  let node = realize_xmnode(node, document);
2676  match node.get_name().as_str() {
2677    "XMTok" => is_a_differential_meaning(node.get_attribute("meaning").as_deref()),
2678    "XMApp" => {
2679      let children = node.get_child_elements();
2680      children.first().is_some_and(|head| {
2681        node_is_a_differential(head, document)
2682          || realize_xmnode(head, document)
2683            .get_attribute("meaning")
2684            .as_deref()
2685            == Some("functional-power")
2686            && children
2687              .get(1)
2688              .is_some_and(|base| node_is_a_differential(base, document))
2689      })
2690    },
2691    "XMDual" => node
2692      .get_child_elements()
2693      .first()
2694      .is_some_and(|content| node_is_a_differential(content, document)),
2695    _ => false,
2696  }
2697}
2698
2699/// Is `op` the invisible times (U+2062) — the juxtaposition's operator, or a lexeme whose node's
2700/// value it is?
2701fn is_invisible_times_operator(op: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
2702  is_invisible_times_op(op)
2703    || is_invisible_times_lexeme(op)
2704    || matches!(op, XM::Lexeme(..))
2705      && realized_value(op, ctxt).is_ok_and(|value| value == "\u{2062}")
2706}
2707
2708/// Perl `isSameExpr` (MathParser.pm:1522-1539) for two operator lexemes already alike in role and
2709/// meaning: the same value (`p_getValue`) and mathstyle, each read through `realizeXMNode`.
2710fn same_operator_token(a: &XM, b: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
2711  let mathstyle = |xm: &XM| match xm {
2712    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes)
2713      .ok()
2714      .and_then(|node| realize_xmnode(node, ctxt.document).get_attribute("mathstyle")),
2715    _ => None,
2716  };
2717  matches!((realized_value(a, ctxt), realized_value(b, ctxt)), (Ok(x), Ok(y)) if x == y)
2718    && mathstyle(a) == mathstyle(b)
2719}
2720
2721/// The division `/` (Perl `MULOP:divide`), bare or as a token.
2722fn is_divide(op: &XM) -> bool {
2723  match op {
2724    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lex.starts_with("MULOP:divide:"),
2725    XM::Token(props, _) => {
2726      props.role.as_deref() == Some("MULOP") && props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("divide")
2727    },
2728    _ => false,
2729  }
2730}
2731
2732/// A Leibniz numerator's differential operator: applied, or standing alone (`\partial/\partial t`).
2733fn is_leibniz_numerator_item(xm: &XM) -> bool {
2734  is_differential(xm) || is_bare_differential_operator(xm)
2735}
2736
2737/// Does `xm`, left of a `/`, hold a Leibniz numerator — a differential operator, alone or last but for
2738/// the factors it would take, in an unfenced product (`leibniz_numerator`)?
2739fn holds_a_leibniz_numerator(xm: &XM) -> bool {
2740  is_leibniz_numerator_item(xm)
2741    || matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(factors), props, meta)
2742      if is_invisible_times_op(op)
2743        && meta.fenced.is_none()
2744        && props.id.is_none()
2745        && factors.iter().flatten().any(is_leibniz_numerator_item))
2746}
2747
2748/// The numerator of a Leibniz quotient in `left` (or in a `\frac` numerator, `regroup_leibniz_numerator`):
2749/// the last differential operator of an unfenced product, with the factors after it as its operand
2750/// (`\partial\rho u` ∂(ρu)), and the factors before it, which multiply the quotient (`T\,\partial F`
2751/// T·…); `left` back when it holds none.
2752fn leibniz_numerator(left: XM) -> Result<(Vec<Option<XM>>, XM), Box<XM>> {
2753  if is_leibniz_numerator_item(&left) {
2754    return Ok((Vec::new(), left));
2755  }
2756  match left {
2757    XM::Apply(op, Args(mut factors), props, meta)
2758      if is_invisible_times_op(&op.0) && meta.fenced.is_none() && props.id.is_none() =>
2759    {
2760      let Some(k) = factors
2761        .iter()
2762        .rposition(|factor| factor.as_ref().is_some_and(is_leibniz_numerator_item))
2763      else {
2764        return Err(Box::new(XM::Apply(op, Args(factors), props, meta)));
2765      };
2766      let after = factors.split_off(k + 1);
2767      let Some(Some(numerator)) = factors.pop() else {
2768        unreachable!()
2769      };
2770      if after.is_empty() {
2771        return Ok((factors, numerator));
2772      }
2773      // The differential operator takes the factors after it: `\partial\rho u` ∂(ρu).
2774      let (head, mut operand) = match numerator {
2775        XM::Apply(head, Args(mut args), _, meta) if meta.differential && args.len() == 1 => {
2776          (head, vec![args.pop().flatten()])
2777        },
2778        bare => (bare.into(), Vec::new()),
2779      };
2780      operand.extend(after);
2781      let operand = if operand.len() == 1 {
2782        operand.pop().flatten()
2783      } else {
2784        Some(XM::Apply(
2785          invisible_times().into(),
2786          Args(operand),
2787          XProps::default(),
2788          Meta::default(),
2789        ))
2790      };
2791      let numerator = XM::Apply(
2792        head,
2793        Args(vec![operand]),
2794        XProps::default(),
2795        Meta::for_differential(),
2796      );
2797      Ok((factors, numerator))
2798    },
2799    other => Err(Box::new(other)),
2800  }
2801}
2802
2803/// A `\frac` numerator over a differential operator (`\frac{\partial\rho u}{\partial t}`, parser.rs
2804/// `is_leibniz_numerator_arg`): its last differential operator takes the factors after it, as in
2805/// `\partial\rho u/\partial t` (∂(ρu), divergence #374; Perl's greedy `bigop` reads it so; `\frac{\partial\Delta W}
2806/// {\partial B}` ∂(ΔW)/∂B, 2605.05995).
2807pub(crate) fn regroup_leibniz_numerator(numerator: XM) -> XM {
2808  match leibniz_numerator(numerator) {
2809    Ok((before, numerator)) if before.is_empty() => numerator,
2810    Ok((mut before, numerator)) => {
2811      before.push(Some(numerator));
2812      XM::Apply(
2813        invisible_times().into(),
2814        Args(before),
2815        XProps::default(),
2816        Meta::default(),
2817      )
2818    },
2819    Err(numerator) => *numerator,
2820  }
2821}
2822
2823/// A `\frac` denominator of differentials under a Leibniz numerator (parser.rs `is_leibniz_denominator_arg`):
2824/// each differential takes the factors up to the next one, the variable it names — `\frac{\partial u_0}
2825/// {\partial\Delta\psi}` ∂u_0/∂(Δψ) (2605.23203, 2605.28495), `\frac{\partial\Delta W}{\partial B}` beside
2826/// `\frac{\partial\mathcal L}{\partial\Delta W}` reads ΔW once (2605.05995), `\frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x\partial y}`
2827/// unchanged (57cj review); an ellipsis stands between two differentials (`\partial x_1^{\gamma_1}\dots\partial
2828/// x_d^{\gamma_d}`). The `\frac` delimits the denominator, which a slash quotient's does not
2829/// (`leibniz_quotient` counts the order there).
2830pub(crate) fn regroup_leibniz_denominator(denominator: XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> XM {
2831  let XM::Apply(op, Args(factors), props, meta) = denominator else {
2832    return denominator;
2833  };
2834  if !(is_invisible_times_op(&op.0) && meta.fenced.is_none() && props.id.is_none())
2835    || !factors
2836      .iter()
2837      .flatten()
2838      .any(|factor| is_partial_derivative(factor) && !differentiates_by_its_subscript(factor))
2839  {
2840    return XM::Apply(op, Args(factors), props, meta);
2841  }
2842  let mut grouped: Vec<Option<XM>> = Vec::new();
2843  // The operand the last differential gathers, while it takes factors.
2844  let mut open: Option<(Operator, Vec<Option<XM>>)> = None;
2845  let close = |open: Option<(Operator, Vec<Option<XM>>)>, grouped: &mut Vec<Option<XM>>| {
2846    if let Some((head, mut operand)) = open {
2847      let operand = if operand.len() == 1 {
2848        operand.pop().flatten()
2849      } else {
2850        Some(XM::Apply(
2851          invisible_times().into(),
2852          Args(operand),
2853          XProps::default(),
2854          Meta::default(),
2855        ))
2856      };
2857      grouped.push(Some(XM::Apply(
2858        head,
2859        Args(vec![operand]),
2860        XProps::default(),
2861        Meta::for_differential(),
2862      )));
2863    }
2864  };
2865  for factor in factors {
2866    match factor {
2867      Some(XM::Apply(head, Args(mut args), _, factor_meta))
2868        if factor_meta.differential
2869          && args.len() == 1
2870          && is_bare_differential_operator(&head.0)
2871          && !has_a_subscript(&head.0) =>
2872      {
2873        close(open.take(), &mut grouped);
2874        open = Some((head, vec![args.pop().flatten()]));
2875      },
2876      Some(ellipsis) if is_ellipsis(&ellipsis, ctxt) => {
2877        close(open.take(), &mut grouped);
2878        grouped.push(Some(ellipsis));
2879      },
2880      // a subscripted derivative is no variable's, it stands alone (`\frac{\partial f}{\partial x\,\partial_y g}`,
2881      // 57cj.2 review)
2882      Some(derivative) if is_partial_derivative(&derivative) => {
2883        close(open.take(), &mut grouped);
2884        grouped.push(Some(derivative));
2885      },
2886      other => match open.as_mut() {
2887        Some((_, operand)) => operand.push(other),
2888        None => grouped.push(other),
2889      },
2890    }
2891  }
2892  close(open.take(), &mut grouped);
2893  match grouped.pop() {
2894    Some(Some(only)) if grouped.is_empty() => only,
2895    last => {
2896      grouped.push(last.flatten());
2897      XM::Apply(op, Args(grouped), props, meta)
2898    },
2899  }
2900}
2901
2902/// Does a scripted head carry a subscript (`\partial_x`, `\partial^2_{xy}`)? A Leibniz denominator's ∂
2903/// names its variable after it; a subscripted one is a derivative of its own (57cj.1 review; latent, the review's
2904/// probe: `\frac{\partial_t u\,v}{\partial_x u\,w}` keeps (∂_x u)·w).
2905fn has_a_subscript(head: &XM) -> bool {
2906  match head {
2907    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..)
2908      if matches!(operator_category(op), Some("SUBSCRIPTOP" | "SUPERSCRIPTOP")) =>
2909    {
2910      operator_category(op) == Some("SUBSCRIPTOP")
2911        || args
2912          .first()
2913          .and_then(Option::as_ref)
2914          .is_some_and(has_a_subscript)
2915    },
2916    _ => false,
2917  }
2918}
2919
2920/// A partial derivative whose operator carries a subscript (`\partial_x u`).
2921fn differentiates_by_its_subscript(xm: &XM) -> bool {
2922  matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(head), ..) if has_a_subscript(head))
2923}
2924
2925/// The order a differential operator states: the number over it (`\partial^2`, `\partial^2_{xy}`), 1
2926/// unwritten, None when it is no number (`\partial^n`).
2927fn differential_order(head: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> Option<u32> {
2928  match head {
2929    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..)
2930      if matches!(operator_category(op), Some("SUBSCRIPTOP" | "SUPERSCRIPTOP")) =>
2931    {
2932      let [Some(base), Some(script)] = args.as_slice() else {
2933        return None;
2934      };
2935      if operator_category(op) == Some("SUPERSCRIPTOP") {
2936        written_number(script, ctxt)
2937      } else {
2938        differential_order(base, ctxt)
2939      }
2940    },
2941    _ => Some(1),
2942  }
2943}
2944
2945/// A script that is a number, as a count (`2` in `\partial^2`, `x^2`).
2946fn written_number(xm: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> Option<u32> {
2947  (operator_category(xm) == Some("NUMBER"))
2948    .then(|| realized_value(xm, ctxt).ok()?.trim().parse().ok())
2949    .flatten()
2950}
2951
2952/// The order a denominator's differential counts toward: its operator's times its variable's power
2953/// (`\partial x^2` 2), None when either is no number.
2954fn differential_power(xm: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> Option<u32> {
2955  let XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(args), ..) = xm else {
2956    return Some(1);
2957  };
2958  let power = match args.as_slice() {
2959    [Some(XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(variable), ..))]
2960      if operator_category(op) == Some("SUPERSCRIPTOP") =>
2961    {
2962      match variable.as_slice() {
2963        [_, Some(power)] => written_number(power, ctxt)?,
2964        _ => 1,
2965      }
2966    },
2967    _ => 1,
2968  };
2969  Some(differential_order(head, ctxt)? * power)
2970}
2971
2972/// Divergence #374: a Leibniz quotient `\partial X/\partial Y` is one derivative, whatever stands around
2973/// it (user ruling 2026-09-29: ∂F/∂T is a derivative). The numerator is the left side's last differential
2974/// operator with the factors after it (`leibniz_numerator`: `T\,\partial F/\partial T` T·(∂F/∂T),
2975/// `\partial\rho u/\partial t` ∂(ρu)/∂t); the denominator the leading differentials the numerator's order
2976/// asks for — `\partial^2 f/\partial x\partial y` ∂²f/(∂x∂y), every one for an order that is no number
2977/// (`\partial^n f/\partial x_1\cdots\partial x_n`); what follows multiplies the quotient, as `a/bc` is
2978/// (a/b)c (`\partial u/\partial x\,v` (∂u/∂x)·v). Perl's greedy `bigop` reads ∂@(F/∂@(T))
2979/// (MathGrammar:717, :605-618; KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #387; 2605.03741, 2605.08634, 2605.15405).
2980fn leibniz_quotient(left: XM, divide: XM, right: XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> XM {
2981  let (mut factors, numerator) = match leibniz_numerator(left) {
2982    Ok(split) => split,
2983    Err(left) => (Vec::new(), *left),
2984  };
2985  let order = match &numerator {
2986    XM::Apply(Operator(head), _, _, meta) if meta.differential => differential_order(head, ctxt),
2987    bare => differential_order(bare, ctxt),
2988  };
2989  let (denominator, after) = match right {
2990    XM::Apply(op, Args(mut denominators), props, meta)
2991      if is_invisible_times_op(&op.0) && meta.fenced.is_none() && props.id.is_none() =>
2992    {
2993      let mut taken = 0;
2994      let mut total = 0;
2995      // the numerator's kind of differential only: `\int_0^1\partial^n f/\partial x^n\,dx` keeps its `dx`
2996      let partial = is_partial_differential(&numerator);
2997      for (k, factor) in denominators.iter().enumerate() {
2998        match factor {
2999          Some(factor) if is_differential(factor) && is_partial_differential(factor) == partial => {
3000            taken = k + 1;
3001            if let (Some(order), Some(power)) = (order, differential_power(factor, ctxt)) {
3002              total += power;
3003              if total >= order {
3004                break;
3005              }
3006            }
3007          },
3008          // an ellipsis between differentials (`\partial x_1\cdots\partial x_n`)
3009          Some(factor) if is_ellipsis(factor, ctxt) => {},
3010          _ => break,
3011        }
3012      }
3013      let after = if taken == 0 {
3014        Vec::new()
3015      } else {
3016        denominators.split_off(taken)
3017      };
3018      let denominator = match denominators.pop() {
3019        Some(Some(only)) if denominators.is_empty() => only,
3020        last => {
3021          denominators.push(last.flatten());
3022          XM::Apply(op, Args(denominators), props, meta)
3023        },
3024      };
3025      (denominator, after)
3026    },
3027    right => (right, Vec::new()),
3028  };
3029  factors.push(Some(XM::Apply(
3030    divide.into(),
3031    Args(vec![Some(numerator), Some(denominator)]),
3032    XProps::default(),
3033    Meta::default(),
3034  )));
3035  factors.extend(after);
3036  match factors.pop() {
3037    Some(Some(quotient)) if factors.is_empty() => quotient,
3038    last => {
3039      factors.push(last.flatten());
3040      XM::Apply(
3041        invisible_times().into(),
3042        Args(factors),
3043        XProps::default(),
3044        Meta::default(),
3045      )
3046    },
3047  }
3048}
3049
3050/// The arguments a known function takes from the group after it, spread as its direct
3051/// operands, or None when the group is one argument. Perl's `addEasyArgs`/`ApplyDelimited`
3052/// (MathGrammar:570-577; `requireArgs` :532-536 after an APPLYOP) reads `OPEN Argument
3053/// (argPunct Argument)* balancedClose`, `argPunct` being PUNCT, MIDDLE or VERTBAR (:656), and
3054/// drops the delimiters: `\max(a,b)` `maximum@(a, b)`, not `maximum@(vector@(a, b))`;
3055/// `\max(a;b)`, `\max[a;b]` (57ba), `\max\{a,b\}`, `\max[a,b]`, `\operatorname{E}[X]` `E@(X)`,
3056/// `\exp\{x\}` (57bb; the 57am probes' `\operatorname{E}\{…\}`, 2605.24123; golden
3057/// `tests/parse/fenced_lists.tex`, "A function takes the arguments between any delimiters").
3058/// A group reads so when it is a grouping fence — `delimited-…`, `list`, `set`, an interval, a
3059/// paren `vector` — opened by a grouping delimiter, parens, brackets or braces (angle brackets are
3060/// an inner product or an average, one argument: `\max\langle a,b\rangle`
3061/// `maximum@(delimited-⟨⟩@(list@(a, b)))`, `\log\langle Z\rangle` `logarithm@(delimited-⟨⟩@(Z))`;
3062/// divergence #363), and closed by its match or by nothing (a row break, a typo: `\exp((n-k)(\ln…`, 2605.25295,
3063/// where Perl, needing `balancedClose`, reads nothing); a close of another kind is no argument's
3064/// (`\max(a,b]` stays a product in Perl; `\exp\lfloor x\rceil` keeps its rounding), and separated by
3065/// `argPunct` only (`\max(a:b)` one argument, Perl `maximum@(a colon b)`). A named function of
3066/// its content stays one argument — `\log\lfloor x\rfloor` `logarithm@(floor@(x))`,
3067/// `\log\lvert x\rvert`, `\max\{x\mid x>0\}` a `conditional-set` — where Perl's grammar,
3068/// reading the arguments first, drops the floor (`logarithm@(x)`) and garbles the set
3069/// (`x * ket@(x) * 0`; divergence #363). One item that is itself a bare list gives its items
3070/// (`\Pr[X=1,Y=2]` Pr@(X = 1, Y = 2)), and the second value says so:
3071/// the list's own presentation then joins the function's (`splice_listed_arguments`); so does a
3072/// single paren item (a `Ref`) that is a bare list — a relation list, one `formulae` item since
3073/// 57bk. None for any other single paren item (the caller's own case) and a bare list, so `\sin(x)`
3074/// and the unknown-`f` apply divergence (OXIDIZED_DESIGN #18) are unaffected.
3075fn fenced_tuple_items(
3076  xm: &XM,
3077  presentation: &XM,
3078  ctxt: &ActionContext,
3079) -> Option<(Vec<Option<XM>>, bool)> {
3080  let arg_punct = |separators: &[XM]| {
3081    separators.iter().skip(1).step_by(2).all(|separator| {
3082      matches!(
3083        get_xm_role(separator).as_deref(),
3084        Some("PUNCT" | "MIDDLE" | "VERTBAR")
3085      )
3086    })
3087  };
3088  let items = match xm {
3089    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(items), ..) => {
3090      let XM::Token(props, _) = op.as_ref() else {
3091        return None;
3092      };
3093      let meaning = props.meaning.as_deref()?;
3094      let grouping = meaning.starts_with("delimited-")
3095        || matches!(
3096          meaning,
3097          "vector"
3098            | "list"
3099            | "set"
3100            | "open-interval"
3101            | "closed-interval"
3102            | "open-closed-interval"
3103            | "closed-open-interval"
3104        );
3105      if !grouping {
3106        return None;
3107      }
3108      // A bare paren `vector` (no delimiters of its own) spreads as before.
3109      if meaning == "vector" && presents_its_items_alone(presentation, items.len()) {
3110        return Some((items.clone(), false));
3111      }
3112      Some(items)
3113    },
3114    // A paren group of one item (`fenced`'s single-item Dual) gives arguments only when that item is
3115    // a bare list: a relation list, one `formulae` item (57bk) — `\Pr(X\le x,Y\le y)`
3116    // Pr@(X <= x, Y <= y), as Perl's `ApplyDelimited` (2605.00042, 2605.01907).
3117    XM::Ref(_) => None,
3118    _ => return None,
3119  };
3120  let XM::Wrap(fenced, ..) = presentation else {
3121    return None;
3122  };
3123  let [open, inner @ .., close] = fenced.as_slice() else {
3124    return None;
3125  };
3126  // Read through an `XMRef`, as a split or gathered row's content branch holds its lexemes (Perl
3127  // `isMatchingClose` realizes the node, MathParser.pm:1379-1384; 57bb review: `\max(a,b)` in a
3128  // split row stayed `maximum@(vector@(a, b))`, 2605.01929, 2605.04581).
3129  let (Ok(open_value), Ok(close_value)) = (realized_value(open, ctxt), realized_value(close, ctxt))
3130  else {
3131    return None;
3132  };
3133  // A close that is missing altogether (the lexer's empty CLOSE: a row break, a typo) still ends the
3134  // argument the author opened — `\operatorname{null}(G(\theta(t))` null@(G@(θ@(t))), 2605.00284;
3135  // a close of another kind pairs the open as something else: `\max(a,b]`, `\exp\lfloor x\rceil`.
3136  if inner.is_empty()
3137    // Angle brackets are an inner product, not an argument list: `\max_m\langle t,b_m\rangle`
3138    // is the maximum of ⟨t, b_m⟩ (57bf review of the scripted-head lift: 95 formulas in 38 papers
3139    // of the A/B, every one an inner product, 2605.02896, 2605.20551; Perl spreads them, divergence
3140    // #363), and `\log\langle Z\rangle` the logarithm of an average (Perl `logarithm@(Z)`).
3141    || !matches!(open_value.as_ref(), "(" | "[" | "{")
3142    || !(close_value.is_empty() || balanced_close(&open_value) == Some(close_value.as_ref()))
3143    || !arg_punct(inner)
3144  {
3145    return None;
3146  }
3147  // One item that is a bare list: the list's items are the arguments.
3148  if let [XM::Dual(list_content, list_presentation, ..)] = inner
3149    && let XM::Apply(Operator(list_op), Args(list_items), ..) = &**list_content
3150    && let XM::Token(list_props, _) = list_op.as_ref()
3151    && matches!(
3152      list_props.meaning.as_deref(),
3153      Some("list" | "formulae" | "vector")
3154    )
3155    && presents_its_items_alone(list_presentation, list_items.len())
3156    && let XM::Wrap(list_separated, ..) = &**list_presentation
3157    && arg_punct(list_separated)
3158  {
3159    return Some((list_items.clone(), true));
3160  }
3161  items.map(|items| (items.clone(), false))
3162}
3163
3164/// The presentation of a group whose one item is a bare list, when a function takes the list's
3165/// items as its arguments (`fenced_tuple_items`): the list's items and separators take its
3166/// place between the delimiters, as Perl's `ApplyDelimited` lays out `open, arguments and
3167/// separators, close` flat — the list's own Wrap would stay behind, an id nothing refers to.
3168fn splice_listed_arguments(presentation: &mut XM) {
3169  if let XM::Wrap(fenced, ..) = presentation
3170    && let [_, XM::Dual(_, list_presentation, ..), _] = fenced.as_mut_slice()
3171    && let XM::Wrap(list_separated, ..) = &mut **list_presentation
3172  {
3173    let listed = std::mem::take(list_separated);
3174    fenced.splice(1..2, listed);
3175  }
3176}
3177
3178pub fn prefix_apply(
3179  _rule_id: i32,
3180  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
3181  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
3182  ctxt: ActionContext,
3183) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
3184  unp!(args => prefixop, arg1);
3185  // Perl: when a FUNCTION applies to a fenced arg (from `fenced` semantic action),
3186  // lift the XMDual to wrap the entire application:
3187  //   Apply(func, Dual(Ref, Wrap)) → Dual(Apply(Ref(func), Ref), Apply(func, Wrap))
3188  // This matches Perl's ApplyFunction XMDual structure. A multi-arg paren
3189  // comma-list (`Apply(vector, [refs])` content) is SPREAD into the operands
3190  // (`\max(a,b)` → `max@(a,b)`), per Perl ApplyDelimited.
3191  // A function, scripted or not, and an operator take the arguments between delimiters alike:
3192  // Perl attaches a head's scripts first (`preScripted[...]`, MathGrammar:282-284, :430-433) and
3193  // `ApplyDelimited` never looks at the head (MathParser.pm:1291-1299); an OPERATOR, nested or
3194  // not, reaches it through `addOpFunArgs` → `addEasyArgs` (:312-313, :553-558, :571-576), and one
3195  // item through `nestOperators`' `OPEN Expression balancedClose` (:669-671) — `\max_i\{a_i,b_i\}`
3196  // `(maximum _ i)@(a _ i, b _ i)`, physics `\Re[\frac XY]` `real-part@(X / Y)` (57bf; 2605.02221,
3197  // 2605.20994).
3198  let takes_arguments = prefixop.as_ref().is_some_and(takes_delimited_arguments);
3199  if takes_arguments
3200    && let Some(XM::Dual(ref content, ref pres, ..)) = arg1
3201    && (matches!(**content, XM::Ref(_)) || fenced_tuple_items(content, pres, &ctxt).is_some())
3202    && matches!(**pres, XM::Wrap(..))
3203  {
3204    let mut func = prefixop.unwrap();
3205    let arg1_inner = arg1.unwrap();
3206    let XM::Dual(content_box, pres_box, ..) = arg1_inner else {
3207      unreachable!()
3208    };
3209    let mut pres_wrap = *pres_box;
3210    // Single fenced arg `(x)` → one operand; n-ary paren comma-list `(a,b,…)`
3211    // → spread its items, dropping the implicit `vector` (Perl ApplyDelimited).
3212    let content_args = match fenced_tuple_items(&content_box, &pres_wrap, &ctxt) {
3213      Some((items, listed)) => {
3214        if listed {
3215          splice_listed_arguments(&mut pres_wrap);
3216        }
3217        items
3218      },
3219      None => vec![Some(*content_box)],
3220    };
3221    let func_refs = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut func], ctxt)?;
3222    let func_ref = func_refs.into_iter().next().unwrap();
3223    let content_apply = XM::Apply(
3224      func_ref.into(),
3225      Args(content_args),
3226      XProps::default(),
3227      Meta::default(),
3228    );
3229    let pres_apply = XM::Apply(
3230      func.into(),
3231      Args(vec![Some(pres_wrap)]),
3232      XProps::default(),
3233      Meta::default(),
3234    );
3235    return Ok(Some(XM::Dual(
3236      Box::new(content_apply),
3237      Box::new(pres_apply),
3238      XProps::default(),
3239      Meta::default(),
3240    )));
3241  }
3242  Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
3243    prefixop.into(),
3244    Args(vec![arg1]),
3245    XProps::default(),
3246    Meta::default(),
3247  )))
3248}
3249/// An item of an operator's bare argument, Perl `aBarearg` (MathGrammar:323-331): see
3250/// `is_bare_item`.
3251pub fn bare_argument_item(
3252  _rule_id: i32,
3253  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
3254  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
3255  _: ActionContext,
3256) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
3257  unp!(args => item);
3258  if item.as_ref().is_some_and(is_bare_item) {
3259    Ok(item)
3260  } else {
3261    Err("bare_argument_item: not an aBarearg".into())
3262  }
3263}

3282/// `trig_arg` juxtaposed with its next item: the bare argument goes on, Perl `moreTrigBareargs`
3283/// (MathGrammar:351-357) — unless the argument ends before the item (`ends_trig_argument`, divergence
3284/// #367): `\sin\theta_W\,C_{uB}` is sin@(θ_W)·C_uB, `\sin\theta d\theta` sin@(θ)·dθ,
3285/// `\sin\theta\mathbf v` sin@(θ)·v, where Perl's greedy argument takes them.
3286pub fn trig_argument_juxtaposition(
3287  rule_id: i32,
3288  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
3289  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
3290  ctxt: ActionContext,
3291) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
3292  if let [Some(argument), Some(item)] = args.as_slice()
3293    && ends_trig_argument(&product_factors(argument), item, &ctxt)
3294  {
3295    return Err("trig_argument_juxtaposition: the bare argument ends before this item".into());
3296  }
3297  if let [Some(argument), Some(item)] = args.as_slice()
3298    && leaves_a_trig_argument_s_chain(argument, item, &ctxt)
3299  {
3300    return Err(
3301      "trig_argument_juxtaposition: the ellipsis leaves the chain ending the argument".into(),
3302    );
3303  }
3304  // … nor after a derivative of a numeric constant, whose monomial takes the item (`numeric_monomial`,
3305  // `ends_in_a_differentiated_constant`): `\sin\partial_t 2\pi i\,u\,v` has no sin@((∂_t 2)·π·i)
3306  if let [Some(argument), Some(item)] = args.as_slice()
3307    && differentiated_constant_takes(product_end(argument, true), product_end(item, false))
3308  {
3309    return Err("trig_argument_juxtaposition: the derivative's constant takes this item".into());
3310  }
3311  apply_invisible_times(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
3312}
