3314/// Does `op` end a trig function's bare argument (user ruling 2026-10-01, open Q1 of 57cj.21)? A BINOP and a large
3315/// MULOP (`is_a_large_mulop`, ⊗ ⊙ and their family) do, where Perl's greedy `moreTrigBareargs` (MathGrammar:351-357) goes
3316/// on across any `MulOp` (its `MulOp : BINOP` too, :688): `\int\sin x\boxast y z\,dx` ∫(⧆(sin x, y z)·dx), was
3317/// ∫(sin@(⧆(x, y)·z)·dx), and `\sin x\otimes y z` (sin x)⊗(y z), was sin@(x⊗(y z)) — an operator that keeps its
3318/// juxtaposed operand whole (#393, #396) joins two operands no bare argument holds. The grammar's trig chains take no
3319/// BINOP (`trig_arg`, `trig_op_bare_arg`, `trig_elided`, grammar/builder.rs); a large MULOP lexes as any MULOP, so the
3320/// chain's actions refuse it (`trig_argument_across_an_operator`, `trig_chain_across_an_operator`,
3321/// `trig_argument_elision`), and `infix_apply_nary` refuses no product after the trig application for it. `\cdot`,
3322/// `\times`, `/` go on (`\sin x\cdot y` sin@(x·y), #367).
3323fn ends_a_trig_bare_argument(op: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
3324  operator_category(op) == Some("BINOP") || is_a_large_mulop(op, ctxt)
3325}
3326
3327/// A MulOp in a trig function's bare argument after a scripted or postfixed item, or in an OPFUNCTION's chain inside
3328/// one (`trig_arg mulop trig_scripted_item`, `trig_op_bare_item mulop op_bare_plain_next`, …): `infix_apply_nary`, but
3329/// not across an operator that ends the argument (`ends_a_trig_bare_argument`: `\sin x_i\otimes y` (sin x_i)⊗y,
3330/// `\sin\log x\otimes y` (sin(log x))⊗y — the OPFUNCTION's chain ends with the argument it is in).
3331pub fn trig_chain_across_an_operator(
3332  rule_id: i32,
3333  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
3334  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
3335  ctxt: ActionContext,
3336) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
3337  if let [_, Some(op), _] = args.as_slice()
3338    && ends_a_trig_bare_argument(op, &ctxt)
3339  {
3340    return Err("trig_chain_across_an_operator: the operator ends the bare argument".into());
3341  }
3342  infix_apply_nary(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
3343}
3344
3345/// `trig_arg mulop factor_base`: the bare argument goes on across a MulOp, Perl's greedy `moreTrigBareargs`
3346/// (MathGrammar:351-357) — not across one that ends it (`ends_a_trig_bare_argument`) —, but no ellipsis goes on a chain
3347/// that ends it (`leaves_a_trig_argument_s_chain`: `\sin\log x\cdot\ldots` sin@(log@(x))·…, as `\sin\log x\ldots`).
3348pub fn trig_argument_across_an_operator(
3349  rule_id: i32,
3350  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
3351  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
3352  ctxt: ActionContext,
3353) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
3354  if let [_, Some(op), _] = args.as_slice()
3355    && ends_a_trig_bare_argument(op, &ctxt)
3356  {
3357    return Err("trig_argument_across_an_operator: the operator ends the bare argument".into());
3358  }
3359  if let [Some(argument), _, Some(item)] = args.as_slice()
3360    && leaves_a_trig_argument_s_chain(argument, item, &ctxt)
3361  {
3362    return Err(
3363      "trig_argument_across_an_operator: the ellipsis leaves the chain ending the argument".into(),
3364    );
3365  }
3366  infix_apply_nary(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
3367}
3368
3369/// Is `item` an ellipsis after a trig argument that ends in an OPFUNCTION's or operator's bare application
3370/// (`\sin\log x`, `\cos\log_2 x`, `\sin\max_i a_i`)? The ellipsis is that chain's, never the trig argument's: between
3371/// two items the chain takes the run (`trig_op_bare_elided`, `leaves_a_bare_argument`: `\sin\log x\ldots y`
3372/// sin@(log@(x·…·y))), and a trailing run leaves every bare argument (user ruling 15, 2026-09-29: "a trailing ellipsis
3373/// leaves any bare argument … an ellipsis stays inside only between two items"): `\sin\log x\ldots` sin@(log@(x))·…, as
3374/// `\sin\log x\cdots` sin@(log@(x))·⋯ and `\log x\ldots` log@(x)·…, whatever the run's first macro — 57cj.17 kept an
3375/// ID-led run in the trig argument, sin@(log@(x)·…·⋯·…), and let a `\cdots`-led one leave (57cj.17 review; latent, no
3376/// corpus witness). The trig actions ask it of the same pair: `trig_argument_juxtaposition` and
3377/// `trig_argument_across_an_operator` refuse to join, `leaves_a_trig_bare_argument` and `trig_argument_across_a_mulop`
3378/// refuse no stop, so exactly one reading survives. Not after a big operator's application (`\sin\log\det A\ldots`,
3379/// SYNC_STATUS (13)), whose operand takes an ellipsis (Q9), nor after an application to a group, which closes
3380/// (`\sin\log(x)\ldots` reads as `\sin x\ldots`, Q10).
3381fn leaves_a_trig_argument_s_chain(argument: &XM, item: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
3382  is_ellipsis(product_end(item, false), ctxt)
3383    && is_bare_operator_application(product_end(argument, true))
3384}
3385
3386/// `trig_elided`, an ELIDEOP run inside a trig argument (57cj.17, the 57cj.16 review), juxtaposed or joined by a MulOp
3387/// (not one that ends the argument, `ends_a_trig_bare_argument`): the argument goes on over the run to an item it chains, as over an ellipsis ID — `\sin x\cdots y`
3388/// sin@(x·⋯·y) as `\sin x\ldots y` sin@(x·…·y), as Perl. Not after an argument ending in an OPFUNCTION's application,
3389/// whose own chain takes the run (no `trig_elidable_arg`, the grammar's: `\sin\log x\cdots\dots\cdot c` stays
3390/// sin@(log@((x·⋯·…)·c)), as Perl, where a second tree sin@(log@(x)·⋯·…)·c survived; nor after a run of ELIDEOPs
3391/// opening it, juxtaposed, `trig_ellipses`' own), and not across what ends the argument
3392/// (`ends_trig_argument`: a space, `\sin x\,\cdots y` and `\sin x\cdots\,y` sin@(x)·⋯·y; a `d`, `\sin x\cdots dy`; a
3393/// symbol of another type, `\sin x\cdots\mathbf y`) — the questions `leaves_a_bare_argument` asks of the twin that leaves the run outside, so
3394/// exactly one reading survives.
3395pub fn trig_argument_elision(
3396  rule_id: i32,
3397  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
3398  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
3399  ctxt: ActionContext,
3400) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
3401  let (Some(Some(argument)), Some(Some(item))) = (args.first(), args.last()) else {
3402    return Err("trig_argument_elision: missing operand".into());
3403  };
3404  if ends_trig_argument(&product_factors(argument), item, &ctxt) {
3405    return Err("trig_argument_elision: the bare argument ends before this item".into());
3406  }
3407  if let [_, Some(op), _] = args.as_slice()
3408    && ends_a_trig_bare_argument(op, &ctxt)
3409  {
3410    return Err("trig_argument_elision: the operator ends the bare argument".into());
3411  }
3412  if args.len() == 3 {
3413    infix_apply_nary(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
3414  } else {
3415    apply_invisible_times(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
3416  }
3417}
3418
3419/// Does a trig argument end in an application whose own chain an ELIDEOP run after it goes on (or leaves) — an
3420/// OPFUNCTION's, a bound head's or an operator's bare application, or an OPFUNCTION before a big operator, whose
3421/// operand takes it (`\sin\log\det A\cdots y` sin@(log@(det@(A·⋯·y))), `\sin\log\sum_i x_i\cdots y`)? The arguments
3422/// `trig_elidable_arg` leaves out, so `leaves_a_bare_argument` refuses no twin of theirs (`\sin\log\det A\cdots y` read
3423/// sin@(log@(det@(A·⋯))·y) when only the bare application was looked through).
3424fn ends_in_its_own_chain(argument: &XM, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> bool {
3425  let last = product_end(argument, true);
3426  is_bare_operator_application(last) || takes_a_big_operator(last, nodes)
3427}
3428
3429/// A big operator's application (`\det A`, `\sum_i x_i`), or an OPFUNCTION's unfenced application ending in one
3430/// (`\log\det A`): `ends_in_its_own_chain`.
3431fn takes_a_big_operator(xm: &XM, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> bool {
3432  match xm {
3433    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), _, meta) if meta.fenced.is_none() => {
3434      is_bigop_or_scripted_bigop(xm, nodes)
3435        || is_opfunction_head(op)
3436          && matches!(args.as_slice(), [Some(arg)]
3437            if takes_a_big_operator(product_end(arg, true), nodes))
3438    },
3439    _ => false,
3440  }
3441}
3442
3443/// The argument of the trig function's bare application `before` that an ELIDEOP run after it would go on
3444/// (`trig_elided`), down its right edge as `leaves_a_trig_bare_argument` reads it (`trig_application_ending`:
3445/// `\partial\sin x\cdots y`, `\sin\cos x\cdots y`, `\log\sin x\cdots\dots`).
3446fn trig_argument_before_a_run(before: &XM) -> Option<&XM> {
3447  let application = trig_application_ending(before);
3448  let XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), _, meta) = application else {
3449    return None;
3450  };
3451  let head = script_nucleus(op);
3452  match args.as_slice() {
3453    [Some(arg)]
3454      if meta.fenced.is_none()
3455        && matches!(head, XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..))
3456        && operator_category(head) == Some("TRIGFUNCTION")
3457        && is_trig_argument(arg) =>
3458    {
3459      Some(arg)
3460    },
3461    _ => None,
3462  }
3463}
3464
3465/// What a derivative of a constant ending a trig argument takes after it (`differentiated_constant_takes`): a numeric
3466/// monomial's constants take any factor (`numeric_monomial`), a function's bare argument a bare item only (juxtaposed
3467/// OPFUNCTIONs are separate factors, and a trig function ends a trig argument).
3468#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
3469enum DifferentiatedConstant {
3470  Monomial,
3471  FunctionArgument,
3472}
3473
3474/// Does `xm` end in a derivative of a numeric constant — a number, a constant monomial a number leads, or a function's
3475/// bare application to a constant, down its right edge (`right_edge`): `\partial_t 2\pi`, `\partial_x 2\log 2`,
3476/// `\partial_x\log 2`? Its monomial or its function's argument would take a factor after it (the constant run ends
3477/// nothing, `crosses_a_bare_argument_end`), so a trig argument neither continues after it nor ends there:
3478/// `\sin\partial_t 2\pi i\,u\,v` has one reading, sin@(∂_t(2πiu))·v, where the ∂-of-constant readings survived to the
3479/// pragma (57cj.8 review NIT 9; latent, its probes).
3480fn ends_in_a_differentiated_constant(xm: &XM) -> Option<DifferentiatedConstant> {
3481  right_edge(xm).into_iter().find_map(|(node, _)| match node {
3482    XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(args), _, meta)
3483      if meta.differential && is_bare_differential_operator(head) =>
3484    {
3485      match args.as_slice() {
3486        [Some(operand)] if is_constant(operand) => {
3487          if is_numeric_lead(operand) || is_numeric_monomial(operand) {
3488            Some(DifferentiatedConstant::Monomial)
3489          } else if is_bare_operator_application(operand) {
3490            Some(DifferentiatedConstant::FunctionArgument)
3491          } else {
3492            None
3493          }
3494        },
3495        _ => None,
3496      }
3497    },
3498    _ => None,
3499  })
3500}
3501
3502/// Does the derivative of a constant ending a trig argument (`ends_in_a_differentiated_constant`) take `item` after it?
3503/// A numeric monomial takes a bare item or a function's application (`\sin\partial_x 2\pi\,\log v` sin@(∂_x(2π·log v))),
3504/// a function's bare argument a bare item only (`\sin\partial_x\log 2\log v` keeps sin@(∂_x log 2)·log v: the grammar
3505/// has no other reading).
3506fn differentiated_constant_takes(argument: &XM, item: &XM) -> bool {
3507  match ends_in_a_differentiated_constant(argument) {
3508    Some(DifferentiatedConstant::Monomial) => {
3509      is_trig_bare_item(item) || is_function_application(item)
3510    },
3511    Some(DifferentiatedConstant::FunctionArgument) => is_trig_bare_item(item),
3512    None => false,
3513  }
3514}

3516/// `trig_arg`'s letter applied to a group (`speculative_prefix_apply`, #18) — not across explicit space after the
3517/// letter, which ends the argument (#367): `\cos\phi\,(1-x)` is cos@(φ)·(1−x), as `\cos\phi\,x` is cos@(φ)·x (57cj.7
3518/// review; 2605.29683 A1.E17 `\cos\phi\,\bigl(10-\cos(6\theta)\bigr)\,r^{6}`, which read cos@(φ@(10−cos 6θ)); 2605.11097
3519/// `\sin^{2}\beta\,\big(F(\dots)-F(\dots)\big)`, 2605.15566, 2605.27600 `\cosh^{2}Z\,(dZ^{2}+d\varphi^{2})`). A tuple too,
3520/// whatever its items: a trig argument is an angle, so the tuple is a vector the trig value scales —
3521/// `\mathbf v=\cos\alpha\,(v_x,0)+\sin\alpha\,(0,v_y)` cos α·(v_x,0) + sin α·(0,v_y) (as 57cj.11 and Perl), `\cos\phi\,(x,y)`
3522/// cos φ·(x,y) (as Perl; an application in 57cj.10-57cj.12) (decided 2026-09-30 by the main loop under the user's ruling "the mathematically correct reading in
3523/// context", 2026-09-29; divergence #367; latent, no corpus witness in the 3,003 A/B sources). A derivative's operand
3524/// keeps an argument list's application (`is_an_argument_list`: `\sin\partial_x u\,(x,0)` sin@(∂_x(u@(x,0)))).
3525pub fn trig_letter_application(
3526  rule_id: i32,
3527  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
3528  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
3529  ctxt: ActionContext,
3530) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
3531  if let [Some(letter), Some(_)] = args.as_slice()
3532    && ends_with_space(letter, ctxt.nodes)
3533  {
3534    return Err(
3535      "trig_letter_application: explicit space ends the argument before the group".into(),
3536    );
3537  }
3538  speculative_prefix_apply(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
3539}
3540
3541/// `trig_arg += letter_postfixed`: a letter's postfixed application to a group, not across explicit space after the
3542/// letter either (`letter_group_across_space`), a tuple too (`trig_letter_application`): `\cos\phi\,(1-x)!`
3543/// cos@(φ)·(1−x)!, `\sin^2\phi\,(1-x)!`, `\cos\phi\,(x,0)!` (57cj.8 review; latent, its probes).
3544pub fn trig_letter_postfixed(
3545  _rule_id: i32,
3546  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
3547  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
3548  ctxt: ActionContext,
3549) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
3550  unp!(args => item);
3551  if item
3552    .as_ref()
3553    .is_some_and(|item| letter_group_across_space(item, ctxt.nodes).is_some())
3554  {
3555    return Err("trig_letter_postfixed: explicit space ends the argument before the group".into());
3556  }
3557  Ok(item)
3558}
3559
3560/// Does explicit space follow `xm` — a positive `rpadding` on its last item, which `filter_hints`
3561/// folds from `\,`, `\:`, `\;`, `~`, `\ `, a `\kern`/`\hspace` under 10pt onto the token or script
3562/// before it? (Wider spaces, `\quad`, split the formula as a PUNCT instead; a net zero or negative
3563/// space, `\!`, `\,\!`, is none.)
3564fn ends_with_space(xm: &XM, nodes: &[libxml::tree::Node]) -> bool {
3565  trailing_padding(xm, nodes).is_some_and(|width| crate::util::get_xmhint_spacing(&width) > 0.0)
3566}
3567
3568/// The space after `xm`: its last token's (`ends_with_space`), down its right edge through products and every
3569/// unfenced application of one argument — a derivative's is its factor's (`\sin\partial_x u\,v` sin@(∂_x u)·v, 57cj
3570/// review), and a bare application's its argument's, however deep (`\sin\partial_x 2\,\partial_y u\,v`
3571/// sin@(∂_x(2·∂_y u))·v, `\sin\partial_x 2\sin u\,v`; 57cj.6 review) — unless the application carries its own; a
3572/// group's, its closing delimiter's, an application to one too (`\sin\partial_x(u)\,v` sin@(∂_x(u))·v, 57cj.1 review;
3573/// `\sin\log(x)\,y` sin@(log(x))·y, `\sin\exp\bigl(x\bigr)\,y`, 57cj.7 review; latent, their probes; the A/B witness of
3574/// the rule, 2605.29683 A1.E17: `\cos\phi\,\bigl(10-\cos(6\theta)\bigr)\,r^{6}` keeps r⁶ outside).
3575fn trailing_padding(xm: &XM, nodes: &[libxml::tree::Node]) -> Option<String> {
3576  let lexeme_padding = |lex: &str| {
3577    lookup_lex_node(lex, nodes)
3578      .ok()
3579      .and_then(|node| node.get_attribute("rpadding"))
3580  };
3581  match product_end(xm, true) {
3582    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lexeme_padding(lex),
3583    XM::Token(props, _) => props.rpadding.as_deref().map(str::to_string),
3584    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), props, meta) => {
3585      if let Some(padding) = props.rpadding.as_deref() {
3586        return Some(padding.to_string());
3587      }
3588      if operator_category(op) == Some("POSTFIX") {
3589        // A postfix's space is its lexeme's: `\sin x!\,y` is sin@(x!)·y (57ca).
3590        return match op.as_ref() {
3591          XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lexeme_padding(lex),
3592          _ => None,
3593        };
3594      }
3595      match args.as_slice() {
3596        [Some(argument)] if meta.fenced.is_none() => trailing_padding(argument, nodes),
3597        _ => None,
3598      }
3599    },
3600    XM::Dual(_, presentation, props, _) => props
3601      .rpadding
3602      .as_deref()
3603      .map(str::to_string)
3604      .or_else(|| trailing_padding(presentation, nodes)),
3605    XM::Wrap(items, ..) => items.last().and_then(|item| trailing_padding(item, nodes)),
3606    _ => None,
3607  }
3608}
3609
3610/// Perl `aTrigBarearg`'s atoms (MathGrammar:341-348, `ATOM_OR_ID : ATOM | ID | ARRAY`, :315): an
3611/// atom, identifier, array, unknown or number, with its scripts — what `trig_arg` takes bare and
3612/// chains. Not a differential `d` (`XDIFFUNK`), which ends the argument (#367): `\sin\theta d\theta`
3613/// is sin@(θ)·dθ, `d\cos\theta_1 d\cos\theta_2` d·cos@(θ₁)·d·cos@(θ₂), where Perl's greedy chain takes it.
3614/// Postfixed, as `addScripts` takes it (`\sin xy!` sin@(x·y!), 57ca).
3615fn is_trig_bare_item(xm: &XM) -> bool {
3616  let xm = postfixed_operand(xm).unwrap_or(xm);
3617  let nucleus = script_nucleus(xm);
3618  matches!(nucleus, XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..))
3619    && matches!(
3620      operator_category(nucleus),
3621      Some("UNKNOWN" | "ID" | "XDIFFID" | "ATOM" | "ARRAY" | "NUMBER")
3622    )
3623    && !is_differential_d(xm)
3624}
3625
3626/// The differential letter `d`, bare or scripted: the lexer's `XDIFFUNK`, which it reads as a plain
3627/// unknown outside an integral's operand (`util::in_an_integral_operand`).
3628fn is_differential_d(xm: &XM) -> bool {
3629  matches!(script_nucleus(xm), XM::Lexeme(lex, _)
3630    if lex.starts_with("XDIFFUNK:d:") || lex.starts_with("UNKNOWN:d:"))
3631}
3632
3633/// An ellipsis — an ELIDEOP (`\cdots`) or an ellipsis ID (`\ldots`, `\dots`) — or an unfenced product of them in any
3634/// order: the run of ellipses that opens a trig argument, which the next ELIDEOP continues whatever the macros — the
3635/// grammar derives every such run (`trig_ellipses`, `trig_ellipsis_ids`), so refusing sin@(run)·⋯ never leaves a
3636/// formula without its tree (`\sin\cdots\cdots x` sin@(⋯·⋯·x), 57cj.12 review; `\sin\ldots\cdots x` sin@(…·⋯·x),
3637/// 57cj.13 review; `\sin\ldots\ldots\cdots x` sin@(…·…·⋯·x), `\sin\cdots\ldots\cdots x`, 57cj.14 review).
3638fn is_an_ellipsis_run(xm: &XM) -> bool {
3639  match xm {
3640    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(factors), _, meta)
3641      if meta.fenced.is_none() && factors.len() >= 2 && is_product_operator(op) =>
3642    {
3643      factors
3644        .iter()
3645        .all(|factor| factor.as_ref().is_some_and(is_an_ellipsis_run))
3646    },
3647    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) if lex.starts_with("ID:") => lex
3648      .split(':')
3649      .nth(1)
3650      .is_some_and(|name| ELLIPSIS_NAMES.contains(&name)),
3651    _ => operator_category(xm) == Some("ELIDEOP"),
3652  }
3653}
3654
3655/// An unfenced juxtaposed product of a trig argument's items — what a large MULOP's application takes as its operand in a
3656/// bare argument's chain (`apply_invisible_times`, Q11).
3657fn is_juxtaposed_trig_items(xm: &XM) -> bool {
3658  matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(factors), _, meta)
3659  if meta.fenced.is_none() && factors.len() >= 2 && is_invisible_times_op(op)
3660    && factors.iter().all(|factor| factor.as_ref().is_some_and(|factor| {
3661      is_trig_bare_item(factor) || operator_category(factor) == Some("ELIDEOP")
3662    })))
3663}
3664
3665/// What `trig_arg` derives: a bare item or a function's application, or a product of them whose
3666/// later factors are bare items or ELIDEOPs (`trig_elided`: `\sin x\cdots y`) — or a run of ellipses opening it
3667/// (`trig_ellipses`: `\cos\cdots x`).
3668fn is_trig_argument(xm: &XM) -> bool {
3669  if is_an_ellipsis_run(xm) {
3670    return true;
3671  }
3672  match xm {
3673    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(factors), _, meta)
3674      if meta.fenced.is_none() && factors.len() >= 2 && is_product_operator(op) =>
3675    {
3676      // (a large MULOP's operand is the juxtaposed items after it, Q11: `\sin x\otimes 2\pi t` sin@(x⊗(2πt)), #396; any
3677      // visible product operator is admitted here, but only a large MULOP's application gets a juxtaposed operand in a
3678      // trig chain — `apply_invisible_times` pushes into no other — so `\sin x\cdot y z`, `\sin x\boxast y z` read as before)
3679      let explicit = !is_invisible_times_op(op);
3680      let mut factors = factors.iter();
3681      factors
3682        .next()
3683        .and_then(Option::as_ref)
3684        .is_some_and(is_trig_argument)
3685        && factors.all(|factor| {
3686          factor.as_ref().is_some_and(|factor| {
3687            is_trig_bare_item(factor)
3688              || operator_category(factor) == Some("ELIDEOP")
3689              || explicit && is_juxtaposed_trig_items(factor)
3690          })
3691        })
3692    },
3693    _ => {
3694      let xm = postfixed_operand(xm).unwrap_or(xm);
3695      is_trig_bare_item(xm)
3696        // (a partial derivative, `trig_arg += diffop_application`: `\sin\partial_x u`, 57cj review)
3697        || is_partial_derivative(xm)
3698        || matches!(xm, XM::Apply(..) | XM::Dual(..))
3699          && matches!(
3700            head_category(xm),
3701            Some("FUNCTION" | "OPFUNCTION" | "UNKNOWN" | "XDIFFUNK")
3702          )
3703    },
3704  }
3705}

3707/// May an ellipsis ID `item` after a trig function's bare argument `arg` stand outside it (user ruling Q10, 2026-10-01: a
3708/// trailing ellipsis leaves a trig argument too, `\sin x\ldots` sin(x)·…, as `\sin x\cdots` sin(x)·⋯ and as ruling 15 has
3709/// every other bare argument)? Unless the argument is a run of ellipses opening it (`\sin\ldots\ldots` sin@(…·…)). The
3710/// product's twin is no reason to refuse it: between two items the run stays inside (`a_run_stays_inside` refuses
3711/// sin(x)·…·y, `\sin x\ldots y` sin@(x·…·y)), and trailing the argument it leaves (`trig_bare_application` refuses
3712/// sin@(x·…)).
3713fn leaves_a_trailing_ellipsis(arg: &XM, item: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
3714  is_ellipsis(item, ctxt) && !is_an_ellipsis_run(arg)
3715}
3716
3717/// A trig function's application to its bare argument (`trigfunction trig_arg`): `prefix_apply`, unless the argument ends
3718/// in an ellipsis after an item — a trailing ellipsis leaves it (user ruling Q10, 2026-10-01; `leaves_a_trailing_ellipsis`):
3719/// `\sin x\ldots` sin(x)·…, was sin@(x·…) as Perl; `\sin x\cdot\ldots` sin(x)·…; `\sin x\ldots\cdots` sin(x)·…·⋯. A run
3720/// that is the whole argument stays (`\sin\ldots` sin@(…)).
3721pub fn trig_bare_application(
3722  rule_id: i32,
3723  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
3724  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
3725  ctxt: ActionContext,
3726) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
3727  if let [_, Some(argument)] = args.as_slice()
3728    && !is_an_ellipsis_run(argument)
3729    && is_ellipsis(product_end(argument, true), &ctxt)
3730  {
3731    return Err("trig_bare_application: a trailing ellipsis leaves the bare argument".into());
3732  }
3733  prefix_apply(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
3734}
3735
3736/// Perl's trig bare argument is greedy (`moreTrigBareargs`, MathGrammar:351-357): a product
3737/// `left · right` whose `left` ends in a trig function's (bare or scripted) bare application and
3738/// whose `right` starts with an item `trig_arg` would take is not a parse — `\cos 2\theta_i` is
3739/// cos@(2·θ_i), `a\cos 2\theta` a·cos@(2θ), `\sin^2 2x` (sin²)@(2x) (57bo). Not where the argument
3740/// ends before that item (`ends_trig_argument`, the same question `trig_argument_juxtaposition` asks,
3741/// so exactly one reading survives; #367), nor after a group (`\sin(x)y`: `trig_factor_arg`, which
3742/// takes no chain).
3743fn leaves_a_trig_bare_argument(left: &XM, right: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
3744  let application = trig_application_ending(product_end(left, true));
3745  let XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), _, meta) = application else {
3746    return false;
3747  };
3748  let head = script_nucleus(op);
3749  let item = product_end(right, false);
3750  meta.fenced.is_none()
3751    && matches!(head, XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..))
3752    && operator_category(head) == Some("TRIGFUNCTION")
3753    && matches!(args.as_slice(), [Some(arg)]
3754      // an unapplied OPFUNCTION ending the argument takes what it applies to (`trig_function_item`):
3755      // `\sin\log_2(x)` sin@(log₂(x)), not sin@(log₂)·x, `\sin\log\max(a,x)` sin@(log(max(a,x))) (57cj.8 review;
3756      // latent, no corpus witness)
3757      if right_edge(arg).last().is_some_and(|(leaf, _)| is_opfunction_head(leaf))
3758        && is_an_opfunction_argument(item)
3759        || is_trig_argument(arg)
3760          && (is_trig_bare_item(item) && !leaves_a_trailing_ellipsis(arg, item, ctxt)
3761            // (an ELIDEOP continues a run of them, any mix, `trig_ellipses`: `\sin\cdots\cdots x` has no sin@(⋯)·⋯·x,
3762            // `\sin\ldots\ldots\cdots x` no sin@(…·…)·⋯·x)
3763            || is_an_ellipsis_run(arg) && operator_category(item) == Some("ELIDEOP"))
3764          && (!ends_trig_argument(&product_factors(arg), item, ctxt)
3765            // … and a bound head's argument a mention of its variable (`ends_a_trig_argument_within`)
3766            || right_edge_binds(arg, item, ctxt))
3767          // (an ellipsis after a chain ending the argument is the chain's, `leaves_a_trig_argument_s_chain`)
3768          && !leaves_a_trig_argument_s_chain(arg, item, ctxt)
3769        // … and a derivative of a numeric constant ending it, what its monomial takes, across a space or a
3770        // type mark too (`ends_in_a_differentiated_constant`): `\sin\partial_t 2\pi i\,u\,v` sin@(∂_t(2πiu))·v
3771        || differentiated_constant_takes(arg, item))
3772}
3773
3774/// A product `left ∘ right` across a MulOp whose `left` ends in a trig function's bare application
3775/// (`trig_application_ending`) and whose `right` starts with an item its argument takes across the MulOp
3776/// (`trig_arg mulop factor_base`, `trig_scripted_item`, `trig_postfixed`): `\sin x\cdot y` is sin@(x·y), not
3777/// sin@(x)·y, as Perl's greedy `moreTrigBareargs` (MathGrammar:351-357) — the twin `leaves_a_trig_bare_argument`
3778/// refuses across juxtaposition. Where the argument ends before the item (`ends_trig_argument`: a space, a `d`, a
3779/// symbol of another type) both readings stay, the student pragmas choosing (the MulOp route asks nothing). Both trees
3780/// used to reach the pragmas, which chose by the letters around them: `\sin\log a_i\cdot\ldots\cdot\cdots\cdot\ldots`
3781/// read sin@(log@(a_i))·…·⋯·… where `\sin\log x\cdot\ldots\cdot\cdots\cdot\ldots` read sin@(log@(x)·…·⋯·…) (57cj.17).
3782fn trig_argument_across_a_mulop(left: &XM, right: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
3783  let XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), _, meta) =
3784    trig_application_ending(product_end(left, true))
3785  else {
3786    return false;
3787  };
3788  let head = script_nucleus(op);
3789  let item = product_end(right, false);
3790  meta.fenced.is_none()
3791    && matches!(head, XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..))
3792    && operator_category(head) == Some("TRIGFUNCTION")
3793    && matches!(args.as_slice(), [Some(arg)]
3794      if is_trig_argument(arg)
3795        && is_trig_bare_item(item)
3796        && !leaves_a_trailing_ellipsis(arg, item, ctxt)
3797        && !ends_trig_argument(&product_factors(arg), item, ctxt)
3798        && !leaves_a_trig_argument_s_chain(arg, item, ctxt))
3799}

3801/// The bare application whose argument an item after `xm` would go on: `xm`, or down its right edge — the one factor a
3802/// differential operator takes (`\partial\sin x y` is ∂(sin(x y)), #374), a composition's inner trig function, whose
3803/// argument is the one that goes on (`trig_composed_arg`: `\sin\cos x y` is sin@(cos@(x y)), not sin@(cos@(x))·y,
3804/// 57cj.10 review), and the last item of an OPFUNCTION's or operator's bare argument, a trig function's application
3805/// whose argument goes on where that chain does not (`op_bare_next` takes no ellipsis): `\log\sin x\ldots\ldots` is
3806/// log@(sin@(x·…·…)), as Perl, where log@(sin@(x))·…·… survived beside it and a second site flipped the reading
3807/// (SYNC_STATUS "Math-parse residuals of the 57cj train" (10); 57cj.16 review), `\log\sin x\cdots\dots` log@(sin@(x·⋯·…))
3808/// (57cj.17).
3809fn trig_application_ending(xm: &XM) -> &XM {
3810  let application = through_differentials(xm);
3811  if let Some(inner) = composed_trig_application(application) {
3812    return trig_application_ending(inner);
3813  }
3814  if is_bare_operator_application(application)
3815    && let XM::Apply(_, Args(args), _, meta) = application
3816    && meta.fenced.is_none()
3817    && let [Some(argument)] = args.as_slice()
3818  {
3819    let inner = trig_application_ending(product_end(argument, true));
3820    if is_trig_application(inner) {
3821      return inner;
3822    }
3823  }
3824  application
3825}
3826
3827/// A trig function's bare application to another's (`trig_composed_arg`: `\sin\cos x`, `\sin^2\cos x`): the inner
3828/// application.
3829fn composed_trig_application(xm: &XM) -> Option<&XM> {
3830  let is_trig_application = |xm: &XM| {
3831    matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(op), _, _, meta)
3832      if meta.fenced.is_none() && is_bare_function_head(op) && head_category(op) == Some("TRIGFUNCTION"))
3833  };
3834  match xm {
3835    XM::Apply(_, Args(args), ..) if is_trig_application(xm) => match args.as_slice() {
3836      [Some(inner)] if is_trig_application(inner) => Some(inner),
3837      _ => None,
3838    },
3839    _ => None,
3840  }
3841}
3842
3843/// An OPFUNCTION's or trig function's application (not a bare head): what a numeric monomial takes after its
3844/// constants (`\sin\partial_x 2\log 2\pi\,u\,v`).
3845fn is_function_application(xm: &XM) -> bool {
3846  !is_bare_function_head(xm)
3847    && matches!(xm, XM::Apply(..) | XM::Dual(..))
3848    && matches!(head_category(xm), Some("OPFUNCTION" | "TRIGFUNCTION"))
3849}
3850
3851/// What an OPFUNCTION applies to right after it: a bare item or a group, scripted or not (`opfunction_application`,
3852/// `scripted_group`: `\sin\log_2(x)^2` sin@(log₂((x)²))).
3853fn is_an_opfunction_argument(item: &XM) -> bool {
3854  let item = script_nucleus(item);
3855  is_bare_item(item)
3856    || matches!(item, XM::Wrap(..))
3857    || matches!(item, XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) if matches!(**presentation, XM::Wrap(..)))
3858}
3859
3860/// Does a head on `argument`'s right edge — its last factor's, or one of the bare applications that factor ends in —
3861/// bind a variable `item` mentions (`mentions_a_bound_variable`)? Its scope follows the variable across a space in a
3862/// trig argument (`ends_a_trig_argument_within`): `\sin\max_i u_i\,v_i` sin@(max_i(u_i·v_i)) (57cj.8 review).
3863fn right_edge_binds(argument: &XM, item: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
3864  let mut xm = product_end(argument, true);
3865  while let XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(args), _, meta) = xm
3866    && meta.fenced.is_none()
3867    && let [Some(operand)] = args.as_slice()
3868  {
3869    if mentions_a_bound_variable(head, item, ctxt) {
3870      return true;
3871    }
3872    xm = product_end(operand, true);
3873  }
3874  false
3875}
3876
3877/// Does the bare argument of a trig function end before `item`? Perl's `moreTrigBareargs`
3878/// (MathGrammar:351-357) is greedy and never looks at an item's type; the argument ends here where
3879/// the source or the item's type says so (divergence #367):
3880///   - explicit space after the argument so far, or before a number (`\cos\theta\;1`: the space is
3881///     the number token's own text) — unless the argument so far is a run of coefficients (user ruling Q5, 2026-10-01:
3882///     `\cos 2\,\theta` cos(2θ)) —, or a differential `d` (`\sin\theta d\theta`);
3883///   - type evidence (user direction 2026-09-29: prune by the types in a compound argument): the
3884///     item carries a mark no scalar angle does (`non_scalar_mark`) — a vector's, operator's or
3885///     set's font or accent, a derivative, a fraction holding a trig function, an adjoint — and the
3886///     argument so far holds something besides numbers (`\sin 2\mathcal P` stays whole) and no item
3887///     with the same mark (`\cosh\mathcal K\mathcal S`, an all-upright document, stay whole).
3888///
3889/// `\cos\phi_m\vec e_{x_m}` is cos@(φ_m)·e⃗, `\sin\theta\mathrm P_1` sin@(θ)·P_1 (57bq; 2605.31180,
3890/// 2605.28946). Both trig actions ask this one question of the same pair — `trig_argument_juxtaposition`
3891/// (join) and `leaves_a_trig_bare_argument` (stop) — so exactly one reading survives.
3892///
3893/// `factors` are the argument's so far (`product_factors`), a derivative's monomial's up to the item
3894/// (`trig_derivative_item`).
3895fn ends_trig_argument(factors: &[&XM], item: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
3896  // A postfixed item is its operand, scripts kept (57ca).
3897  let mut item = item;
3898  while let Some(base) = postfix_base(item) {
3899    item = base;
3900  }
3901  // (a coefficient run — numbers, π, constants — ends nothing at a space: the angle it scales follows, user ruling Q5,
3902  // 2026-10-01: `\cos 2\,\theta` cos(2θ), `\sin 2\pi\,ft` sin(2πft), `\partial_x\cos 2\pi\,u` ∂_x cos(2πu))
3903  let coefficients_only = !factors.is_empty() && constant_run(factors) == factors.len();
3904  if !coefficients_only
3905    && (factors
3906      .last()
3907      .is_some_and(|last| ends_with_space(last, ctxt.nodes))
3908      || starts_with_space(item, ctxt.nodes))
3909    || is_differential_d(item)
3910  {
3911    return true;
3912  }
3913  let Some(mark) = non_scalar_mark(item, ctxt) else {
3914    return false;
3915  };
3916  constant_run(factors) < factors.len()
3917    && factors
3918      .iter()
3919      .all(|factor| non_scalar_mark(factor, ctxt) != Some(mark))
3920}
3921
3922/// A constant (57cj.8 review; latent, its probes): a number — NUMBER, or the lexer's ATOM_NUMBER, a fraction, root or
3923/// power of numbers and π (util.rs `is_numeric_constant`, the same notion) — or π, raised to a constant power or not
3924/// (`2^3`, `\pi^2`, `\sqrt2^3`; not `\pi^a` or `\pi_a`, a field or a policy); a sum, quotient or product of constants,
3925/// an imaginary unit right after one counting (`2\pi i`, `constant_run`); a group holding one; a function applied to
3926/// one (`\log 2`, `\cos\frac{\pi}{4}`). What only scales an angle, the trig argument so far holding no angle yet
3927/// (`\cos 2\pi\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf r`, 57bq review); what a derivative's monomial takes as it takes a number, a derivative
3928/// of it differentiating a constant (`crosses_a_bare_argument_end`, `differentiates_a_number`; 57cj.7 review).
3929fn is_constant(xm: &XM) -> bool {
3930  match xm {
3931    XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..) => is_numeric_factor(xm) || is_pi(xm),
3932    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..) => {
3933      let args: Vec<&XM> = args.iter().flatten().collect();
3934      if args.is_empty() {
3935        return false;
3936      }
3937      match operator_category(op) {
3938        Some("SUPERSCRIPTOP") => args.len() == 2 && args.iter().all(|arg| is_constant(arg)),
3939        Some("ADDOP" | "FRACOP") => args.iter().all(|arg| is_constant(arg)),
3940        _ if is_product_operator(op) => constant_run(&args) == args.len(),
3941        _ => is_bare_function_head(op) && matches!(args.as_slice(), [arg] if is_constant(arg)),
3942      }
3943    },
3944    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) => is_constant(presentation),
3945    XM::Wrap(items, ..) => {
3946      let inner: Vec<&XM> = items
3947        .iter()
3948        .filter(|item| !matches!(operator_category(item), Some("OPEN" | "CLOSE" | "PUNCT")))
3949        .collect();
3950      !inner.is_empty() && inner.iter().all(|item| is_constant(item))
3951    },
3952    _ => false,
3953  }
3954}
3955
3956/// π, its lexeme (`\pi`, name `pi`).
3957fn is_pi(xm: &XM) -> bool {
3958  matches!(xm, XM::Lexeme(lex, _) if lex.split(':').nth(1) == Some("pi"))
3959}
3960
3961/// The imaginary unit, unscripted: `i`, upright or italic, `\imath`, or a token meaning it — a constant right after
3962/// another (`constant_run`; util.rs `is_imaginary_unit_token`, the lexer's). 373 formulas with π and an `i` after it in
3963/// the delta A/B's 3,003 papers, the review's sample of 25 all the unit (`\frac{1}{2\pi i}`, `e^{-2\pi i(kx+\eta v)}`;
3964/// 57cj.8 review).
3965fn is_imaginary_unit(xm: &XM) -> bool {
3966  matches!(xm, XM::Lexeme(lex, _)
3967    if matches!(lex.split(':').nth(1), Some("i" | "imath" | "imaginary-unit")))
3968}
3969
3970/// How many of `factors` lead as constants (`is_constant`), an imaginary unit right after one counting
3971/// (`\sin\partial_t 2\pi i\,u\,v` sin@(∂_t(2πiu))·v, 57cj.8 review; a leading `i` is a letter, `\sin\partial_x i\,u\,v`).
3972fn constant_run(factors: &[&XM]) -> usize {
3973  let mut run = 0;
3974  for factor in factors {
3975    if is_constant(factor) || run > 0 && is_imaginary_unit(factor) {
3976      run += 1;
3977    } else {
3978      break;
3979    }
3980  }
3981  run
3982}
3983
3984/// The factors of an unfenced product, `xm` alone when it is none.
3985fn product_factors(xm: &XM) -> Vec<&XM> {
3986  match xm {
3987    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), _, meta)
3988      if meta.fenced.is_none() && args.len() >= 2 && is_product_operator(op) =>
3989    {
3990      args.iter().flatten().flat_map(product_factors).collect()
3991    },
3992    _ => vec![xm],
3993  }
3994}
3995
3996/// A number whose own text starts with space: the lexer keeps `\;` or `\,` before a number inside
3997/// the number token (`\cos\theta\;1`, 2605.14924, 2605.26410).
3998fn starts_with_space(xm: &XM, nodes: &[libxml::tree::Node]) -> bool {
3999  match script_nucleus(product_end(xm, false)) {
4000    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) if lex.starts_with("NUMBER:") => {
4001      lookup_lex_node(lex, nodes).ok().is_some_and(|node| {
4002        crate::data::resolve_xmref(node)
4003          .unwrap_or_else(|| node.clone())
4004          .get_content()
4005          .starts_with(char::is_whitespace)
4006      })
4007    },
4008    _ => false,
4009  }
4010}
4011
4012/// A mark in the source that a symbol is no scalar angle: the class of font or accent the author gave
4013/// it, or its shape — bold, calligraphic, script, blackboard, fraktur, sans-serif, an upright Latin
4014/// letter (`\mathrm`, `\mathtt`); a `\vec`/`\overrightarrow`, `\hat`/`\widehat` or `\dot`/`\ddot` accent; a Leibniz
4015/// derivative `\frac{\partial Y}{\partial\theta}`; a fraction or other built atom holding a trig
4016/// function (Perl's `aTrigBarearg` refuses a trig function, MathGrammar:339); an adjoint or transpose
4017/// `A^\dagger`, `A^\top`, `A^{\mathrm T}`. Not `\tilde`, `\bar`, a Greek capital or a capital italic
4018/// letter, which name angles too (`\cos\omega\tilde t`, `\cos\omega T`). Read from the lexeme's node
4019/// through an XMRef; a scripted item's from its base (and its superscript, for the adjoint).
4020fn non_scalar_mark(item: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> Option<&'static str> {
4021  if let XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..) = item
4022    && operator_category(op) == Some("SUPERSCRIPTOP")
4023    && let [Some(_), Some(script)] = args.as_slice()
4024    && is_adjoint_mark(script, ctxt)
4025  {
4026    return Some("adjoint");
4027  }
4028  if let Some(base) = script_base(item) {
4029    return non_scalar_mark(base, ctxt);
4030  }
4031  let XM::Lexeme(lex, _) = item else {
4032    return None;
4033  };
4034  let node = lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes).ok()?;
4035  node_mark(
4036    &crate::data::resolve_xmref(node).unwrap_or_else(|| node.clone()),
4037    ctxt.document,
4038  )
4039}
4040
4041/// The mark a lexeme's node carries (see `non_scalar_mark`). A token's font is its `_font`, decoded
4042/// (the `font` attribute is written after the parse).
4043fn node_mark(node: &libxml::tree::Node, document: &Document) -> Option<&'static str> {
4044  match node.get_name().as_str() {
4045    "XMTok" => token_font_mark(node, document),
4046    "XMDual" => node
4047      .get_child_elements()
4048      .get(1)
4049      .and_then(|presentation| node_mark(presentation, document)),
4050    "XMApp" => {
4051      let children = node.get_child_elements();
4052      let head = children.first()?;
4053      if head.get_attribute("role").as_deref() == Some("OVERACCENT") {
4054        return match head.get_attribute("name").as_deref() {
4055          Some("vec" | "overrightarrow") => Some("vector-accent"),
4056          Some("hat" | "widehat") => Some("hat-accent"),
4057          Some("dot" | "ddot") => Some("dot-accent"),
4058          _ => children.get(1).and_then(|base| node_mark(base, document)),
4059        };
4060      }
4061      if head.get_attribute("meaning").as_deref() == Some("divide")
4062        && is_leibniz_fraction(&children[1..])
4063      {
4064        return Some("derivative");
4065      }
4066      holds_trig_function(node).then_some("trig")
4067    },
4068    "XMWrap" | "XMArg" => holds_trig_function(node).then_some("trig"),
4069    _ => None,
4070  }
4071}
4072
4073/// A token's font class: bold; a calligraphic, script, blackboard, fraktur or sans-serif family; or an
4074/// upright Latin letter (`\mathrm{P}`; an italic letter is the default).
4075fn token_font_mark(token: &libxml::tree::Node, document: &Document) -> Option<&'static str> {
4076  let font = token
4077    .get_attribute("_font")
4078    .and_then(|hash| document.decode_font(&hash))?;
4079  if font.get_series().is_some_and(|series| series == "bold") {
4080    return Some("bold");
4081  }
4082  if let Some(family) = font.get_family()
4083    && let Some(mark) = [
4084      "caligraphic",
4085      "script",
4086      "blackboard",
4087      "fraktur",
4088      "sansserif",
4089    ]
4090    .into_iter()
4091    .find(|mark| family == mark)
4092  {
4093    return Some(mark);
4094  }
4095  (font.get_shape().is_some_and(|shape| shape == "upright")
4096    && is_ascii_letter(&token.get_content()))
4097  .then_some("upright")
4098}
4099
4100/// A fraction whose numerator and denominator each start with a differential — `d`, `∂`, `δ`, upright
4101/// or not — and whose denominator is a product or an application (`\frac{d\theta}{dt}`,
4102/// `\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}`, not `\frac{d_1}{d_2}`). The parts are parsed by now: a
4103/// product's first factor, an application's head, a script's base lead them (57bq review).
4104fn is_leibniz_fraction(parts: &[libxml::tree::Node]) -> bool {
4105  let [numerator, denominator] = parts else {
4106    return false;
4107  };
4108  let is_differential = |part: &libxml::tree::Node| {
4109    leading_token(part).is_some_and(|token| {
4110      token.get_attribute("role").as_deref() == Some("DIFFOP")
4111        || matches!(token.get_content().as_str(), "d" | "\u{2202}" | "\u{3B4}")
4112    })
4113  };
4114  is_differential(numerator)
4115    && is_differential(denominator)
4116    && content_of(denominator).is_some_and(|node| {
4117      node.get_name() == "XMApp"
4118        && node.get_child_elements().first().is_some_and(|head| {
4119          !head
4120            .get_attribute("role")
4121            .is_some_and(|role| role.ends_with("SCRIPTOP"))
4122        })
4123    })
4124}
4125
4126/// The node an `XMArg` or `XMWrap` of one item stands for.
4127fn content_of(node: &libxml::tree::Node) -> Option<libxml::tree::Node> {
4128  match node.get_name().as_str() {
4129    "XMArg" | "XMWrap" => match node.get_child_elements().as_slice() {
4130      [only] => content_of(only),
4131      _ => None,
4132    },
4133    _ => Some(node.clone()),
4134  }
4135}
4136
4137/// The token a parsed part starts with: a product's first factor's, a script's base's, an
4138/// application's head's (a function or a differential operator), a Dual's presentation's.
4139fn leading_token(node: &libxml::tree::Node) -> Option<libxml::tree::Node> {
4140  match node.get_name().as_str() {
4141    "XMTok" => Some(node.clone()),
4142    "XMApp" => {
4143      let children = node.get_child_elements();
4144      let head = children.first()?;
4145      let role = head.get_attribute("role").unwrap_or_default();
4146      let is_product = head.get_attribute("meaning").as_deref() == Some("times") || role == "MULOP";
4147      if is_product || role.ends_with("SCRIPTOP") {
4148        children.get(1).and_then(leading_token)
4149      } else {
4150        leading_token(head)
4151      }
4152    },
4153    "XMDual" => node.get_child_elements().get(1).and_then(leading_token),
4154    _ => node.get_child_elements().first().and_then(leading_token),
4155  }
4156}
4157
4158/// A single ASCII letter.
4159fn is_ascii_letter(text: &str) -> bool {
4160  let mut chars = text.chars();
4161  matches!((chars.next(), chars.next()), (Some(c), None) if c.is_ascii_alphabetic())
4162}
4163
4164/// Does a built atom hold a trig function anywhere?
4165fn holds_trig_function(node: &libxml::tree::Node) -> bool {
4166  node.get_child_elements().iter().any(|child| {
4167    (child.get_name() == "XMTok" && child.get_attribute("role").as_deref() == Some("TRIGFUNCTION"))
4168      || holds_trig_function(child)
4169  })
4170}
4171
4172/// A superscript that marks an adjoint or a transpose: `\dagger`, `\top`, `\intercal`, or an upright
4173/// or sans-serif `T`.
4174fn is_adjoint_mark(script: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
4175  let XM::Lexeme(lex, _) = script else {
4176    return false;
4177  };
4178  let Ok(node) = lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes) else {
4179    return false;
4180  };
4181  // A split row's content branch reaches the script through an XMRef to its whole script node.
4182  let mut node = crate::data::resolve_xmref(node).unwrap_or_else(|| node.clone());
4183  while node.get_name() != "XMTok" {
4184    match node.get_child_elements().as_slice() {
4185      [.., last] if node.get_name() == "XMApp" => node = last.clone(),
4186      [only] => node = only.clone(),
4187      _ => return false,
4188    }
4189  }
4190  matches!(
4191    node.get_attribute("name").as_deref(),
4192    Some("dagger" | "top" | "intercal")
4193  ) || matches!(
4194    node.get_attribute("meaning").as_deref(),
4195    Some("top" | "transpose" | "adjoint")
4196  ) || matches!(
4197    node.get_content().as_str(),
4198    "\u{2020}" | "\u{22A4}" | "\u{22BA}"
4199  ) || node.get_content() == "T"
4200    && matches!(
4201      token_font_mark(&node, ctxt.document),
4202      Some("upright" | "sansserif")
4203    )
4204}
4205
4206/// Perl `addOpFunArgs` (MathGrammar:553-558): an operator or an OPFUNCTION applies to a
4207/// parenthesized group or a bare argument (`APPLYOP(?) barearg`), never to an operator. While its nest is open — no
4208/// function nested yet — `nestOperators` (:663-671; `compound_operator`) takes a leading function
4209/// or operator into it instead, so the argument cannot start with one: `\nabla\log p\cdot v` is
4210/// (∇@log)@(p·v), `\nabla\nabla^2 u` (∇@∇²)@(u).
4211pub fn operator_bare_apply(
4212  rule_id: i32,
4213  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
4214  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
4215  ctxt: ActionContext,
4216) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
4217  if let [Some(head), Some(arg)] = args.as_slice()
4218    && (is_operator_head(arg)
4219      || nest_is_open(head) && {
4220        // through a postfix: `\nabla\log^2!` nests as `\nabla\log^2` does (57ca); an expectation's
4221        // application it takes whole (`open_op_head expectation_application`, builder.rs)
4222        let first = product_end(arg, false);
4223        matches!(
4224          head_category(postfixed_operand(first).unwrap_or(first)),
4225          Some("FUNCTION" | "OPFUNCTION" | "TRIGFUNCTION")
4226        )
4227      })
4228  {
4229    return Err("operator_bare_apply: the operator nests over it, or takes no operator".into());
4230  }
4231  // An ellipsis ends no bare argument (`is_bare_continuation`): an ID one, which `op_bare_next` reads
4232  // as any identifier, leaves as an ELIDEOP does — `\nabla u\ldots` ∇@(u)·…, `\log x_1\ldots\log x_n`
4233  // log@(x_1)·…·log@(x_n) (57cb review).
4234  if let [_, Some(arg)] = args.as_slice()
4235    && product_factors(arg).len() >= 2
4236    && {
4237      // under a script or a postfix too, as `is_bare_continuation` reads it: `\log x\ldots!`
4238      let end = product_end(arg, true);
4239      is_ellipsis(script_nucleus(postfixed_operand(end).unwrap_or(end)), &ctxt)
4240    }
4241  {
4242    return Err("operator_bare_apply: an ellipsis ends no bare argument".into());
4243  }
4244  // A derivative that starts the bare argument ends where the argument ends: its numeric monomial takes no
4245  // OPFUNCTION or operator the argument would not take (57cj.6 review: `\log\partial_x 2u\log v` is
4246  // log@(∂_x(2u))·log@(v), `\nabla\partial_x 2u\,\log v`, `\max_i\partial_x 2u_i\log v`), unless the head binds a
4247  // variable the factor mentions (`bound_application`: `\max_i\partial_x 2u_i\log v_i`).
4248  if let [Some(head), Some(arg)] = args.as_slice()
4249    && crosses_a_bare_argument_end(
4250      product_end(arg, false),
4251      ctxt.nodes,
4252      // (a function's or operator's bare argument in it ends where its own head ends it)
4253      &mut |at: &BareBoundaryAt| {
4254        let first = product_end(at.next, false);
4255        at.within == BareBoundary::Monomial
4256          && is_opfunction_or_operator(first)
4257          && !mentions_a_bound_variable(head, first, &ctxt)
4258      },
4259    )
4260  {
4261    return Err(
4262      "operator_bare_apply: the derivative's monomial runs past the argument's end".into(),
4263    );
4264  }
4265  prefix_apply(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
4266}
4267
4268/// `trig_arg += diffop_application` (grammar/builder.rs): a derivative in a trig function's bare argument ends
4269/// where that argument ends — its numeric monomial crosses no explicit space, `d` or type mark (`ends_trig_argument`,
4270/// #367), and takes no function or operator after it, as juxtaposed trig functions are separate factors (57cj.6
4271/// review: `\sin\partial_x 2u\,v` sin@(∂_x(2u))·v as `\sin\partial_x u\,v` is sin@(∂_x u)·v, `\sin\partial_t 2\pi u\,v`,
4272/// `\sin\partial_x 2u\mathbf v`, `\sin\partial_x 2u\cos v`); a function's or operator's bare argument in it crosses
4273/// none of the argument's own ends either (57cj.7 review: `\sin\partial_x\log u\,v` sin@(∂_x(log u))·v,
4274/// `\sin\partial_x 2\log u\,v`), and takes what its own head takes.
4275pub fn trig_derivative_item(
4276  _rule_id: i32,
4277  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
4278  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
4279  ctxt: ActionContext,
4280) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
4281  unp!(args => item);
4282  if let Some(derivative) = &item
4283    && crosses_a_bare_argument_end(derivative, ctxt.nodes, &mut |at: &BareBoundaryAt| {
4284      ends_a_trig_argument_within(at, &ctxt)
4285    })
4286  {
4287    return Err(
4288      "trig_derivative_item: the derivative's monomial runs past the argument's end".into(),
4289    );
4290  }
4291  Ok(item)
4292}
4293
4294/// `trig_arg += trig_function_item` (grammar/builder.rs): an OPFUNCTION's application in a trig function's argument,
4295/// as any OPFUNCTION's (Perl `aTrigBarearg : preScripted['OPFUNCTION'] addOpFunArgs`, MathGrammar:341-343) — its bare
4296/// argument ending where the trig argument ends (`ends_a_trig_argument_within`): `\sin\log u\,v` sin@(log u)·v,
4297/// `\sin\log_2 x` sin@(log₂(x)), `\sin\log 2x` sin@(log(2x)), `\sin\max_i u_i\,v_i` sin@(max_i(u_i·v_i)) (57cj.8
4298/// review: Rust-only unparsed or misread before, Perl parses them; latent, no corpus witness).
4299pub fn trig_function_item(
4300  _rule_id: i32,
4301  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
4302  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
4303  ctxt: ActionContext,
4304) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
4305  unp!(args => item);
4306  if let Some(application) = &item
4307    && crosses_within(
4308      application,
4309      BareBoundary::UnderAHead,
4310      false,
4311      ctxt.nodes,
4312      &mut |at: &BareBoundaryAt| ends_a_trig_argument_within(at, &ctxt),
4313    )
4314  {
4315    return Err("trig_function_item: the bare argument runs past the trig argument's end".into());
4316  }
4317  Ok(item)
4318}
4319
4320/// Does the trig argument that holds `at` end there (`trig_derivative_item`, `trig_function_item`)? Where the trig
4321/// argument itself would (`ends_trig_argument`: explicit space, `d`, a type mark), and before a trig function, as
4322/// juxtaposed trig functions are separate factors (`\sin\log x\cos y` sin@(log x)·cos y, where an OPFUNCTION's
4323/// argument alone takes it, `\log x\cos y` log@(x·cos y)) — unless a bound head's variable is mentioned after it, the
4324/// head's scope following it (user ruling 2026-09-30; `\sin\partial_x\max_i u_i\,v_i` sin@(∂_x(max_i(u_i·v_i))), 57cj.8
4325/// review); in a derivative's own monomial also before an OPFUNCTION or operator (57cj.6 review).
4326fn ends_a_trig_argument_within(at: &BareBoundaryAt, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
4327  let first = product_end(at.next, false);
4328  if at
4329    .head
4330    .is_some_and(|head| mentions_a_bound_variable(head, first, ctxt))
4331  {
4332    return false;
4333  }
4334  ends_trig_argument(at.factors, at.next, ctxt)
4335    || matches!(head_category(first), Some("TRIGFUNCTION"))
4336    || at.within == BareBoundary::Monomial && is_opfunction_or_operator(first)
4337}
4338
4339/// Where a boundary between two factors lies (`crosses_a_bare_argument_end`): in a derivative's numeric monomial the
4340/// enclosing argument holds, or under a function's or operator's head nested in it, whose own bare argument that head
4341/// ends — only what ends the whole enclosing argument ends it there.
4342#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
4343enum BareBoundary {
4344  Monomial,
4345  UnderAHead,
4346}
4347
4348/// A boundary `crosses_a_bare_argument_end` meets: the factors so far, the next, where it lies, and the head whose
4349/// bare argument holds it (none in a monomial, or between a letter and its group).
4350struct BareBoundaryAt<'a> {
4351  factors: &'a [&'a XM],
4352  next:    &'a XM,
4353  within:  BareBoundary,
4354  head:    Option<&'a XM>,
4355}
4356
4357/// Does a partial derivative's numeric monomial — or one a derivative in it holds, or a function's or operator's
4358/// bare argument in either, or a letter's application to a group — run past an enclosing bare argument's end, `ends`
4359/// at a boundary between two of its factors? Not where everything under the derivative before it is constant: ending
4360/// there would differentiate a constant, so a space there ends nothing (`\sin\partial_x 2\,\partial_y u`
4361/// sin@(∂_x(2·∂_y u)), `\sin\partial_x 2\,u\,v` sin@(∂_x(2u))·v, 57cj.6 review; `\sin\partial_x 2\pi\,u\,v`
4362/// sin@(∂_x(2πu))·v, 57cj.7 review), judged down the whole path — through a function's argument too (`\sin\partial_x
4363/// \log 2\,u\,v` sin@(∂_x(log(2u)))·v, `\sin\partial_x 2\log 2\pi\,u\,v`; 57cj.8 review; `is_constant`; latent, no
4364/// corpus witness). A letter's application to a group across a space crosses that space (`\sin\partial_x u\,(1-x)`
4365/// sin@(∂_x u)·(1−x), 57cj.8 review).
4366fn crosses_a_bare_argument_end(
4367  derivative: &XM,
4368  nodes: &[XMLNode],
4369  ends: &mut dyn FnMut(&BareBoundaryAt) -> bool,
4370) -> bool {
4371  is_partial_derivative(derivative)
4372    && crosses_within(derivative, BareBoundary::Monomial, true, nodes, ends)
4373}
4374
4375/// `crosses_a_bare_argument_end` at `xm`, whose boundaries lie `within` a monomial the enclosing argument holds or
4376/// under a head nested in it — a partial derivative's operand, a function's or operator's bare argument, a letter's
4377/// group — with everything under the derivative before `xm` constant or not (`constant_before`).
4378fn crosses_within(
4379  xm: &XM,
4380  within: BareBoundary,
4381  constant_before: bool,
4382  nodes: &[XMLNode],
4383  ends: &mut dyn FnMut(&BareBoundaryAt) -> bool,
4384) -> bool {
4385  if let Some(base) = postfix_base(xm) {
4386    return crosses_within(base, within, constant_before, nodes, ends);
4387  }
4388  if let Some((letter, group)) = letter_application(xm)
4389    && !is_an_argument_list(group, nodes)
4390  {
4391    return ends(&BareBoundaryAt {
4392      factors: &[letter],
4393      next: group,
4394      within,
4395      head: None,
4396    });
4397  }
4398  let XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(args), _, meta) = xm else {
4399    return false;
4400  };
4401  let [Some(operand)] = args.as_slice() else {
4402    return false;
4403  };
4404  if is_partial_derivative(xm) {
4405    // (a derivative's operand starts its own run: `\partial_y 3` is a derivative of a constant)
4406    return if is_numeric_monomial(operand) {
4407      product_crosses(operand, true, within, None, nodes, ends)
4408    } else {
4409      crosses_within(operand, within, true, nodes, ends)
4410    };
4411  }
4412  // a function's or operator's application to a bare argument: `\log u\,v`, `\nabla u\,v`
4413  meta.fenced.is_none()
4414    && !meta.differential
4415    && !is_bare_differential_operator(head)
4416    && matches!(
4417      head_category(xm),
4418      Some("OPFUNCTION" | "TRIGFUNCTION" | "OPERATOR")
4419    )
4420    && !matches!(operand, XM::Dual(..) | XM::Wrap(..))
4421    && !matches!(operand, XM::Apply(_, _, _, operand_meta) if operand_meta.fenced.is_some())
4422    && product_crosses(
4423      operand,
4424      constant_before,
4425      BareBoundary::UnderAHead,
4426      Some(head),
4427      nodes,
4428      ends,
4429    )
4430}
4431
4432/// `crosses_within` over the factors of one bare product: any factor's own, or a boundary between them that ends
4433/// while something before it under the derivative is not constant (`constant_run`'s notion: an imaginary unit right
4434/// after a constant of this product counts).
4435fn product_crosses(
4436  product: &XM,
4437  constant_before: bool,
4438  within: BareBoundary,
4439  head: Option<&XM>,
4440  nodes: &[XMLNode],
4441  ends: &mut dyn FnMut(&BareBoundaryAt) -> bool,
4442) -> bool {
4443  // (the monomial's factors flat: `number tight_term` nests the tail's product, `2(πuv)`)
4444  let factors = product_factors(product);
4445  let mut constant = constant_before;
4446  let mut run = 0;
4447  for (k, factor) in factors.iter().enumerate() {
4448    if crosses_within(factor, within, constant, nodes, ends) {
4449      return true;
4450    }
4451    let constant_factor = is_constant(factor) || run > 0 && run == k && is_imaginary_unit(factor);
4452    run += usize::from(constant_factor && run == k);
4453    constant &= constant_factor;
4454    if !constant
4455      && let Some(next) = factors.get(k + 1)
4456      && ends(&BareBoundaryAt {
4457        factors: &factors[..=k],
4458        next,
4459        within,
4460        head,
4461      })
4462    {
4463      return true;
4464    }
4465  }
4466  false
4467}
4468
4469/// A letter applied to its group (`speculative_prefix_apply`, #18: `u(1-x)`), as (letter, group).
4470fn letter_application(xm: &XM) -> Option<(&XM, &XM)> {
4471  match xm {
4472    XM::Apply(Operator(letter), Args(args), _, meta)
4473      if meta.fenced.is_none()
4474        && matches!(**letter, XM::Lexeme(..))
4475        && matches!(operator_category(letter), Some("UNKNOWN" | "XDIFFUNK")) =>
4476    {
4477      match args.as_slice() {
4478        [Some(group @ (XM::Dual(..) | XM::Wrap(..)))] => Some((&**letter, group)),
4479        _ => None,
4480      }
4481    },
4482    _ => None,
4483  }
4484}
4485
4486/// The group of a letter applied to it across explicit space after the letter (`letter_application`,
4487/// `ends_with_space`), under its postfixes and scripts: `\phi\,(1-x)`, `\phi\,(1-x)!`. In a trig argument and a
4488/// derivative's operand the space ends the application (`trig_letter_postfixed`, `differential_operator_apply`; 57cj.8
4489/// review) — in a derivative's operand not before an argument list (`is_letter_application_across_space`) — elsewhere
4490/// the letter still applies (`k\,(x-y)` k@(x−y); a ruling is pending, divergence #18).
4491fn letter_group_across_space<'a>(xm: &'a XM, nodes: &[libxml::tree::Node]) -> Option<&'a XM> {
4492  let mut xm = xm;
4493  while let Some(base) = postfix_base(xm).or_else(|| script_base(xm)) {
4494    xm = base;
4495  }
4496  letter_application(xm)
4497    .filter(|(letter, _)| ends_with_space(letter, nodes))
4498    .map(|(_, group)| group)
4499}
4500
4501/// A letter applied to a group across explicit space (`letter_group_across_space`) that is no argument list
4502/// (`is_an_argument_list`): what a derivative's operand refuses (`differential_operator_apply`).
4503fn is_letter_application_across_space(xm: &XM, nodes: &[libxml::tree::Node]) -> bool {
4504  letter_group_across_space(xm, nodes).is_some_and(|group| !is_an_argument_list(group, nodes))
4505}
4506
4507/// A parenthesized comma list of variables — letters, scripted or accented letters, ellipses, placeholder slots:
4508/// `(x,t)`, `(x_1,\ldots,x_n)`, `(q,\dot q,t)`, `(\cdot,t)` — or an evaluation point, variables beside constants: `(0,t)`,
4509/// `(x,0)`, `(x,-1)`, `(x,\infty)`, `(0^+,t)` — is an argument list, which keeps a letter's application across a space in
4510/// a derivative's operand: no tuple holding a variable multiplies (57cj.9 review: `\partial_t u\,(x,t)` ∂_t(u@(x,t)),
4511/// `\sin\partial_x u\,(x,t)`; the #18 row's "an argument list keeps the application", 2605.24758; 57cj.11 review: a
4512/// boundary or initial condition `\partial_x u\,(0,t)=0` ∂_x(u@(0,t)), `\partial_q L\,(q,\dot q,t)`,
4513/// `\partial_t\psi\,(\vec r,t)`, as the bare letter's `u\,(x,0)=g(x)` u@(x,0); 57cj.12 review: `\partial_x u\,(x,\infty)`,
4514/// the standard `\partial_x u\,(\cdot,t)`, a one-sided limit `\partial_x u\,(0^+,t)`, `\partial_t f\,(\hat{x_1},t)`).
4515/// Any other group is a vector or a list the letter multiplies: constants alone (`\partial_x u\,(1,0)` (∂_x u)·(1,0),
4516/// where Perl reads ∂_x(u·(1,0)) and the ∂ one-factor ruling moves the tuple out, #374; π, e and i count as constants,
4517/// `\partial_t f\,(i,0)`), an application, a power, a sum or a scaled letter among the items (`\partial_x u\,(-x,t)`,
4518/// `\partial_x u\,(2x,t)`: meant as evaluation points, a residual), brackets or another separator
4519/// (`\partial_x u\,(x,t;\lambda)`, a parameter list, a residual) — 57cj.10-57cj.12 reviews; latent, no corpus witness.
4520/// A trig argument is an angle, so there a tuple after a space is a vector the trig value scales, whatever its items
4521/// (`trig_letter_application`, decided 2026-09-30): the rule is the derivative operand's only.
4522fn is_an_argument_list(group: &XM, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> bool {
4523  let presentation = match group {
4524    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) => presentation.as_ref(),
4525    other => other,
4526  };
4527  let XM::Wrap(items, ..) = presentation else {
4528    return false;
4529  };
4530  let [open, inner @ .., close] = items.as_slice() else {
4531    return false;
4532  };
4533  let is_comma = |item: &XM| matches!(delimiter_role_text(item), Some(("PUNCT", ",")));
4534  let is_variable = |item: &XM| is_a_variable_item(item, nodes);
4535  matches!(delimiter_role_text(open), Some(("OPEN", "(")))
4536    && matches!(delimiter_role_text(close), Some(("CLOSE", ")")))
4537    && inner.iter().any(is_comma)
4538    && inner.iter().any(is_variable)
4539    && inner
4540      .iter()
4541      .all(|item| is_comma(item) || is_variable(item) || is_an_evaluation_constant(item))
4542}
4543
4544/// A letter (an UNKNOWN, whatever its font: `x`, `\alpha`, `\mathbf{x}`; not π or an unscripted e or i, constants), an accented one
4545/// (`\hat x`, `\dot q`, `\vec r`, `\bar x`, `\hat{x_1}`), a scripted one (`x_1`, `x'`, `x^{(1)}`, `x_i^j`, `\hat x_1`), an
4546/// ellipsis (`\ldots`, `\dots`, `\cdots`) or a placeholder slot (`is_a_placeholder_slot`: `u(\cdot,t)`): an item of an
4547/// argument list (`is_an_argument_list`). A letter to a constant power is an expression, as a sum is:
4548/// `\partial_t u\,(x^2,y)` (∂_t u)·(x², y).
4549fn is_a_variable_item(item: &XM, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> bool {
4550  is_a_variable(item, nodes)
4551    || operator_category(item) == Some("ELIDEOP")
4552    || is_a_placeholder_slot(item)
4553    || match item {
4554      XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => {
4555        lex.starts_with("ID:")
4556          && lex
4557            .split(':')
4558            .nth(1)
4559            .is_some_and(|name| ELLIPSIS_NAMES.contains(&name))
4560      },
4561      XM::Token(props, _) => props
4562        .name
4563        .as_deref()
4564        .is_some_and(|name| ELLIPSIS_NAMES.contains(&name)),
4565      _ => false,
4566    }
4567}
4568
4569/// The mark of an argument's slot alone (a MULOP): `\cdot` or `\bullet` (`u(\cdot,t)`, `f(\bullet)`, as
4570/// `bar_placeholder`'s `\|\cdot\|`) or the wildcard `\ast` (`\Delta(\ast,\ast)`, a Hamming distance's wildcard slots,
4571/// 2605.02499; `(\ast,\ast,(\Delta^j)_{j=1}^K)`, 2605.18079 — the only operator alone in a tuple across the 3,003 A/B
4572/// sources). Not another product operator (`(\otimes,t)`, `(\times,t)`, `(\star,t)` stay a vector, as Perl's open
4573/// interval: Perl's `AnyOp` takes every operator alone before a PUNCT or CLOSE, MathGrammar:204-206, and singles out
4574/// none as a slot; 57cj.13 review).
4575fn is_a_placeholder_slot(item: &XM) -> bool {
4576  const SLOT_MARKS: [&str; 3] = ["cdot", "bullet", "ast"];
4577  matches!(operator_category(item), Some("MULOP" | "BINOP"))
4578    && match item {
4579      XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lex
4580        .split(':')
4581        .nth(1)
4582        .is_some_and(|name| SLOT_MARKS.contains(&name)),
4583      XM::Token(props, _) => props
4584        .name
4585        .as_deref()
4586        .is_some_and(|name| SLOT_MARKS.contains(&name)),
4587      _ => false,
4588    }
4589}
4590
4591/// A constant item of an evaluation point (`is_an_argument_list`): a constant (`is_constant`: a number, π, a fraction
4592/// or power of them), e or i (`is_e_or_i`), ∞, a signed one (`-1`, `-\infty`), or a number approached from one side,
4593/// a sign as its superscript (`0^+`, `L^-` is a scripted letter, a variable).
4594fn is_an_evaluation_constant(item: &XM) -> bool {
4595  match item {
4596    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => {
4597      is_constant(item) || is_e_or_i(item) || lex.split(':').nth(1) == Some("infinity")
4598    },
4599    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..) => match (operator_category(op), args.as_slice()) {
4600      (Some("ADDOP"), [Some(operand)]) => is_an_evaluation_constant(operand),
4601      (Some("SUPERSCRIPTOP"), [Some(base), Some(script)]) => {
4602        is_constant(item) || is_constant(base) && operator_category(script) == Some("ADDOP")
4603      },
4604      _ => is_constant(item),
4605    },
4606    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) => is_constant(item) || is_an_evaluation_constant(presentation),
4607    _ => is_constant(item),
4608  }
4609}
4610
4611/// An unscripted e or i, the exponential base or the imaginary unit — a constant of an evaluation point, as π is
4612/// (`\partial_t f\,(i,0)` a vector; `(x,i)`, `(i,j)` hold a variable).
4613fn is_e_or_i(xm: &XM) -> bool {
4614  is_imaginary_unit(xm)
4615    || matches!(xm, XM::Lexeme(lex, _)
4616      if matches!(lex.split(':').nth(1), Some("e" | "exponential-e")))
4617}
4618
4619/// A letter, bare, accented (`is_accented_letter`) or scripted by anything but a constant power
4620/// (`is_a_variable_item`). An unscripted e or i is a constant (`is_e_or_i`); subscripted or primed it is a letter — an
4621/// index or a basis vector, `\partial_t a\,(i_1,\ldots,i_k)`, `(i',t)`, `(e_1,t)`, `(\mathbf e_1,t)` (57cj.13 review) —
4622/// and raised to any other power it is the exponential or a power of the imaginary unit, no variable: `(e^{x},t)`,
4623/// `(e^{i\theta},t)`, `(i^n,t)` are vectors, as Perl reads them (57cj.14 review). The whole script chain decides, not
4624/// its outer layer, so the order TeX renders alike does not matter: a letter if any layer is a subscript or a script
4625/// opening with a prime, and no layer a constant power — `(e^x_k,t)` as `(e_k^x,t)`, `e'^x` (TeX's one superscript
4626/// `e^{\prime x}`) as `{e'}^x`; `(x^2_k,t)`, `(e_1^2,t)` are powers (57cj.15 review).
4627fn is_a_variable(xm: &XM, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> bool {
4628  if script_base(xm).is_some() {
4629    let mut indexes_a_letter = false;
4630    let mut layer = xm;
4631    while let XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..) = layer
4632      && script_base(layer).is_some()
4633    {
4634      let [Some(base), Some(script)] = args.as_slice() else {
4635        return false;
4636      };
4637      let is_a_power = operator_category(op) == Some("SUPERSCRIPTOP")
4638        && (!matches!(script, XM::Wrap(..) | XM::Dual(..)) && is_constant(script)
4639          || raises_a_prime_to_a_constant(script, nodes));
4640      if is_a_power {
4641        return false;
4642      }
4643      indexes_a_letter |=
4644        operator_category(op) == Some("SUBSCRIPTOP") || opens_with_a_prime(script, nodes);
4645      layer = base;
4646    }
4647    return is_a_variable(layer, nodes) || indexes_a_letter && is_e_or_i(layer);
4648  }
4649  match xm {
4650    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) if operator_category(xm) == Some("ATOM") => {
4651      lookup_lex_node(lex, nodes).is_ok_and(is_accented_letter)
4652    },
4653    _ => operator_category(xm) == Some("UNKNOWN") && !is_pi(xm) && !is_e_or_i(xm),
4654  }
4655}
4656
4657/// A superscript TeX merged a prime into, raising it to a constant: `e'^2` is TeX's one superscript `e^{\prime 2}`, the
4658/// constant power (e′)², which `is_constant` cannot see through the prime (`prime@(absent, 2)`, an ATOM lexeme standing
4659/// for the XMApp): `(e'^2,t)` is a vector as `(e_1^2,t)` is, and `(x'^2,t)` as `(x^2,y)` (57cj.16 review NIT 3; latent,
4660/// no primed-power tuple in the 3,003 A/B sources). What follows the prime is read as any power (`util::is_constant_node`:
4661/// `e'^{-1}`, `e'^{1/2}`, `e'^\pi`); `e'^x` keeps the letter, and so does a fenced superscript, an order as in
4662/// `is_a_variable`'s plain power (`(x'^{(2)},t)` as `(x^{(2)},t)`, 57cj.17 review NIT 4).
4663fn raises_a_prime_to_a_constant(script: &XM, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> bool {
4664  let is_absent =
4665    |xm: &XM| matches!(xm, XM::Token(props, _) if props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("absent"));
4666  match script {
4667    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..) if operator_category(op) == Some("SUPOP") => {
4668      let raised: Vec<&XM> = args
4669        .iter()
4670        .flatten()
4671        .filter(|arg| !is_absent(arg))
4672        .collect();
4673      !raised.is_empty()
4674        && raised
4675          .iter()
4676          .all(|arg| !matches!(arg, XM::Wrap(..) | XM::Dual(..)) && is_constant(arg))
4677    },
4678    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) if operator_category(script) == Some("ATOM") => {
4679      lookup_lex_node(lex, nodes).is_ok_and(|node| {
4680        // (from the math idstore only, as `opens_with_a_prime`)
4681        let resolve = |node: &XMLNode| {
4682          crate::data::resolve_xmref_in_store(node).unwrap_or_else(|| node.clone())
4683        };
4684        let node = resolve(node);
4685        let children = element_nodes(&node);
4686        let Some((prime, raised)) = children.split_first() else {
4687          return false;
4688        };
4689        let raised: Vec<&XMLNode> = raised
4690          .iter()
4691          .filter(|child| child.get_attribute("meaning").as_deref() != Some("absent"))
4692          .collect();
4693        node.get_name() == "XMApp"
4694          && resolve(prime).get_attribute("role").as_deref() == Some("SUPOP")
4695          && !raised.is_empty()
4696          && raised.iter().all(|child| {
4697            !matches!(resolve(child).get_name().as_str(), "XMWrap" | "XMDual")
4698              && crate::util::is_constant_node(child)
4699          })
4700      })
4701    },
4702    _ => false,
4703  }
4704}
4705
4706/// A script that is a prime or opens with one: `'`, `''` (one `prime2` SUPOP), and the superscript TeX merges a prime
4707/// into, `e'^x` = `e^{\prime x}` (the prime applied to what follows it, an XMApp the script's ATOM lexeme stands for).
4708fn opens_with_a_prime(script: &XM, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> bool {
4709  let first = product_end(script, false);
4710  match first {
4711    XM::Apply(Operator(op), ..) => operator_category(op) == Some("SUPOP"),
4712    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) if operator_category(first) == Some("ATOM") => {
4713      lookup_lex_node(lex, nodes).is_ok_and(|node| {
4714        // (from the math idstore only, as `is_accented_letter`)
4715        let resolve = |node: &XMLNode| {
4716          crate::data::resolve_xmref_in_store(node).unwrap_or_else(|| node.clone())
4717        };
4718        let node = resolve(node);
4719        node.get_name() == "XMApp"
4720          && element_nodes(&node).first().is_some_and(|op| {
4721            let op = resolve(op);
4722            op.get_name() == "XMTok" && op.get_attribute("role").as_deref() == Some("SUPOP")
4723          })
4724      })
4725    },
4726    _ => operator_category(first) == Some("SUPOP"),
4727  }
4728}
4729
4730/// An accent over a letter (`\hat x`, `\dot q`, `\vec r`, `\underline x`) or over a letter with a subscript or a
4731/// superscript that is no constant power, the test a bare letter's power takes (`is_a_variable`: `\hat{x_1}`, `\bar{x_i}`,
4732/// `\hat{x^n}`; `\hat{x^2}`, `\hat{x^{-1}}`, `\hat{x^{1/2}}` are powers, as `x^{-1}` is, 57cj.13 review): an application of an
4733/// OVERACCENT or UNDERACCENT to an UNKNOWN token or its script application, which lexes as one ATOM (util.rs
4734/// `node_to_grammar_lexemes_ctx`), read through XMRefs — a variable of an argument list (`is_a_variable`; 57cj.11
4735/// review: `\partial_q L\,(q,\dot q,t)`; 57cj.12 review: `\partial_t f\,(\hat{x_1},t)`).
4736fn is_accented_letter(node: &XMLNode) -> bool {
4737  // (from the math idstore only: a miss walks no document, util.rs `is_numeric_constant`'s lesson)
4738  let resolve =
4739    |node: &XMLNode| crate::data::resolve_xmref_in_store(node).unwrap_or_else(|| node.clone());
4740  let node = resolve(node);
4741  let role = |node: &XMLNode| {
4742    let node = resolve(node);
4743    (node.get_name() == "XMTok")
4744      .then(|| node.get_attribute("role"))
4745      .flatten()
4746  };
4747  let is_a_letter = |node: &XMLNode| {
4748    let node = resolve(node);
4749    role(&node).as_deref() == Some("UNKNOWN")
4750      || node.get_name() == "XMApp"
4751        && matches!(element_nodes(&node).as_slice(), [script_op, letter, script]
4752        if role(letter).as_deref() == Some("UNKNOWN")
4753          && match role(script_op).as_deref() {
4754            Some("SUBSCRIPTOP") => true,
4755            Some("SUPERSCRIPTOP") => {
4756              let script = resolve(script);
4757              matches!(script.get_name().as_str(), "XMWrap" | "XMDual")
4758                || !crate::util::is_constant_node(&script)
4759            },
4760            _ => false,
4761          })
4762  };
4763  node.get_name() == "XMApp"
4764    && matches!(element_nodes(&node).as_slice(), [accent, base]
4765      if matches!(role(accent).as_deref(), Some("OVERACCENT" | "UNDERACCENT"))
4766        && is_a_letter(base))
4767}
4768
4769/// An OPFUNCTION or an operator, bare or applied (not a trig function, which continues an OPFUNCTION's bare
4770/// argument: `\log x\sin y` log@(x·sin@(y))).
4771fn is_opfunction_or_operator(xm: &XM) -> bool {
4772  is_operator_head(xm)
4773    || matches!(
4774      head_category(postfixed_operand(xm).unwrap_or(xm)),
4775      Some("OPFUNCTION" | "OPERATOR")
4776    )
4777}
4778
4779/// `bound_application`, `bound_operator_application` (grammar/builder.rs): the bare application of a
4780/// head whose subscript binds a variable takes the next item of its argument, juxtaposed or after a
4781/// MulOp or BinOp — an OPFUNCTION's application that mentions a variable the head binds, or after one
4782/// any bare item (`op_bare_next`). User ruling 2026-09-30, "a scripted operator's scope follows its
4783/// bound variable": `\max_i a_i\log b_i` is max_i@(a_i·log@(b_i)), as Perl's greedy `barearg`
4784/// (MathGrammar:321-337, :553-558), and `\max_x f(x)\log y` stays max_x@(f@(x))·log@(y) (#376). The
4785/// argument and the item join as a bare argument's items do (`apply_invisible_times`,
4786/// `infix_apply_nary`: an application the argument ends in refuses what its own head would take, so the
4787/// innermost bound head takes a mention), and the head applies to the whole (`operator_bare_apply`).
4788pub fn bound_argument_extends(
4789  rule_id: i32,
4790  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
4791  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
4792  ctxt: ActionContext,
4793) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
4794  let (Some(Some(application @ XM::Apply(Operator(head), ..))), Some(Some(item))) =
4795    (args.first(), args.last())
4796  else {
4797    return Err("bound_argument_extends: no application or item".into());
4798  };
4799  if !is_bare_operator_application(application) {
4800    return Err("bound_argument_extends: not a bare argument".into());
4801  }
4802  if is_opfunction_application(item) && !mentions_a_bound_variable(head, item, &ctxt) {
4803    return Err(
4804      "bound_argument_extends: the application mentions no variable the head binds".into(),
4805    );
4806  }
4807  let mut args = args.into_iter();
4808  let Some(Some(XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(mut argument), ..))) = args.next() else {
4809    return Err("bound_argument_extends: no application".into());
4810  };
4811  let mut joined = vec![argument.pop().flatten()];
4812  joined.extend(args);
4813  let joined = if joined.len() == 2 {
4814    apply_invisible_times(rule_id, joined, pragmas, ActionContext {
4815      nodes:    ctxt.nodes,
4816      document: &mut *ctxt.document,
4817    })?
4818  } else {
4819    infix_apply_nary(rule_id, joined, pragmas, ActionContext {
4820      nodes:    ctxt.nodes,
4821      document: &mut *ctxt.document,
4822    })?
4823  };
4824  operator_bare_apply(rule_id, vec![Some(*head), joined], pragmas, ctxt)
4825}
