4827/// Perl `addEasyArgs` (MathGrammar:571-576): an OPFUNCTION applies to a balanced group, `OPEN …
4828/// CLOSE` — not a bar pair, an `aBarearg` (:330) and so the start of its greedy bare argument:
4829/// `\log(n)^2` is (log@(n))² (divergence #351), `\log|z|^{2}dz` log@(|z|²·dz), as Perl.
4830pub fn group_apply(
4831  rule_id: i32,
4832  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
4833  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
4834  ctxt: ActionContext,
4835) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
4836  if let [_, Some(arg)] = args.as_slice()
4837    && is_function_group(arg)
4838  {
4839    prefix_apply(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
4840  } else {
4841    Err("group_apply: not a balanced group".into())
4842  }
4843}
4844
4845/// A scripted OPFUNCTION (`\min_w`, `\max_i`) applied to a scripted group, as a limit takes its
4846/// operand: `\min_w(y-w)^2` is min_w@((y−w)²) (divergence #351 covers only an unscripted head).
4847/// Only a group with scripts — a scripted bare item is the bare argument's.
4848pub fn scripted_group_apply(
4849  rule_id: i32,
4850  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
4851  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
4852  ctxt: ActionContext,
4853) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
4854  if let [_, Some(arg)] = args.as_slice()
4855    && script_base(arg).is_some()
4856    && is_function_group(script_nucleus(arg))
4857  {
4858    prefix_apply(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
4859  } else {
4860    Err("scripted_group_apply: not a scripted group".into())
4861  }
4862}

4864/// Is `head`'s nest of operators still open (Perl `nestOperators`, MathGrammar:663-671): an
4865/// operator, scripted or not, or one nested over operators only?
4866fn nest_is_open(head: &XM) -> bool {
4867  match (script_base(head), head) {
4868    (Some(base), _) => nest_is_open(base),
4869    (None, XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..)) if is_nested_operator(op, args) => {
4870      matches!(args.0.as_slice(),
4871        [Some(nested)] if !is_function_head(nested) && nest_is_open(nested))
4872    },
4873    (None, _) => is_operator_head(head),
4874  }
4875}

4877/// Perl: ApplyDelimited — function application with parenthesized arguments.
4878/// Creates XMDual with content=Apply(XMRef(f),XMRef(args)) and
4879/// presentation=Apply(f, XMWrap(open, args, close)).
4880///
4881/// Uses _xmkey for deferred ID resolution: sets _xmkey on the original
4882/// DOM nodes (via lookup_lex_node), creates XMRef with matching _xmkey.
4883/// The resolve_xmkeys step after DOM insertion resolves these to idref.
4884/// Perl: ApplyDelimited — function application with parenthesized arguments.
4885/// Produces Apply(func, content) — same as prefix_apply for now.
4886/// Perl MathGrammar: function(args) → XMDual(Apply(XMRef, XMRef), Apply(func, XMWrap(open, args,
4887/// close))) Produces XMDual wrapping that preserves both semantic and presentation forms.
4888/// Content: Apply(XMRef(func), XMRef(args)) — pure semantic
4889/// Presentation: Apply(func, XMWrap(open, args, close)) — visual with delimiters
4890pub fn apply_delimited(
4891  _rule_id: i32,
4892  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
4893  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
4894  ctxt: ActionContext,
4895) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
4896  unp!(args => func, open, content, close);
4897  let mut func_node = func.unwrap();
4898  let mut content_node = content.unwrap();
4899  // Create XMRefs for the semantic (content) branch
4900  let mut xmrefs = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut func_node, &mut content_node], ctxt)?;
4901  let func_ref = xmrefs.remove(0);
4902  let content_ref = xmrefs.remove(0);
4903  // Content branch: Apply(XMRef(func), XMRef(content))
4904  let content_apply = XM::Apply(
4905    func_ref.into(),
4906    Args(vec![Some(content_ref)]),
4907    XProps::default(),
4908    Meta::default(),
4909  );
4910  // Presentation branch: Apply(func, XMWrap(open, content, close))
4911  let pres_wrap = XM::Wrap(
4912    vec![open.unwrap(), content_node, close.unwrap()],
4913    XProps::default(),
4914    Meta::default(),
4915  );
4916  let pres_apply = XM::Apply(
4917    func_node.into(),
4918    Args(vec![Some(pres_wrap)]),
4919    XProps::default(),
4920    Meta::default(),
4921  );
4922  // XMDual(content, presentation)
4923  Ok(Some(XM::Dual(
4924    Box::new(content_apply),
4925    Box::new(pres_apply),
4926    XProps::default(),
4927    Meta::default(),
4928  )))
4929}
4930/// Perl: standalone modifier `\mod expr` → Apply(mod, Absent, expr)
4931/// The absent first operand represents the missing left side.
4932pub fn modifier_prefix_apply(
4933  _rule_id: i32,

4935  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
4936  _: ActionContext,
4937) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
4938  unp!(args => modop, arg1);
4939  let absent = XM::Token(
4940    XProps {
4941      meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("absent")),
4942      ..XProps::default()
4943    },
4944    Meta::default(),
4945  );
4946  Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
4947    modop.into(),
4948    Args(vec![Some(absent), arg1]),
4949    XProps::default(),
4950    Meta::default(),
4951  )))
4952}

4978/// Perl MathGrammar L224-233: addExpressionModifier with parenthesized relop/modifierop
4979/// `x(>0)` → `Apply(annotated, x, Fence(OPEN, Apply(relop, Absent, 0), CLOSE))`
4980/// `h(\in C)` → `Apply(annotated, h, Fence(OPEN, Apply(\in, Absent, C), CLOSE))`
4981pub fn annotated_fenced_modifier(
4982  _rule_id: i32,
4983  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
4984  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
4985  ctxt: ActionContext,
4986) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
4987  unp!(args => expr, open, op, inner_expr, close);
4988  let annotated = XM::Token(
4989    XProps {
4990      meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("annotated")),
4991      ..XProps::default()
4992    },
4993    Meta::default(),
4994  );
4995  let absent = XM::Token(
4996    XProps {
4997      meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("absent")),
4998      ..XProps::default()
4999    },
5000    Meta::default(),
5001  );
5002  // Build Apply(op, Absent, inner_expr) for the modifier content
5003  let mut modifier_apply = XM::Apply(
5004    op.into(),
5005    Args(vec![Some(absent), inner_expr]),
5006    XProps::default(),
5007    Meta::default(),
5008  );
5009  // Fence the modifier: Dual(XMRef, XMWrap(OPEN, Apply(...), CLOSE))
5010  // matching Perl's Fence() which creates XMDual for parenthesized groups
5011  let mut fenced_xmrefs = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut modifier_apply], ctxt)?;
5012  let fenced = XM::Dual(
5013    Box::new(fenced_xmrefs.remove(0)),
5014    Box::new(XM::Wrap(
5015      vec![open.unwrap(), modifier_apply, close.unwrap()],
5016      XProps::default(),
5017      Meta::default(),
5018    )),
5019    XProps::default(),
5020    Meta::default(),
5021  );
5022  Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
5023    annotated.into(),
5024    Args(vec![expr, Some(fenced)]),
5025    XProps::default(),
5026    Meta::default(),
5027  )))
5028}
5029
5030/// Perl MathGrammar L223: expression PUNCT OPEN relop/modifierop Expression CLOSE
5031/// Semicolon annotation: a;(<e) → annotated(a, Fence((, absent < e, )))
5032/// Drops the PUNCT arg and delegates to annotated_fenced_modifier.
5033pub fn annotated_punct_fenced_modifier(
5034  rule_id: i32,
5035  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
5036  p: &[ValidationPragmatics],
5037  ctxt: ActionContext,
5038) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
5039  // args: [expr, punct, open, op, inner_expr, close]
5040  // Drop punct (index 1) and delegate
5041  args.remove(1); // remove punct
5042  annotated_fenced_modifier(rule_id, args, p, ctxt)
5043}

5045/// Speculative prefix application for `unknown fenced_factor`.
5046/// Produces an XMApp tree competing with the invisible-times interpretation
5047/// in Marpa's ambiguous forest. The pragmatic layer selects the
5048/// mathematically-consistent winner (see `FencedLettersAreFunctionArguments`).
5049///
5050/// **Intentional Rust divergence from Perl**: In Perl (Parse::RecDescent), speculation
5051/// only marks tokens with `possibleFunction='yes'` and falls back to invisible-times
5052/// multiplication. The Rust Marpa grammar directly produces the function application
5053/// parse `f@(x)`, which is the semantically superior interpretation — it avoids an
5054/// artificial invisible MULOP token that was a crutch for Parse::RecDescent's
5055/// backtracking parser. See docs/parity/OXIDIZED_DESIGN.md.
5056pub fn speculative_prefix_apply(
5057  _rule_id: i32,
5058  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
5059  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
5060  ctxt: ActionContext,
5061) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
5062  unp!(args => prefixop, arg1);
5063  // A letter whose own group holds it multiplies the group: `x(x+1)`, `n(n+1)/2`,
5064  // `\lambda(\lambda I-A)` are products, as Perl reads every unknown (`doubtArgs`,
5065  // MathGrammar:515-528) — a function is not applied to an expression in itself (57bz; ~1,190 of
5066  // the 1,219 formulas / 342 papers its delta A/B changed; 2605.28300, 2605.02279, 2605.04013,
5067  // 2605.30479, 2605.00539, 2605.31439).
5068  if let (Some(head), Some(group)) = (&prefixop, &arg1)
5069    && letter_recurs_in_its_group(head, group, &ctxt)
5070  {
5071    return Err("speculative_prefix_apply: the letter recurs in its group".into());
5072  }
5073  // … nor a group across explicit space, unless an argument list (user ruling Q6, 2026-10-01: `space_before_a_group`)
5074  if let (Some(head), Some(group)) = (&prefixop, &arg1)
5075    && space_before_a_group(head, group, &ctxt)
5076  {
5077    return Err("speculative_prefix_apply: explicit space before the group multiplies it".into());
5078  }
5079  // Mirror of `prefix_apply_applyop`: when arg1 is a fenced
5080  // modifier expression (`(>0)`, `(\in C)`), reject — the
5081  // legitimate parse goes through `annotated_fenced_modifier`.
5082  if let Some(ref arg) = arg1 {
5083    if is_fenced_modifier_dual(arg) {
5084      return Err(
5085        "speculative_prefix_apply: arg is a fenced modifier expression — \
5086         prefer annotated_fenced_modifier"
5087          .into(),
5088      );
5089    }
5090    // K-12 algebra: `letter |x|` reads as multiplication
5091    // (`letter * |x|`), NOT function application (`letter @
5092    // |x|`). The grammar admits speculative function-app via
5093    // `unknown group_factor → speculative_prefix_apply` for a group
5094    // only — the bar pairs are `bare_abs` — but a group between
5095    // bar glyphs, amsmath's `\lvert…\rvert`, is bars to the reader
5096    // too. Reject it so `tight_term factor → apply_invisible_times`
5097    // wins, giving a unique multiplication parse, as for
5098    // `a|a|+b|b|+c|c|`.
5099    //
5100    // Implication: QM-context cases like `<a|f|b>` and
5101    // `\langle B|sum|C\rangle` that rely on the speculative
5102    // function-app for `letter |x|` lose that reading. The
5103    // affected tests (qm/mathtools/count_parses/physics) are
5104    // re-blessed to the multiplication interpretation.
5105    if is_vertbar_fenced_dual(arg) {
5106      return Err(
5107        "speculative_prefix_apply: arg is vertbar-fenced — \
5108         prefer K-12 multiplication via apply_invisible_times"
5109          .into(),
5110      );
5111    }
5112    // Nor a Dirac bracket: a letter before a bra, ket, inner product or operator product multiplies
5113    // it, `H|\psi\rangle` H·ket, `c\langle u|u\rangle` c·⟨u|u⟩, as Perl (which applies no unknown,
5114    // `doubtArgs`, MathGrammar:518) — divergence #18 applies a letter to a group (user ruling
5115    // 2026-09-29; 57bp, ~45 formulas / 15 papers, 2605.20339, 2605.23874, 2605.28949).
5116    if dirac_meaning(arg).is_some() {
5117      return Err("speculative_prefix_apply: a Dirac bracket is no argument".into());
5118    }
5119  }
5120  Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
5121    prefixop.into(),
5122    Args(vec![arg1]),
5123    XProps::default(),
5124    Meta::default(),
5125  )))
5126}
5127
5128/// Detect `XM::Dual(_, Wrap[OPEN-vertbar, …, CLOSE-vertbar])` — a
5129/// bilaterally-vertbar-fenced absolute-value or norm shape. The
5130/// `fenced` action produces this for `|expr|`, `||expr||`, and
5131/// `\left|expr\right|`. We use it to reject these as candidates
5132/// for function-application speculation; K-12 algebra reads
5133/// `letter |x|` as multiplication, not function-app.
5134fn is_vertbar_fenced_dual(arg: &XM) -> bool {
5135  let XM::Dual(_, ref presentation, _, ref meta) = *arg else {
5136    return false;
5137  };
5138  if meta.bar_fence {
5139    return true;
5140  }
5141  let XM::Wrap(ref items, ..) = **presentation else {
5142    return false;
5143  };
5144  let is_vertbar = |x: Option<&XM>| -> bool {
5145    match x {
5146      Some(XM::Token(p, _)) => {
5147        p.content.as_deref() == Some("|") || p.content.as_deref() == Some("‖")
5148      },
5149      Some(XM::Lexeme(name, _)) => {
5150        name.starts_with("VERTBAR:") || name.starts_with("STRETCHY_VERTBAR:")
5151      },
5152      _ => false,
5153    }
5154  };
5155  is_vertbar(items.first()) && is_vertbar(items.last())
5156}
5157/// Perl: limit-from@(number, sign) — directional limits like 0+, 1-
5158/// Matches factor_base followed by addop. Semantic checks:
5159/// 1. The addop must be + or - (not other ADDOP like ⊕)
5160/// 2. The factor_base should be a number or simple ID (not a compound expression)
5161///
5162/// If checks fail, prunes the parse so Marpa tries addition instead.
5163pub fn limit_from_apply(
5164  _rule_id: i32,
5165  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
5166  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
5167  ctxt: ActionContext,
5168) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
5169  // Check the addop is + or -
5170  let is_plus_minus = args.get(1).and_then(|a| a.as_ref()).is_some_and(|xm| {
5171    let val = match xm {
5172      XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes)
5173        .ok()
5174        .and_then(|n| n.get_attribute("meaning")),
5175      XM::Token(props, _) => props.meaning.as_ref().map(|c| c.to_string()),
5176      _ => None,
5177    };
5178    matches!(val.as_deref(), Some("plus") | Some("minus"))
5179  });
5180  if !is_plus_minus {
5181    return Err("limit_from_apply: addop is not +/-, pruning".into());
5182  }
5183  unp!(args => base, sign);
5184  let op = XM::Token(
5185    XProps {
5186      meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("limit-from")),
5187      ..XProps::default()
5188    },
5189    Meta::default(),
5190  );
5191  Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
5192    op.into(),
5193    Args(vec![base, sign]),
5194    XProps::default(),
5195    Meta::default(),
5196  )))
5197}
5198
5199/// Perl IntFactor: diffd ATOM_OR_ID/UNKNOWN => Apply(DIFFOP(d), var)
5200/// Matches `d` followed by a factor. The semantic action checks that the first
5201/// token's text content is literally "d" (case-sensitive). If not, prunes the parse.
5202/// When matched, annotates the `d` token with role=DIFFOP, meaning=differential-d.
5203pub fn diffop_apply(
5204  _rule_id: i32,
5205  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
5206  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
5207  ctxt: ActionContext,
5208) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
5209  unp!(args => diffd, arg1);
5210  let annotated = differential_d(diffd, &ctxt)?;
5211  // A numeric power on the variable is the differential's: a line element `ds^2` is (ds)², `\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}`'s
5212  // denominator (dx)², `ds_r^2` (ds_r)² — an index stays the variable's (`dx^\mu`, `dx_1`) (57cj.23, the merge review).
5213  if let Some(XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(parts), props, meta)) = &arg1
5214    && operator_category(op) == Some("SUPERSCRIPTOP")
5215    && let [Some(base), Some(power)] = parts.as_slice()
5216    && is_a_numeric_power(power)
5217  {
5218    let differential = XM::Apply(
5219      annotated.into(),
5220      Args(vec![Some(base.clone())]),
5221      XProps::default(),
5222      Meta::for_differential(),
5223    );
5224    return Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
5225      Operator(op.clone()),
5226      Args(vec![Some(differential), Some(power.clone())]),
5227      props.clone(),
5228      meta.clone(),
5229    )));
5230  }
5231  Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
5232    annotated.into(),
5233    Args(vec![arg1]),
5234    XProps::default(),
5235    Meta::for_differential(),
5236  )))
5237}
5238
5239/// A number as a power (`diffop_apply`): `2`, `3`, the lexer's NUMBER or a non-negative ATOM_NUMBER.
5240fn is_a_numeric_power(xm: &XM) -> bool {
5241  match xm {
5242    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) if lex.starts_with("ATOM_NUMBER:") => {
5243      !lex["ATOM_NUMBER:".len()..].starts_with('-')
5244    },
5245    XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..) => operator_category(xm) == Some("NUMBER"),
5246    _ => false,
5247  }
5248}
5249
5250/// A differential's power before its variable, `d^3` in `\int d^3x\,f` (`raised_differential_d`, divergence #395;
5251/// 2605.29990, 2605.21314, 2605.23046): the annotated `d` (`differential_d`) takes the superscript as any base does,
5252/// `(differential-d ^ 3)` as a bound differential's `\rmd^3` reads. Only a count is a power (`is_a_power_count`), and
5253/// only in an integral's operand, where Perl reads `diffd` at all (`moreIntOpArgFactors`, MathGrammar:633-638), as every
5254/// letter `d` (the lexer's `XDIFFUNK`, `util::in_an_integral_operand`): a dimension outside the operand stays a letter's
5255/// power, before the integral sign, `d^2h^2\int_t^{t+h}…` (2605.07939), `\leq 9\tilde L_f^2d^2h\sum\int…` (2605.26800), or
5256/// after a relation, `\int f\le C d^2 n`.
5257pub fn differential_d_power(
5258  _rule_id: i32,
5259  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
5260  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
5261  ctxt: ActionContext,
5262) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
5263  unp!(args => diffd, script);
5264  let Some(script) = script else {
5265    return Err("differential_d_power: no script".into());
5266  };
5267  if !matches!(&script, XM::Wrap(parts, ..) if parts.get(1).is_some_and(is_a_power_count)) {
5268    return Err("differential_d_power: the script is no power".into());
5269  }
5270  let annotated = differential_d(diffd, &ctxt)?;
5271  new_script(annotated, script, ctxt)
5272}
5273
5274/// A differential's power (`differential_d_power`): a count — a number, a single-character letter (not the transpose
5275/// `T`; a named one, `alpha`, is no count), or a
5276/// sum, difference or product of counts, parsed or the lexer's atom of one (`d^{d-1}`, `d^{2N}`). Not a negative
5277/// number (`d^{-1}`), a group (`d^{(2)}`, an order as `x^{(2)}` is), a symbol (`d^\infty`, `d^\natural`, 2605.01646), an
5278/// accented letter (`d^{\hat n}`), a prime, a star or a dagger.
5279fn is_a_power_count(xm: &XM) -> bool {
5280  let text = |xm: &XM| -> Option<String> {
5281    match xm {
5282      XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lex.split(':').nth(1).map(str::to_owned),
5283      XM::Token(props, _) => props.content.as_deref().map(str::to_owned),
5284      _ => None,
5285    }
5286  };
5287  match xm {
5288    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) if lex.starts_with("ATOM_NUMBER:") => {
5289      !lex["ATOM_NUMBER:".len()..].starts_with('-')
5290    },
5291    XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..) => match operator_category(xm) {
5292      Some("NUMBER") => true,
5293      Some("UNKNOWN" | "XDIFFUNK") => text(xm).is_some_and(|t| t.chars().count() == 1 && t != "T"),
5294      // the lexer's atom of a count — a number or a letter (a gathered row's content branch spells a script so,
5295      // `d^{4}` ATOM `4`, 2605.29990's split), or a sum or product of counts in prefix order: `-d1` for d−1, `⁢2N`
5296      // for 2N (a sign before one operand, `-n`, is no count)
5297      Some("ATOM") => text(xm).is_some_and(|t| {
5298        let mut chars = t.chars();
5299        let first = chars.next();
5300        let rest: Vec<char> = chars.collect();
5301        t.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit())
5302          || (t.chars().count() == 1 && t != "T" && t.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphabetic()))
5303          || (matches!(first, Some('-' | '+' | '\u{2062}'))
5304            && rest.len() >= 2
5305            && rest.iter().all(char::is_ascii_alphanumeric))
5306      }),
5307      _ => false,
5308    },
5309    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..) => {
5310      args.len() >= 2
5311        && (is_invisible_times_op(op) || operator_category(op) == Some("ADDOP"))
5312        && args
5313          .iter()
5314          .all(|arg| arg.as_ref().is_some_and(is_a_power_count))
5315    },
5316    _ => false,
5317  }
5318}
5319
5320/// A differential's power applied to its variable, `(d³)@(x)` (`raised_differential_d`, divergence #395).
5321pub fn differential_power_apply(
5322  _rule_id: i32,
5323  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
5324  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
5325  _: ActionContext,
5326) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
5327  unp!(args => power, variable);
5328  Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
5329    power.into(),
5330    Args(vec![variable]),
5331    XProps::default(),
5332    Meta::for_differential(),
5333  )))
5334}
5335
5336/// The letter `d` of an integral's differential, annotated as Perl's IntFactor does (MathGrammar:643-647):
5337/// role DIFFOP, meaning differential-d. Refused for any other letter; outside an integral's operand the lexer gave the
5338/// `d` no differential lexeme — Perl reads `diffd` only among an INTOP's arguments (`moreIntOpArgFactors`,
5339/// MathGrammar:633-638).
5340fn differential_d(diffd: Option<XM>, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
5341  // Check that the first token is literally "d"
5342  let is_d = diffd.as_ref().is_some_and(|xm| match xm {
5343    XM::Token(props, _) => props.content.as_deref() == Some("d"),
5344    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lex.split(':').nth(1) == Some("d"),
5345    _ => false,
5346  });
5347  if !is_d {
5348    return Err("diffop_apply: first token is not 'd', pruning parse".into());
5349  }
5350  // Perl: diffd is only recognized inside IntOpArgFactors (integral context): the lexer gives a `d` its differential
5351  // lexeme (`XDIFFUNK`/`XDIFFID`, the only one the grammar's differential rules take) in an integral's operand only,
5352  // `util::in_an_integral_operand` (SYNC (17)).
5353  // Annotate the d token: role=DIFFOP, meaning=differential-d
5354  Ok(match diffd {
5355    Some(XM::Token(mut props, meta)) => {
5356      props.role = Some(Cow::Borrowed("DIFFOP"));
5357      props.meaning = Some(Cow::Borrowed("differential-d"));
5358      Some(XM::Token(props, meta))
5359    },
5360    // Perl `Annotate` (MathParser.pm:1206-1235) annotates the node itself rather than a fresh
5361    // `d` — the token keeps its xml:id, so a content branch's XMRef to it still resolves, and
5362    // its font — and on an XMRef yields `<XMRef idref role meaning/>`, carrying the ref's
5363    // `_xmkey` as Perl `createXMRefs` does (Package.pm:1557-1561). The token's props are the
5364    // ones `XProps` reads. Golden
5365    // tests/parse/integrals_and_differentials.tex#gathered_row_keeps_its_differential (arXiv
5366    // 2605.01547, 2605.23309 split integrands).
5367    Some(XM::Lexeme(lex, meta)) => match lookup_lex_node(&lex, ctxt.nodes) {
5368      Ok(node) if node.get_name() == "XMRef" => Some(XM::Ref(XProps {
5369        id: node.get_attribute("idref").map(Cow::Owned),
5370        xmkey: node.get_attribute("_xmkey").map(Cow::Owned),
5371        role: Some(Cow::Borrowed("DIFFOP")),
5372        meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("differential-d")),
5373        ..XProps::default()
5374      })),
5375      Ok(node) => {
5376        let mut props = XProps::from(node);
5377        props.role = Some(Cow::Borrowed("DIFFOP"));
5378        props.meaning = Some(Cow::Borrowed("differential-d"));
5379        Some(XM::Token(props, meta))
5380      },
5381      Err(_) => Some(XM::Token(
5382        XProps {
5383          content: Some(Cow::Borrowed("d")),
5384          role: Some(Cow::Borrowed("DIFFOP")),
5385          meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("differential-d")),
5386          ..XProps::default()
5387        },
5388        meta,
5389      )),
5390    },
5391    other => other,
5392  })
5393}
5394/// Divergence #374 (user ruling 2026-09-29): a differential operator's application to the one factor
5395/// after it (`diffop_application`) — a finished factor, as a differential `d x` is (`diffop_apply`,
5396/// `Meta::differential`): the factors after it are its product's, not its operand's
5397/// (`\partial_x u\cdot v` (∂_x u)·v), where Perl's `bigop` takes them (MathGrammar:717, :605-618; 2605.03741,
5398/// 2605.08634, 2605.24774).
5399pub fn differential_operator_apply(
5400  rule_id: i32,
5401  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
5402  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
5403  ctxt: ActionContext,
5404) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
5405  // A letter's application to a group across explicit space is no operand of its own, nor a factor of a numeric
5406  // monomial's: `\partial_x u\,(1-x)` is (∂_x u)·(1−x), and `\partial_x 2u\,(1-x)` ∂_x(2·u·(1−x)), the monomial taking the
5407  // group as a factor (in a trig argument the space ends it: `\sin\partial_x 2u\,(1-x)` sin@(∂_x(2u))·(1−x)) — the space
5408  // ends the application, as in a trig argument (57cj.8 review; 2605.24151 `\partial_z\rho\,(\tfrac12|\nabla\theta|^2)`, 2605.18945;
5409  // `\partial_x u(1-x)` stays ∂_x(u(1−x)), #18).
5410  if let [_, Some(operand)] = args.as_slice() {
5411    let factors = if is_numeric_monomial(operand) {
5412      product_factors(operand)
5413    } else {
5414      vec![operand]
5415    };
5416    if factors
5417      .iter()
5418      .any(|factor| is_letter_application_across_space(factor, ctxt.nodes))
5419    {
5420      return Err(
5421        "differential_operator_apply: explicit space ends the letter's application".into(),
5422      );
5423    }
5424  }
5425  Ok(
5426    prefix_apply(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)?.map(|applied| match applied {
5427      XM::Apply(op, args, props, _) => XM::Apply(op, args, props, Meta::for_differential()),
5428      other => other,
5429    }),
5430  )
5431}
5432
5433/// A differential's or a differential operator's application (`Meta::differential`): `d x`,
5434/// `\partial_x u`.
5435/// `op_head mulop diffop_operand` (`divergence_operand`): an operator's head joined by `\cdot` or `\times` to the factor
5436/// after it — a divergence or a curl, `\nabla\cdot u`, `\nabla\times E` — one factor a derivative takes whole (user ruling
5437/// 2026-10-01: `\partial_t\nabla\cdot u` ∂_t(∇·u), `\partial_t\nabla\times E=0` ∂_t(∇×E) = 0; was (∂_t∇)·u, divergence #374);
5438/// `infix_apply_nary` refuses the twin that differentiates the bare head (`differentiates_a_divergence_s_head`).
5439pub fn divergence_or_curl(
5440  rule_id: i32,
5441  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
5442  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
5443  ctxt: ActionContext,
5444) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
5445  match args.as_slice() {
5446    [_, Some(op), _] if is_a_divergence_s_operator(op, &ctxt) => {
5447      infix_apply_nary(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
5448    },
5449    _ => Err("divergence_or_curl: no dot or cross product".into()),
5450  }
5451}
5452
5453/// `\cdot` or `\times`, bare: the operator of a divergence or a curl after an operator's head (`divergence_or_curl`).
5454fn is_a_divergence_s_operator(op: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
5455  operator_category(op) == Some("MULOP")
5456    && matches!(op, XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..))
5457    && realized_value(op, ctxt).is_ok_and(|value| matches!(value.as_ref(), "\u{22C5}" | "\u{00D7}"))
5458}
5459
5460/// Is `left · right` a derivative of an operator's bare head before the dot or cross product of a divergence or a curl
5461/// (`divergence_or_curl` takes it whole): `\partial_t\nabla\cdot u` has no (∂_t∇)·u. Not before a big operator, which the
5462/// derivative's one factor cannot be (`\partial_t\nabla\cdot\sum_i u_i` keeps (∂_t∇)·∑).
5463fn differentiates_a_divergence_s_head(
5464  left: &XM,
5465  op: &XM,
5466  right: &XM,
5467  ctxt: &ActionContext,
5468) -> bool {
5469  let XM::Apply(_, Args(args), _, meta) = product_end(left, true) else {
5470    return false;
5471  };
5472  meta.differential
5473    && matches!(args.as_slice(), [Some(head)]
5474      if matches!(script_nucleus(head), XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..))
5475        && operator_category(script_nucleus(head)) == Some("OPERATOR"))
5476    && is_a_divergence_s_operator(op, ctxt)
5477    && !is_summation_like(product_end(right, false))
5478}
5479
5480fn is_differential(xm: &XM) -> bool { matches!(xm, XM::Apply(_, _, _, meta) if meta.differential) }
5481
5482/// A differential operator standing alone, bare or scripted: `\partial`, `\partial^2`, `\partial_x`.
5483fn is_bare_differential_operator(xm: &XM) -> bool {
5484  let nucleus = script_nucleus(xm);
5485  matches!(nucleus, XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..)) && operator_category(nucleus) == Some("DIFFOP")
5486}
5487
5488/// What a differential operator's application holds, through every differential operator
5489/// (`\partial\sin x` → `\sin x`): the one factor it takes ends as that factor does (divergence #374).
5490fn through_differentials(xm: &XM) -> &XM {
5491  match xm {
5492    XM::Apply(_, Args(args), _, meta) if meta.differential => match args.as_slice() {
5493      [Some(operand)] => through_differentials(operand),
5494      _ => xm,
5495    },
5496    _ => xm,
5497  }
5498}
5499
5500/// Is `xm` — a differential operator, bare, scripted or applied — a partial one, `\partial` or an
5501/// accented `\bar\partial` (util.rs lexes it a DIFFOP), rather than a `d` (`d x`, iopart's `\rmd x`,
5502/// physics' `\dd`)? A Leibniz quotient's denominator takes the numerator's kind only (57cj review:
5503/// `\int_0^1\partial^n f/\partial x^n\,dx` keeps its `dx`; latent, the review's probe, no corpus witness).
5504fn is_partial_differential(xm: &XM) -> bool {
5505  let head = match xm {
5506    XM::Apply(Operator(head), _, _, meta) if meta.differential => head.as_ref(),
5507    other => other,
5508  };
5509  let nucleus = script_nucleus(head);
5510  operator_category(nucleus) == Some("DIFFOP")
5511    && match nucleus {
5512      XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lex
5513        .split(':')
5514        .nth(1)
5515        .is_some_and(|name| name.contains("partial") || name.contains('\u{2202}')),
5516      XM::Token(props, _) => props
5517        .meaning
5518        .as_deref()
5519        .is_some_and(|meaning| meaning.contains("partial")),
5520      _ => false,
5521    }
5522}
5523
5524/// A partial differential operator's application to its one factor (`diffop_application`,
5525/// `differential_operator_apply`): `\partial_x u` — a bare item an operator's, an OPFUNCTION's or a
5526/// trig function's bare argument takes (57cj review: `\nabla\partial_x u` ∇@(∂_x u), `\sin\partial_x u`
5527/// sin@(∂_x u)); not a differential `d x`, which ends a trig argument (#367).
5528fn is_partial_derivative(xm: &XM) -> bool {
5529  is_differential(xm)
5530    && is_partial_differential(xm)
5531    && matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(head), ..) if is_bare_differential_operator(head))
5532}
5533
5534/// A number standing as a factor: a NUMBER, or a fraction or root of numbers, which the lexer reads whole
5535/// (`\frac12`, `ATOM_NUMBER:12`, `\sqrt2`, util.rs `is_numeric_constant`).
5536fn is_numeric_factor(xm: &XM) -> bool {
5537  match xm {
5538    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) if lex.starts_with("ATOM_NUMBER:") => true,
5539    XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..) => operator_category(xm) == Some("NUMBER"),
5540    _ => false,
5541  }
5542}
5543
5544/// A differential operator applied to a number alone, which the factors juxtaposed after it join
5545/// (`numeric_monomial`, 57cj review): the product `(\partial_x 2)\,u` ranks below ∂_x(2u)
5546/// (`differentiated_number_sites`, `DifferentiatedNumbersTakeTheirFactors`).
5547fn differentiates_a_number(xm: &XM) -> bool {
5548  matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(args), _, meta)
5549    if meta.differential
5550      && is_bare_differential_operator(head)
5551      && matches!(args.as_slice(), [Some(operand)]
5552        if is_numeric_lead(operand)
5553          || is_numeric_monomial(operand)
5554          // (a function's bare application to a constant, whose argument takes the factors after it: `\partial_x\log 2\,u`;
5555          // not a bare π, which leads no monomial — `\int f\,d\pi(x,y)` keeps its measure dπ, 57cj.9 A/B, 2605.00545)
5556          || is_constant(operand) && is_bare_operator_application(operand)))
5557}
5558
5559/// A product a number leads (`numeric_monomial`): `2\pi`, `\frac12 u^2`, `2^3u` (`is_numeric_lead`).
5560fn is_numeric_monomial(xm: &XM) -> bool {
5561  matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(factors), _, meta)
5562    if meta.fenced.is_none()
5563      && is_invisible_times_op(op)
5564      && factors.first().and_then(Option::as_ref).is_some_and(is_numeric_lead))
5565}
5566
5567/// What leads a numeric monomial (`numeric_monomial`): a number, or one raised to a constant power (`numeric_power`:
5568/// `\partial_x 2^3u` ∂_x(2³·u), `\partial_x\sqrt2^3u`; 57cj.8 review, latent, its probes).
5569fn is_numeric_lead(xm: &XM) -> bool {
5570  is_numeric_factor(xm)
5571    || matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..)
5572      if operator_category(op) == Some("SUPERSCRIPTOP")
5573        && matches!(args.as_slice(), [Some(base), Some(power)]
5574          // (a constant group raised to a constant power: `(2\pi)^{-3}`, 57cj.9 review)
5575          if (is_numeric_lead(base) || matches!(base, XM::Dual(..) | XM::Wrap(..)) && is_constant(base))
5576            && is_constant(power)))
5577}
5578
5579/// `numeric_power`: a number raised to a constant power, which leads a numeric monomial (`is_numeric_lead`); another
5580/// power is a factor of the derivative alone (`\partial_x 2^n u` (∂_x 2ⁿ)·u, ∂ taking one factor).
5581pub fn numeric_power_script(
5582  rule_id: i32,
5583  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
5584  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
5585  ctxt: ActionContext,
5586) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
5587  let power = postfix_script(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)?;
5588  if !power.as_ref().is_some_and(is_numeric_lead) {
5589    return Err("numeric_power_script: no constant power".into());
5590  }
5591  Ok(power)
5592}
5593
5594/// A differential operator, applied or bare, the first factor of `xm`: what a numeric monomial with a
5595/// factor of its own stops before (`numeric_monomial_product`, `differentiates_a_number`).
5596fn starts_with_a_derivative(xm: &XM) -> bool {
5597  let first = product_end(xm, false);
5598  is_partial_derivative(first) || is_bare_differential_operator(first)
5599}
5600
5601/// An integral's differential `d x` (`diffop_apply`), or its `d` read as a letter (XDIFFUNK), the first factor
5602/// of `xm`: what a numeric monomial always stops before (57cj.2 review: `\int\partial_x 2uv\,dx` keeps its `dx`).
5603fn starts_with_a_d_differential(xm: &XM) -> bool {
5604  let first = product_end(xm, false);
5605  (is_differential(first) && !is_partial_derivative(first) && !is_bare_differential_operator(first))
5606    // the integral's letter `d` only (the lexer's XDIFFUNK), not a `d` outside one (`\partial_x 2d` ∂_x(2d))
5607    || matches!(script_nucleus(first), XM::Lexeme(lex, _) if lex.starts_with("XDIFFUNK:d:"))
5608}
5609
5610/// `DifferentiatedNumbersTakeTheirFactors` (latent, no corpus witness: the 57cj reviews' probes): how many times
5611/// does the product `xm` leave outside a differential operator's number a factor juxtaposed after it that the
5612/// number's monomial takes (`numeric_monomial`, 57cj review: `\partial_x 2u` is ∂_x(2u), not ∂_x(2)·u)? Not an
5613/// integral's differential, nor a derivative after a monomial with a factor of its own (`numeric_monomial_product`;
5614/// 57cj.1, 57cj.2 reviews), nor what no monomial takes, an operator or a function with no argument
5615/// (`\partial_x 2u\,\nabla\cdot v` (∂_x(2u)·∇)·v, 57cj.5 review; an applied one it takes, `\partial_x 2u\,\nabla\,\partial_y 3w`).
5616/// Every differentiated number on the left factor's right edge counts — through a differential operator's operand
5617/// and a function's or operator's bare argument, `\partial_x\partial_y 2u` ∂_x(∂_y(2u)), `\sin\partial_x 2\,\partial_y u`
5618/// sin@(∂_x(2·∂_y u)) (`right_edge`; 57cj.5 review). A soft, counting preference (57cj.3, 57cj.4 reviews): one site it
5619/// cannot hold does not make the others split (`…+\partial_y 3w` keeps ∂_y(3w)). A product between delimiters counts
5620/// as any other: the split inside `(\partial_y 3w)` is the same split. Only juxtaposition: the monomial takes no
5621/// factor across a MulOp (`\partial_x 2\cdot u`).
5622pub(crate) fn differentiated_number_sites(xm: &XM) -> usize {
5623  let XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(factors), ..) = xm else {
5624    return 0;
5625  };
5626  if !is_invisible_times_op(op) {
5627    return 0;
5628  }
5629  factors
5630    .windows(2)
5631    .map(|pair| match pair {
5632      [Some(left), Some(right)] => right_edge(left)
5633        .into_iter()
5634        // (inside a function's or operator's bare argument, which has ended before `right`, a number with factors of
5635        // its own takes nothing more: only a differentiated constant counts there, a number or its coefficient run,
5636        // `\sin\partial_x 2\pi\,u\,v`; 57cj.6, 57cj.7 reviews)
5637        .filter(|(operator, in_a_bare_argument)| {
5638          differentiates_a_number(operator)
5639            && !(*in_a_bare_argument && differentiates_a_monomial(operator))
5640            && !(starts_with_a_d_differential(right)
5641              || starts_with_an_unapplied_head(right)
5642              || differentiates_a_monomial(operator) && starts_with_a_derivative(right))
5643        })
5644        .count(),
5645      _ => 0,
5646    })
5647    .sum()
5648}
5649
5650/// `LetterDsBeforeVariablesAreDifferentials` (57cj.20, SYNC (16); 2605.28900, 2605.08899): how many times does the
5651/// product `xm` read an integral's letter `d` — or its power, `d^3` — as a factor before a variable, bare or post-scripted, that its
5652/// differential takes (`diffop_apply`, `differential_power_apply`)? Perl's IntFactor tries `diffd ATOM_OR_ID
5653/// addScripts` before `Factor` (MathGrammar:640-647), so a `d` the differential can take is one: `\int f\,dx_1`
5654/// f·differential-d@(x₁), not f·d·x₁. A soft, counting preference: the trees with the fewest such letters are kept, so
5655/// a site no tree reads as a differential (no INTOP: the lexer's `d` is a plain unknown, util.rs; a numerator,
5656/// `StandaloneDiffopsAreNotNumerators`) counts in every tree alike and decides nothing. Only juxtaposition, as
5657/// the grammar's `factor` rule: `d\cdot x_1` has no differential reading.
5658pub(crate) fn letter_differential_sites(xm: &XM) -> usize {
5659  let XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(factors), ..) = xm else {
5660    return 0;
5661  };
5662  if !is_invisible_times_op(op) {
5663    return 0;
5664  }
5665  // (the factors meet at their edges: a slash quotient on the left ends in its denominator's last factor,
5666  // `dx/dt^2` (differential-d@(x)/d)·t² beside differential-d@(x)/differential-d@(t²), a bare argument in its own,
5667  // `ends_in_a_letter_differential_d`; a group ends at its delimiter)
5668  factors
5669    .windows(2)
5670    .filter(|pair| {
5671      matches!(pair, [Some(left), Some(right)]
5672        if ends_in_a_letter_differential_d(left)
5673          && is_a_differential_variable(unfenced_product_end(right, false)))
5674    })
5675    .count()
5676}
5677
5678/// The first (`last` false) or last factor of an undelimited product, as `product_end`, not entering a group.
5679fn unfenced_product_end(xm: &XM, last: bool) -> &XM {
5680  match xm {
5681    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, _, meta)
5682      if meta.fenced.is_none() && args.0.len() >= 2 && is_product_operator(op) =>
5683    {
5684      match if last { args.0.last() } else { args.0.first() } {
5685        Some(Some(factor)) => unfenced_product_end(factor, last),
5686        _ => xm,
5687      }
5688    },
5689    _ => xm,
5690  }
5691}
5692
5693/// The integral's letter `d` (the lexer's `XDIFFUNK`/`XDIFFID`, which `diffop_apply` annotates), alone or raised to a
5694/// power (`raised_differential_d`): `d`, `\mathrm{d}`, `d^3`, `d^n`.
5695fn is_a_letter_differential_d(xm: &XM) -> bool {
5696  let is_d = |xm: &XM| matches!(xm, XM::Lexeme(lex, _) if lex.starts_with("XDIFFUNK:d:") || lex.starts_with("XDIFFID:d:"));
5697  is_d(xm)
5698    || matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..)
5699      if operator_category(op) == Some("SUPERSCRIPTOP")
5700        && matches!(args.as_slice(), [Some(base), Some(power)] if is_d(base) && is_a_power_count(power)))
5701}
5702
5703/// Does `xm` end in an integral's letter `d` (`is_a_letter_differential_d`): its last factor, or the last factor of a
5704/// bare argument it ends in — `\int\cos d\theta` read cos@(d)·θ beside cos@(d·θ) holds the same letter before θ
5705/// (57cj.20 review; a trig argument takes no differential, #367). A group ends the walk.
5706fn ends_in_a_letter_differential_d(xm: &XM) -> bool {
5707  let mut node = unfenced_product_end(xm, true);
5708  loop {
5709    if is_a_letter_differential_d(node) {
5710      return true;
5711    }
5712    match node {
5713      XM::Apply(_, Args(args), _, meta) if meta.fenced.is_none() => match args.as_slice() {
5714        [Some(argument)]
5715          if !matches!(argument, XM::Dual(..) | XM::Wrap(..))
5716            && !matches!(argument, XM::Apply(_, _, _, inner) if inner.fenced.is_some()) =>
5717        {
5718          node = unfenced_product_end(argument, true);
5719        },
5720        _ => return false,
5721      },
5722      _ => return false,
5723    }
5724  }
5725}
5726
5727/// What a differential takes after its `d` (`diffop_apply`'s `factor_base`, `differential_variable`): a letter,
5728/// identifier, atom, array or number, bare or with post-scripts of its own.
5729fn is_a_differential_variable(xm: &XM) -> bool {
5730  matches!(
5731    operator_category(script_nucleus(xm)),
5732    Some("UNKNOWN" | "ID" | "ATOM" | "ARRAY" | "NUMBER" | "XDIFFUNK" | "XDIFFID")
5733  ) && matches!(script_nucleus(xm), XM::Lexeme(..))
5734}
5735
5736/// The nodes on `xm`'s right edge, outermost first: its last factor, and down through each unfenced application
5737/// of one undelimited argument (a differential operator's operand, a function's or operator's bare argument, a
5738/// sign) to that argument's last factor; a group's application ends the walk (`differentiated_number_sites`). Each
5739/// node comes with whether a function's or operator's bare argument holds it.
5740fn right_edge(xm: &XM) -> Vec<(&XM, bool)> {
5741  let mut edge = Vec::new();
5742  let mut node = product_end(xm, true);
5743  let mut in_a_bare_argument = false;
5744  loop {
5745    edge.push((node, in_a_bare_argument));
5746    match node {
5747      XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(args), _, meta) if meta.fenced.is_none() => {
5748        match args.as_slice() {
5749          [Some(argument)]
5750            if !matches!(argument, XM::Dual(..) | XM::Wrap(..))
5751              && !matches!(argument, XM::Apply(_, _, _, argument_meta) if argument_meta.fenced.is_some()) =>
5752          {
5753            in_a_bare_argument |= !meta.differential
5754              && matches!(
5755                head_category(head),
5756                Some("OPFUNCTION" | "TRIGFUNCTION" | "OPERATOR" | "FUNCTION")
5757              );
5758            node = product_end(argument, true);
5759          },
5760          _ => break,
5761        }
5762      },
5763      _ => break,
5764    }
5765  }
5766  edge
5767}
5768
5769/// Does `xm` start with an operator or a function that takes no argument there (`\nabla`, `\nabla^2`, `\log`): what
5770/// no numeric monomial takes (`numeric_monomial = number tight_term`; `bare_op_term`, `bare_opfunction_term`).
5771fn starts_with_an_unapplied_head(xm: &XM) -> bool {
5772  let first = product_end(xm, false);
5773  is_operator_head(first) || is_bare_function_head(first)
5774}
5775
5776/// Is `xm` a differential operator applied to a numeric monomial with a factor of its own after its constants
5777/// (`\partial_x(2u)`, `\partial_t(\frac12|u|^2)`, `\partial_x(2\pi u)`), not to a constant alone (`\partial_x 2`,
5778/// `\partial_x 2\pi`, `\partial_x(2\pi i)`, which a differentiated number counts as; 57cj.7, 57cj.8 reviews, latent, no
5779/// corpus witness)?
5780fn differentiates_a_monomial(xm: &XM) -> bool {
5781  matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(args), _, meta)
5782    if meta.differential
5783      && is_bare_differential_operator(head)
5784      && matches!(args.as_slice(), [Some(operand)]
5785        if is_numeric_monomial(operand) && !is_constant(operand)))
5786}
5787
5788/// A differential operator applied to an ellipsis alone (`\partial_i\ldots`).
5789fn differentiates_an_ellipsis(xm: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
5790  matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(args), _, meta)
5791    if meta.differential
5792      && is_bare_differential_operator(head)
5793      && matches!(args.as_slice(), [Some(operand)] if is_ellipsis(operand, ctxt)))
5794}
5795
5796/// `numeric_monomial`'s first product: a number and the factors after it, one operand of a differential
5797/// operator (57cj review: `\partial_x\frac12 u^2` ∂_x(½u²), `\partial_x 2u` ∂_x(2u), `\partial_t 2\pi iu`, as
5798/// Perl's greedy `bigop` reads them) — up to an integral's differential (`\int\partial_t\frac12|u|^2\,dx`
5799/// ∫(∂_t(½|u|²)·dx), its `d` read as a letter too) and a derivative after a factor of its own (`\partial_x 2u\,\partial_y v`
5800/// (∂_x(2u))·∂_y v; 57cj.1 review); a derivative right after the number it takes (`\partial_x 2\,\partial_y u`
5801/// ∂_x(2·∂_y u), as 57ci and Perl; 57cj.2 review), or after its constant run (`\partial_x 2\pi\,\partial_y u`
5802/// ∂_x(2π·∂_y u), `\partial_t 2\pi i\,\partial_x u`; 57cj.7, 57cj.8 reviews, latent, no corpus witness).
5803pub fn numeric_monomial_product(
5804  rule_id: i32,
5805  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
5806  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
5807  ctxt: ActionContext,
5808) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
5809  if let [Some(number), Some(tail)] = args.as_slice() {
5810    let factors = product_factors(tail);
5811    // (past the number's constant run, `\partial_x 2\pi\,\partial_y u` ∂_x(2π·∂_y u); 57cj.7, 57cj.8 reviews; the
5812    // leading number is in the run, so the tail's share is one less)
5813    let run = constant_run(
5814      &std::iter::once(number)
5815        .chain(factors.iter().copied())
5816        .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
5817    );
5818    if factors
5819      .iter()
5820      .any(|factor| starts_with_a_d_differential(factor))
5821      || factors
5822        .iter()
5823        .skip(run.saturating_sub(1))
5824        .skip(1)
5825        .any(|factor| starts_with_a_derivative(factor))
5826    {
5827      return Err("numeric_monomial_product: a differential ends the monomial".into());
5828    }
5829  }
5830  apply_invisible_times(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
5831}
5832
5833/// APPLYOP explicit application: operator APPLYOP term => Apply(operator, term)
5834/// The APPLYOP token is consumed/discarded.
5835pub fn prefix_apply_applyop(
5836  _rule_id: i32,
5837  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
5838  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
5839  _: ActionContext,
5840) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
5841  unp!(args => prefixop, _applyop, arg1);
5842  // Early-action prune: when arg1 is a fenced modifier expression
5843  // — i.e. a Dual whose content is a relop/metarelop Apply with
5844  // `absent` as the FIRST argument (the `prefix_relop_apply`
5845  // shape) — we must NOT treat it as a function argument. The
5846  // grammar's `expression lparen relop expression rparen →
5847  // annotated_fenced_modifier` already builds the correct
5848  // `annotated@(x, fenced-modifier)` tree. Function-application
5849  // here corrupts to `x@(absent > 0)` which is meaningless.
5850  if let Some(ref arg) = arg1
5851    && is_fenced_modifier_dual(arg)
5852  {
5853    return Err(
5854      "prefix_apply_applyop: arg is a fenced modifier expression — \
5855         prefer annotated_fenced_modifier over function application"
5856        .into(),
5857    );
5858  }
5859  Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
5860    prefixop.into(),
5861    Args(vec![arg1]),
5862    XProps::default(),
5863    Meta::default(),
5864  )))
5865}
5866
5867/// Detect the "fenced modifier" shape: an `XM::Dual` whose
5868/// fenced content is a RELOP/METARELOP Apply with `absent` as the
5869/// first argument (the `prefix_relop_apply` shape produced by
5870/// `relop expression → prefix_relop_apply`).
5871///
5872/// The Dual produced by `fenced` / `annotated_fenced_modifier` has
5873/// shape `Dual(Ref(id), Wrap[OPEN, Apply(op, absent, expr), CLOSE])`
5874/// — the semantic Apply lives inside the **presentation Wrap**,
5875/// referenced by Ref from the content. So we look there for the
5876/// absent-prefixed Apply.
5877///
5878/// Used in `prefix_apply_applyop` and `apply_invisible_times` to
5879/// reject treating `(>0)` / `(\in C)` as a function argument when
5880/// the legitimate parse is `annotated@(x, fenced-modifier)`.
5881fn is_fenced_modifier_dual(arg: &XM) -> bool {
5882  let XM::Dual(ref content, ref presentation, ..) = *arg else {
5883    return false;
5884  };
5885  let has_absent_prefix = |args: &Args| -> bool {
5886    let first = args.trees().first().copied().cloned();
5887    matches!(first,
5888      Some(XM::Token(p, _)) if p.meaning.as_deref() == Some("absent"))
5889  };
5890  // Path A — content is an Apply directly:
5891  if let XM::Apply(_, args, ..) = &**content {
5892    return has_absent_prefix(args);
5893  }
5894  // Path B — content is a Ref; find the Apply in the presentation Wrap.
5895  if let XM::Wrap(items, ..) = &**presentation {
5896    for item in items {
5897      if let XM::Apply(_, args, ..) = item
5898        && has_absent_prefix(args)
5899      {
5900        return true;
5901      }
5902    }
5903  }
5904  false
5905}
5906
5907/// Perl: moreTerms2 trailing-operator → Apply(New('limit-from'), term, addop)
5908/// Perl MathGrammar L720-723: Combine SUPOP tokens (\prime\prime → prime2).
5909/// Left-recursive: `supops supop` accumulates count.
5910pub fn combine_supops(
5911  _rule_id: i32,
5912  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
5913  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
5914  ctxt: ActionContext,
5915) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
5916  let left = args.remove(0).unwrap();
5917  let right = args.remove(0).unwrap();
5918  // Count existing primes: if left is already a combined supops Token, extract count
5919  let (left_count, left_text) = match &left {
5920    XM::Token(props, _) => {
5921      let name = props.name.as_deref().unwrap_or("");
5922      if let Some(n_str) = name.strip_prefix("prime") {
5923        let content_str = props.content.as_deref().unwrap_or("′");
5924        (
5925          n_str.parse::<usize>().unwrap_or(1),
5926          Some(content_str.to_string()),
5927        )
5928      } else {
5929        (1, left.get_value(ctxt.nodes).ok().map(|c| c.into_owned()))
5930      }
5931    },
5932    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => (
5933      1,
5934      lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes)
5935        .ok()
5936        .map(|n| n.get_content()),
5937    ),
5938    _ => (1, None),
5939  };
5940  let right_text = match &right {
5941    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes)
5942      .ok()
5943      .map(|n| n.get_content()),
5944    _ => None,
5945  };
5946  let count = left_count + 1;
5947  let combined_text = match (left_text, right_text) {
5948    (Some(l), Some(r)) => format!("{l}{r}"),
5949    (Some(l), None) => format!("{l}′"),
5950    (None, Some(r)) => format!("′{r}"),
5951    (None, None) => "′′".to_string(),
5952  };
5953  Ok(Some(XM::Token(
5954    XProps {
5955      role: Some(Cow::Borrowed("SUPOP")),
5956      name: Some(Cow::Owned(format!("prime{count}"))),
5957      content: Some(Cow::Owned(combined_text)),
5958      ..XProps::default()
5959    },
5960    Meta::default(),
5961  )))
5962}
5963
5964/// Handles `a+` (limit from above) and similar trailing operators.
5965/// When the expression is an n-ary Apply with the same operator (e.g. a+b+c+),
5966/// only wraps the LAST term in limit-from (matching Perl behavior):
5967///   Apply(+, a, b, c) + → Apply(+, a, b, Apply(limit-from, c, +))
5968pub fn postfix_apply(
5969  _rule_id: i32,
5970  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
5971  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
5972  _: ActionContext,
5973) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
5974  unp!(args => arg, op);
5975  let limit_from = XM::Token(
5976    XProps {
5977      meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("limit-from")),
5978      ..XProps::default()
5979    },
5980    Meta::default(),
5981  );
5982  // Check if arg is an n-ary Apply with the same operator as op
5983  if let (Some(XM::Apply(app_op, app_args, app_props, app_meta)), Some(op_xm)) = (&arg, &op) {
5984    let same_op = match (app_op.0.as_ref(), op_xm) {
5985      // Compare Lexemes: both are lexeme strings like "ADDOP:plus:+"
5986      (XM::Lexeme(a_lex, _), XM::Lexeme(o_lex, _)) => {
5987        // Compare role:meaning prefix (ignoring the actual symbol after last :)
5988        let a_parts: Vec<_> = a_lex.splitn(3, ':').collect();
5989        let o_parts: Vec<_> = o_lex.splitn(3, ':').collect();
5990        a_parts.len() >= 2
5991          && o_parts.len() >= 2
5992          && a_parts[0] == o_parts[0]
5993          && a_parts[1] == o_parts[1]
5994      },
5995      // Compare realized Tokens
5996      (XM::Token(a_props, _), XM::Token(o_props, _)) => {
5997        a_props.meaning == o_props.meaning && a_props.meaning.is_some()
5998      },
5999      _ => false,
6000    };
6001    if same_op && app_args.0.len() >= 2 {
6002      // Wrap only the last argument in limit-from
6003      let mut new_args = app_args.0.clone();
6004      let last_arg = new_args.pop().unwrap();
6005      let wrapped = XM::Apply(
6006        limit_from.into(),
6007        Args(vec![last_arg, op]),
6008        XProps::default(),
6009        Meta::default(),
6010      );
6011      new_args.push(Some(wrapped));
6012      return Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
6013        app_op.clone(),
6014        Args(new_args),
6015        app_props.clone(),
6016        app_meta.clone(),
6017      )));
6018    }
6019  }
6020  // Fallback: wrap the entire expression
6021  Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
6022    limit_from.into(),
6023    Args(vec![arg, op]),
6024    XProps::default(),
6025    Meta::default(),
6026  )))
6027}

6029/// The operand of a POSTFIX application (`n!` → `n`, `(n+1)!` → `(n+1)`): the factor the postfix
6030/// took, which the checks that read a factor see through (57bw).
6031pub(crate) fn postfix_base(xm: &XM) -> Option<&XM> {
6032  match xm {
6033    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..) if operator_category(op) == Some("POSTFIX") => {
6034      match args.as_slice() {
6035        [Some(base)] => Some(base),
6036        _ => None,
6037      }
6038    },
6039    _ => None,
6040  }
6041}
6042
6043/// What a postfix took, under all its scripts and any further postfixes (`n(n-1)!^2` → `n(n-1)`,
6044/// `g(y)!_k^2` → `g(y)`); none when `xm` carries no postfix.
6045pub(crate) fn postfixed_operand(xm: &XM) -> Option<&XM> {
6046  let mut operand = script_nucleus(xm);
6047  let mut postfixed = false;
6048  while let Some(base) = postfix_base(operand) {
6049    operand = script_nucleus(base);
6050    postfixed = true;
6051  }
6052  postfixed.then_some(operand)
6053}
6054
6055/// Perl MathGrammar:419-424 (`addScripts`): a POSTFIX applies to the factor before it, `n!` is
6056/// factorial@(n).
6057pub fn apply_postfix(
6058  _rule_id: i32,
6059  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
6060  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
6061  _: ActionContext,
6062) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
6063  unp!(args => base, op);
6064  Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
6065    op.into(),
6066    Args(vec![base]),
6067    XProps::default(),
6068    Meta::default(),
6069  )))
6070}

6072/// Perl MathGrammar L709-711: TwoPartRelop — combines two adjacent relops.
6073/// E.g. `>=` → "greater-than-or-equals", `<<` → "much-less-than"
6074pub fn two_part_relop_combine(
6075  _rule_id: i32,
6076  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
6077  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
6078  ctxt: ActionContext,
6079) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
6080  unp!(args => op1, op2);
6081  // Extract meanings from the lexeme nodes
6082  let (m1, content1) = if let Some(XM::Lexeme(ref lex, _)) = op1 {
6083    let node = lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes)?;
6084    let m = node.get_attribute("meaning").unwrap_or_default();
6085    let c = node.get_content();
6086    (m, c)
6087  } else {
6088    (String::new(), String::new())
6089  };
6090  let (m2, content2) = if let Some(XM::Lexeme(ref lex, _)) = op2 {
6091    let node = lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes)?;
6092    let m = node.get_attribute("meaning").unwrap_or_default();
6093    let c = node.get_content();
6094    (m, c)
6095  } else {
6096    (String::new(), String::new())
6097  };
6098  // Perl: TwoPartRelop logic
6099  let meaning = if m1 == m2 {
6100    format!("much-{m1}")
6101  } else {
6102    format!("{m1}-or-{m2}")
6103  };
6104  let content = format!("{content1}{content2}");
6105  Ok(Some(XM::Token(
6106    XProps {
6107      role: Some(Cow::Borrowed("RELOP")),
6108      meaning: Some(Cow::Owned(meaning)),
6109      content: Some(Cow::Owned(content)),
6110      ..XProps::default()
6111    },
6112    Meta::default(),
6113  )))
6114}

6116/// Perl `absExpression : <rulevar: local $forbidEvalAt = 1>` (MathGrammar:410; the evalAt
6117/// alternatives of `moreFactors` test it, :259-262): no evaluation bar is read inside a `|…|`
6118/// pair. `|\nabla a|_L|\nabla b|_L` is |∇a|_L·|∇b|_L, not an evaluation bar closing over both
6119/// (2605.12082, 2605.04766; repro math-parse/evaluated_at_stays_outside_absolute_bars).
6120/// Divergence #350 (OXIDIZED_DESIGN_DIVERGENCES): only single-bar pairs (`|…|`, `||…||`) — the
6121/// ones a bar can be misread in — and not within a nested group; Perl forbids it in `\|…\|`,
6122/// `\left|…\right|` and every nested group too, leaving `\|u|_{\Gamma}\|`, `|g(f|_{x=0})|`
6123/// unparsed (2605.01526, 2605.04708, 2605.07463). And a preference, not a prune: the reading with the
6124/// fewest marked fences wins (`XM::prefer_fewest_evaluation_bars_inside`), so a pair whose every
6125/// reading nests one keeps it — `|f(x)|_{0}^{1}|`, `\Big|\partial_a^k(\ldots)\Big|_{a=a_m}\Big|`, which
6126/// Perl leaves unparsed.
6127fn holds_evaluation_bar(xm: &XM) -> bool { holds_bar_reading(xm, &["evaluated-at"]) }
6128
6129/// A `\left|` read as a divider or a ket's opening bar (`divider_bar`, `ket_bar`) whose next item
6130/// evaluates at a stretchy bar: TeX paired that `\left|` with the `\right|` the item evaluates at
6131/// (`\left(\epsilon\left|\nabla u\right|_{L^2}\right)`), so the reading is refuted. Only
6132/// `prefer_fewer_conditionals` had hidden it, and not beside another conditional (57ap review; 46
6133/// formulas of 2605 put a factor and `\left|…\right|_` in a fence). In parentheses and brackets Perl
6134/// reads the pair too, trying `Factor` before `evalAtOp` (MathGrammar:257-263); in braces it tries
6135/// the set-builder bar first (`scriptFactorOpen`, :486-491) and reads a conditional set — Rust keeps
6136/// TeX's pairing there (divergence #358). A plain `|` evaluation bar is TeX's to pair with no
6137/// `\left|`, so `\left\{x\left|f|_{x=0}>0\right.\right\}` divides, as Perl. (An evaluation bar inside a
6138/// nested group, `\left|(f\right|_{x=0})`, is not seen — groups that cross each other.)
6139fn left_bar_pairs_an_evaluation_bar(bar: &XM, next: &XM) -> bool {
6140  matches!(bar, XM::Lexeme(lex, _) if lex.starts_with("LEFT_STRETCHY_VERTBAR:"))
6141    && holds_stretchy_evaluation_bar(next)
6142}
6143
6144/// Does `xm` evaluate at a stretchy bar — a `\right|`, the bar TeX pairs with a `\left|` — outside a
6145/// nested group? `eval_at` presents `base|_{sub}` as a script application on `[base, bar]`.
6146fn holds_stretchy_evaluation_bar(xm: &XM) -> bool {
6147  match xm {
6148    XM::Dual(content, presentation, ..)
6149      if matches!(&**content, XM::Apply(Operator(op), ..)
6150        if matches!(&**op, XM::Token(props, _) if props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("evaluated-at"))) =>
6151    {
6152      evaluation_bar_is_stretchy(presentation)
6153    },
6154    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) => {
6155      holds_stretchy_evaluation_bar(op)
6156        || args.0.iter().flatten().any(holds_stretchy_evaluation_bar)
6157    },
6158    // A nested group — a fence, a delimited argument — pairs its own bars.
6159    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) if matches!(**presentation, XM::Wrap(..)) => false,
6160    XM::Dual(content, presentation, ..) => {
6161      holds_stretchy_evaluation_bar(content) || holds_stretchy_evaluation_bar(presentation)
6162    },
6163    _ => false,
6164  }
6165}
6166
6167/// The bar of an `eval_at` presentation — the last of the scripted `[base, bar]` wrap, under a
6168/// superscript and a subscript application — is stretchy.
6169fn evaluation_bar_is_stretchy(presentation: &XM) -> bool {
6170  match presentation {
6171    XM::Apply(_, args, ..) => args
6172      .0
6173      .first()
6174      .and_then(Option::as_ref)
6175      .is_some_and(|scripted| match scripted {
6176        XM::Wrap(items, ..) => items.last().is_some_and(
6177          |bar| matches!(bar, XM::Token(props, _) if props.stretchy.as_deref() == Some("true")),
6178        ),
6179        inner => evaluation_bar_is_stretchy(inner),
6180      }),
6181    _ => false,
6182  }
6183}
6184
6185/// Does `xm` hold a pair of bars read as a fence — an absolute value, a norm, or any group a bar
6186/// opens (`\mid f|`, `delimited-∣|`)? Its presentation opens with a bar.
6187pub(crate) fn holds_bar_pair(xm: &XM) -> bool {
6188  match xm {
6189    XM::Dual(content, presentation, _, meta) => {
6190      let opened_by_a_bar = match &**presentation {
6191        XM::Wrap(items, ..) => items.first().is_some_and(is_a_bar),
6192        _ => false,
6193      };
6194      meta.bar_fence || opened_by_a_bar || holds_bar_pair(content) || holds_bar_pair(presentation)
6195    },
6196    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) => {
6197      holds_bar_pair(op) || args.0.iter().flatten().any(holds_bar_pair)
6198    },
6199    XM::Wrap(items, ..) => items.iter().any(holds_bar_pair),
6200    _ => false,
6201  }
6202}
6203
6204/// Is `xm` a bar token: `|`, `\mid`, a stretchy bar?
6205fn is_a_bar(xm: &XM) -> bool {
6206  matches!(
6207    operator_category(xm),
6208    Some("VERTBAR" | "LEFT_STRETCHY_VERTBAR" | "MIDDLE")
6209  )
6210}
6211
6212/// Does `xm`'s presentation open with a bar — its leftmost token, reached through the first
6213/// operand of an infix, relation or script application?
6214pub(crate) fn opens_with_a_bar(xm: &XM) -> bool {
6215  match xm {
6216    XM::Dual(_, presentation, _, meta) => meta.bar_fence || opens_with_a_bar(presentation),
6217    XM::Wrap(items, ..) => items.first().is_some_and(opens_with_a_bar),
6218    XM::Apply(_, args, ..) if args.0.len() >= 2 => args
6219      .0
6220      .first()
6221      .and_then(Option::as_ref)
6222      .is_some_and(opens_with_a_bar),
6223    XM::Token(..) | XM::Lexeme(..) => is_a_bar(xm),
6224    _ => false,
6225  }
6226}
6227
6228/// Does `xm` read one of its bars as an operator of `meanings` — an evaluation bar, a conditional —
6229/// outside a nested group, which pairs its own bars?
6230fn holds_bar_reading(xm: &XM, meanings: &[&str]) -> bool {
6231  match xm {
6232    XM::Token(props, _) | XM::Ref(props) => props
6233      .meaning
6234      .as_deref()
6235      .is_some_and(|m| meanings.contains(&m)),
6236    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) => {
6237      holds_bar_reading(op, meanings)
6238        || args
6239          .0
6240          .iter()
6241          .flatten()
6242          .any(|a| holds_bar_reading(a, meanings))
6243    },
6244    // A nested group — a fence, a delimited argument — pairs its own bars.
6245    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) if matches!(**presentation, XM::Wrap(..)) => false,
6246    XM::Dual(content, presentation, ..) => {
6247      holds_bar_reading(content, meanings) || holds_bar_reading(presentation, meanings)
6248    },
6249    _ => false,
6250  }
6251}
6252
6253/// The Dirac meaning of `xm` — a bra, ket, inner product or operator product (`qm_fenced`).
6254fn dirac_meaning(xm: &XM) -> Option<&str> {
6255  let XM::Dual(content, ..) = xm else {
6256    return None;
6257  };
6258  let XM::Apply(Operator(op), ..) = &**content else {
6259    return None;
6260  };
6261  let XM::Token(props, _) = op.as_ref() else {
6262    return None;
6263  };
6264  props.meaning.as_deref().filter(|m| {
6265    matches!(
6266      *m,
6267      "bra" | "ket" | "inner-product" | "quantum-operator-product"
6268    )
6269  })
6270}
6271
6272/// Does `xm` hold a ket outside a nested group (a fence, a Dirac bracket, pairs its own)?
6273fn holds_ket(xm: &XM) -> bool {
6274  if let Some(meaning) = dirac_meaning(xm) {
6275    return meaning == "ket";
6276  }
6277  match xm {
6278    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) => holds_ket(op) || args.0.iter().flatten().any(holds_ket),
6279    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) if matches!(**presentation, XM::Wrap(..)) => false,
6280    XM::Dual(content, ..) => holds_ket(content),
6281    _ => false,
6282  }
6283}
6284
6285/// Does `xm` hold an open bra outside a nested group: a factor ending in a bra that the next factor
6286/// does not close — a factor not opening with a bar? Perl's `maybeBra` reads a braket before a bra
6287/// (`ketExpression maybeBraket`, MathGrammar:373-379), so such a bra would have been a bracket's; a
6288/// bra before a bar, an operator's end or its group's end stays one (`|c\langle u|\rangle`
6289/// ket@(c·bra@(u)), `\langle|a\rangle\langle a|+|b\rangle\langle b|\rangle`).
6290fn holds_open_bra(xm: &XM) -> bool {
6291  if dirac_meaning(xm).is_some() {
6292    return false;
6293  }
6294  match xm {
6295    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..) => {
6296      let factors: Vec<&XM> = args.iter().flatten().collect();
6297      (is_product_operator(op)
6298        && factors
6299          .windows(2)
6300          .any(|pair| ends_with_bra(pair[0]) && !opens_with_a_bar(pair[1])))
6301        || holds_open_bra(op)
6302        || factors.into_iter().any(holds_open_bra)
6303    },
6304    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) if matches!(**presentation, XM::Wrap(..)) => false,
6305    XM::Dual(content, ..) => holds_open_bra(content),
6306    _ => false,
6307  }
6308}
6309
6310/// Does `xm` end with a bra — its last factor, or the base of its last scripted item?
6311fn ends_with_bra(xm: &XM) -> bool {
6312  if dirac_meaning(xm) == Some("bra") {
6313    return true;
6314  }
6315  if let Some(base) = script_base(xm) {
6316    return ends_with_bra(base);
6317  }
6318  match xm {
6319    XM::Apply(_, args, ..) => args
6320      .0
6321      .last()
6322      .and_then(Option::as_ref)
6323      .is_some_and(ends_with_bra),
6324    _ => false,
6325  }
6326}
6327
6328thread_local! {
6329  /// Perl `$LaTeXML::MathParser::MAX_ABS_DEPTH` (MathParser.pm:814): how deep bar fences may nest
6330  /// in the parse under way — 1, then 2 and 3 on the retries of `MathParser::parse_lexemes`.
6331  static MAX_ABS_DEPTH: Cell<u8> = const { Cell::new(1) };
6332  /// Perl `SawNotation('AbsFail')` (MathGrammar:412): a bar fence nested deeper than allowed.
6333  static ABS_FAIL: Cell<bool> = const { Cell::new(false) };
6334}
6335
6336/// Set how deep bar fences may nest (Perl `MAX_ABS_DEPTH`), clearing `AbsFail`; the previous limit.
6337pub(crate) fn set_max_abs_depth(depth: u8) -> u8 {
6338  ABS_FAIL.with(|fail| fail.set(false));
6339  MAX_ABS_DEPTH.with(|max| max.replace(depth))
6340}
6341
6342/// Did a bar fence nest deeper than allowed since the limit was set (Perl `AbsFail`)?
6343pub(crate) fn abs_fail() -> bool { ABS_FAIL.with(Cell::get) }
6344
6345/// The depth of the bar fences `xm` holds, Perl's `absExpression` nesting (MathGrammar:410-412): a
6346/// bar fence's own (`Meta::abs_depth`), through groups and applications — not a script's, whose
6347/// `Subscript`/`Superscript` start the count over (:84-89).
6348fn abs_depth_within(xm: &XM) -> u8 {
6349  match xm {
6350    XM::Dual(.., meta) if meta.bar_fence => meta.abs_depth,
6351    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) => abs_depth_within(presentation),
6352    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..)
6353      if operator_category(op).is_some_and(|c| c.ends_with("SCRIPTOP")) =>
6354    {
6355      args
6356        .0
6357        .first()
6358        .and_then(Option::as_ref)
6359        .map_or(0, abs_depth_within)
6360    },
6361    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) => args
6362      .0
6363      .iter()
6364      .flatten()
6365      .map(abs_depth_within)
6366      .fold(abs_depth_within(op), u8::max),
6367    XM::Wrap(items, ..) | XM::Arg(items) | XM::Choices(items) => {
6368      items.iter().map(abs_depth_within).max().unwrap_or(0)
6369    },
6370    XM::Token(..) | XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Ref(_) => 0,
6371  }
6372}
6373
6374/// Mark an absolute value or norm (`Meta::bar_fence`): one between two single `|`
6375/// (`Meta::single_bar_pair`), one whose single-bar content holds an evaluation bar
6376/// (`Meta::evaluation_bar_inside`, see [`holds_evaluation_bar`]). Perl's `absExpression`
6377/// (MathGrammar:410-412) nests no deeper than `MAX_ABS_DEPTH`, so a deeper fence fails the
6378/// reading, noting `AbsFail` for the retry (MathParser.pm:831-836): the bars of `\log|a|+\log|b|`
6379/// are two absolute values, not one around `a·|+\log|·b` (repro
6380/// math-parse/bar_pairs_nest_as_shallow_as_they_can).
6381fn mark_bar_fence(
6382  mut fence: XM,
6383  single_bar_pair: bool,
6384  evaluation_bar_inside: bool,
6385) -> Result<XM, Box<dyn Error>> {
6386  if let XM::Dual(_, presentation, _, meta) = &mut fence {
6387    let depth = abs_depth_within(presentation).saturating_add(1);
6388    if depth > MAX_ABS_DEPTH.with(Cell::get) {
6389      ABS_FAIL.with(|fail| fail.set(true));
6390      return Err("bar fence: nested deeper than MAX_ABS_DEPTH (Perl AbsFail)".into());
6391    }
6392    meta.bar_fence = true;
6393    meta.single_bar_pair = single_bar_pair;
6394    meta.evaluation_bar_inside = evaluation_bar_inside;
6395    meta.abs_depth = depth;
6396  }
6397  Ok(fence)
6398}
6399
6400/// Is `xm` an absolute value between two single `|` (`Meta::single_bar_pair`)?
6401fn is_single_bar_pair(xm: &XM) -> bool { matches!(xm, XM::Dual(.., meta) if meta.single_bar_pair) }
6402
6403pub fn fenced(
6404  rule_id: i32,
6405  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
6406  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
6407  ctxt: ActionContext,
6408) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
6409  unp!(args => open_opt, arg_opt, close_opt);
6410  let mut arg = arg_opt.unwrap();
6411  let open = open_opt.unwrap();
6412  let close = close_opt.unwrap();
6413  // let xmrefs = create_xmrefs(&[&arg], ctxt)?.remove(0);
6414  // Ok(Some(
6415  //   XM::Dual(Box::new(xmrefs), Box::new(
6416  //     XM::Wrap(vec![open_opt.unwrap(),arg,close_opt.unwrap()], XProps::default(),
6417  // Meta::default())   ), XProps::default(), Meta::default())
6418  // ))
6419  let o = realized_value(&open, &ctxt)?;
6420  let c = realized_value(&close, &ctxt)?;
6421  let op_name = format!("delimited-{}{}", o, c);
6422  // An angle fence holds no open bra: Perl reads a `\langle` label before a bar as a braket first
6423  // (`maybeBra`: `ketExpression maybeBraket`, MathGrammar:373-379), so `\langle Hx|x\rangle=\langle
6424  // x|Hx\rangle` and `\langle Ax|y\rangle\langle x|Ay\rangle` are inner products, never one fence
6425  // whose inner `\langle` opens a bra (57bp; 2605.30176, 2605.16417). A bra ending a factor stays, as
6426  // Perl's list fence `\big\langle Tx_i,|\zeta_k\rangle\langle\zeta_j|\big\rangle` (2605.21982).
6427  if matches!(
6428    (o.as_ref(), c.as_ref()),
6429    ("\u{27E8}", "\u{27E9}") | ("langle", "rangle")
6430  ) && holds_open_bra(&arg)
6431  {
6432    return Err("fenced: an angle fence holds no open bra".into());
6433  }
6434  // Perl's grammar (MathGrammar:462-475) fences a bracket or brace list two ways: a list of
6435  // expressions is `Fence`'s many items, named by its tables (`fence`); a list holding a relation is
6436  // one `Formulae` item (:69), fenced as one — `\{x=1;y=2\}` set@(formulae@(…)), `[x=1,y=2]`
6437  // delimited-[]@(formulae@(…)), never an interval of equations.
6438  if matches!((o.as_ref(), c.as_ref()), ("[", "]") | ("{", "}")) {
6439    match fenced_list(&arg) {
6440      Some(FencedList::Expressions) => {
6441        let stuff = fenced_list_items(open, arg, close).into_iter().map(Some);
6442        return fence(rule_id, stuff.collect(), pragmas, ctxt);
6443      },
6444      Some(FencedList::Formulae) => arg = as_formulae(arg),
6445      None => {},
6446    }
6447  }
6448
6449  // TODO: For now assume a single argument in arg; specialize in other functions such as
6450  // "open_interval",       for the other cases from the classic MathParser.pm
6451  if op_name == "delimited-()" {
6452    // A paren list holding a relation is one `Formulae` item too, `(a<1,b<2)` formulae@(a < 1, b < 2)
6453    // (Perl `OPEN Formulae CLOSE`, MathGrammar:69, parens around one item transparent, MathParser.pm:
6454    // 1412-1415; a bracket, brace or conditional list since 57au/57bh; was `vector@(…)`, 57bk,
6455    // 2605.00042, 2605.01907, 2605.00130). A function still takes its items (`fenced_tuple_items`).
6456    let relation_list = matches!(fenced_list(&arg), Some(FencedList::Formulae));
6457    if relation_list {
6458      arg = as_formulae(arg);
6459    }
6460    // Check if arg is a multi-item list (XM::Dual from list_apply/formulae_apply).
6461    // If so, use interpret_delimited for per-item XMRefs (matching Perl's NewFenced).
6462    // A bare list only: its presentation `[item, separator, item, …]`. A list already fenced —
6463    // `\left([a;b]\right)`, a bracket list since 57au one Dual whose presentation carries its own
6464    // delimiters — is one item, and parens around one item are transparent (Perl `Fence`,
6465    // MathParser.pm:1412-1415); reading its presentation's even places took the delimiters and
6466    // separators for the items (`vector@([, ;, ])`, 118 formulas of the 57av train A/B; 2605.08815
6467    // S2.E4, 2605.00444, 2605.00423).
6468    let is_multi_item = !relation_list
6469      && match &arg {
6470        XM::Dual(content, presentation, ..) => matches!(&**content, XM::Apply(op_box, args, ..)
6471        if args.0.len() >= 2 && matches!(&*op_box.0,
6472          XM::Token(p, _) if matches!(p.meaning.as_deref(),
6473            Some("vector") | Some("list") | Some("formulae")))
6474          && presents_its_items_alone(presentation, args.0.len())),
6475        XM::Apply(op_box, args, ..) => {
6476          args.0.len() >= 2
6477            && matches!(&*op_box.0,
6478        XM::Token(p, _) if matches!(p.meaning.as_deref(),
6479          Some("vector") | Some("list") | Some("formulae")))
6480        },
6481        _ => false,
6482      };
6483    if is_multi_item {
6484      // Perl `Fence` (MathParser.pm:1390-1417) names a fenced list by its delimiters and its FIRST
6485      // separator: the enclose tables (:1368-1377) hold comma lists only, so parens around a `;`
6486      // list make a `list` (`p(x;\theta)` Perl `p * list@(x, theta)`, `(a,b;c)` a `vector`), and
6487      // the presentation keeps the separators as written — rebuilding it with commas of our own
6488      // rendered `p(x;\theta)` as `p(x,θ)` (2605.00042 `J(H;\alpha)`, 2605.00130 `I(X;F')`; 57ay
6489      // review). Two items with a comma stay a `vector` here: the `interval` action offers the
6490      // open interval.
6491      let (inner, comma_list) = match arg {
6492        // A bare list Dual (`presents_its_items_alone`): its presentation is the items with their
6493        // separators between.
6494        XM::Dual(_, pres, ..) => {
6495          let XM::Wrap(wrap_items, ..) = *pres else {
6496            unreachable!("is_multi_item: a bare list presents its items in a Wrap")
6497          };
6498          let first_separator = realized_value(&wrap_items[1], &ctxt)?;
6499          let comma_list = first_separator == ",";
6500          (wrap_items, comma_list)
6501        },
6502        // A bare Apply carries no separators of its own: comma-joined. No producer of a Dual-less
6503        // list is known (57ba review); kept as the fallback the shape check admits.
6504        XM::Apply(_, args_inner, ..) => {
6505          let comma = XM::Token(
6506            XProps {
6507              role: Some(Cow::Borrowed("PUNCT")),
6508              content: Some(Cow::Borrowed(",")),
6509              ..XProps::default()
6510            },
6511            Meta::default(),
6512          );
6513          let mut inner = Vec::new();
6514          for (i, item) in args_inner.0.into_iter().flatten().enumerate() {
6515            if i > 0 {
6516              inner.push(comma.clone());
6517            }
6518            inner.push(item);
6519          }
6520          (inner, true)
6521        },
6522        _ => unreachable!(),
6523      };
6524      let op = XProps {
6525        meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed(if comma_list { "vector" } else { "list" })),
6526        ..XProps::default()
6527      };
6528      let mut stuff = vec![open];
6529      stuff.extend(inner);
6530      stuff.push(close);
6531      interpret_delimited(op.into(), stuff, ctxt).map(Some)
6532    } else {
6533      // Single arg: XMDual(XMRef(arg), XMWrap((,arg,)))
6534      // create_xmrefs skips ephemeral variants (XMHint, and the default
6535      // skip-without-warning arm), so refs may come back empty when the
6536      // delimited body was just a spacing hint. In that case the Dual
6537      // with an XMRef to nothing would be meaningless, so fall back to
6538      // a bare Wrap (arxiv hep-ph/9210235 hit this on `\lparen \,
6539      // \rparen` where the sole arg was an XMHint that got filtered).
6540      let mut arg_xmrefs = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut arg], ctxt)?;
6541      if arg_xmrefs.is_empty() {
6542        return Ok(Some(XM::Wrap(
6543          vec![open, arg, close],
6544          XProps::default(),
6545          Meta::default(),
6546        )));
6547      }
6548      Ok(Some(XM::Dual(
6549        Box::new(arg_xmrefs.remove(0)),
6550        Box::new(XM::Wrap(
6551          vec![open, arg, close],
6552          XProps::default(),
6553          Meta::default(),
6554        )),
6555        XProps::default(),
6556        Meta::default(),
6557      )))
6558    }
6559  } else if op_name == "delimited-{}" {
6560    // Perl enclose1: {expr} => set
6561    let op = XProps {
6562      meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("set")),
6563      ..XProps::default()
6564    };
6565    interpret_delimited(op.into(), vec![open, arg, close], ctxt).map(Some)
6566  } else if op_name == "delimited-||" {
6567    // Single bars only; `\left|…\right|` pairs are the lexer's (divergence #350).
6568    let single_bar_pair = operator_category(&open) == Some("VERTBAR");
6569    // Bars, not `\lvert…\rvert` (an OPEN/CLOSE pair, a group as in Perl).
6570    let bar_fence = matches!(
6571      operator_category(&open),
6572      Some("VERTBAR" | "LEFT_STRETCHY_VERTBAR")
6573    );
6574    let evaluation_bar_inside = single_bar_pair && holds_evaluation_bar(&arg);
6575    // Four single bars around `x` are a norm (`norm_fenced`), never |(|x|)|: Perl tries
6576    // `SINGLEVERTBAR SINGLEVERTBAR absExpression …` (MathGrammar:294) before `VERTBAR absExpression
6577    // VERTBAR` (:299) — `\log||x||_2^2` (57am review round 5).
6578    if single_bar_pair && is_single_bar_pair(&arg) {
6579      return Err("fenced: four single bars are a norm, not nested absolute values".into());
6580    }
6581    // A pair of single bars holds no ket: Perl reads each `|…\rangle` as a ket before it can close an
6582    // absolute value (its ordered alternatives, MathGrammar:298-303), so `|a\rangle\langle
6583    // a||b\rangle\langle b|` is a product of projectors, never an absolute value around
