6584    // `|b\rangle\langle b|` (57bp review; `absExpression` itself only forbids evaluation bars, :410).
6585    if single_bar_pair && holds_ket(&arg) {
6586      return Err("fenced: an absolute value holds no ket".into());
6587    }
6588    // Absolute-value `|x|`. The kerned-stack `\left|\left|x\right|\right|`
6589    // (double-bar norm) and triple variant are now recognized at the
6590    // grammar level via stretchy_(norm|triple_norm)_fenced (task #263),
6591    // so we no longer need a post-hoc tree-inspecting promotion here.
6592    let op = XProps {
6593      meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("absolute-value")),
6594      ..XProps::default()
6595    };
6596    let open_m = morph_vertbar(open, "OPEN", ctxt.nodes);
6597    let close_m = morph_vertbar(close, "CLOSE", ctxt.nodes);
6598    let fence = interpret_delimited(op.into(), vec![open_m, arg, close_m], ctxt)?;
6599    Ok(Some(if bar_fence {
6600      mark_bar_fence(fence, single_bar_pair, evaluation_bar_inside)?
6601    } else {
6602      fence
6603    }))
6604  } else {
6605    // A `\left\|…\right\|` pair is bars, as in Perl (the lexer's stretchy bars; `\lVert…\rVert`
6606    // is an OPEN/CLOSE group).
6607    let bar_fence = operator_category(&open) == Some("LEFT_STRETCHY_VERTBAR");
6608    let mark = |fence: XM| {
6609      if bar_fence {
6610        mark_bar_fence(fence, false, false)
6611      } else {
6612        Ok(fence)
6613      }
6614    };
6615    // Check for known delimiter meanings
6616    let meaning = match (o.as_ref(), c.as_ref()) {
6617      ("\u{230A}", "\u{230B}") => Some("floor"),   // ⌊ ⌋
6618      ("\u{2308}", "\u{2309}") => Some("ceiling"), // ⌈ ⌉
6619      ("\u{2016}", "\u{2016}") => Some("norm"),    // ‖ ‖
6620      ("lfloor", "rfloor") => Some("floor"),       // name-based match
6621      ("lceil", "rceil") => Some("ceiling"),       // name-based match
6622      _ => None,
6623    };
6624    if let Some(m) = meaning {
6625      let op = XProps {
6626        meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed(m)),
6627        ..XProps::default()
6628      };
6629      mark(interpret_delimited(
6630        op.into(),
6631        vec![open, arg, close],
6632        ctxt,
6633      )?)
6634      .map(Some)
6635    } else {
6636      let op = xnew(op_name);
6637      mark(interpret_delimited(
6638        op.into(),
6639        vec![open, arg, close],
6640        ctxt,
6641      )?)
6642      .map(Some)
6643    }
6644  }
6645}
6646
6647/// What a bracket or brace pair encloses, when it is a list of two or more items: a `list`/`formulae`
6648/// Dual whose presentation is `[item, separator, item, …]`.
6649enum FencedList {
6650  /// Every item an expression: Perl's `Fence` over the items (`OPEN Expression (punct
6651  /// Expression)+ CLOSE`, MathGrammar:462, 472-475).
6652  Expressions,
6653  /// An item is a relation: one `Formulae` item (`OPEN Formulae CLOSE`, MathGrammar:69).
6654  Formulae,
6655}
6656
6657fn fenced_list(arg: &XM) -> Option<FencedList> {
6658  let XM::Dual(content, presentation, ..) = arg else {
6659    return None;
6660  };
6661  let XM::Apply(op, args, ..) = &**content else {
6662    return None;
6663  };
6664  let XM::Token(props, _) = &*op.0 else {
6665    return None;
6666  };
6667  let XM::Wrap(items, ..) = &**presentation else {
6668    return None;
6669  };
6670  let meaning = props.meaning.as_deref();
6671  if !matches!(meaning, Some("list" | "formulae"))
6672    || args.0.len() < 2
6673    || !presents_its_items_alone(presentation, args.0.len())
6674  {
6675    return None;
6676  }
6677  Some(
6678    if meaning == Some("formulae") || items.iter().step_by(2).any(is_relational_item) {
6679      FencedList::Formulae
6680    } else {
6681      FencedList::Expressions
6682    },
6683  )
6684}
6685
6686/// `[open, items and separators as written, close]` from a list `fenced_list` admitted.
6687fn fenced_list_items(open: XM, arg: XM, close: XM) -> Vec<XM> {
6688  let XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) = arg else {
6689    unreachable!("fenced_list admits only a Dual");
6690  };
6691  let XM::Wrap(items, ..) = *presentation else {
6692    unreachable!("fenced_list admits only a Wrap presentation");
6693  };
6694  let mut stuff = Vec::with_capacity(items.len() + 2);
6695  stuff.push(open);
6696  stuff.extend(items);
6697  stuff.push(close);
6698  stuff
6699}
6700
6701/// A fenced list holding a relation, as Perl's `NewFormulae` names it: `formulae`, which
6702/// `rename_fenced_lists` leaves alone.
6703fn as_formulae(mut arg: XM) -> XM {
6704  if let XM::Dual(ref mut content, ..) = arg
6705    && let XM::Apply(ref mut op, ..) = **content
6706    && let XM::Token(ref mut props, _) = *op.0
6707  {
6708    props.meaning = Some(Cow::Borrowed("formulae"));
6709  }
6710  arg
6711}
6712
6713// Empty fenced expression: OPEN CLOSE with no content => list()
6714// Perl: Apply(List, []) wrapped in XMDual with XMWrap(OPEN, CLOSE)
6715pub fn empty_fenced(
6716  _rule_id: i32,
6717  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
6718  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
6719  _ctxt: ActionContext,
6720) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
6721  unp!(args => open_opt, close_opt);
6722  let open = open_opt.unwrap();
6723  let close = close_opt.unwrap();
6724  let list_op = XProps {
6725    meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("list")),
6726    ..XProps::default()
6727  };
6728  // Build: Dual(Apply(list), Wrap(open, close))
6729  Ok(Some(XM::Dual(
6730    Box::new(XM::Apply(
6731      list_op.into(),
6732      vec![].into(),
6733      XProps::default(),
6734      Meta::default(),
6735    )),
6736    Box::new(XM::Wrap(
6737      vec![open, close],
6738      XProps::default(),
6739      Meta::default(),
6740    )),
6741    XProps::default(),
6742    Meta::default(),
6743  )))
6744}
6745
6746/// Perl `%balanced` (MathParser.pm:1348-1356): the close each open delimiter
6747/// balances.
6748fn balanced_close(open: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
6749  Some(match open {
6750    "(" => ")",
6751    "[" => "]",
6752    "{" => "}",
6753    "|" => "|",
6754    "||" => "||",
6755    "\u{2016}" => "\u{2016}",
6756    "\u{2980}" => "\u{2980}",
6757    "\u{230A}" => "\u{230B}", // lfloor, rfloor
6758    "\u{2308}" => "\u{2309}", // lceil, rceil
6759    "\u{2329}" => "\u{232A}", // angle brackets (deprecated code points)
6760    "\u{27E8}" => "\u{27E9}", // angle brackets
6761    "\u{2225}" => "\u{2225}", // lVert, rVert
6762    _ => return None,
6763  })
6764}
6765
6766/// Perl `p_getValue(realizeXMNode($x))` (MathParser.pm:135-150, 1070-1078): a lexeme's value
6767/// read through the node it names when it is an `XMRef`, as a gathered/split row's content
6768/// branch holds them (arXiv 2605.00284 split `u(t,x)`, 2605.01361 `\{i\mid…\}`).
6769fn realized_value<'a>(xm: &'a XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> Result<Cow<'a, str>, Box<dyn Error>> {
6770  match xm {
6771    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => {
6772      let node = lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes)?;
6773      Ok(Cow::Owned(p_get_value(&realize_xmnode(
6774        node,
6775        ctxt.document,
6776      ))))
6777    },
6778    other => other.get_value(ctxt.nodes),
6779  }
6780}
6781
6782/// Perl `isMatchingClose` (MathParser.pm:1379-1384): the close's value is the
6783/// one the open's value balances, each read through `realizeXMNode`, so a
6784/// delimiter that is an `XMRef` answers with the value of the node it names.
6785fn is_matching_close(open: &XM, close: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
6786  let (Ok(open), Ok(close)) = (realized_value(open, ctxt), realized_value(close, ctxt)) else {
6787    return false;
6788  };
6789  balanced_close(&open).is_some_and(|expect| expect == close)
6790}
6791
6792/// An empty fence from GENERIC open and close delimiters: only when the close
6793/// balances the open (Perl MathGrammar:463-464 `balancedClose`, :729). Any other
6794/// pair fails the parse, as in Perl, which leaves the formula unparsed with its
6795/// content kept. `\mathopen{}\mathclose{\left(x\right)}` lexes as an empty OPEN
6796/// and a CLOSE that CARRIES the `x`; building `list@()` from them dropped the
6797/// `x` from the content tree (arXiv 2605.13448, 2605.22010, 2605.21750;
6798/// guard `perfect_kernel_batch56::empty_fence_needs_a_balanced_close`).
6799pub fn balanced_empty_fenced(
6800  rule_id: i32,
6801  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
6802  prag: &[ValidationPragmatics],
6803  ctxt: ActionContext,
6804) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
6805  if let (Some(Some(open)), Some(Some(close))) = (args.first(), args.get(1))
6806    && !is_matching_close(open, close, &ctxt)
6807  {
6808    return Err("empty fence: the close does not balance the open (Perl balancedClose)".into());
6809  }
6810  empty_fenced(rule_id, args, prag, ctxt)
6811}
6812
6813// similar to fenced but the operator is a kind of tuple or interval, such as "open-interval"
6814// and the arguments are delimited with a comma
6815pub fn interval(
6816  _rule_id: i32,
6817  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
6818  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
6819  ctxt: ActionContext,
6820) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
6821  unp!(args => open_opt, arg1_opt, sep_opt, arg2_opt, close_opt);
6822  let open = open_opt.unwrap();
6823  let mut arg1 = arg1_opt.unwrap();
6824  let sep = sep_opt.unwrap();
6825  let mut arg2 = arg2_opt.unwrap();
6826  let close = close_opt.unwrap();
6827
6828  // Extract text values from lexemes (like fenced does)
6829  let o = realized_value(&open, &ctxt)?;
6830  let c = realized_value(&close, &ctxt)?;
6831  // Perl's `%enclose2` (MathParser.pm:1368-1373) is keyed by the delimiters AND the separator, and
6832  // names comma pairs only; any other pair falls to `list` (`Fence`, :1405-1409): `(a;b)`, `[a;b]`,
6833  // `(a;b]` — `[\mathbf{a};\mathbf{b}]` read `closed-interval` (2605.00423), `K_t=[K_{t-1};k_t]`
6834  // (2605.00435; 57ay review).
6835  // A reversed pair is the French open interval, written with `;` as often as with `,` (divergence
6836  // #362): `]0;1[` stays `open-interval`, which Perl cannot parse at all.
6837  let reversed = (o.as_ref(), c.as_ref()) == ("]", "[");
6838  let op_meaning = if realized_value(&sep, &ctxt)? != "," && !reversed {
6839    "list"
6840  } else {
6841    match (o.as_ref(), c.as_ref()) {
6842      ("(", ")") | ("]", "[") => "open-interval",
6843      ("[", "]") => "closed-interval",
6844      ("[", ")") => "closed-open-interval",
6845      ("(", "]") => "open-closed-interval",
6846      ("⟨", "⟩") => "list", // angle brackets: ⟨a,b⟩ → list, not tuple
6847      _ => "tuple",
6848    }
6849  };
6850
6851  // Create operator as XM::Token with meaning attribute
6852  let op: XM = XProps {
6853    meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed(op_meaning)),
6854    ..XProps::default()
6855  }
6856  .into();
6857
6858  let ref_args = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut arg1, &mut arg2], ctxt)?;
6859  // Marked here, where the delimiters' values are known (see `is_unbalanced_fence`).
6860  let mut meta = Meta::default();
6861  meta.unbalanced_fence = balanced_close(&o) != Some(c.as_ref());
6862
6863  Ok(Some(XM::Dual(
6864    Box::new(XM::Apply(
6865      op.into(),
6866      ref_args.into(),
6867      XProps::default(),
6868      Meta::default(),
6869    )),
6870    Box::new(XM::Wrap(
6871      vec![open, arg1, sep, arg2, close],
6872      XProps::default(),
6873      Meta::default(),
6874    )),
6875    XProps::default(),
6876    meta,
6877  )))
6878}
6879
6880/// Perl's Fence (MathParser.pm): generalized fenced expression with
6881/// comma-separated items. Determines meaning from delimiter+punctuation
6882/// pattern using the Perl enclose tables.
6883/// Receives: open, item1, punct1, item2, [punct2, item3, ...], close
6884pub fn fence(
6885  rule_id: i32,
6886  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
6887  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
6888  ctxt: ActionContext,
6889) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
6890  // Collect all non-None args into a flat stuff vector
6891  let stuff: Vec<XM> = args.into_iter().flatten().collect();
6892  if stuff.len() < 2 {
6893    // A fence needs at least an open + close delimiter. A degenerate match
6894    // (all-None args, or a single surviving delimiter) would panic on
6895    // `stuff[0]` / `stuff[len-1]` or underflow `len - 2` — prune this parse.
6896    return Err("fence: need at least open + close delimiters".into());
6897  }
6898  // Perl reads the delimiters and the punctuation through `realizeXMNode` (MathParser.pm:1398,
6899  // 1402): in a gathered/split row's content branch they are XMRefs, and `|y|` there is
6900  // `absolute-value@(y)` as inline (golden
6901  // tests/parse/bar_pairs.tex#named_vertbar_parses_as_absolute_value).
6902  let o = realized_value(&stuff[0], &ctxt)?;
6903  let c = realized_value(&stuff[stuff.len() - 1], &ctxt)?;
6904  // Count items (every other element between open and close is an item)
6905  let n = (stuff.len() - 2).div_ceil(2); // number of items
6906  // Get first punctuation value for enclose2/encloseN lookup
6907  let p = if n >= 2 {
6908    realized_value(&stuff[2], &ctxt).ok()
6909  } else {
6910    None
6911  };
6912  let p_str = p.as_deref().unwrap_or(",");
6913  // Canonicalize the single "such-that / divides / given" bar. `\mid` reaches
6914  // here as ∣ (U+2223) or the CS-name "mid" (def_math infers a name from the
6915  // CS, unlike Perl's `DefMathI('\mid', undef, …)`), whereas bare `|`/`\vert`
6916  // reach here as "|". They are the same separator for the conditional /
6917  // conditional-set readings — Perl's VERTBAR terminal is content-agnostic
6918  // (MathGrammar:797) — so without this, `\{x\mid P\}` / `(a\mid b)` fell to
6919  // `list` instead of `conditional-set` / `conditional`. Mirror the lexeme-side
6920  // canonicalization in util.rs (VERTBAR:mid → VERTBAR:|).
6921  let p_str = if matches!(p_str, "\u{2223}" | "mid") {
6922    "|"
6923  } else {
6924    p_str
6925  };
6926  // A metarelation between the items other than a colon is one relation, fenced as one item (a
6927  // colon is a set-builder's in braces, Perl `suchThatOp`; elsewhere a separator here, `(a:b)`
6928  // `list@(a, b)`, where Perl reads `a colon b` — #366): Perl reads `OPEN Formulae CLOSE` with a `metarelopFormula` (MathGrammar:69, :118-125) and
6929  // `Fence` of one item (MathParser.pm:1412-1415) — `(p\iff q)` p iff q, `\{a\iff b\}` set@(a iff b),
6930  // `\{\Gamma\vdash A,B\}` set@(Gamma proves list@(A, B)); `suchThatOp` takes a colon only (:499-501).
6931  // Naming the pair from the tables dropped the relation (`list@(p, q)`; `(S\not\vdash c)` lost its
6932  // negation; 57bk, 2605.08011, 2605.06214, 2605.25146, 2605.00251).
6933  if n == 2
6934    && p_str != ":"
6935    && matches!(&stuff[2], XM::Lexeme(lex, _) if lex.starts_with("METARELOP:"))
6936  {
6937    let [open, left, relop, right, close]: [XM; 5] = stuff
6938      .try_into()
6939      .map_err(|_| "fence: a metarelation between two items")?;
6940    // A list beside the metarelation holding a relation is Perl's `Formulae`, as beside a bar:
6941    // `\{a<1,b\vdash c\}` set@(proves@(formulae@(a < 1, b), c)) (57bk review).
6942    let (left, right) = (
6943      relation_list_as_formulae(left),
6944      relation_list_as_formulae(right),
6945    );
6946    let relation = infix_relation(
6947      rule_id,
6948      vec![Some(left), Some(relop), Some(right)],
6949      pragmas,
6950      ActionContext {
6951        nodes:    ctxt.nodes,
6952        document: &mut *ctxt.document,
6953      },
6954    )?
6955    .ok_or("fence: no relation")?;
6956    return fenced(
6957      rule_id,
6958      vec![Some(open), Some(relation), Some(close)],
6959      pragmas,
6960      ctxt,
6961    );
6962  }
6963
6964  // Perl's enclose tables: determine operator meaning from delimiters + punctuation
6965  let op_meaning = match n {
6966    0 => "list",
6967    1 => match (o.as_ref(), c.as_ref()) {
6968      ("{", "}") => "set",
6969      ("|", "|") => "absolute-value",
6970      ("\u{2308}", "\u{2309}") => "ceiling",             // ⌈ ⌉
6971      ("\u{230A}", "\u{230B}") => "floor",               // ⌊ ⌋
6972      ("\u{2016}", "\u{2016}") | ("||", "||") => "norm", // ‖ ‖
6973      _ => return Ok(None),                              // fall through, shouldn't happen
6974    },
6975    2 => match (o.as_ref(), p_str, c.as_ref()) {
6976      ("{", ",", "}") => "set",
6977      ("{", ":", "}") | ("{", "|", "}") => "conditional-set",
6978      ("(", "|", ")") => "conditional",
6979      ("(", ",", ")") => "open-interval",
6980      ("[", ",", "]") => "closed-interval",
6981      ("(", ",", "]") => "open-closed-interval",
6982      ("[", ",", ")") => "closed-open-interval",
6983      _ => "list",
6984    },
6985    _ => match (o.as_ref(), p_str, c.as_ref()) {
6986      ("{", ",", "}") => "set",
6987      ("(", ",", ")") => "vector",
6988      _ => "list",
6989    },
6990  };
6991
6992  let op: XM = XProps {
6993    meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed(op_meaning)),
6994    ..XProps::default()
6995  }
6996  .into();
6997  // Change VERTBAR separators inside fences to MIDDLE role — Perl's `MorphVertbar(…,'MIDDLE')` for
6998  // the set-builder bar (MathGrammar:500); Perl marks the `(a|b)` bar a MODIFIEROP `conditional`
6999  // (:261-263) instead, an older convention here. Separators are at the even indices ≥ 2 of
7000  // [open, item, sep, item, ..., close]. A stretchy `\left|`/`\right|` divider
7001  // (`P\left(\left.A\right|B\right)`, 57ap) is re-roled on a copy: the parse may still be pruned.
7002  let last = stuff.len().saturating_sub(1);
7003  if (2..last)
7004    .step_by(2)
7005    .any(|i| left_bar_pairs_an_evaluation_bar(&stuff[i], &stuff[i + 1]))
7006  {
7007    return Err("fence: a `\\left|` divider pairs the item's evaluation bar".into());
7008  }
7009  let mut stuff: Vec<XM> = stuff
7010    .into_iter()
7011    .enumerate()
7012    .map(|(i, item)| match item {
7013      XM::Lexeme(ref lex, _)
7014        if i >= 2
7015          && i < last
7016          && i % 2 == 0
7017          && (lex.starts_with("LEFT_STRETCHY_VERTBAR:")
7018            || lex.starts_with("RIGHT_STRETCHY_VERTBAR:")) =>
7019      {
7020        morph_vertbar(item, "MIDDLE", ctxt.nodes)
7021      },
7022      other => other,
7023    })
7024    .collect();
7025  for i in (2..stuff.len().saturating_sub(1)).step_by(2) {
7026    match &mut stuff[i] {
7027      XM::Token(props, _) if props.role.as_deref() == Some("VERTBAR") => {
7028        props.role = Some(Cow::Borrowed("MIDDLE"));
7029      },
7030      &mut XM::Lexeme(ref lex, ref meta) if lex.starts_with("VERTBAR:") => {
7031        // For lexemes, change the role on the underlying DOM node
7032        if let Some(ref cv) = meta.curry_level {
7033          let cv_str = cv.to_string();
7034          if let Some(idx_str) = cv_str.strip_prefix(':')
7035            && let Ok(lex_idx) = idx_str.parse::<usize>()
7036          {
7037            let idx = if lex_idx > 0 { lex_idx - 1 } else { 0 };
7038            if idx < ctxt.nodes.len() {
7039              let mut node = ctxt.nodes[idx].clone();
7040              let _ = node.set_attribute("role", "MIDDLE");
7041            }
7042          }
7043        }
7044      },
7045      _ => {},
7046    }
7047  }
7048  if matches!(op_meaning, "conditional" | "conditional-set") {
7049    stuff = stuff
7050      .into_iter()
7051      .enumerate()
7052      .map(|(i, item)| {
7053        if i % 2 == 1 {
7054          relation_list_as_formulae(item)
7055        } else {
7056          item
7057        }
7058      })
7059      .collect();
7060  }
7061  interpret_delimited(op, stuff, ctxt).map(Some)
7062}
7063
7064/// A list beside a conditional bar that holds a relation is Perl's `Formulae`
7065/// (`FormulaNOBar suchThatOp Formulae`, MathGrammar:487-491; `NewFormulae`, MathParser.pm:1439-1448),
7066/// as a fenced one is (`fenced_list`): `\{x : a<1, b<2\}` is
7067/// `conditional-set@(x, formulae@(a < 1, b < 2))`, `\{x|y,z\}` keeps `list@(y, z)`.
7068fn relation_list_as_formulae(arg: XM) -> XM {
7069  if matches!(fenced_list(&arg), Some(FencedList::Formulae)) {
7070    as_formulae(arg)
7071  } else {
7072    arg
7073  }
7074}
7075
7076/// `[a|b]` / `[a \mid b]` — a bracketed conditional. Perl produces
7077/// `delimited-[]@(conditional@(a,b))`. Unlike `(a|b)` (→ `conditional@`) and
7078/// `\{a|b\}` (→ `conditional-set@`), the bare `a|b` conditional reduces only at
7079/// statement level (not as an `expression`), so `[a|b]` had no fence rule and
7080/// fell to `ltx_math_unparsed` — even though `[(a|b)]` already works. Build the
7081/// inner `conditional@(a,b)` with a delimiter-less presentation, then wrap it in
7082/// `delimited-[]` via the same `fenced` path `[(a|b)]` uses. `E[X|Y]`
7083/// (conditional expectation) is the canonical witness.
7084pub fn bracket_conditional(
7085  rule_id: i32,
7086  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
7087  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
7088  ctxt: ActionContext,
7089) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
7090  let mut stuff: Vec<XM> = args.into_iter().flatten().collect();
7091  // Expect [lbracket, a, bar, b, rbracket]; bail defensively otherwise.
7092  if stuff.len() != 5 {
7093    return Ok(None);
7094  }
7095  let rbracket = stuff.pop().unwrap();
7096  let b = stuff.pop().unwrap();
7097  let bar = stuff.pop().unwrap();
7098  if left_bar_pairs_an_evaluation_bar(&bar, &b) {
7099    return Err("bracket_conditional: a `\\left|` divider pairs the item's evaluation bar".into());
7100  }
7101  let mut a = relation_list_as_formulae(stuff.pop().unwrap());
7102  let mut b = relation_list_as_formulae(b);
7103  let lbracket = stuff.pop().unwrap();
7104  // Inner conditional@(a,b) — refs created via a ctxt reborrow so the original
7105  // `ctxt` remains available for the outer `fenced` wrap.
7106  let inner_refs = {
7107    let inner_ctxt = ActionContext {
7108      nodes:    ctxt.nodes,
7109      document: &mut *ctxt.document,
7110    };
7111    create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut a, &mut b], inner_ctxt)?
7112  };
7113  let cond_op: XM = XProps {
7114    meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("conditional")),
7115    ..XProps::default()
7116  }
7117  .into();
7118  let inner = XM::Dual(
7119    Box::new(XM::Apply(
7120      cond_op.into(),
7121      inner_refs.into(),
7122      XProps::default(),
7123      Meta::default(),
7124    )),
7125    Box::new(XM::Wrap(
7126      vec![a, bar, b],
7127      XProps::default(),
7128      Meta::default(),
7129    )),
7130    XProps::default(),
7131    Meta::default(),
7132  );
7133  // Wrap in delimited-[] using the standard single-arg fenced path.
7134  fenced(
7135    rule_id,
7136    vec![Some(lbracket), Some(inner), Some(rbracket)],
7137    pragmas,
7138    ctxt,
7139  )
7140}
7141
7142/// This is similar, but "interprets" a delimited list as being the
7143/// application of some operator to the items in the list.
7144fn interpret_delimited(
7145  op: XM,
7146  mut stuff: Vec<XM>,
7147  ctxt: ActionContext,
7148) -> Result<XM, Box<dyn Error>> {
7149  let upto = stuff.len() - 1;
7150  let (_seps, mut args) = extract_separators(&mut stuff[1..upto]);
7151  let ref_args = create_xmrefs(&mut args, ctxt)?;
7152  Ok(XM::Dual(
7153    Box::new(XM::Apply(
7154      op.into(),
7155      ref_args.into(),
7156      XProps::default(),
7157      Meta::default(),
7158    )),
7159    Box::new(XM::Wrap(stuff, XProps::default(), Meta::default())),
7160    XProps::default(),
7161    Meta::default(),
7162  ))
7163}
7164
7165/// Does `trailer` close a script's content? Only Perl's `Subscript`/`Superscript` start rules end in
7166/// `endPunct(?)`, which wraps the content in a one-item list (MathGrammar:84-92, `endPunct : PUNCT |
7167/// PERIOD` :129; MathParser.pm:1463-1475): `x_{a,}` x _ (list@(a)), `x_{a;}` too. Elsewhere Perl has no
7168/// closing mark — `parse_single` sets it aside for `Anything,` (MathParser.pm:657-670), and plain
7169/// `Anything` (an `XMArg` or `XMWrap`, MathGrammar:64-82) fails on it — and Rust reads it as presentation
7170/// (OXIDIZED_DESIGN #361): `\boxed{a+b.}` a + b, where the mark's value once chose `list@` for any
7171/// container (763 formulas in 82 papers of the 57ar A/B; 2605.00380 `\boxed{…}`, 2605.01199
7172/// `\xrightarrow{a.s.}`). The script is the mark's container: its `rule` attribute (base_xmath.rs,
7173/// tex_math.rs `XMArg rule='Subscript'`) — a gathered row's content branch holds an XMRef, whose
7174/// container is no script. A wide space's stand-in mark is a detached node (`filter_hints`,
7175/// util.rs), placed right after the node it follows: its container is that node's (`x_{a\qquad}`,
7176/// 57ax review).
7177fn closes_a_script(trailer: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
7178  let XM::Lexeme(lex, _) = trailer else {
7179    return false;
7180  };
7181  let Ok(node) = lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes) else {
7182    return false;
7183  };
7184  let container = node.get_parent().or_else(|| {
7185    let position = ctxt.nodes.iter().position(|n| n == node)?;
7186    ctxt.nodes.get(position.checked_sub(1)?)?.get_parent()
7187  });
7188  container
7189    .and_then(|container| container.get_attribute("rule"))
7190    .is_some_and(|rule| matches!(rule.as_str(), "Subscript" | "Superscript"))
7191}
7192
7193/// A trailing presentational embellishment,
7194/// represent by containing it in the presentation arm of an XMDual
7195pub fn postfix_embellished(
7196  _rule_id: i32,
7197  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
7198  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
7199  ctxt: ActionContext,
7200) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
7201  let mut arg = args.remove(0).unwrap();
7202  let trailer = args.remove(0).unwrap();
7203  let in_a_script = closes_a_script(&trailer, &ctxt);
7204  let mut ref_arg = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut arg], ctxt)?;
7205  if ref_arg.is_empty() {
7206    // create_xmrefs skips ephemeral variants (XMHint etc.), so refs come back
7207    // empty when the script content was spacing-only (e.g. `x^{\,,}`). A Dual
7208    // with an XMRef to nothing is meaningless and `remove(0)` would panic —
7209    // fall back to a bare Wrap, mirroring the `fenced` empty-refs guard
7210    // (semantics.rs:2138, hep-ph/9210235).
7211    return Ok(Some(XM::Wrap(
7212      vec![arg, trailer],
7213      XProps::default(),
7214      Meta::default(),
7215    )));
7216  }
7217  let content = if in_a_script {
7218    // Perl `NewList(item, punct)` for a script's `endPunct` (MathParser.pm:1463-1475): a one-item
7219    // list, whatever the mark.
7220    Box::new(XM::Apply(
7221      XProps {
7222        meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("list")),
7223        ..XProps::default()
7224      }
7225      .into(),
7226      Args(vec![Some(ref_arg.remove(0))]),
7227      XProps::default(),
7228      Meta::default(),
7229    ))
7230  } else {
7231    Box::new(ref_arg.remove(0))
7232  };
7233  Ok(Some(XM::Dual(
7234    content,
7235    Box::new(XM::Wrap(
7236      vec![arg, trailer],
7237      XProps::default(),
7238      Meta::default(),
7239    )),
7240    XProps::default(),
7241    Meta::default(),
7242  )))
7243}
7244/// Wrap start_script + parsed content together.
7245/// Returns XM::Wrap([start_script, content]) so new_script can use the parsed
7246/// content instead of re-reading from DOM (which loses XMDual structures).
7247pub fn faux_wrap(
7248  _rule_id: i32,
7249  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
7250  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
7251  _: ActionContext,
7252) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
7253  unp!(args => start_script, content, _end_script);
7254  // Bundle both the script wrapper lexeme and the parsed expression.
7255  // new_script_inner will detect this Wrap and use the parsed content.
7256  Ok(Some(XM::Wrap(
7257    vec![
7258      start_script.unwrap(),
7259      content.unwrap_or(XM::Token(XProps::default(), Meta::default())),
7260    ],
7261    XProps::default(),
7262    Meta::default(),
7263  )))
7264}
7265
7266pub fn standalone_script(
7267  _rule_id: i32,
7268  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
7269  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
7270  ctxt: ActionContext,
7271) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
7272  unp!(args => start_script, content, _end_script);
7273  // A float script of an absent base (Perl `NewScript(Absent(), …)`, MathGrammar:79-80), its script
7274  // the parsed content, bundled as `faux_wrap` does: re-reading the script from the DOM loses a
7275  // content XMDual (`\Gamma^{{}^{(2)}}_{ij}`, `{}^{(a,b)}_{c}` gave an XMRef with no idref, 57bj review).
7276  let script = XM::Wrap(
7277    vec![
7278      start_script.unwrap(),
7279      content.unwrap_or(XM::Token(XProps::default(), Meta::default())),
7280    ],
7281    XProps::default(),
7282    Meta::default(),
7283  );
7284  new_script(None, script, ctxt)
7285}
7286
7287pub fn postfix_script(
7288  _rule_id: i32,
7289  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
7290  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
7291  ctxt: ActionContext,
7292) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
7293  unp!(args => base, op);
7294  // 3-arg rules (e.g. mulop postsubarg postsuperarg): chain both scripts
7295  let op2 = args.pop().flatten();
7296  let intermediate = new_script(base, op.unwrap(), ActionContext {
7297    nodes:    ctxt.nodes,
7298    document: &mut *ctxt.document,
7299  })?;
7300  if let Some(op2) = op2 {
7301    new_script(intermediate, op2, ctxt)
7302  } else {
7303    Ok(intermediate)
7304  }
7305}
7306
7307/// Perl `DecorateOperator` (MathParser.pm:1649-1654), applied per script by `addOpDecoration`
7308/// (MathGrammar:692-697): the operator takes the script as any base does (`NewScript`), and the
7309/// scripted operator keeps the operator's role, so it still reads as an operator of its kind —
7310/// `a\leq_k b` is `a <= _ k b`, a relation, not `(<= _ k)@(a, b)` (arXiv 2605.03594
7311/// `\lesssim_{\kappa,L,U}`, 2605.28533 `<_{FOSD}`, 2605.20841 `\equiv_D`, `\lor_G`).
7312pub fn decorate_operator(
7313  _rule_id: i32,
7314  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
7315  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
7316  ctxt: ActionContext,
7317) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
7318  unp!(args => op, script);
7319  let role = op.as_ref().and_then(|op| operator_role(op, ctxt.nodes));
7320  let Some(script) = script else {
7321    return Err("decorate_operator: no script".into());
7322  };
7323  Ok(new_script(op, script, ctxt)?.map(|mut decorated| {
7324    if let XM::Apply(_, _, ref mut props, _) = decorated {
7325      props.role = role.map(Cow::Owned);
7326    }
7327    decorated
7328  }))
7329}
7330
7331pub fn prefix_script(
7332  _rule_id: i32,
7333  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
7334  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
7335  ctxt: ActionContext,
7336) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
7337  unp!(args => op, base);
7338  new_script(base, op.unwrap(), ctxt)
7339}
7340
7341/// Like prefix_script but forces "pre" position for POST scripts used as pre-scripts.
7342/// Perl: parse_kludgeScripts_rec calls NewScript($base, $script, 'pre') for POST scripts
7343/// that follow FLOAT scripts from the same empty {} base.
7344pub fn prefix_script_pre(
7345  _rule_id: i32,
7346  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
7347  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
7348  ctxt: ActionContext,
7349) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
7350  unp!(args => op, base);
7351  new_script_forced_pre(base, op.unwrap(), ctxt)
7352}
7353
7354/// Parse a scriptpos string like "post2" into position type and level.
7355/// Follows Perl's: ($sx, $sl) = ($scriptpos || 'post') =~ /^(pre|mid|post)?(\d+)?$/
7356fn parse_scriptpos(s: &str) -> (&'static str, u32) {
7357  let s = if s.is_empty() { "post" } else { s };
7358  let x = if s.starts_with("pre") {
7359    "pre"
7360  } else if s.starts_with("mid") {
7361    "mid"
7362  } else {
7363    "post"
7364  };
7365  let l: u32 = s
7366    .trim_start_matches(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic())
7367    .parse()
7368    .unwrap_or(1);
7369  (x, l)
7370}
7371
7372/// This is loosely in the lines of MathParser::NewScript, but taking into account
7373/// the realities of our new data structures.
7374pub fn new_script(
7375  base: Option<XM>,
7376  script: XM,
7377  ctxt: ActionContext,
7378) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
7379  new_script_inner(base, script, ctxt, false)
7380}
7381
7382/// Like new_script but forces "pre" position (Perl: NewScript($base, $script, 'pre')).
7383/// Used for POST scripts kludged into pre-script position. Sets "pre" without _wasfloat.
7384fn new_script_forced_pre(
7385  base: Option<XM>,
7386  script: XM,
7387  ctxt: ActionContext,
7388) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
7389  new_script_inner(base, script, ctxt, true)
7390}
7391
7392fn new_script_inner(
7393  base: Option<XM>,
7394  script: XM,
7395  ctxt: ActionContext,
7396  force_pre: bool,
7397) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
7398  // faux_wrap now returns XM::Wrap([start_script_lexeme, parsed_content]).
7399  // Extract both pieces. The lexeme provides role/scriptpos metadata;
7400  // the parsed content is used instead of re-reading from DOM.
7401  let (script_lex, parsed_content) = match script {
7402    XM::Wrap(mut items, ..) if items.len() == 2 => {
7403      let content = items.pop().unwrap();
7404      let lex = items.pop().unwrap();
7405      (lex, Some(content))
7406    },
7407    XM::Lexeme(..) => (script, None),
7408    other => panic!(
7409      "new_script expects faux_wrap Wrap or Lexeme, got {:?}",
7410      other
7411    ),
7412  };
7413
7414  if let XM::Lexeme(ref lex, _) = script_lex {
7415    let script_wrap = lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes)?;
7416    let node_role = script_wrap.get_attribute("role").unwrap();
7417    let is_float = !force_pre && node_role.starts_with("FLOAT");
7418    let is_super = node_role.ends_with("SUPERSCRIPT");
7419    let role = Cow::Borrowed(if is_super {
7420      "SUPERSCRIPTOP"
7421    } else {
7422      "SUBSCRIPTOP"
7423    });
7424
7425    // Perl: Extract base's scriptpos to determine binding level
7426    let (bx, mut bl, base_wasfloat, base_bumplevel) = extract_base_scriptpos(&base, &ctxt);
7427
7428    // Read scriptpos from the script node
7429    let raw_sp = script_wrap.get_attribute("scriptpos").unwrap_or_default();
7430    let (sx, mut sl) = parse_scriptpos(&raw_sp);
7431    let sx_defined = !raw_sp.is_empty() && sx != "post";
7432
7433    if bl == 0 {
7434      bl = if sl > 0 { sl } else { 1 };
7435    }
7436    if sl == 0 {
7437      sl = if bl > 0 { bl } else { 1 };
7438    }
7439
7440    let sx = if sx_defined {
7441      sx
7442    } else if bl == sl {
7443      bx
7444    } else {
7445      "post"
7446    };
7447
7448    let x = if force_pre || is_float {
7449      "pre"
7450    } else if bl == sl {
7451      bx
7452    } else {
7453      if !sx.is_empty() { sx } else { "post" }
7454    };
7455
7456    // Perl NewScript L1624-1643: a pre-script donates its lpadding to the new
7457    // combined app, a post/mid script its rpadding. Capture now (owned), before
7458    // `script_lex` is consumed below, so a thinspace folded onto the script
7459    // marker by filter_hints (e.g. `\,` in `x^2\,dx`) rides onto the rebuilt app.
7460    let (lpad_xfer, rpad_xfer): (Option<String>, Option<String>) = if x == "pre" {
7461      (
7462        script_wrap
7463          .get_attribute("lpadding")
7464          .filter(|s| !s.is_empty()),
7465        None,
7466      )
7467    } else {
7468      (
7469        None,
7470        script_wrap
7471          .get_attribute("rpadding")
7472          .filter(|s| !s.is_empty()),
7473      )
7474    };
7475
7476    let mut l = if sl > 0 {
7477      sl
7478    } else if bl > 0 {
7479      bl
7480    } else {
7481      0
7482    };
7483
7484    let mut bumped = false;
7485    if base_wasfloat {
7486      l += 1;
7487      bumped = true;
7488    } else if base_bumplevel > 0 {
7489      l = base_bumplevel;
7490    }
7491
7492    let scriptpos: Cow<'static, str> = format!("{x}{l}").into();
7493    let op = new_props(
7494      None,
7495      None,
7496      Some(raw_map!("role"=>role, "scriptpos"=>scriptpos)),
7497    );
7498    // Use parsed content if available, otherwise fall back to obtain_arg (DOM re-read)
7499    let script_arg = if let Some(content) = parsed_content {
7500      Some(content)
7501    } else {
7502      obtain_arg(script_lex, 0, ctxt)?
7503    };
7504    let mut meta = if bumped {
7505      Meta::with_bumplevel(l)
7506    } else {
7507      Meta::default()
7508    };
7509    if is_float {
7510      meta.set_wasfloat();
7511    }
7512    // Perl: NewScript(Absent(), ...) when base is None (standalone floating scripts)
7513    let base_arg = base.or_else(|| {
7514      Some(XM::Token(
7515        XProps {
7516          meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("absent")),
7517          ..XProps::default()
7518        },
7519        Meta::default(),
7520      ))
7521    });
7522    let app_props = XProps {
7523      lpadding: lpad_xfer.map(Cow::Owned),
7524      rpadding: rpad_xfer.map(Cow::Owned),
7525      ..XProps::default()
7526    };
7527    Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
7528      op.into(),
7529      Args(vec![base_arg, script_arg]),
7530      app_props,
7531      meta,
7532    )))
7533  } else {
7534    panic!(
7535      "new_script expects Lexeme inside faux_wrap, got {:?}",
7536      script_lex
7537    );
7538  }
7539}
7540
7541/// Extract scriptpos info from the base of a script operation.
7542/// Returns (position_string, level, was_float, bump_level)
7543fn extract_base_scriptpos(
7544  base: &Option<XM>,
7545  ctxt: &ActionContext,
7546) -> (&'static str, u32, bool, u32) {
7547  match base {
7548    Some(XM::Apply(op, _, _props, meta)) => {
7549      // Check if the operator is a SCRIPTOP
7550      if let XM::Token(ref op_props, _) = *op.0 {
7551        let role = op_props.role.as_deref().unwrap_or("");
7552        if role.ends_with("SCRIPTOP") {
7553          let sp = op_props.scriptpos.as_deref().unwrap_or("post");
7554          let (bx, bl) = parse_scriptpos(sp);
7555          let wasfloat = meta.wasfloat();
7556          let bumplevel = meta.bumplevel();
7557          return (bx, bl, wasfloat, bumplevel);
7558        }
7559      }
7560      ("post", 0, false, 0)
7561    },
7562    // For Lexeme bases (e.g., \sum with scriptpos="mid"),
7563    // look up the XML node to get scriptpos
7564    Some(XM::Lexeme(lex, _)) => {
7565      if let Ok(node) = lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes) {
7566        let sp = node.get_attribute("scriptpos").unwrap_or_default();
7567        if !sp.is_empty() {
7568          let (bx, bl) = parse_scriptpos(&sp);
7569          return (bx, bl, false, 0);
7570        }
7571      }
7572      ("post", 0, false, 0)
7573    },
7574    Some(XM::Token(props, _)) => {
7575      let sp = props.scriptpos.as_deref().unwrap_or("post");
7576      let (bx, bl) = parse_scriptpos(sp);
7577      (bx, bl, false, 0)
7578    },
7579    _ => ("post", 0, false, 0),
7580  }
7581}
7582
7583// Get n-th arg of an XMApp.
7584// However, this is really only used to get the script out of a sub/super script
7585pub fn obtain_arg(tree: XM, n: usize, ctxt: ActionContext) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
7586  match &tree {
7587    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => {
7588      let lex_node = lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes)?;
7589      let args = element_nodes(lex_node);
7590      let nth = args.get(n).map(XM::from);
7591      Ok(nth)
7592      // TODO:
7593      // Tricky case: if $node is an XMRef, we'll want to reference the SUB node too
7594      // and not just use it directly; else that node will be duplicated in both branches of XMDual
7595      // if ($nth && !$node->isSameNode($onode)) {
7596      //   return LaTeXML::Package::createXMRefs($LaTeXML::MathParser::DOCUMENT, $nth); }
7597    },
7598    XM::Apply(_, args, ..) => match args.0.get(n) {
7599      Some(t) => Ok(t.clone()),
7600      None => Ok(None),
7601    },
7602    // Other XM variants (Token, Dual, Wrap, Choices, Arg, Ref) don't
7603    // carry positional args — Perl's obtain_arg returns undef for these.
7604    _ => Ok(None),
7605  }
7606}
7607
7608/// The `meaning` on an `XM::Dual`'s content operator, if it is an `Apply`
7609/// whose operator is a meaning-bearing token. Used to recognise the
7610/// `qm_bra`/`qm_ket` fences (content `Apply(meaning="bra"/"ket")`).
7611fn dual_content_meaning(xm: &XM) -> Option<&str> {
7612  if let XM::Dual(content, ..) = xm
7613    && let XM::Apply(op, ..) = &**content
7614    && let XM::Token(props, _) = &*op.0
7615  {
7616    return props.meaning.as_deref();
7617  }
7618  None
7619}
7620
7621/// True iff the leftmost factor of `xm` (descending through the first arg of
7622/// invisible-times/prefix applications) is a Dirac `bra` (`⟨…|`).
7623fn reaches_dirac_bra_on_left(xm: &XM) -> bool {
7624  if dual_content_meaning(xm) == Some("bra") {
7625    return true;
7626  }
7627  // A script closes its bra: `\langle 0|_Z|0\rangle` is (bra@(0))_Z·ket@(0), as Perl (57bp review).
7628  if script_base(xm).is_some() {
7629    return false;
7630  }
7631  if let XM::Apply(_, args, ..) = xm
7632    && let Some(Some(first)) = args.0.first()
7633  {
7634    return reaches_dirac_bra_on_left(first);
7635  }
7636  false
7637}
7638
7639/// True iff the rightmost factor of `xm` (descending through the last arg of
7640/// applications) is a Dirac `ket` (`|…⟩`).
7641fn reaches_dirac_ket_on_right(xm: &XM) -> bool {
7642  if dual_content_meaning(xm) == Some("ket") {
7643    return true;
7644  }
7645  if script_base(xm).is_some() {
7646    return false;
7647  }
7648  if let XM::Apply(_, args, ..) = xm
7649    && let Some(Some(last)) = args.0.last()
7650  {
7651    return reaches_dirac_ket_on_right(last);
7652  }
7653  false
7654}
7655
7656/// Does the product `left · right` split a Dirac bracket? Marpa also reads one `⟨…|…|…⟩` span as the
7657/// product bra `⟨…|` · (middle) · ket `|…⟩`, which splits its matched `⟨…⟩` across the factors: one
7658/// matrix element, `qm_bracket`'s (Perl's `maybeBraket`, MathGrammar:381-393). The product splits one
7659/// where a factor of `left` reaches a bra, `right` ends in a ket — scripted too, the script being the
7660/// bracket's (`\langle a|H|b\rangle_A`, Perl's `addScripts` after `maybeBraket`) — and the factors
7661/// between them are a label: not none, and none a label may not hold (`is_forbidden_dirac_label`, and
7662/// no open bra among them). A bra right before the ket, or before a ket or an open bra, is a factor of
7663/// its own: Perl's `maybeBra` falls back to the bra when no `ketExpression` follows its bar, which
7664/// cannot start one (`$forbidVertBar`, MathGrammar:301, :373-379) — `\langle x||y\rangle` bra@(x)·ket@(y),
7665/// `\langle x||y\rangle c` bra@(x)·ket@(y)·c, `\langle a||b\rangle|c\rangle` bra@(a)·ket@(b)·ket@(c) (57bt;
7666/// 2605.29622 `\langle ij||ab\rangle`, unparsed while every bra-then-ket product was refuted). Every factor
7667/// is looked at, not the first alone: `c\langle a|H|b\rangle` is c·⟨a|H|b⟩ only, as `\langle a|H|b\rangle c`
7668/// is ⟨a|H|b⟩·c. A ket before a bra (`|…⟩⟨…|`, an outer product) splits nothing.
7669fn splits_a_dirac_bracket(left: &XM, right: &XM) -> bool {
7670  let ket = script_base(right).unwrap_or(right);
7671  if !reaches_dirac_ket_on_right(ket) {
7672    return false;
7673  }
7674  // What `right` holds before its ket — an operator or a function applied to it (`H|b\rangle`, `\nabla|b\rangle`) —
7675  // is middle.
7676  let right_holds_more = dirac_meaning(ket) != Some("ket");
7677  let factors = product_factors(left);
7678  factors.iter().enumerate().any(|(i, factor)| {
7679    let middle = &factors[i + 1..];
7680    reaches_dirac_bra_on_left(factor)
7681      && (right_holds_more || !middle.is_empty())
7682      && !middle.iter().any(|item| is_forbidden_dirac_label(item))
7683      && !middle
7684        .windows(2)
7685        .any(|pair| ends_with_bra(pair[0]) && !opens_with_a_bar(pair[1]))
7686  })
7687}
7688
7689/// `function_factor bigop_operand`: a function, scripted or not, times the bigop after it —
7690/// Perl's `Factor moreFactors` (`\min_\theta\sum_i \ell_i` is min_θ * ∑…, `\log\int f`
7691/// log * ∫f). Not `apply_invisible_times`, whose left-function pruning (a function applies to
7692/// what follows it) would refute the only reading: a bigop application is a term, never a
7693/// function's argument. Golden: tests/parse/bigop_operands.tex#function_before_a_bigop_is_a_factor.
7694///
7695/// Mid-term (`tight_term function_factor bigop_operand`), the factors before the function join the
7696/// same product, as Perl's left-flattening `ApplyNary` (MathParser.pm:1497-1517) builds it — unless
7697/// the left product is fenced or has an id (:1503-1509):
7698/// `2\sin\int f` is times(2, sin, ∫f), `2x\sin\int f` times(2, x, sin, ∫f).
7699pub fn function_times_bigop(
7700  _rule_id: i32,
7701  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
7702  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
7703  ctxt: ActionContext,
7704) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
7705  let bigop = args.pop().flatten();
7706  let function = args.pop().flatten();
7707  let takes = matches!((&function, &bigop), (Some(function), Some(bigop))
7708    if takes_the_limit_operator(function, bigop, &ctxt));
7709  let mut factors = args
7710    .pop()
7711    .flatten()
7712    .map(open_product_factors)
7713    .unwrap_or_default();
7714  factors.push(function);
7715  factors.push(bigop);
7716  let product = XM::Apply(
7717    invisible_times().into(),
7718    Args(factors),
7719    XProps::default(),
7720    Meta::default(),
7721  );
7722  Ok(Some(if takes {
7723    function_takes_a_limit_operator(product)
7724  } else {
7725    product
7726  }))
7727}
7728
7729/// The factors of an unfenced invisible product without an id, `xm` alone otherwise: Perl's
7730/// left-flattening `ApplyNary` (MathParser.pm:1497-1517), which keeps a product whole whose `enclose`
7731/// or `xml:id` is set (:1503-1509).
7732fn open_product_factors(xm: XM) -> Vec<Option<XM>> {
7733  match xm {
7734    XM::Apply(op, Args(factors), props, meta)
7735      if meta.fenced.is_none()
7736        && props.id.is_none()
7737        && matches!(&*op.0, XM::Token(props, _)
7738          if props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("times")
7739            && props.content.as_deref() == Some("\u{2062}")) =>
7740    {
7741      factors
7742    },
7743    xm => vec![Some(xm)],
7744  }
7745}
7746
7747/// `tight_term bigop_operand`, `bare_opfunction_term bigop_operand`: the product
7748/// (`apply_invisible_times`), whose big operator an expectation ending the left side takes
7749/// (`expectation_takes_the_big_operator`): `\mathbb{E}\frac1n\sum_i X_i` 𝔼@((1/n)·∑…),
7750/// `\frac1n\mathbb{E}\sum_i X_i` (1/n)·𝔼@(∑…).
7751pub fn product_before_a_big_operator(
7752  rule_id: i32,
7753  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
7754  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
7755  ctxt: ActionContext,
7756) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
7757  let takes = matches!(args.as_slice(), [Some(left), Some(bigop)]
7758    if takes_the_limit_operator(product_end(left, true), bigop, &ctxt));
7759  let product =
7760    apply_invisible_times(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)?.map(expectation_takes_the_big_operator);
7761  Ok(if takes {
7762    product.map(function_takes_a_limit_operator)
7763  } else {
7764    product
7765  })
7766}
7767
7768/// May the function before `bigop` take it (`function_takes_a_limit_operator`)? Not a trig function when the limit-type
7769/// operator's operand crosses the end of the trig argument it would be (`ends_trig_argument`, #367): `\sin\det A\,y`
7770/// stays sin·det@(A·y), as Perl, not sin@(det(A·y)) across the space (57cj.8 review; latent, its probes).
7771fn takes_the_limit_operator(function: &XM, bigop: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
7772  if head_category(script_nucleus(function)) != Some("TRIGFUNCTION") {
7773    return true;
7774  }
7775  let XM::Apply(_, Args(args), _, meta) = through_differentials(bigop) else {
7776    return true;
7777  };
7778  let [Some(operand)] = args.as_slice() else {
7779    return true;
7780  };
7781  if meta.fenced.is_some() || matches!(operand, XM::Dual(..) | XM::Wrap(..)) {
7782    return true;
7783  }
7784  let factors = product_factors(operand);
7785  !factors
7786    .windows(2)
7787    .enumerate()
7788    .any(|(k, pair)| ends_trig_argument(&factors[..=k], pair[1], ctxt))
7789}
7790
7791/// `function_factor bigop_operand`: `function_times_bigop`, whose function takes the big operator — an expectation
7792/// (`expectation_takes_the_big_operator`): `\mathbb{E}\sum_i X_i` 𝔼@(∑…), any other function too since 57cj.22
7793/// (`function_takes_a_limit_operator`, user ruling Q7): `\log\sum_i x_i` log@(∑…).
7794pub fn function_before_a_big_operator(
7795  rule_id: i32,
7796  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
7797  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
7798  ctxt: ActionContext,
7799) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
7800  Ok(function_times_bigop(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)?.map(expectation_takes_the_big_operator))
7801}
7802
7803/// An expectation takes the summation-like big operator after it (user ruling 2026-09-30, "follow
7804/// the mathematical meaning": the expectation of a big-operator expression is of the whole of it,
7805/// parentheses or not). Alone: `\mathbb{E}\sum_i X_i` 𝔼@(∑_i X_i),
7806/// `\varepsilon\mathbb{E}\int_0^T|u(s)|^2\,ds` ε·𝔼@(∫…) (2605.13204 S2.Ex6.m1),
7807/// `\mathbb{E}\sup_g\int g\,d\mu` (2605.03300 S3.E17.m2). After the coefficients of its bare
7808/// argument: `\mathbb{E}_{\{…\}}\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n[…]` 𝔼@((1/n)·∑…) (2605.02116 A3.Ex163.m2),
7809/// `\eta\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\rho}\gamma\sum_a…` η·𝔼@(γ·∑…) (2605.06977 A3.Ex74.m1). As a function's
7810/// whole bare argument, which nests it (57cb): `\max_\pi\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\pi}\sum_t`
7811/// max_π@(𝔼@(∑…)) (2605.11975 S6.E24.m1), `\Tr\mathbb{E}\prod H` (2605.02768 S1.Ex1.m1). Any other
7812/// OPFUNCTION takes a big operator after it too (`function_takes_a_limit_operator`, #390 and user rulings Q7 and
7813/// 2026-10-01c: `\log\sum_i x_i` log@(∑…)), after its argument's coefficients too, in the expectation's argument as well:
7814/// `\mathbb{E}_{z_j}\min_\mu\frac{\tau}{m}\sum_j` 𝔼@(min_μ@((τ/m)·∑…)) (2605.02116 A5.Ex283.m1).
7815///
7816/// The grammar derives each shape once, as the product it is for any OPFUNCTION; this reads that
7817/// derivation, so no rule and no refused tree is added (`parse_tree_count_limits`). `product`'s
7818/// last factor is the big operator, and the deepest expectation the factor before it ends in takes
7819/// it (`ends_in_an_expectation`). Not a differential operator (DIFFOP, as
7820/// `ends_in_a_bigop_application` reads it, divergence #374): `\int_0^T\mathbb{E}X_t\,\dd t` keeps
7821/// its differential. A group closes the expectation (`\mathbb{E}[X]\sum_i Y_i` 𝔼@(X)·∑), and an
7822/// explicit MulOp is another rule (`\mathbb{E}X\cdot\sum_i Y_i`, `term mulop bigop_operand`).
7823fn expectation_takes_the_big_operator(product: XM) -> XM {
7824  match product {
7825    XM::Apply(op, Args(mut factors), props, meta)
7826      if is_invisible_times_op(&op.0)
7827        && matches!(factors.as_slice(), [.., Some(before), Some(bigop)]
7828          if is_summation_like(bigop) && ends_in_an_expectation(before)) =>
7829    {
7830      if let (Some(Some(bigop)), Some(Some(before))) = (factors.pop(), factors.pop()) {
7831        let taken = take_the_big_operator(before, bigop);
7832        if factors.is_empty() {
7833          return taken;
7834        }
7835        factors.push(Some(taken));
7836      }
7837      XM::Apply(op, Args(factors), props, meta)
7838    },
7839    product => product,
7840  }
7841}
7842
7843/// Divergence #390 (57cj.8 review; surpass, KNOWN_PERL_ERRORS #400): a function — an OPFUNCTION or a trig function,
7844/// bare or scripted, or an operator's nest over one — right before a limit-type operator's application takes it as
7845/// its argument: `\log\det\Sigma` log@(det@(Σ)), `\sin\det A`, `\cos\sup_t u`, `\log\inf_x u`, `\nabla_x\log\det(A)`
7846/// ((∇_x)@(log))@(det@(A)), `\operatorname*{arg\,max}_s\log\det(L_s)`, and one through a derivative
7847/// (`\sin\partial_x\det A` sin@(∂_x(det A))) — where Perl, whose OPFUNCTION takes no big operator (`aBarearg`,
7848/// MathGrammar:323-331) and LIMITOP is one (:717), multiplies them: logarithm * determinant@(A). 243 formulas in 55 of
7849/// the 3,003 A/B papers, most `\log\det\Sigma` (2605.00130, 2605.26554, 2605.02883, 2605.03984, 2605.24401, 2605.25592,
7850/// 2605.14289; `\max_j\sup_z` 2605.02556, `\Im\lim` 2605.28932). … and a summation-like operator's too (user ruling Q7,
7851/// 2026-10-01; `is_a_summation_like_application`; was Perl's product): `\log\sum_i x_i` log@(∑…), `\sin\log\sum_i x_i`
7852/// sin@(log@(∑…)), `\exp\int_0^t a(s)\,ds`, `\max_\theta\sum_i\ell_i`, `\nabla\nabla\log\sum_i p_i` ∇(∇(log(∑…))) (57cj.23: down
7853/// an operator's nest, `take_a_limit_operator`); and after the coefficients of the function's bare argument too (user ruling
7854/// 2026-10-01c, `takes_after_its_coefficients`: `\min_\theta\frac1n\sum_i\ell_i` min_θ((1/n)·∑…), as an expectation's,
7855/// `expectation_takes_the_big_operator`). The grammar derives the product once, as for any big operator; this reads it.
7856fn function_takes_a_limit_operator(product: XM) -> XM {
7857  match product {
7858    XM::Apply(op, Args(mut factors), props, meta)
7859      if is_invisible_times_op(&op.0)
7860        && matches!(factors.as_slice(), [.., Some(before), Some(bigop)]
7861          if (ends_in_a_function_head(before) || takes_after_its_coefficients(before))
7862            && (is_a_limit_operator_application(bigop) || is_a_summation_like_application(bigop))
7863            && !qualifies_the_limit_operator(last_function_head(before), bigop)) =>
7864    {
7865      if let (Some(Some(bigop)), Some(Some(before))) = (factors.pop(), factors.pop()) {
7866        let taken = take_a_limit_operator(before, bigop);
7867        if factors.is_empty() {
7868          return taken;
7869        }
7870        factors.push(Some(taken));
7871      }
7872      XM::Apply(op, Args(factors), props, meta)
7873    },
7874    product => product,
7875  }
7876}
7877
7878/// An unapplied OPFUNCTION or trig function, bare or scripted, an operator's nest over one (`\nabla_x\log`), or a
7879/// function's bare application to one (`\log\log`, `\min_\theta\log`, `\log\max_i`, `\arg\min_x\log`, 57cj.9 and
7880/// 57cj.10 reviews; 2605.14289 `\log\exp\sup_x f`): what takes a limit-type operator's application
7881/// (`function_takes_a_limit_operator`), unless the head right before the operator names its variant
7882/// (`qualifies_the_limit_operator`).
7883fn ends_in_a_function_head(xm: &XM) -> bool {
7884  is_bare_function_head(xm)
7885    || matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, _, meta)
7886      if meta.fenced.is_none()
7887        && (is_nested_operator(op, args) || is_bare_function_head(op))
7888        && matches!(args.0.as_slice(), [Some(inner)] if ends_in_a_function_head(inner)))
7889}
7890
7891/// The head right before a limit-type operator in `xm`, which `ends_in_a_function_head`: `xm` when it is a bare or
7892/// scripted head, the head its bare argument ends in otherwise (`\log\arg` → `\arg`, `\nabla_x\log` → `\log`).
7893fn last_function_head(xm: &XM) -> &XM {
7894  match xm {
7895    XM::Apply(_, Args(args), ..) if !is_bare_function_head(xm) => match args.as_slice() {
7896      [Some(inner)] => last_function_head(inner),
7897      _ => xm,
7898    },
7899    _ => xm,
7900  }
7901}
7902
7903/// Does `head` name the variant of the limit-type operator `bigop` rather than a function of its value? `\arg` before
7904/// an infimum or a supremum — `\arg\inf f(\theta)` is one arg-inf, not the complex argument of an infimum (2605.30648,
7905/// 2605.16560) — and `\operatorname{ess}` before every limit-type operator (`\operatorname{ess}\sup`,
7906/// `\operatorname{ess}\lim_{x\to a}f(x)`, `\operatorname{ess}\det A`): they keep Perl's product (57cj.9 review; SYNC row
7907/// "Math-parse residuals of the 57cj train"). `ess` is never a function of a value, only a qualifier (57cj.11 review);
7908/// `\arg` is one, the complex argument, so before any other operator it takes it: `\arg\det U` argument@(det U) (the
7909/// strong-CP phase `\bar\theta=\theta-\arg\det M_q`), `\arg\lim_{z\to0}f(z)` (57cj.10 review). Before a minimum or a
7910/// maximum, OPFUNCTIONs and no limit-type operator, both words apply (`\arg\min_x f` argument@(min_x f),
7911/// `\operatorname{ess}\max_x f` ess@(max_x f), as Perl): the one arg-min or ess-max operator is unmodelled (SYNC).
7912fn qualifies_the_limit_operator(head: &XM, bigop: &XM) -> bool {
7913  let XM::Lexeme(lex, _) = script_nucleus(head) else {
7914    return false;
7915  };
7916  // (`\arg` means `argument`; `\operatorname{arg}` spells it, 57cj.12 review)
7917  match lex.split(':').nth(1) {
7918    Some("argument" | "arg") => {
7919      head_meaning(bigop).is_some_and(|meaning| matches!(meaning, "infimum" | "supremum"))
7920    },
7921    Some("ess") => true,
7922    _ => false,
7923  }
7924}
7925
7926/// The meaning a head's lexeme or token names (`LIMITOP:supremum:3` supremum), through its scripts and applications.
7927fn head_meaning(xm: &XM) -> Option<&str> {
7928  match xm {
7929    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lex.split(':').nth(1),
7930    XM::Token(props, _) => props.meaning.as_deref(),
7931    XM::Apply(Operator(op), ..) => head_meaning(script_base(xm).unwrap_or(op)),
7932    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) => head_meaning(presentation),
7933    _ => None,
7934  }
7935}
7936
7937/// `before`, which `ends_in_a_function_head`, taking `bigop`: a head or an operator's nest applies to it
7938/// (`((\nabla_x)@(\log))@(\det A)`), a function's bare application takes it in its argument (`\log@(\log@(\det A))`).
7939fn take_a_limit_operator(before: XM, bigop: XM) -> XM {
7940  match before {
7941    // (a function's or an operator's bare application: down its nest — `\nabla\nabla\log\sum_i p_i` ∇(∇(log(∑…))), 57cj.23,
7942    // the merge review, where the curried (∇∇log)(∑…) read — or after its argument's coefficients, which the big
7943    // operator's application joins: `\min_\theta\frac1n\sum_i\ell_i` min_θ((1/n)·∑…), user ruling 2026-10-01c)
7944    XM::Apply(op, Args(mut args), props, meta)
7945      if meta.fenced.is_none()
7946        && args.len() == 1
7947        && (is_bare_function_head(&op.0) || is_operator_head(&op.0)) =>
7948    {
7949      let inner = args.pop().flatten().map(|inner| {
7950        if ends_in_a_function_head(&inner) {
7951          take_a_limit_operator(inner, bigop)
7952        } else {
7953          invisible_product(inner, bigop)
7954        }
7955      });
7956      XM::Apply(op, Args(vec![inner]), props, meta)
7957    },
7958    before => XM::Apply(
7959      before.into(),
7960      Args(vec![Some(bigop)]),
7961      XProps::default(),
7962      Meta::default(),
7963    ),
7964  }
7965}
7966
7967/// Does a function's bare application end before a big operator after its argument's coefficients, which the operator's
7968/// application joins (user ruling 2026-10-01c: a function before ∑/∏/∫ takes it even with coefficients between, as 𝔼 does,
7969/// `expectation_takes_the_big_operator`): an OPFUNCTION's whatever its argument (`\min_\theta\frac1n\sum_i\ell_i`,
7970/// `\min_\mu\frac{\tau}{m}\sum_j`, 2605.02116), a trig function's only when its argument is constants — an angle is no
7971/// coefficient (`\sin\theta\sum_l P_l` stays sin θ·∑…, `\sin 2\sum_i x_i` sin(2∑…)).
7972fn takes_after_its_coefficients(before: &XM) -> bool {
7973  let XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), _, meta) = before else {
7974    return false;
7975  };
7976  let [Some(argument)] = args.as_slice() else {
7977    return false;
7978  };
7979  if meta.fenced.is_some() || !is_bare_function_head(op) || ends_in_a_function_head(argument) {
7980    return false;
7981  }
7982  match head_category(script_nucleus(op)) {
7983    Some("OPFUNCTION") => true,
7984    Some("TRIGFUNCTION") => {
7985      let factors = product_factors(argument);
7986      constant_run(&factors) == factors.len()
7987    },
7988    _ => false,
7989  }
7990}
7991
7992/// A summation-like big operator's application or bare head — ∑, ∏, ∫, ⋃ (SUMOP, BIGOP, INTOP; Perl's `bigop` less LIMITOP
7993/// and DIFFOP) — which a function right before it takes (user ruling Q7, 2026-10-01: `\log\sum_i x_i` log(∑ x_i),
7994/// `\sin\log\sum_i x_i` sin(log(∑ x_i)), `\exp\int_0^t a(s)\,ds` exp(∫ a ds); `function_takes_a_limit_operator`).
7995fn is_a_summation_like_application(xm: &XM) -> bool {
7996  matches!(
7997    xm,
7998    XM::Apply(..) | XM::Dual(..) | XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..)
7999  ) && script_base(xm).is_none()
8000    && matches!(head_category(xm), Some("SUMOP" | "BIGOP" | "INTOP"))
8001}
8002
8003/// A limit-type operator's application (LIMITOP: `\det A`, `\sup_t u`, `\lim u`, `\dim V`), or a derivative's of one.
8004fn is_a_limit_operator_application(xm: &XM) -> bool {
8005  if is_differential(xm) {
8006    let operand = through_differentials(xm);
8007    return !std::ptr::eq(operand, xm) && is_a_limit_operator_application(operand);
8008  }
8009  matches!(xm, XM::Apply(..) | XM::Dual(..))
8010    && script_base(xm).is_none()
8011    && head_category(xm) == Some("LIMITOP")
8012}
8013
8014/// A summation-like big operator, bare, scripted or applied: ∑, ∏, ∫, ⋃, sup, lim, det (BIGOP,
8015/// SUMOP, INTOP, LIMITOP — Perl's `bigop`, MathGrammar:717, less DIFFOP).
8016fn is_summation_like(xm: &XM) -> bool {
8017  matches!(
8018    head_category(xm),
8019    Some("BIGOP" | "SUMOP" | "INTOP" | "LIMITOP")
8020  )
8021}
8022
8023/// Does `xm` end in an expectation that takes a big operator after it: a bare or scripted 𝔼
8024/// (`\mathbb{E}\sum`), an expectation's bare application (`\mathbb{E}\frac1n\sum`), or a function's
8025/// or operator's bare application whose argument does (`\max_\pi\mathbb{E}_\tau\sum`)? A group
8026/// application is closed: `\mathbb{E}[X]`, `\mathbb{E}_x[X]^2`.
8027fn ends_in_an_expectation(xm: &XM) -> bool {
8028  is_expectation_operator(xm)
8029    || bare_application(xm)
8030      .is_some_and(|(head, arg)| is_expectation_operator(head) || ends_in_an_expectation(arg))
8031}
8032
8033/// An OPFUNCTION's or operator's application to a bare argument (`is_bare_operator_application`),
8034/// as (head, argument).
8035fn bare_application(xm: &XM) -> Option<(&XM, &XM)> {
8036  match xm {
8037    XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(args), _, meta)
8038      if meta.fenced.is_none() && is_bare_operator_application(xm) =>
8039    {
8040      match args.as_slice() {
8041        [Some(arg)] => Some((&**head, arg)),
8042        _ => None,
8043      }
8044    },
8045    _ => None,
8046  }
8047}
8048
8049/// `xm`, which `ends_in_an_expectation`, with its deepest expectation taking `bigop`: a bare one is
8050/// applied to it, an application takes it after its argument — `𝔼@(1/n)` 𝔼@((1/n)·∑…),
8051/// `max_π@(𝔼_τ)` max_π@(𝔼_τ@(∑…)).
8052fn take_the_big_operator(xm: XM, bigop: XM) -> XM {
8053  if is_expectation_operator(&xm) {
8054    return XM::Apply(
8055      xm.into(),
8056      Args(vec![Some(bigop)]),
8057      XProps::default(),
8058      Meta::default(),
8059    );
8060  }
8061  match xm {
8062    XM::Apply(head, Args(mut args), props, meta) => {
8063      let arg = match args.pop().flatten() {
8064        Some(arg) if ends_in_an_expectation(&arg) => take_the_big_operator(arg, bigop),
8065        // (a function ending the argument takes a limit-type operator: `\mathbb{E}\log\det\Sigma` 𝔼@(log@(det Σ)))
8066        Some(arg) => function_takes_a_limit_operator(invisible_product(arg, bigop)),
8067        None => bigop,
8068      };
8069      XM::Apply(head, Args(vec![Some(arg)]), props, meta)
8070    },
8071    xm => invisible_product(xm, bigop),
8072  }
8073}
8074
8075/// `left` times `right`: one product, with `left`'s factors when it is an open one
8076/// (`open_product_factors`).
8077fn invisible_product(left: XM, right: XM) -> XM {
8078  let mut factors = open_product_factors(left);
8079  factors.push(Some(right));
8080  XM::Apply(
8081    invisible_times().into(),
8082    Args(factors),
8083    XProps::default(),
8084    Meta::default(),
8085  )
8086}
8087
8088/// The `tight_term factor` product: invisible times, unless the grammar reads the factor as an
8089/// application of what precedes it, where the product would be a second derivation multiplying the
8090/// trees chain by chain (57bl review: five chains of three, 32 → 1,024 trees; ten `\nabla(a)(b)`
8091/// terms 1,024 trees, 1.21 GB). Refused, each mirroring the rule it shadows:
8092/// - a group in parentheses or brackets after a letter that follows an application
8093///   (`application_before_a_letter`, `letter_after_an_application_apply`; user ruling 2026-09-29):
8094///   `f(x)g(y)` f@(x)·g@(y) — unless the letter recurs in its group (`letter_recurs_in_its_group`,
8095///   57bz): `f(x)x(x+1)` f@(x)·x·(x+1);
8096/// - a delimited group after an operator's application to a delimited group, alone or ending a
8097///   product (`D(a)(b)`, `c\nabla(a)(b)`; `operator_application_apply` through `op_application`,
8098///   which `tight_term`, an OPFUNCTION and a closed nest take alike): (D@(a))@(b), whatever the
8099///   delimiters, as Perl's `addEasyArgs` takes any balanced group (`\nabla(a)\{b\}`), except a Dirac
8100///   bracket, which Perl multiplies (`\nabla(u)\langle a|b\rangle`). Not after a bar group
8101///   (`\nabla|u|(v)` has no curried derivation, 57bn).
8102pub fn factor_product(
8103  rule_id: i32,
8104  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
8105  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
8106  ctxt: ActionContext,
8107) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
8108  if let [Some(left), Some(right)] = args.as_slice() {
8109    // A postfixed group is its group here, under scripts too (`f(n)g(n)!` as `f(n)g(n)`,
8110    // `f(x)g(y)!^2`).
8111    let right = postfixed_operand(right).unwrap_or(right);
8112    if is_paren_or_bracket_group(right)
8113      && letter_after_an_application(left, &ctxt)
8114      && !letter_recurs_in_its_group(product_end(left, true), right, &ctxt)
8115    {
8116      return Err("factor_product: the letter after an application takes this group".into());
8117    }
8118    let last = product_end(left, true);
8119    if is_delimited_group(right)
8120      && is_operator_group_application(last)
8121      && operator_group_argument_is_delimited(last)
8122    {
8123      return Err("factor_product: the operator's application takes this group".into());
8124    }
8125  }
8126  apply_invisible_times(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
8127}
8128
8129/// `application_before_a_letter speculative_item`: the letter after an application takes a group in
8130/// parentheses or brackets only, as the fenced-letters pragma reads a letter at the start of a
8131/// product (`is_dual_fenced_rhs`, pragmatics.rs); a brace, bar, floor or angle group multiplies there
8132/// and here — `P(A)P\{X>0\}` P@(A)·P·set, `U(t)H|\psi\rangle` U@(t)·H·ket, as Perl (57bl review).
8133pub fn letter_after_an_application_apply(
8134  rule_id: i32,
8135  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
8136  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
8137  ctxt: ActionContext,
8138) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
8139  // A postfixed letter's application (`letter_postfixed`) reads as the application it holds:
8140  // `f(n)g(n)!` f@(n)·(g@(n))! (57bw).
8141  if !args
8142    .get(1)
8143    .and_then(Option::as_ref)
8144    .map(|item| postfixed_operand(item).unwrap_or(item))
8145    .is_some_and(is_letter_application_to_a_paren_or_bracket_group)
8146  {
8147    return Err("letter_after_an_application_apply: only a paren or bracket group".into());
8148  }
8149  apply_invisible_times(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
8150}
8151
8152/// `application_before_a_letter = speculative_item`: a chain starts with a letter's application to
8153/// a paren or bracket group only — `H|n\rangle f(n)` is H·ket·f·n, `P\{A\}P(B)` P·set·P·B, as the
8154/// same letter alone and Perl (57bn review: the letter after it had forced H@(ket)).
8155pub fn letter_application_to_a_group(
8156  _rule_id: i32,
8157  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
8158  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
8159  _: ActionContext,
8160) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
8161  unp!(args => item);
8162  if item
8163    .as_ref()
8164    .is_some_and(is_letter_application_to_a_paren_or_bracket_group)
8165  {
8166    Ok(item)
8167  } else {
8168    Err("letter_application_to_a_group: only a paren or bracket group".into())
8169  }
8170}
8171
8172/// A letter's application (`speculative_prefix_apply`, the group kept whole) to a paren or bracket
8173/// group.
8174fn is_letter_application_to_a_paren_or_bracket_group(xm: &XM) -> bool {
8175  matches!(xm, XM::Apply(_, Args(items), ..)
8176    if matches!(items.as_slice(), [Some(group)] if is_paren_or_bracket_group(group)))
8177}
8178
8179/// A delimiter's role and text, from a lexeme (`ROLE:text:index`) or a token.
8180fn delimiter_role_text(xm: &XM) -> Option<(&str, &str)> {
8181  match xm {
8182    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => {
8183      let (role, rest) = lex.split_once(':')?;
8184      let (text, _index) = rest.rsplit_once(':')?;
8185      Some((role, text))
8186    },
8187    XM::Token(props, _) => Some((props.role.as_deref()?, props.content.as_deref()?)),
8188    _ => None,
8189  }
8190}
8191
8192/// A fenced group written between parentheses or between brackets — what the fenced-letters pragma
8193/// reads as a letter's argument — no fenced modifier `(>0)`, which `speculative_prefix_apply` refuses.
8194fn is_paren_or_bracket_group(xm: &XM) -> bool {
8195  if is_fenced_modifier_dual(xm) {
8196    return false;
8197  }
8198  let XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) = xm else {
8199    return false;
8200  };
8201  let XM::Wrap(items, ..) = &**presentation else {
8202    return false;
8203  };
8204  matches!(
8205    (
8206      items.first().and_then(delimiter_role_text),
8207      items.last().and_then(delimiter_role_text)
8208    ),
8209    (Some(("OPEN", "(")), Some(("CLOSE", ")"))) | (Some(("OPEN", "[")), Some(("CLOSE", "]")))
8210  )
8211}
8212
8213/// Are these a group's written delimiters, an opening and a closing one (`group_factor`: parens,
8214/// brackets, braces, angle brackets, generic delimiters), not an absent `\right.`? A bar pair's
8215/// delimiters read OPEN/CLOSE too (`morph_vertbar`): on the right `is_function_group` refuses it
8216/// (`bar_fence`); on the left `prefix_apply` does not lift a bar group, so no `Wrap` argument shows.
8217fn are_group_delimiters(items: &[XM]) -> bool {
8218  matches!(
8219    (
8220      items.first().and_then(delimiter_role_text),
8221      items.last().and_then(delimiter_role_text)
8222    ),
8223    (
8224      Some(("OPEN" | "OTHER_OPEN", _)),
8225      Some(("CLOSE" | "OTHER_CLOSE", _))
8226    )
8227  )
8228}
8229
8230/// A group `group_factor` derives: a fenced group between written delimiters, no fenced modifier,
8231/// and no Dirac bracket (a bar between its delimiters, `\langle a|b\rangle`).
8232fn is_delimited_group(xm: &XM) -> bool {
8233  is_function_group(xm)
8234    && !is_unbalanced_fence(xm)
8235    && matches!(xm, XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..)
8236    if matches!(&**presentation, XM::Wrap(items, ..)
8237      if are_group_delimiters(items)
8238        && !items[1..items.len() - 1].iter().any(|item| {
8239          delimiter_role_text(item).is_some_and(|(role, _)| role.ends_with("VERTBAR") || role == "MIDDLE")
8240        })))
8241}
8242
8243/// An operator's application whose argument group has written delimiters (`operator_group_application`
8244/// takes a `group_factor`), lifted over them: presentation `Apply(op, [Wrap(open … close)])`.
8245fn operator_group_argument_is_delimited(xm: &XM) -> bool {
8246  matches!(xm, XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..)
8247    if matches!(&**presentation, XM::Apply(_, Args(args), ..)
8248      if matches!(args.as_slice(), [Some(XM::Wrap(items, ..))] if are_group_delimiters(items))))
8249}
8250
8251/// Is `xm` a product ending in a bare unknown letter right after an application that
8252/// `application_before_a_letter` ends in: a letter's own (`speculative_item`), or a function's, an
8253/// OPFUNCTION's, a trig function's or an operator's application to a group (`delimited_application`,
8254/// `operator_group_application`; scripted heads as those rules take them)?
8255fn letter_after_an_application(xm: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
8256  let XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(factors), ..) = xm else {
8257    return false;
8258  };
8259  if !is_product_operator(op) {
8260    return false;
8261  }
8262  let [before @ .., Some(letter)] = factors.as_slice() else {
8263    return false;
8264  };
8265  if !matches!(letter, XM::Lexeme(lex, _) if lex.starts_with("UNKNOWN:") || lex.starts_with("XDIFFUNK:"))
8266  {
8267    return false;
8268  }
8269  // An ellipsis is transparent to the chain (`ellipsis_after_an_application`): the letter follows
8270  // the factor before the ellipses, or opens the chain when they start the product.
8271  let mut before = before;
8272  let mut skipped = false;
8273  while let [rest @ .., Some(last)] = before
8274    && is_ellipsis(last, ctxt)
8275  {
8276    before = rest;
8277    skipped = true;
8278  }
8279  match before.last() {
8280    None => skipped,
8281    Some(Some(before)) => is_application_before_a_letter(before),
8282    Some(None) => false,
8283  }
8284}
8285
8286/// `application_before_a_letter = elideop | ellipsis_id`: an ellipsis opens a chain (`\cdots g(n)`,
8287/// `\phi(\cdots\phi(W_1x))`).
8288pub fn ellipsis_opens_an_application_chain(
8289  _rule_id: i32,
8290  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
8291  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
8292  ctxt: ActionContext,
8293) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
8294  unp!(args => item);
8295  if item.as_ref().is_some_and(|item| is_ellipsis(item, &ctxt)) {
8296    Ok(item)
8297  } else {
8298    Err("ellipsis_opens_an_application_chain: not an ellipsis".into())
8299  }
8300}
8301
8302/// `application_before_a_letter (elideop | ellipsis_id)`: the chain goes on across an ellipsis
8303/// (`g(1)g(2)\cdots g(n)`, 2605.23467, 2605.10016, 2605.05078); the grammar offers no other ID
8304/// (`f(x)\infty g(y)` stays a product).
8305pub fn ellipsis_after_an_application(
8306  rule_id: i32,
8307  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
8308  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
8309  ctxt: ActionContext,
8310) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
8311  if !args
8312    .get(1)
8313    .and_then(Option::as_ref)
8314    .is_some_and(|item| is_ellipsis(item, &ctxt))
8315  {
8316    return Err("ellipsis_after_an_application: not an ellipsis".into());
8317  }
8318  apply_invisible_times(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
8319}
8320
8321fn is_application_before_a_letter(xm: &XM) -> bool {
8322  match xm {
8323    // A differential operator's application to a group or to an application before a letter
8324    // (`diffop_group_application`): `\partial_{11}l(F(x),Y)f(x)` (2605.00581).
8325    XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(args), _, meta)
8326      if meta.differential && is_bare_differential_operator(head) =>
8327    {
8328      matches!(args.as_slice(), [Some(operand)]
8329        if is_application_before_a_letter(operand) || is_delimited_group(operand))
8330    },
8331    // A letter's application to a group (`speculative_prefix_apply` keeps the group whole).
8332    XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(args), ..) => {
8333      matches!(head.as_ref(), XM::Lexeme(lex, _) if lex.starts_with("UNKNOWN:") || lex.starts_with("XDIFFUNK:"))
8334        && matches!(args.as_slice(), [Some(group)] if is_paren_or_bracket_group(group))
8335    },
8336    // A head's application to a group, lifted over the delimiters (`prefix_apply`).
8337    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) => {
8338      let XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(args), ..) = &**presentation else {
8339        return false;
8340      };
8341      if !matches!(args.as_slice(), [Some(XM::Wrap(..))]) {
8342        return false;
8343      }
8344      let head = head.as_ref();
8345      match script_base(head) {
8346        Some(base) => {
8347          matches!(
8348            operator_category(base),
8349            Some("OPFUNCTION" | "TRIGFUNCTION" | "OPERATOR")
8350          )
8351        },
8352        None => {
8353          matches!(head, XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..))
8354            && matches!(
8355              operator_category(head),
8356              Some("FUNCTION" | "OPFUNCTION" | "TRIGFUNCTION" | "OPERATOR")
8357            )
8358        },
8359      }
8360    },
8361    _ => false,
8362  }
8363}
8364
8365/// `D(a)(b)`: a bare or scripted operator's application to one group applies to the next group
8366/// (Perl `nestOperators`' OPEN branch takes one Expression, MathGrammar:669-671, then `addOpFunArgs`
8367/// the next group); an application to a list is `addEasyArgs`', which ends the Factor —
8368/// `\nabla(u,w)(v)` nabla@(u, w)·v, as Perl (57bl review).
8369pub fn operator_application_apply(
8370  rule_id: i32,
8371  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
8372  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
8373  ctxt: ActionContext,
8374) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
8375  if !args
8376    .first()
8377    .and_then(Option::as_ref)
8378    .is_some_and(is_operator_group_application)
8379  {
8380    return Err("operator_application_apply: an operator's application to a list ends it".into());
8381  }
8382  // A fenced modifier annotates what precedes it (`\nabla(u)(>0)` annotated@(∇@(u), absent > 0),
8383  // as 57bk and Perl; 57bn review), as `speculative_prefix_apply` refuses it too.
8384  if args
8385    .get(1)
8386    .and_then(Option::as_ref)
8387    .is_some_and(is_fenced_modifier_dual)
8388  {
8389    return Err("operator_application_apply: a fenced modifier is no argument".into());
8390  }
8391  prefix_apply(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
8392}
8393
8394/// A bare or scripted operator's application to one group, lifted over its delimiters: the head
8395/// that applies to the next group too (`D(a)(b)`, 57bl).
8396pub(crate) fn is_operator_group_application(xm: &XM) -> bool {
8397  matches!(xm, XM::Dual(content, presentation, ..)
8398    if matches!(&**content, XM::Apply(_, Args(items), ..) if items.len() == 1)
8399      && matches!(&**presentation, XM::Apply(Operator(op), ..) if is_bare_or_scripted_operator(op)))
8400}
8401
8402pub fn apply_invisible_times(
8403  _rule_id: i32,
8404  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
8405  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
8406  ctxt: ActionContext,
8407) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
8408  unp!(args => left, right);
8409  let mut left = left;
8410  let mut right = right;
8411  // Balanced-Dirac-delimiter refutation (`splits_a_dirac_bracket`): a bra, a label and a ket are one
8412  // bracket, `qm_bracket`'s, never three factors.
8413  if let (Some(l), Some(r)) = (&left, &right)
8414    && splits_a_dirac_bracket(l, r)
8415  {
8416    // Hard-reject via Err (not Ok(None)): Err prunes this parse tree so the
8417    // `qm_bracket` alternative survives; Ok(None) would instead yield a None
8418    // value that propagates up to a parent action (e.g. list_apply's
8419    // `right.unwrap()`) and panics.
8420    return Err("apply_invisible_times: refute Dirac bra·…·ket product (use qm_bracket)".into());
8421  }
8422  if let Some(ref l) = left {
8423    let operator = product_end(l, true);
8424    // (A differential operator's number takes the factors juxtaposed after it — a soft preference, the
8425    // pragma `DifferentiatedNumbersTakeTheirFactors` over `differentiated_number_sites`: refused here,
8426    // the product killed the last parse where the monomial cannot hold what follows, 57cj.3 review.)
8427    // … and its ellipsis the differential operator after it (`elided_diffop_application`, 57cj review):
8428    // `\partial_i\ldots\partial_j u` is ∂_i(…·∂_j u), not ∂_i(…)·∂_j u.
8429    if differentiates_an_ellipsis(operator, &ctxt)
8430      && right.as_ref().is_some_and(|r| {
8431        let first = product_end(r, false);
8432        is_differential(first) || is_bare_differential_operator(first)
8433      })
8434    {
8435      return Err(
8436        "apply_invisible_times: the differential operator's ellipsis takes the right".into(),
8437      );
8438    }
