8439    if is_operator_head(operator) {
8440      // Perl's OPERATOR is a Factor (MathGrammar:312-313), so one ending a product applies as one
8441      // starting it does: what it takes cannot follow it in a product (`operator_takes`) —
8442      // `\nabla u` is ∇@(u), `\mu\nabla^2 u` μ·(∇²)@(u), `\nabla_x^2 u` ((∇_x)²)@(u) — and anything
8443      // else can: a big operator's application (`\nabla_x\log\det(A)` is (∇_x)@(log)·det(A),
8444      // 2605.03984, 2605.24401, 2605.25592, 2605.14289), an operator after a closed nest
8445      // (`\nabla\log\nabla^2 u` is ∇@(log)·(∇²)@(u)). Golden
8446      // tests/parse/operator_application.tex#operator_nests_over_an_operator.
8447      if right.as_ref().is_some_and(|r| operator_takes(operator, r)) {
8448        return Err("apply_invisible_times: the operator on the left takes the right".into());
8449      }
8450    } else {
8451      // OPFUNCTION/TRIGFUNCTION/FUNCTION tokens, scripted or not (`\log_e x`), absorb the next
8452      // argument via prefix_apply, NOT via invisible times — unless it is a function too: Perl's
8453      // `fgh` with all FUNCTION is f·g·h.
8454      // An OPFUNCTION or TRIGFUNCTION that ends a product applies as one starting it (it takes a
8455      // bare argument): `a\log b c` is a·log@(b c), not a·log·b·c.
8456      let role_of = |xm: &XM| match xm {
8457        XM::Token(..) | XM::Lexeme(..) => operator_role(xm, ctxt.nodes),
8458        _ => script_base(xm).and_then(|base| operator_role(base, ctxt.nodes)),
8459      };
8460      // Only when it would take what follows (a bare argument, `addOpFunArgs`); before anything
8461      // else — a big operator's application, an operator's — it takes nothing and the product goes
8462      // on (`moreFactors`): `\tfrac12\log\det(\Sigma)`, `\tau\log\sum_i e^{x_i}`.
8463      let role = role_of(l).or_else(|| {
8464        right
8465          .as_ref()
8466          .filter(|r| {
8467            let first = product_end(r, false);
8468            // … or a group, which `addEasyArgs` takes (:571-576): `\lambda^2\log(|A|)^2` is
8469            // λ²·(log@(|A|))², not λ²·log·(|A|)².
8470            is_bare_item(first)
8471              || is_function_group(script_nucleus(first)) && !is_unbalanced_fence(first)
8472          })
8473          .and_then(|_| role_of(operator))
8474          .filter(|r| matches!(r.as_str(), "OPFUNCTION" | "TRIGFUNCTION"))
8475      });
8476      let is_function_role =
8477        |role: Option<&str>| matches!(role, Some("OPFUNCTION" | "TRIGFUNCTION" | "FUNCTION"));
8478      // … nor an operator or its application, which is no function's argument (`aBarearg`):
8479      // `\log\nabla^2` is log·∇², `\log\nabla f` log·∇@(f), `\log\nabla(a-b)` log·∇@(a − b), and
8480      // `\min_h\operatorname*{R}(h,P)` as Perl (57bf lifted the last two; train A/B 2605.13395,
8481      // 2605.19415, 2605.28109).
8482      if is_function_role(role.as_deref())
8483        && !right.as_ref().is_some_and(|r| {
8484          is_function_role(operator_role(r, ctxt.nodes).as_deref())
8485            || is_unbalanced_fence(product_end(r, false))
8486            || is_operator_head(r)
8487            || is_operator_head(product_end(r, false))
8488            || is_operator_application(product_end(r, false))
8489        })
8490      {
8491        return Err(
8492          "apply_invisible_times: left is OPFUNCTION/TRIGFUNCTION/FUNCTION, prefer prefix_apply"
8493            .into(),
8494        );
8495      }
8496    }
8497  }
8498  // Perl's greedy `barearg` (MathGrammar:321-337): an operator applied to a bare argument takes
8499  // the bare arguments after it — `\nabla u v` is ∇@(u v), not ∇@(u)·v.
8500  if let (Some(l), Some(r)) = (&left, &right)
8501    && leaves_a_bare_argument(l, r, None, &ctxt)
8502  {
8503    return Err("apply_invisible_times: the operator on the left takes this bare argument".into());
8504  }
8505  // Early-action prune for the fenced-modifier shape on the RHS:
8506  // `x (>0)` / `x (\in C)` — the legitimate parse is
8507  // `annotated_fenced_modifier`, NOT `x * (>0)` (implicit-times)
8508  // and NOT `x@(>0)` (function-app, handled in `prefix_apply_applyop`).
8509  if let Some(ref r) = right
8510    && is_fenced_modifier_dual(r)
8511  {
8512    return Err(
8513      "apply_invisible_times: right is a fenced modifier expression — \
8514         prefer annotated_fenced_modifier"
8515        .into(),
8516    );
8517  }
8518  // Bigop application results should not participate in invisible-times on their right.
8519  // When ∫_0^∞ x^2 dx is parsed, both `∫_0^∞(x^2 dx)` (absorption) and
8520  // `∫_0^∞(x^2) * dx` (flat) exist. Prune the flat parse by rejecting
8521  // invisible-times where the left is Apply(bigop, ...).
8522  // Perl: addIntOpArgs/addOpArgs absorbs the full integrand; we match by pruning.
8523  if let Some(ref l) = left
8524    && is_bigop_or_scripted_bigop(l, ctxt.nodes)
8525  {
8526    return Err("apply_invisible_times: left is bigop/scripted bigop, prefer absorption".into());
8527  }
8528  // Note: bare OPFUNCTION absorption (diffd@(x) vs diffd*x) is handled by
8529  // the FunctionsPreferWiderAbsorption pragmatic, which compares competing
8530  // trees and rejects the narrow parse.
8531  // Perl: scripted function application — f^2(a), f'(a), g_n(x).
8532  // When left is a scripted Apply whose base has FUNCTION/OPFUNCTION/TRIGFUNCTION role,
8533  // and right is a fenced XMDual (from parenthesized fencing), produce function
8534  // application with XMDual wrapping instead of invisible times.
8535  if let Some(ref l) = left
8536    && let Some(ref r) = right
8537  {
8538    let is_scripted_function = is_scripted_function_head(l, ctxt.nodes);
8539    let is_fenced_dual = matches!(r, XM::Dual(c, p, _, _)
8540        if matches!(**c, XM::Ref(_)) && matches!(**p, XM::Wrap(..)));
8541    if is_scripted_function && is_fenced_dual {
8542      // Lift the fenced XMDual: Apply(f^2, Dual(Ref, Wrap)) → Dual(Apply(Ref(f^2), Ref(arg)),
8543      // Apply(f^2, Wrap))
8544      let mut func = left.take().unwrap();
8545      let arg_dual = right.take().unwrap();
8546      let XM::Dual(content_box, pres_box, ..) = arg_dual else {
8547        unreachable!()
8548      };
8549      let content_ref = *content_box;
8550      let pres_wrap = *pres_box;
8551      let func_refs = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut func], ctxt)?;
8552      let func_ref = func_refs.into_iter().next().unwrap();
8553      let content_apply = XM::Apply(
8554        func_ref.into(),
8555        Args(vec![Some(content_ref)]),
8556        XProps::default(),
8557        Meta::default(),
8558      );
8559      let pres_apply = XM::Apply(
8560        func.into(),
8561        Args(vec![Some(pres_wrap)]),
8562        XProps::default(),
8563        Meta::default(),
8564      );
8565      return Ok(Some(XM::Dual(
8566        Box::new(content_apply),
8567        Box::new(pres_apply),
8568        XProps::default(),
8569        Meta::default(),
8570      )));
8571    }
8572  }
8573
8574  // Perl: trigBarearg greedily absorbs ALL following bare factors: \sin xyz → sin(x*y*z).
8575  // Reject invisible_times(trig_app(args), bare_factor) — the factor should be absorbed
8576  // into the trig argument via trig_arg rule, not multiplied outside.
8577  if let (Some(l), Some(r)) = (&left, &right)
8578    && leaves_a_trig_bare_argument(l, r, &ctxt)
8579  {
8580    return Err(
8581      "apply_invisible_times: trig function should absorb bare factor via trig_arg".into(),
8582    );
8583  }
8584  // Perl: MaybeFunction — mark UNKNOWN tokens as possibleFunction when MATHPARSER_SPECULATE is set
8585  // and the right side is a delimited group (parenthesized)
8586  maybe_mark_possible_function(&mut left, &right, ctxt.nodes);
8587
8588  // A large MULOP's application followed by a run of ellipses, then an item, in a bare argument's chain: the run was no
8589  // trailing one, so it and the item join the operand — `\log x\otimes y\cdots z` log@(x⊗(y·⋯·z)), as `x\otimes y\cdots z`
8590  // x⊗(y·⋯·z) at a term's level (Q11, #396; 57cj.20.Q11 review). A trailing run stays outside (user ruling 15).
8591  if let (Some(XM::Apply(Operator(times_op), Args(factors), times_props, times_meta)), Some(r)) =
8592    (&left, &right)
8593    && times_meta.fenced.is_none()
8594    && times_props.id.is_none()
8595    && is_invisible_times_op(times_op)
8596    && let [Some(application), run @ ..] = factors.as_slice()
8597    && !run.is_empty()
8598    && run.iter().all(|factor| {
8599      factor
8600        .as_ref()
8601        .is_some_and(|factor| is_ellipsis(factor, &ctxt))
8602    })
8603    && !is_ellipsis(r, &ctxt)
8604    && !is_an_integral_differential_factor(r, &ctxt)
8605    && !is_differential(r)
8606    && let XM::Apply(Operator(l_op), Args(l_args), l_props, l_meta) = application
8607    && l_meta.fenced.is_none()
8608    && l_props.id.is_none()
8609    && l_args.len() >= 2
8610    && is_a_large_mulop(l_op, &ctxt)
8611  {
8612    let mut l_args = l_args.clone();
8613    let last = l_args.pop().flatten();
8614    let mut operand: Vec<Option<XM>> = match last {
8615      Some(XM::Apply(last_op, Args(items), last_props, last_meta))
8616        if last_meta.fenced.is_none()
8617          && last_props.id.is_none()
8618          && is_invisible_times_operator(&last_op.0, &ctxt) =>
8619      {
8620        items
8621      },
8622      other => vec![other],
8623    };
8624    operand.extend(run.iter().cloned());
8625    operand.push(right.clone());
8626    l_args.push(Some(XM::Apply(
8627      Operator(times_op.clone()),
8628      Args(operand),
8629      XProps::default(),
8630      Meta::default(),
8631    )));
8632    return Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
8633      Operator(l_op.clone()),
8634      Args(l_args),
8635      l_props.clone(),
8636      l_meta.clone(),
8637    )));
8638  }
8639  // left-to-right associative -- if "left" is already a "times", tuck "right" in:
8640  if let Some(XM::Apply(ref op, ref mut left_args, _, ref _m)) = left
8641    && let XM::Token(xop, _xmeta) = &*op.0
8642  {
8643    match xop.meaning {
8644      Some(ref name) if name == "times" => {
8645        // No external operator to absorb here — `apply_invisible_times`
8646        // synthesizes its own `times` token, so there's no second
8647        // operator with an xml:id to redirect. Just absorb the
8648        // right-hand factor into the existing chain.
8649        left_args.0.push(right);
8650        return Ok(left);
8651      },
8652      _ => {},
8653    }
8654  }
8655  // Mixed number detection: NUMBER followed by FRACOP → invisible plus
8656  // Perl: 2\frac{3}{4} = 2 + 3/4; 123\frac{12}{34} = 123 + 12/34 (all-integer)
8657  // But 123.456\frac{12}{34} = 123.456 × (12/34) (decimal prefix → not mixed)
8658  let l_num = is_number(&left);
8659  let l_integer = l_num && is_integer_number(&left);
8660  let mut r_frac = is_fracop(&right);
8661  // Also check via nodes: if right is a Lexeme pointing to a DOM node with FRACOP inside
8662  if l_num
8663    && !r_frac
8664    && let Some(XM::Lexeme(ref _lex, ref meta)) = right
8665  {
8666    // Use curry_level to find the node — it encodes the node position
8667    if let Some(ref cv) = meta.curry_level {
8668      let cv_str = cv.to_string();
8669      // Extract index from ":N" format — node index is N-1 (lexeme counter is 1-based)
8670      if let Some(idx_str) = cv_str.strip_prefix(':')
8671        && let Ok(lex_idx) = idx_str.parse::<usize>()
8672      {
8673        let idx = if lex_idx > 0 { lex_idx - 1 } else { 0 };
8674        if idx < ctxt.nodes.len() {
8675          let node = &ctxt.nodes[idx];
8676          if node.get_name() == "XMApp" {
8677            for child in node.get_child_elements() {
8678              if child.get_attribute("role").as_deref() == Some("FRACOP") {
8679                r_frac = true;
8680                break;
8681              }
8682            }
8683          }
8684        }
8685      }
8686    }
8687  }
8688  // Mixed number only when BOTH sides of the fraction are pure integers.
8689  // Perl: 2\frac{3}{4} → 2+3/4, but 123\frac{12.0}{34} → 123×(12.0/34)
8690  let mut is_mixed_number = l_integer && r_frac;
8691  if is_mixed_number {
8692    // Check the fraction's numerator/denominator are pure integers via DOM nodes.
8693    // The fraction is often opaque in the XM tree (represented as an ATOM Lexeme).
8694    // We need to examine the DOM node's XMArg children for non-NUMBER content.
8695    let frac_node_opt = find_fracop_node(&right, ctxt.nodes);
8696    if let Some(frac_node) = frac_node_opt {
8697      // Check all non-operator children (numerator, denominator) for pure integer content.
8698      // Children are bare XMTok elements, not wrapped in XMArg.
8699      for child in frac_node.get_child_elements() {
8700        let role = child.get_attribute("role").unwrap_or_default();
8701        if role == "FRACOP" {
8702          continue;
8703        } // skip the operator
8704        let content = child.get_content();
8705        if role != "NUMBER" || content.contains('.') {
8706          is_mixed_number = false;
8707          break;
8708        }
8709      }
8710    }
8711  }
8712  let op = if is_mixed_number {
8713    invisible_plus()
8714  } else {
8715    invisible_times()
8716  };
8717  // A large MULOP's application on the left — in a bare argument's chain, `\sin x\otimes y z`, where the grammar joins
8718  // the next item to the chain so far — takes the juxtaposed item into its last operand (Q11, divergence #396):
8719  // sin@(x⊗(y z)), as `x\otimes y z` x⊗(y z) at a term's level. Not a differential (an integral's, which closes the
8720  // integrand: `\int\log f\otimes g\,dx` keeps log(f⊗g)·dx) nor an ellipsis (a trailing one leaves, user ruling 15; a
8721  // run between two items joins, above). Residual: a mixed number joins as a product here, `\log x\otimes 2\frac34`
8722  // log(x⊗(2·¾)), where `x\otimes 2\frac34` is x⊗(2+¾) (57cj.20.Q11 review NIT 6).
8723  if !is_mixed_number
8724    && let (Some(l), Some(r)) = (&left, &right)
8725    && !is_an_integral_differential_factor(r, &ctxt)
8726    && !is_differential(r)
8727    && !is_ellipsis(r, &ctxt)
8728    && let XM::Apply(Operator(l_op), Args(l_args), l_props, l_meta) = l
8729    && l_meta.fenced.is_none()
8730    && l_props.id.is_none()
8731    && l_args.len() >= 2
8732    && is_a_large_mulop(l_op, &ctxt)
8733  {
8734    let mut l_args = l_args.clone();
8735    let last = l_args.pop().flatten();
8736    let joined = match last {
8737      Some(XM::Apply(last_op, Args(mut factors), last_props, last_meta))
8738        if last_meta.fenced.is_none()
8739          && last_props.id.is_none()
8740          && is_invisible_times_operator(&last_op.0, &ctxt) =>
8741      {
8742        factors.push(right);
8743        XM::Apply(last_op, Args(factors), last_props, last_meta)
8744      },
8745      other => XM::Apply(
8746        op.into(),
8747        Args(vec![other, right]),
8748        XProps::default(),
8749        Meta::default(),
8750      ),
8751    };
8752    l_args.push(Some(joined));
8753    return Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
8754      Operator(l_op.clone()),
8755      Args(l_args),
8756      l_props.clone(),
8757      l_meta.clone(),
8758    )));
8759  }
8760
8761  Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
8762    op.into(),
8763    Args(vec![left, right]),
8764    XProps::default(),
8765    Meta::default(),
8766  )))
8767}

8769pub fn compound_operator_2(
8770  _rule_id: i32,
8771  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
8772  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
8773  ctxt: ActionContext,
8774) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
8775  unp!(args => op1, op2);
8776  // invisible comma:
8777  let comma = invisible_comma();
8778  // TODO: We need to extend that rule to the n-ary case
8779  // Currently following the original MathGrammar and creating a List XMDual
8780  new_list(vec![op1.unwrap(), comma.into(), op2.unwrap()], ctxt)
8781}

8783pub fn new_props(
8784  meaning: Option<Cow<'static, str>>,
8785  content: Option<Cow<'static, str>>,
8786  props_opt: Option<HashMap<&'static str, Cow<'static, str>>>,
8787) -> XProps {
8788  let mut props = props_opt.unwrap_or_default();
8789  let role = props.remove("role");
8790  let name = props.remove("name");
8791  let id = props.remove("id");
8792  let idref = props.remove("idref");
8793  let fontref = props.remove("_font");
8794  let scriptpos = props.remove("scriptpos");
8795  // TODO: explicit "font" prop path not yet wired — current callers never
8796  // pass it. If ever hit, fall through to the content-based specialization
8797  // (same as None), which is an approximation but won't crash.
8798  let font = match props.remove("font") {
8799    Some(_) | None => {
8800      if let Some(ref text) = content {
8801        if !text.is_empty() && !text.chars().all(|c| c.is_whitespace()) {
8802          font::FONT_TEXT_DEFAULT.specialize(text)
8803        } else {
8804          Font::default()
8805        }
8806      } else {
8807        Font::default()
8808      }
8809    },
8810  };
8811  XProps {
8812    meaning,
8813    content,
8814    role,
8815    name,
8816    scriptpos,
8817    id,
8818    idref,
8819    fontref,
8820    font: Some(Rc::new(font)),
8821    ..Default::default()
8822  }
8823}
8824
8825pub fn new_list(mut pieces: Vec<XM>, ctxt: ActionContext) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
8826  // drop placeholder token for missing trailing punct, if any
8827  if pieces.len() > 1 {
8828    let last_meaning_opt = pieces.last().unwrap().get_token_meaning(ctxt.nodes)?;
8829    if let Some(last_meaning) = last_meaning_opt
8830      && last_meaning == "absent"
8831    {
8832      pieces.pop();
8833    }
8834  }
8835  if pieces.len() == 1 {
8836    Ok(pieces.pop())
8837  } else {
8838    let (_seps, mut items) = extract_separators(&mut pieces);
8839    Ok(Some(XM::Dual(
8840      Box::new(XM::Apply(
8841        new_props(Some(Cow::Borrowed("list")), None, None).into(),
8842        create_xmrefs(&mut items, ctxt)?.into(),
8843        XProps::default(),
8844        Meta::default(),
8845      )),
8846      Box::new(XM::Wrap(pieces, XProps::default(), Meta::default())),
8847      XProps::default(),
8848      Meta::default(),
8849    )))
8850  }
8851}
8852
8853/// Given  alternating expressions & separators (punctuation,...)
8854/// extract the separators as a concatenated string,
8855/// returning (separators, args...)
8856/// But note that the separators are never used for anything!?
8857fn extract_separators(items: &mut [XM]) -> (Vec<&mut XM>, Vec<&mut XM>) {
8858  // TODO: consider using the separators at some point, but not for now
8859  let punct = Vec::new();
8860  // `items` alternates [arg, sep, arg, sep, …, arg]; args count is
8861  // `ceil(items.len() / 2)`. Pre-size to skip Vec doublings.
8862  let mut args = Vec::with_capacity(items.len().div_ceil(2));
8863  let mut items_iter = items.iter_mut();
8864  while let Some(arg) = items_iter.next() {
8865    args.push(arg);
8866    let _discard_punct = items_iter.next();
8867  }
8868  (punct, args)
8869}
8870
8871// Some handy shorthands.
8872/// Morph a VERTBAR token to OPEN or CLOSE (or MIDDLE/PUNCT) — mirrors Perl's MorphVertbar.
8873/// For delimiter roles (OPEN, CLOSE, MIDDLE), `|` stays `|`.
8874/// For operator roles (PUNCT), `|` becomes `⁣` (U+2223 DIVIDES).
8875fn morph_vertbar(xm: XM, role: &'static str, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> XM {
8876  // Character substitution: for delimiter category keep `|` as-is.
8877  // For operator category: `|` → `⁣` (U+2223).
8878  let is_delimiter = matches!(role, "OPEN" | "CLOSE" | "MIDDLE");
8879  match xm {
8880    XM::Lexeme(lex, meta) => match lookup_lex_node(&lex, nodes) {
8881      Ok(node) => {
8882        let mut props = XProps::from(node);
8883        props.role = Some(Cow::Borrowed(role));
8884        if !is_delimiter
8885          && let Some(ref c) = props.content.clone()
8886          && c == "|"
8887        {
8888          props.content = Some(Cow::Borrowed("\u{2223}"));
8889        }
8890        XM::Token(props, meta)
8891      },
8892      _ => XM::Lexeme(lex, meta),
8893    },
8894    XM::Token(mut props, meta) => {
8895      props.role = Some(Cow::Borrowed(role));
8896      if !is_delimiter
8897        && let Some(ref c) = props.content.clone()
8898        && c == "|"
8899      {
8900        props.content = Some(Cow::Borrowed("\u{2223}"));
8901      }
8902      XM::Token(props, meta)
8903    },
8904    xm => xm,
8905  }
8906}
8907
8908/// Perl: MaybeFunction — when MATHPARSER_SPECULATE is set and an UNKNOWN token
8909/// is used as the left operand of invisible times with a delimited right side,
8910/// mark the token with possibleFunction="yes".
8911fn maybe_mark_possible_function(left: &mut Option<XM>, right: &Option<XM>, nodes: &[XMLNode]) {
8912  // Only active when MATHPARSER_SPECULATE is set. Use with_value to
8913  // avoid cloning the Stored envelope on every invisible-times probe
8914  // (runs per token in the math parser).
8915  let speculate = latexml_core::state::with_value("MATHPARSER_SPECULATE", |v| {
8916    matches!(v, Some(latexml_core::state::Stored::Bool(true)))
8917  });
8918  if !speculate {
8919    return;
8920  }
8921  // Check if right side contains delimiters (parenthesized group)
8922  let right_has_delimiters = matches!(right, Some(XM::Dual(..)) | Some(XM::Wrap(..)));
8923  if !right_has_delimiters {
8924    return;
8925  }
8926  // Navigate through XMApp wrappers to find the innermost token (matching Perl's descent)
8927  mark_inner_possible_function(left, nodes);
8928}
8929
8930fn mark_inner_possible_function(xm: &mut Option<XM>, nodes: &[XMLNode]) {
8931  match xm {
8932    Some(XM::Token(props, _)) if props.role.as_deref() == Some("UNKNOWN") => {
8933      props.possible_function = Some(Cow::Borrowed("yes"));
8934    },
8935    &mut Some(XM::Lexeme(ref lex, _)) if lex.starts_with("UNKNOWN:") => {
8936      // Lexemes are "ROLE:content:id" references to XML nodes.
8937      // Set the attribute directly on the underlying XML node.
8938      if let Some(id_str) = lex.split(':').next_back()
8939        && let Ok(id) = id_str.parse::<usize>()
8940        && id > 0
8941        && id <= nodes.len()
8942      {
8943        let mut node = nodes[id - 1].clone();
8944        let _ = node.set_attribute("possibleFunction", "yes");
8945      }
8946    },
8947    Some(XM::Apply(_, args, ..)) => {
8948      if let Some(first) = args.0.first_mut() {
8949        mark_inner_possible_function(first, nodes);
8950      }
8951    },
8952    _ => {},
8953  }
8954}

8956/// Check if an XM NUMBER has integer content (no decimal point)
8957fn is_integer_number(xm: &Option<XM>) -> bool {
8958  match xm {
8959    Some(XM::Token(props, _)) => {
8960      props.role.as_deref() == Some("NUMBER")
8961        && props.meaning.as_ref().is_none_or(|m| !m.contains('.'))
8962    },
8963    Some(XM::Lexeme(lex, _)) => lex.starts_with("NUMBER:") && !lex.contains('.'),
8964    _ => false,
8965  }
8966}

8968fn is_number(xm: &Option<XM>) -> bool {
8969  match xm {
8970    Some(XM::Token(props, _)) => props.role.as_deref() == Some("NUMBER"),
8971    Some(XM::Lexeme(lex, _)) => lex.starts_with("NUMBER:"),
8972    _ => false,
8973  }
8974}

8976/// Find the DOM node for a fraction from an XM tree
8977fn find_fracop_node<'a>(
8978  xm: &Option<XM>,
8979  nodes: &'a [libxml::tree::Node],
8980) -> Option<&'a libxml::tree::Node> {
8981  // Try via Lexeme curry_level (node index)
8982  let meta = match xm {
8983    Some(XM::Lexeme(_, m)) => Some(m),
8984    Some(XM::Apply(_, _, _, m)) => Some(m),
8985    _ => None,
8986  };
8987  if let Some(meta) = meta {
8988    if let Some(ref cv) = meta.curry_level {
8989      let cv_str = cv.to_string();
8990      if let Some(idx_str) = cv_str.strip_prefix(':')
8991        && let Ok(lex_idx) = idx_str.parse::<usize>()
8992      {
8993        let idx = if lex_idx > 0 { lex_idx - 1 } else { 0 };
8994        if idx < nodes.len() && nodes[idx].get_name() == "XMApp" {
8995          return Some(&nodes[idx]);
8996        }
8997      }
8998    }
8999    // Try via Lexeme content: "ROLE:meaning:N" → index N-1
9000    if let Some(XM::Lexeme(lex, _)) = xm
9001      && let Some(idx_str) = lex.rsplit(':').next()
9002      && let Ok(lex_idx) = idx_str.parse::<usize>()
9003    {
9004      let idx = if lex_idx > 0 { lex_idx - 1 } else { 0 };
9005      if idx < nodes.len() && nodes[idx].get_name() == "XMApp" {
9006        return Some(&nodes[idx]);
9007      }
9008    }
9009  }
9010  None
9011}

9013fn is_fracop(xm: &Option<XM>) -> bool {
9014  match xm {
9015    Some(XM::Apply(op, ..)) => {
9016      if let XM::Token(props, _) = &*op.0 {
9017        props.role.as_deref() == Some("FRACOP")
9018      } else if let XM::Lexeme(lex, _) = &*op.0 {
9019        lex.starts_with("FRACOP:")
9020      } else {
9021        false
9022      }
9023    },
9024    _ => false,
9025  }
9026}

9038/// An invisible-times product whose last factor is a bare ellipsis (`b\cdots`) that elides the operation before it
9039/// (`infix_apply_and_elide`) — not one after a head or its bare application, which the ellipsis reaches
9040/// (`reaches_a_following_ellipsis`: `a+\sin x\cdots` a + sin@(x)·⋯, 57cj.13 review), nor the last of a run of them,
9041/// which elides no operation (`ends_an_elided_run`: `a+x\cdots\cdots+c` a + x·⋯·⋯ + c, as Perl).
9042fn ends_in_a_bare_ellipsis(xm: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
9043  matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), _, meta)
9044    if meta.fenced.is_none()
9045      && matches!(&**op, XM::Token(props, _) if props.content.as_deref() == Some("\u{2062}"))
9046      && matches!(args.as_slice(), [.., Some(before), Some(last)]
9047        if operator_category(last) == Some("ELIDEOP")
9048          && !ends_an_elided_run(before, ctxt)
9049          && !reaches_a_following_ellipsis(product_end(before, true))))
9050}
9051
9052/// Does `xm` end in an ellipsis, an ELIDEOP or an ID, so that an ELIDEOP after it continues a run of ellipses, any mix,
9053/// rather than eliding the operation before the run? The run is one unit, a product of its ellipses (as `trig_ellipses`
9054/// reads it in a trig argument): `a+x\cdots\cdots+c` is a + x·⋯·⋯ + c, `a+\cdots\cdots\cdots+c` a + ⋯·⋯·⋯ + c and
9055/// `a+x\ldots\cdots+c` a + x·…·⋯ + c, as Perl — refused as a bare ellipsis (`ends_in_a_bare_ellipsis`) and as the
9056/// elided addition (`infix_apply_and_elide`: its twin a + x·⋯ + ⋯) the first two had no parse, and the elided addition
9057/// took the last run apart, a + x·… + ⋯ (57cj.16 ellipsis grid).
9058fn ends_an_elided_run(xm: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
9059  is_ellipsis(product_end(xm, true), ctxt)
9060}
