9088/// Check if an XM node is a bigop or a scripted bigop (at any depth).
9089/// e.g. ∫, ∫_0, ∫_0^∞, {}_a^b∫_c^d — all contain a bigop at the base.
9090fn is_bigop_or_scripted_bigop(xm: &XM, nodes: &[libxml::tree::Node]) -> bool {
9091  match xm {
9092    XM::Token(props, _) => {
9093      matches!(
9094        props.role.as_deref(),
9095        Some("INTOP") | Some("BIGOP") | Some("SUMOP") | Some("LIMITOP") | Some("DIFFOP")
9096      )
9097    },
9098    XM::Lexeme(lex_id, _) => {
9099      matches!(
9100        get_lexeme_role(lex_id, nodes).as_deref(),
9101        Some("INTOP") | Some("BIGOP") | Some("SUMOP") | Some("LIMITOP") | Some("DIFFOP")
9102      )
9103    },
9104    // A differential is a finished factor (`Meta::differential`): `\int_0^1 dx\,f` is
9105    // ∫(d@(x)·f), its `d` no big operator absorbing `f`, and a differential operator's application
9106    // (`\partial_x u\,v` (∂_x u)·v); a big operator's application only through its operand:
9107    // `\partial_t\int_\Omega u\,dx` is ∂_t(∫(u dx)), not (∂_t∫u)·dx (divergence #374).
9108    XM::Apply(_, args, _, meta) if meta.differential => args
9109      .0
9110      .first()
9111      .and_then(Option::as_ref)
9112      .is_some_and(|operand| is_bigop_or_scripted_bigop(operand, nodes)),
9113    XM::Apply(op, args, ..) => {
9114      let op_role = get_operator_role(op, nodes);
9115      // Direct bigop application: Apply(INTOP, ...)
9116      if matches!(
9117        op_role.as_deref(),
9118        Some("INTOP") | Some("BIGOP") | Some("SUMOP") | Some("LIMITOP") | Some("DIFFOP")
9119      ) {
9120        return true;
9121      }
9122      // Scripted: Apply(SUBSCRIPTOP/SUPERSCRIPTOP, base, script)
9123      // Recursively check the base (first arg)
9124      if matches!(
9125        op_role.as_deref(),
9126        Some("SUBSCRIPTOP")
9127          | Some("SUPERSCRIPTOP")
9128          | Some("POSTSUBSCRIPT")
9129          | Some("POSTSUPERSCRIPT")
9130      ) && let Some(Some(base)) = args.0.first()
9131      {
9132        return is_bigop_or_scripted_bigop(base, nodes);
9133      }
9134      false
9135    },
9136    _ => false,
9137  }
9138}
9139
9140/// Check if an XM node is a scripted function head: Apply(SCRIPTOP, FUNCTION_base, script)
9141/// at any nesting depth. e.g. f^2, f', f_n, sin^2 — all have a FUNCTION at the base.
9142fn is_scripted_function_head(xm: &XM, nodes: &[libxml::tree::Node]) -> bool {
9143  match xm {
9144    // A bare function token is not "scripted" — handled by the earlier check
9145    XM::Token(..) | XM::Lexeme(..) => false,
9146    XM::Apply(op, args, ..) => {
9147      let op_role = get_operator_role(op, nodes);
9148      // Must be a script operator (SUBSCRIPTOP, SUPERSCRIPTOP, etc.)
9149      if matches!(
9150        op_role.as_deref(),
9151        Some("SUBSCRIPTOP")
9152          | Some("SUPERSCRIPTOP")
9153          | Some("POSTSUBSCRIPT")
9154          | Some("POSTSUPERSCRIPT")
9155      ) {
9156        // Check the base (first arg) — is it a FUNCTION or another scripted function?
9157        if let Some(Some(base)) = args.0.first() {
9158          return is_function_role_item(base, nodes) || is_scripted_function_head(base, nodes);
9159        }
9160      }
9161      false
9162    },
9163    _ => false,
9164  }
9165}
9166
9167/// Check if an XM item has a FUNCTION/OPFUNCTION/TRIGFUNCTION role.
9168fn is_function_role_item(xm: &XM, nodes: &[libxml::tree::Node]) -> bool {
9169  matches!(
9170    operator_role(xm, nodes).as_deref(),
9171    Some("FUNCTION") | Some("OPFUNCTION") | Some("TRIGFUNCTION")
9172  )
9173}
9174
9175/// The category an item is headed by, as Perl's operand patterns match it: a token's (a lexeme's
9176/// lexer category, a token's role); a decorated operator's role; a scripted item's base's; an
9177/// application's operator's; a function application's (an `XMDual`) presentation's.
9178fn head_category(xm: &XM) -> Option<&str> {
9179  match xm {
9180    XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..) => operator_category(xm),
9181    XM::Apply(_, _, props, _) if props.role.is_some() => props.role.as_deref(),
9182    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) => {
9183      let category = head_category(op)?;
9184      if category.ends_with("SCRIPTOP") {
9185        args
9186          .0
9187          .first()
9188          .and_then(Option::as_ref)
9189          .and_then(head_category)
9190      } else {
9191        Some(category)
9192      }
9193    },
9194    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) => head_category(presentation),
9195    _ => None,
9196  }
9197}
9198
9199/// Is `xm` a scripted item, `Apply(SCRIPTOP, [base, script])`? Its base, if so.
9200fn script_base(xm: &XM) -> Option<&XM> {
9201  match xm {
9202    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..)
9203      if operator_category(op).is_some_and(|c| c.ends_with("SCRIPTOP")) =>
9204    {
9205      args.0.first().and_then(Option::as_ref)
9206    },
9207    _ => None,
9208  }
9209}
9210
9211/// The base under every script of `xm` — `(y_j)` in `(y_j)_{j=1}^{n}` — `xm` itself when unscripted.
9212pub(crate) fn script_nucleus(xm: &XM) -> &XM {
9213  match script_base(xm) {
9214    Some(base) => script_nucleus(base),
9215    None => xm,
9216  }
9217}
9218
9219/// Perl `aBarearg` (MathGrammar:323-331), an operand an operator or OPFUNCTION takes without
9220/// parentheses: a function (bare, scripted or applied), an atom, identifier, unknown or number
9221/// (scripted or not), an unknown applied to its group (Perl's `doubtArgs` leaves the `(`; divergence
9222/// #18 applies it), or an absolute value `|…|`; scripted or postfixed (Perl's `addScripts` takes
9223/// POSTFIX, MathGrammar:423). Not a parenthesized group, an operator or big operator.
9224fn is_bare_item(xm: &XM) -> bool {
9225  if let Some(base) = script_base(xm).or_else(|| postfix_base(xm)) {
9226    return is_bare_item(base);
9227  }
9228  match xm {
9229    XM::Dual(_, presentation, _, meta) if matches!(**presentation, XM::Wrap(..)) => {
9230      meta.bar_fence || is_bare_abs(presentation)
9231    },
9232    XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..) => matches!(
9233      operator_category(xm),
9234      Some(
9235        "UNKNOWN"
9236          | "XDIFFUNK"
9237          | "ID"
9238          | "XDIFFID"
9239          | "ATOM"
9240          | "NUMBER"
9241          | "ARRAY"
9242          | "FUNCTION"
9243          | "OPFUNCTION"
9244          | "TRIGFUNCTION"
9245          // Perl's `\cdots` is an ID (divergence #3 keeps ELIDEOP): an ellipsis in a bare argument,
9246          // `\max_{m}|a||b|\cdots|c|` (57bx, 2605.23673).
9247          | "ELIDEOP"
9248      )
9249    ),
9250    // A partial derivative, a finished factor (57cj review: `\nabla\partial_x u` ∇@(∂_x u)).
9251    XM::Apply(..) if is_partial_derivative(xm) => true,
9252    // An unknown applied to its group is Perl's `doubtArgs` as divergence #18 reads it.
9253    XM::Apply(..) | XM::Dual(..) => matches!(
9254      head_category(xm),
9255      Some("FUNCTION" | "OPFUNCTION" | "TRIGFUNCTION" | "UNKNOWN" | "XDIFFUNK")
9256    ),
9257    _ => false,
9258  }
9259}
9260
9261/// A group `bare_abs` builds (Perl `VERTBAR absExpression VERTBAR`, MathGrammar:329-330), read by
9262/// its delimiters where the fence carries no `Meta::bar_fence` mark: VERTBARs — `|…|`, `\|…\|`,
9263/// `\left|…\right|`, `\left\|…\right\|`, morphed to OPEN/CLOSE by the fence (`morph_vertbar`) —
9264/// not an OPEN/CLOSE of its own such as amsmath's `\lvert`/`\rvert` (amsmath.sty.ltxml:1150-1153).
9265fn is_bare_abs(wrap: &XM) -> bool {
9266  let XM::Wrap(items, ..) = wrap else {
9267    return false;
9268  };
9269  let is_bar = |item: Option<&XM>| match item {
9270    Some(bar @ XM::Lexeme(..)) => matches!(
9271      operator_category(bar),
9272      Some("VERTBAR" | "LEFT_STRETCHY_VERTBAR" | "RIGHT_STRETCHY_VERTBAR")
9273    ),
9274    // A `‖` is a bar as `\|` or `\left\|` (`name="||"`); the norm merged from two `|`s,
9275    // `||v||`, is one by its mark (divergence #353).
9276    Some(XM::Token(props, _)) => match props.content.as_deref() {
9277      Some("|") => !matches!(props.name.as_deref(), Some("lvert" | "rvert")),
9278      Some("‖") => props.name.as_deref() == Some("||"),
9279      _ => false,
9280    },
9281    _ => false,
9282  };
9283  is_bar(items.first()) && is_bar(items.last())
9284}
9285
9286/// Is `op` what joins the factors of a product (Perl `moreFactors`, `moreBareargs`, MathGrammar:
9287/// 252-265, :333-337): a MulOp — a MULOP or BINOP, bare or decorated — or the invisible times?
9288fn is_product_operator(op: &XM) -> bool { matches!(operator_category(op), Some("MULOP" | "BINOP")) }
9289
9290/// The first (`last` false) or last factor of a product, `xm` itself when it is none.
9291fn product_end(xm: &XM, last: bool) -> &XM {
9292  match xm {
9293    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) if args.0.len() >= 2 && is_product_operator(op) => {
9294      let end = if last { args.0.last() } else { args.0.first() };
9295      match end {
9296        Some(Some(factor)) => product_end(factor, last),
9297        _ => xm,
9298      }
9299    },
9300    _ => xm,
9301  }
9302}
9303
9304/// Perl `barearg` (MathGrammar:321): one `aBarearg`, or a product of them.
9305fn is_bare_argument(xm: &XM) -> bool {
9306  match xm {
9307    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) if args.0.len() >= 2 && is_product_operator(op) => args
9308      .0
9309      .iter()
9310      .all(|factor| factor.as_ref().is_some_and(is_bare_argument)),
9311    _ => is_bare_item(xm),
9312  }
9313}
9314
9315/// Perl `OPERATOR addScripts nestOperators` (MathGrammar:312-313, :663-671): an OPERATOR, scripted
9316/// or not, or one nested over a function or another operator — what applies to an argument.
9317fn is_operator_head(xm: &XM) -> bool {
9318  if let Some(base) = script_base(xm) {
9319    return is_operator_head(base);
9320  }
9321  match xm {
9322    XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..) => operator_category(xm) == Some("OPERATOR"),
9323    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) => is_nested_operator(op, args),
9324    _ => false,
9325  }
9326}
9327
9328/// Is `op` applied to `args` an operator nested over a function, scripted or not, or an operator
9329/// (Perl `nestOperators`, MathGrammar:663-671; `compound_operator`)? Only an open nest nests: after
9330/// a function it is closed.
9331fn is_nested_operator(op: &XM, args: &Args) -> bool {
9332  nest_is_open(op)
9333    && matches!(args.0.as_slice(), [Some(nested)]
9334      if is_operator_head(nested) || is_function_head(nested))
9335}
9336
9337/// Is `xm` a head that takes the arguments between delimiters — a function or an operator, bare,
9338/// scripted or nested over a function or an operator (`prefix_apply`'s lift, 57bf):
9339/// `\nabla\log(p,q)` `(nabla@(logarithm))@(p, q)` as Perl (`OPERATOR addScripts nestOperators
9340/// addOpFunArgs`, MathGrammar:312-313; 57bf review).
9341fn takes_delimited_arguments(xm: &XM) -> bool {
9342  match script_base(xm) {
9343    Some(base) => takes_delimited_arguments(base),
9344    None => match xm {
9345      XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..) => matches!(
9346        operator_category(xm),
9347        Some("FUNCTION" | "OPFUNCTION" | "TRIGFUNCTION" | "OPERATOR")
9348      ),
9349      XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) => is_nested_operator(op, args),
9350      // … or a bare or scripted operator's application to one group, which applies to the next group
9351      // too: `D(a)(b)` (D@(a))@(b), Perl's ApplyDelimited Dual (57bl; 2605.01526
9352      // `\nabla(F\circ\gamma)(w)`).
9353      XM::Dual(..) => is_operator_group_application(xm),
9354      _ => false,
9355    },
9356  }
9357}
9358
9359/// A bare or scripted OPERATOR, not a nest (`D`, `\nabla_x`), whose application to a group applies to
9360/// the next group (57bl).
9361pub(crate) fn is_bare_or_scripted_operator(xm: &XM) -> bool {
9362  match script_base(xm) {
9363    Some(base) => is_bare_or_scripted_operator(base),
9364    None => {
9365      matches!(xm, XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..)) && operator_category(xm) == Some("OPERATOR")
9366    },
9367  }
9368}
9369
9370/// A function, with its scripts (Perl `FUNCTION addScripts`, and likewise OPFUNCTION and
9371/// TRIGFUNCTION), not applied.
9372fn is_function_head(xm: &XM) -> bool {
9373  match script_base(xm) {
9374    Some(base) => is_function_head(base),
9375    None => {
9376      matches!(xm, XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..))
9377        && matches!(
9378          operator_category(xm),
9379          Some("FUNCTION" | "OPFUNCTION" | "TRIGFUNCTION")
9380        )
9381    },
9382  }
9383}
9384
9385/// Perl `addOpFunArgs : APPLYOP(?) barearg` (MathGrammar:553-558): an operator or an OPFUNCTION,
9386/// scripted or not, applied to a bare argument.
9387fn is_bare_operator_application(xm: &XM) -> bool {
9388  matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..)
9389    if (is_operator_head(op) && !is_nested_operator(op, args) || is_opfunction_head(op))
9390      && matches!(args.0.as_slice(), [Some(arg)]
9391        if is_bare_argument(arg) && !(nest_is_open(op) && is_closed_expectation_application(arg))))
9392}
9393
9394/// An expectation's or probability's application that is no bare application — to a group, with
9395/// its scripts: `𝔼[X]`, `𝔼_x(f)`, `𝔼[X]^2`. An operator takes it whole (`open_op_head expectation_application`),
9396/// and it ends the operator's argument as a group does: `\nabla\mathbb{E}[X]Y` is ∇@(𝔼@(X))·Y,
9397/// `\alpha_t\nabla^\top_{x_t}\mathbb{E}[x|x_t]\Sigma_t^{-1}` α_t·∇@(𝔼@(x | x_t))·Σ_t⁻¹ (2605.20593).
9398fn is_closed_expectation_application(xm: &XM) -> bool {
9399  let application = match script_nucleus(xm) {
9400    // a group application: the presentation holds the lexeme
9401    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) => presentation.as_ref(),
9402    nucleus => nucleus,
9403  };
9404  matches!(application, XM::Apply(Operator(op), ..) if is_expectation_operator(op))
9405    && !is_bare_operator_application(application)
9406}
9407
9408/// An operator's application, as the grammar builds it or as `prefix_apply` lifts it over the
9409/// delimiters it takes its arguments between (a Dual presenting the application, 57bf).
9410fn is_operator_application(xm: &XM) -> bool {
9411  let application = match xm {
9412    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) => presentation,
9413    _ => xm,
9414  };
9415  // … or of an operator's application to the next group, `\log\nabla(u)(v)` log·(∇@(u))@(v) as Perl
9416  // (57bl review).
9417  matches!(application, XM::Apply(Operator(op), ..)
9418    if is_operator_head(op) || is_operator_group_application(op))
9419}
9420
9421/// An OPFUNCTION, scripted or not, not applied (Perl `preScripted['OPFUNCTION']`).
9422fn is_opfunction_head(xm: &XM) -> bool {
9423  match script_base(xm) {
9424    Some(base) => is_opfunction_head(base),
9425    None => {
9426      matches!(xm, XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..)) && operator_category(xm) == Some("OPFUNCTION")
9427    },
9428  }
9429}
9430
9431/// Perl's `barearg` is greedy (MathGrammar:321-337): an operator or OPFUNCTION applied to a bare
9432/// argument takes every bare argument after it, so a product `left · right` leaving one outside
9433/// the application that ends `left` is not a parse — `\nabla u v` is ∇@(u v), `a\nabla u\cdot v`
9434/// a·∇@(u·v), `\log x y` log@(x y), `\max_i a_i\cdot b_i` max_i@(a_i·b_i) — nor one leaving outside a
9435/// later OPFUNCTION's application that a bound head's argument takes (`bound_head_takes`, 57cg):
9436/// `\max_i a_i\log b_i` is max_i@(a_i·log@(b_i)).
9437fn leaves_a_bare_argument(left: &XM, right: &XM, join: Option<&XM>, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
9438  let juxtaposed = join.is_none();
9439  // … the one factor a differential operator takes too: `\partial\log x\cdot y` is ∂(log(x·y)) (#374)
9440  let application = through_differentials(product_end(left, true));
9441  // An ellipsis after a bare application stays inside it before a continuation item (`op_bare_elided`,
9442  // 57cb): `\log x\cdots y` is log@(x·⋯·y), not log@(x)·⋯·y; `\ldots` alike — and a run of them, whatever the
9443  // macros (`op_bare_elided` goes on over an ELIDEOP, an ID is a bare item): `\log x\cdots\cdots y` log@(x·⋯·⋯·y),
9444  // `\log\ldots\ldots\cdots x` log@(…·…·⋯·x), as Perl (57cj.14 review; was log@(x)·⋯·⋯·y).
9445  // The run may open `right` too, wherever the product splits it: a MulOp's right operand is a juxtaposed product
9446  // (`term mulop tight_term`), so `\log x\cdot\cdots y` derived (log@(x)·⋯)·y beside log@((x·⋯)·y), both surviving —
9447  // `\sin x\cdot\cdots y`, `\sin\ldots\cdot\cdots x`, `\nabla u\cdot\cdots v`, `\max_i a_i\times\cdots b`, `\sin x\cdot\cdots\ldots`
9448  // alike, 2^n readings at n sites (57cj.17 review; latent, no corpus witness). So the question is asked at every
9449  // junction the juxtaposed product would have: the split itself, and each one inside the right's opening run up to its
9450  // first other factor — the run there the left's trailing ellipses and the right's opening ones before it.
9451  let right_factors = product_factors(right);
9452  let opening = right_factors
9453    .iter()
9454    .take_while(|factor| is_ellipsis(factor, ctxt))
9455    .count();
9456  let mut factors = product_factors(left);
9457  let ends_in_an_ellipsis = is_ellipsis(application, ctxt);
9458  // (a run across an operator that ends a trig function's bare argument, the join or one before the left's own run, is
9459  // no trig argument's: `\sin x\boxast\cdots\boxast y` ⧆(sin x, ⋯, y), `ends_a_trig_bare_argument`)
9460  let across_a_trig_end = join.is_some_and(|op| ends_a_trig_bare_argument(op, ctxt))
9461    || ends_in_an_ellipsis && ends_a_trig_bare_argument_before_its_run(left, ctxt);
9462  if ends_in_an_ellipsis
9463    && a_run_stays_inside(&factors, product_end(right, false), across_a_trig_end, ctxt)
9464  {
9465    return true;
9466  }
9467  for junction in 1..=opening.min(right_factors.len().saturating_sub(1)) {
9468    factors.push(right_factors[junction - 1]);
9469    if a_run_stays_inside(&factors, right_factors[junction], across_a_trig_end, ctxt) {
9470      return true;
9471    }
9472  }
9473  if ends_in_an_ellipsis {
9474    return false;
9475  }
9476  // After a bare function head that ends the argument (`\log\mathbb E_y`), what that head would take
9477  // as its first item — a function's application too — is its argument, not a factor after:
9478  // `\log\mathbb E_y\exp(x)` is log@(𝔼_y@(exp(x))) (57cb).
9479  let first = product_end(right, false);
9480  if bound_head_takes(application, first, ctxt) {
9481    return true;
9482  }
9483  // An expectation's bare argument takes a derivative after it (`expectation_bare_arg`, user ruling 2026-10-01):
9484  // `\mathbb{E}\partial_\theta\log p\,\partial_\theta\log p^\top` has no 𝔼(∂_θ log p)·∂_θ log p^⊤
9485  // (… down the right edge's bare applications: `\nabla\mathbb{E}\partial_x u\,\partial_y v` ∇(𝔼(∂_x u·∂_y v)))
9486  // (a derivative, not an integral's differential: `\int_0^T\mathbb{E}|Y(s)|\,\mathrm{d}s` keeps ∫(𝔼(|Y(s)|)·ds), 2605.13204)
9487  if is_differential(first)
9488    && !matches!(first, XM::Apply(Operator(head), ..) if is_a_differential(script_nucleus(head), ctxt))
9489  {
9490    let mut edge = application;
9491    while let Some((head, argument)) = bare_application(edge) {
9492      if is_expectation_operator(head) {
9493        return true;
9494      }
9495      edge = product_end(argument, true);
9496    }
9497  }
9498  let takes = if is_bare_function_head(last_bare_leaf(application)) {
9499    is_bare_item(first)
9500  } else {
9501    is_bare_continuation(first, ctxt)
9502  };
9503  is_bare_operator_application(application)
9504    && (takes
9505      // What the bare argument's last item would take right after it, not across a MulOp
9506      // (`\log p\cdot(R-B)` is log@(p)·(R−B)).
9507      || juxtaposed && takes_the_group(last_bare_leaf(application), right, ctxt))
9508}
9509
9510/// Is the ellipsis run ending `left` joined to the factor before it, or within itself, by an operator that ends a trig
9511/// function's bare argument (`ends_a_trig_bare_argument`; `leaves_a_bare_argument`)? `left`'s factors as `product_factors`
9512/// flattens them, each with the operator it joined by: `⧆(sin x, ⋯)` yes, `(sin x ⊗ …)·…` yes, `(sin x)·⋯` and
9513/// `⧆(a, (sin x)·⋯)` no.
9514fn ends_a_trig_bare_argument_before_its_run(left: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
9515  let mut joins = Vec::new();
9516  product_factor_joins(left, None, &mut joins);
9517  joins
9518    .iter()
9519    .rev()
9520    .take_while(|(_, factor)| is_ellipsis(factor, ctxt))
9521    .any(|(join, _)| join.is_some_and(|op| ends_a_trig_bare_argument(op, ctxt)))
9522}
9523
9524/// `product_factors` with the operator each factor joined the product by (None for the first).
9525fn product_factor_joins<'a>(
9526  xm: &'a XM,
9527  join: Option<&'a XM>,
9528  out: &mut Vec<(Option<&'a XM>, &'a XM)>,
9529) {
9530  match xm {
9531    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), _, meta)
9532      if meta.fenced.is_none() && args.len() >= 2 && is_product_operator(op) =>
9533    {
9534      for (k, arg) in args.iter().flatten().enumerate() {
9535        product_factor_joins(arg, if k == 0 { join } else { Some(op) }, out);
9536      }
9537    },
9538    _ => out.push((join, xm)),
9539  }
9540}
9541
9542/// Does an ellipsis run ending `factors` (a product's, in order) stay inside the bare application before it, so that
9543/// `item` after the run goes on that application's argument rather than multiplying it (`leaves_a_bare_argument`)? An
9544/// OPFUNCTION's or operator's bare application takes a continuation item (`op_bare_elided`), an OPFUNCTION's chain
9545/// ending a trig function's argument one other than a trig function's application (`trig_op_bare_elided`), and a trig
9546/// function's own bare application an item it chains (`trig_elided`) — where nothing ends the argument.
9547fn a_run_stays_inside(
9548  factors: &[&XM],
9549  item: &XM,
9550  across_a_trig_end: bool,
9551  ctxt: &ActionContext,
9552) -> bool {
9553  let run = factors
9554    .iter()
9555    .rev()
9556    .take_while(|factor| is_ellipsis(factor, ctxt))
9557    .count();
9558  if factors.len() <= run {
9559    return false;
9560  }
9561  // … through the one factor a differential operator takes, as `leaves_a_bare_argument` looks (#374):
9562  // `\partial\log x\ldots y` is ∂(log(x·…·y)), `\partial\nabla u\cdots v` ∂(∇(u·⋯·v)), as Perl and as
9563  // `\partial\log x\cdot y` ∂(log(x·y)), not ∂(log x)·…·y (57cj.18 review; latent, no corpus witness)
9564  let before = through_differentials(product_end(factors[factors.len() - run - 1], true));
9565  is_bare_continuation(item, ctxt)
9566    && (is_bare_operator_application(before)
9567      // … an OPFUNCTION's application ending a trig function's argument too, whose chain goes on over the run
9568      // (`trig_op_bare_elided`) to an item other than a trig function's application (`op_bare_plain_next`):
9569      // `\sin\log x\cdots y` is sin@(log@(x·⋯·y)), as Perl, not sin@(log@(x))·⋯·y — the two trees left the
9570      // reading to the forest's order, which a second site flipped (57cj.16 ellipsis grid)
9571      || !across_a_trig_end
9572        && trig_argument_ending_in_an_opfunction_application(before, ctxt).is_some_and(|argument| {
9573        !is_trig_application(item)
9574          // (… where nothing ends the trig argument, `ends_trig_argument`: a space, `\sin\log x\,\cdots\,y`
9575          // keeps sin@(log@(x))·⋯·y; a `d`; a symbol of another type, `\sin\log x\cdots\mathbf y`)
9576          && !factors[factors.len() - run - 1..]
9577            .iter()
9578            .any(|factor| ends_with_space(factor, ctxt.nodes))
9579          && !ends_trig_argument(&product_factors(argument), item, ctxt)
9580      }))
9581    // … and a trig function's own bare application before the run, whose argument goes on over it (`trig_elided`)
9582    // to an item it chains (`is_trig_bare_item`; not a trig function's application, `\cos\theta_1\cdots\cos\theta_n`):
9583    // `\sin x\cdots y` is sin@(x·⋯·y), as `\sin x\ldots y` sin@(x·…·y) and Perl, not sin@(x)·⋯·y (57cj.16 review) —
9584    // where nothing ends the argument, the questions `trig_argument_elision` asks of the run and the item
9585    || !across_a_trig_end
9586      && trig_argument_before_a_run(before).is_some_and(|argument| {
9587      let mut run_factors = product_factors(argument);
9588      run_factors.extend_from_slice(&factors[factors.len() - run..]);
9589      // (another ellipsis continues the run, no item it reaches: a trailing run leaves, Q10, `\sin x\ldots\ldots`
9590      // sin(x)·…·… — unless the argument is a run itself, which the ellipsis goes on, `\sin\ldots\times\cdots\times\ldots`
9591      // sin@(…×⋯×…))
9592      is_trig_bare_item(item)
9593        && (!is_ellipsis(item, ctxt) || is_an_ellipsis_run(argument))
9594        // (not after an OPFUNCTION's or operator's application ending the argument, whose chain the run goes on —
9595        // the branch above — or leaves, `\sin\log x\cdots\dots` sin@(log@(x))·⋯·…: `trig_argument_elision`)
9596        && !ends_in_its_own_chain(argument, ctxt.nodes)
9597        && !factors[factors.len() - run - 1..]
9598          .iter()
9599          .any(|factor| ends_with_space(factor, ctxt.nodes))
9600        && !ends_trig_argument(&run_factors, item, ctxt)
9601    })
9602}
9603
9604/// The argument of a trig function's bare application that ends in an OPFUNCTION's bare application, through
9605/// compositions (`\sin\log x`, `\sin\cos\log x`, the innermost trig function's) and the ellipses the chain took already
9606/// (`\cos\log_2 x\ldots`): the chain an ellipsis run after it goes on in (`trig_op_bare_elided`).
9607fn trig_argument_ending_in_an_opfunction_application<'a>(
9608  xm: &'a XM,
9609  ctxt: &ActionContext,
9610) -> Option<&'a XM> {
9611  let XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), _, meta) = xm else {
9612    return None;
9613  };
9614  let [Some(arg)] = args.as_slice() else {
9615    return None;
9616  };
9617  if meta.fenced.is_some()
9618    || !is_bare_function_head(op)
9619    || head_category(op) != Some("TRIGFUNCTION")
9620  {
9621    return None;
9622  }
9623  let last = product_factors(arg)
9624    .into_iter()
9625    .rev()
9626    .find(|factor| !is_ellipsis(factor, ctxt))
9627    .map(|factor| product_end(factor, true))?;
9628  if is_bare_operator_application(last) && is_opfunction_application(last) {
9629    Some(arg)
9630  } else {
9631    trig_argument_ending_in_an_opfunction_application(last, ctxt)
9632  }
9633}
9634
9635/// A trig function's application, bare or not (`\cos y`, `\sin^2(x)`): no item of an OPFUNCTION's chain inside a trig
9636/// argument (`op_bare_plain_next`; juxtaposed trig functions are separate factors).
9637fn is_trig_application(xm: &XM) -> bool {
9638  matches!(xm, XM::Apply(..) | XM::Dual(..))
9639    && !is_function_head(xm)
9640    && head_category(xm) == Some("TRIGFUNCTION")
9641}
9642
9643/// Does a bound head at the end of `application` — it, or an application its bare argument ends in —
9644/// take `item`, the OPFUNCTION's application after it (`bound_application`, user ruling 2026-09-30): a
9645/// head whose subscript binds a variable `item` mentions free? Only where the grammar lets the
9646/// argument's last item extend, so the refused product always has its extended twin: through an
9647/// OPFUNCTION's, a nest's or an operator's bare argument (`op_bare_item`, `bound_item`, `compound_operator
9648/// applied_func`), where an OPFUNCTION's application stands as a `bound_item`: `\operatorname*{argmin}_w
9649/// a_w\max_i b_{iw}\log c_i` is argmin_w@(a_w·max_i@(b_iw·log c_i)) (57cg review). An operator's
9650/// argument a function's application starts ends the walk: `operator_bare_apply` refuses to extend it
9651/// (its open-nest branch, 57cd).
9652fn bound_head_takes(application: &XM, item: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
9653  if !is_opfunction_application(item) {
9654    return false;
9655  }
9656  let mut application = application;
9657  while let XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(args), ..) = application
9658    && let [Some(argument)] = args.as_slice()
9659    && is_bare_operator_application(application)
9660  {
9661    if is_bare_or_scripted_operator(head) {
9662      let first = product_end(argument, false);
9663      if matches!(
9664        head_category(postfixed_operand(first).unwrap_or(first)),
9665        Some("FUNCTION" | "OPFUNCTION" | "TRIGFUNCTION")
9666      ) {
9667        return false;
9668      }
9669    }
9670    if mentions_a_bound_variable(head, item, ctxt) {
9671      return true;
9672    }
9673    application = product_end(argument, true);
9674  }
9675  false
9676}
9677
9678/// What `bound_item` derives (grammar/builder.rs): an OPFUNCTION's application, bare, to a group, or a
9679/// group application with its scripts (`\log(n)^2`) — not a bare head (`\log_2`), nor a postfixed
9680/// application.
9681fn is_opfunction_application(xm: &XM) -> bool {
9682  matches!(xm, XM::Apply(..) | XM::Dual(..))
9683    && !is_function_head(xm)
9684    && head_category(xm) == Some("OPFUNCTION")
9685}
9686
9687/// Does `item` mention free a variable `head`'s subscript binds?
9688fn mentions_a_bound_variable(head: &XM, item: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
9689  let variables = bound_variables(head, ctxt);
9690  !variables.is_empty() && mentions_free(item, &variables, ctxt)
9691}
9692
9693/// A letter a head's subscript binds, or an occurrence of one: its text and its font class
9694/// (`token_font_mark`) — the same letter in another font is another variable, as
9695/// `letter_recurs_in_its_group` reads it (`\max_{\boldsymbol\gamma\in H}` binds a bold γ, 2605.26653).
9696type Variable = (String, Option<&'static str>);
9697
9698/// The OPFUNCTIONs whose scripts are limits, by their lexemes — the grammar's `limits_opfunction`
9699/// tokens (grammar/builder.rs): `\max`, `\min`, `\gcd`, `\Pr` (plain.tex:1073-1074, :1083-1084;
9700/// math_common.pool.ltxml:742, :759-764, `scriptpos => \&doScriptpos`, TeX_Math.pool.ltxml:350) — and
9701/// the named `argmin`/`argmax` and an expectation, whose subscript binds its variable as theirs does
9702/// (`\operatorname{argmin}_w`, `\mathbb{E}_{y\sim p}`; user ruling 2026-09-30).
9703const LIMITS_OPFUNCTIONS: [&str; 7] = [
9704  "OPFUNCTION:maximum:",
9705  "OPFUNCTION:minimum:",
9706  "OPFUNCTION:gcd:",
9707  "OPFUNCTION:Pr:",
9708  "OPFUNCTION:argmin:",
9709  "OPFUNCTION:argmax:",
9710  // (either spelling: `EXPECTATION:𝔼:` and `EXPECTATION:𝔼.letter:`, parser.rs `type_expectation_lexemes`)
9711  "EXPECTATION:\u{1D53C}",
9712];
9713
9714/// Does a head bind its subscript: its scripts are limits — TeX's `\mathop` without `\nolimits`, a
9715/// `limits_opfunction` (`LIMITS_OPFUNCTIONS`), or an operator LaTeXML gives a `scriptpos`, amsopn's
9716/// starred `\operatorname*` and `\DeclareMathOperator*` (amsopn.sty:43-45 `\qopname\newmcodes@ m`;
9717/// amsopn.sty.ltxml:23-29, :50-53)? A nolimits function's script is a base or a parameter
9718/// (`\log_a b\cdot\log_b a`, `\exp_p`, `\operatorname{rank}_K`: plain.tex:1054, :1082), an operator's
9719/// its variable of differentiation (`\nabla_x`, no `scriptpos`): neither binds.
9720fn binds_its_subscript(nucleus: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
9721  let XM::Lexeme(lex, _) = nucleus else {
9722    return false;
9723  };
9724  LIMITS_OPFUNCTIONS
9725    .iter()
9726    .any(|prefix| lex.starts_with(prefix))
9727    || operator_category(nucleus) == Some("OPERATOR")
9728      && lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes).is_ok_and(|node| {
9729        realize_xmnode(node, ctxt.document)
9730          .get_attribute("scriptpos")
9731          .is_some_and(|position| !position.is_empty())
9732      })
9733}
9734
9735/// The variables a head binds (`binds_its_subscript`): its subscripts' (`\max_{i}^{n}`: i). A subscript
9736/// binds a letter (`\max_i`), an inequality chain's interior operands (`\min_{1\le i\le n}` i), another
9737/// relation's first operand that holds one (`\min_{\mu\in\mathbb R}` μ, `\max_{S\ni M}` S, `\min_{|\mu|\le 2B}` μ,
9738/// `\max_{k\notin\{i,j\}}` k), each item of
9739/// a list (`\max_{x\in X,y\in Y}` x and y, `\max_{i,j}`), a scripted letter by its base (`\max_{x'}`,
9740/// `\min_{x_1}`: x).
9741fn bound_variables(head: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> Vec<Variable> {
9742  let mut variables = Vec::new();
9743  if binds_its_subscript(script_nucleus(head), ctxt) {
9744    subscript_variables(head, ctxt, true, &mut variables);
9745  }
9746  variables
9747}
9748
9749/// The variables an application's operator binds anew inside an item: a bound head's
9750/// (`bound_variables`) or a big operator's (`\sum_{j\in S}`) — plain letters only: a scripted binder
9751/// binds a variable of its own, not its base letter (`\mathbb{E}_{y'}` hides no y:
9752/// `\mathbb{E}_{y\sim p}\tau\log\mathbb{E}_{y'}\exp(y\cdot y')` mentions y, 2605.02116).
9753fn binder_variables(op: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> Vec<Variable> {
9754  let mut variables = Vec::new();
9755  let nucleus = script_nucleus(op);
9756  if script_base(op).is_some()
9757    && (binds_its_subscript(nucleus, ctxt)
9758      || matches!(
9759        operator_category(nucleus),
9760        Some("SUMOP" | "INTOP" | "BIGOP" | "LIMITOP")
9761      ))
9762  {
9763    subscript_variables(op, ctxt, false, &mut variables);
9764  }
9765  variables
9766}
9767
9768/// The variables of every subscript on a scripted head; a scripted letter by its base only
9769/// `with_scripted`.
9770fn subscript_variables(
9771  head: &XM,
9772  ctxt: &ActionContext,
9773  with_scripted: bool,
9774  variables: &mut Vec<Variable>,
9775) {
9776  if let XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..) = head
9777    && let [Some(base), Some(script)] = args.as_slice()
9778    && operator_category(op).is_some_and(|category| category.ends_with("SCRIPTOP"))
9779  {
9780    if operator_category(op) == Some("SUBSCRIPTOP") {
9781      script_variables(script, ctxt, with_scripted, variables);
9782    }
9783    subscript_variables(base, ctxt, with_scripted, variables);
9784  }
9785}
9786
9787/// A subscript's variables: its lexeme's node — a letter, or the formula a pre-parsed script holds
9788/// (`ATOM:∈μR`) — or, a script the formula's own parse read, every letter in it.
9789fn script_variables(
9790  script: &XM,
9791  ctxt: &ActionContext,
9792  with_scripted: bool,
9793  variables: &mut Vec<Variable>,
9794) {
9795  match script {
9796    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => {
9797      if let Ok(node) = lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes) {
9798        node_bound_variables(node, ctxt.document, with_scripted, variables);
9799      }
9800    },
9801    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..) => {
9802      script_variables(op, ctxt, with_scripted, variables);
9803      for arg in args.iter().flatten() {
9804        script_variables(arg, ctxt, with_scripted, variables);
9805      }
9806    },
9807    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) => script_variables(presentation, ctxt, with_scripted, variables),
9808    XM::Wrap(items, ..) | XM::Arg(items) | XM::Choices(items) => {
9809      for item in items {
9810        script_variables(item, ctxt, with_scripted, variables);
9811      }
9812    },
9813    XM::Token(..) | XM::Ref(..) => {},
9814  }
9815}
9816
9817/// `bound_variables` of a subscript node: an inequality chain's interior operands, another relation's
9818/// first operand that holds a letter, each item of a list, else every letter.
9819fn node_bound_variables(
9820  node: &XMLNode,
9821  document: &Document,
9822  with_scripted: bool,
9823  variables: &mut Vec<Variable>,
9824) {
9825  let node = realize_xmnode(node, document);
9826  let children = node.get_child_elements();
9827  let is_relation = |node: &XMLNode| {
9828    let node = realize_xmnode(node, document);
9829    matches!(
9830      node.get_attribute("role").as_deref(),
9831      Some("RELOP" | "ARROW")
9832    ) || node.get_attribute("meaning").as_deref() == Some("multirelation")
9833  };
9834  let is_list = |node: &XMLNode| {
9835    matches!(
9836      realize_xmnode(node, document)
9837        .get_attribute("meaning")
9838        .as_deref(),
9839      Some("list" | "formulae")
9840    )
9841  };
9842  match (node.get_name().as_str(), children.split_first()) {
9843    ("XMApp", Some((op, operands))) if is_relation(op) => {
9844      let inequalities = operands
9845        .iter()
9846        .filter(|&operand| is_relation(operand))
9847        .all(|relation| {
9848          matches!(
9849            realize_xmnode(relation, document)
9850              .get_attribute("meaning")
9851              .as_deref(),
9852            Some("less-than" | "less-than-or-equals" | "greater-than" | "greater-than-or-equals")
9853          )
9854        });
9855      let operands: Vec<&XMLNode> = operands
9856        .iter()
9857        .filter(|&operand| !is_relation(operand))
9858        .collect();
9859      // A chain of inequalities binds what it bounds on both sides, its interior operands:
9860      // `\max_{a\le x\le b}` x, `\max_{1\le i<j\le n}` i and j (57cg review); any other relation its first
9861      // operand with a letter, `\max_{i\in S}` i, `\max_{i\ne j}` i, `\max_{x\in A\subset B}` x.
9862      if inequalities && let [_, interior @ .., _] = operands.as_slice() {
9863        let before = variables.len();
9864        for operand in interior {
9865          node_letters(operand, document, with_scripted, variables);
9866        }
9867        if variables.len() > before {
9868          return;
9869        }
9870      }
9871      for operand in operands {
9872        let before = variables.len();
9873        node_letters(operand, document, with_scripted, variables);
9874        if variables.len() > before {
9875          break;
9876        }
9877      }
9878    },
9879    ("XMApp", Some((op, operands))) if is_list(op) => {
9880      for operand in operands {
9881        node_bound_variables(operand, document, with_scripted, variables);
9882      }
9883    },
9884    // a list of relations presents its items; its content lists them (`formulae@(x∈X, y∈Y)`)
9885    ("XMDual", Some((content, _))) => {
9886      node_bound_variables(content, document, with_scripted, variables)
9887    },
9888    _ => node_letters(&node, document, with_scripted, variables),
9889  }
9890}
9891
9892/// Every letter of a node, a scripted item by its base `with_scripted` (`x_i`, `x'`: x; `|\mu|` μ;
9893/// `(i,j)` i and j).
9894fn node_letters(
9895  node: &XMLNode,
9896  document: &Document,
9897  with_scripted: bool,
9898  letters: &mut Vec<Variable>,
9899) {
9900  let node = realize_xmnode(node, document);
9901  let children = node.get_child_elements();
9902  match (node.get_name().as_str(), children.as_slice()) {
9903    ("XMTok", _) => letters.extend(node_letter(&node, document)),
9904    ("XMApp", [op, base, _]) if is_script_node(op, document) => {
9905      if with_scripted {
9906        node_letters(base, document, with_scripted, letters)
9907      }
9908    },
9909    ("XMDual", [_, presentation]) => node_letters(presentation, document, with_scripted, letters),
9910    (_, children) => {
9911      for child in children {
9912        node_letters(child, document, with_scripted, letters);
9913      }
9914    },
9915  }
9916}
9917
9918/// A token node's letter: one alphabetic character of an unknown or identifier (`\mu`,
9919/// `\boldsymbol\gamma`, `\mathcal D`) — not a number, an operator, or a name (`max`).
9920fn node_letter(node: &XMLNode, document: &Document) -> Option<Variable> {
9921  if node.get_name() != "XMTok"
9922    || !matches!(
9923      node.get_attribute("role").as_deref(),
9924      None | Some("UNKNOWN" | "ID")
9925    )
9926  {
9927    return None;
9928  }
9929  let text = node.get_content();
9930  let letter = {
9931    let mut chars = text.chars();
9932    chars.next().is_some_and(char::is_alphabetic) && chars.next().is_none()
9933  };
9934  letter.then(|| (text, token_font_mark(node, document)))
9935}
9936
9937/// A sub- or superscript operator node.
9938fn is_script_node(op: &XMLNode, document: &Document) -> bool {
9939  matches!(
9940    realize_xmnode(op, document)
9941      .get_attribute("role")
9942      .as_deref(),
9943    Some("SUBSCRIPTOP" | "SUPERSCRIPTOP")
9944  )
9945}
9946
9947/// Does `xm` mention one of `variables` free — the letter in its font anywhere in it, a script's too
9948/// (`\log b_i` mentions i), but not where a bound head or a big operator in it binds the letter anew:
9949/// `\max_{z\in A}|f(z)|\max_{z\in A}|g(z)|`, the second max's z is its own (2605.24231), while
9950/// `\max_{j\le i}` mentions i. Every choice of an ambiguous item must.
9951fn mentions_free(xm: &XM, variables: &[Variable], ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
9952  match xm {
9953    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes)
9954      .is_ok_and(|node| node_mentions_free(node, variables, ctxt.document)),
9955    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..) => {
9956      let rebound = binder_variables(op, ctxt);
9957      let free: Vec<Variable> = variables
9958        .iter()
9959        .filter(|variable| !rebound.contains(variable))
9960        .cloned()
9961        .collect();
9962      !free.is_empty()
9963        && (mentions_free(op, &free, ctxt)
9964          || args
9965            .iter()
9966            .flatten()
9967            .any(|arg| mentions_free(arg, &free, ctxt)))
9968    },
9969    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) => mentions_free(presentation, variables, ctxt),
9970    XM::Wrap(items, ..) | XM::Arg(items) => items
9971      .iter()
9972      .any(|item| mentions_free(item, variables, ctxt)),
9973    XM::Choices(items) => {
9974      !items.is_empty()
9975        && items
9976          .iter()
9977          .all(|item| mentions_free(item, variables, ctxt))
9978    },
9979    XM::Token(..) | XM::Ref(..) => false,
9980  }
9981}
9982
9983/// `mentions_free` in a node a lexeme names: a letter, or the parsed formula a pre-parsed ATOM holds
9984/// (a fraction, a script).
9985fn node_mentions_free(node: &XMLNode, variables: &[Variable], document: &Document) -> bool {
9986  let node = realize_xmnode(node, document);
9987  let children = node.get_child_elements();
9988  match (node.get_name().as_str(), children.as_slice()) {
9989    ("XMTok", _) => node_letter(&node, document).is_some_and(|letter| variables.contains(&letter)),
9990    ("XMDual", [_, presentation]) => node_mentions_free(presentation, variables, document),
9991    ("XMHint", _) => false,
9992    ("XMApp", [op, ..]) => {
9993      let rebound = node_binder_variables(op, document);
9994      let free: Vec<Variable> = variables
9995        .iter()
9996        .filter(|variable| !rebound.contains(variable))
9997        .cloned()
9998        .collect();
9999      !free.is_empty()
10000        && children
10001          .iter()
10002          .any(|child| node_mentions_free(child, &free, document))
10003    },
10004    (_, children) => children
10005      .iter()
10006      .any(|child| node_mentions_free(child, variables, document)),
10007  }
10008}
10009
10010/// `binder_variables` of an operator node: a scripted big operator's or limits head's subscripts'.
10011fn node_binder_variables(op: &XMLNode, document: &Document) -> Vec<Variable> {
10012  let mut variables = Vec::new();
10013  let mut nucleus = realize_xmnode(op, document).into_owned();
10014  while nucleus.get_name() == "XMApp"
10015    && let [script_op, base, _] = nucleus.get_child_elements().as_slice()
10016    && is_script_node(script_op, document)
10017  {
10018    nucleus = realize_xmnode(base, document).into_owned();
10019  }
10020  let binds = match nucleus.get_attribute("role").as_deref() {
10021    Some("SUMOP" | "INTOP" | "BIGOP" | "LIMITOP") => true,
10022    Some("OPFUNCTION") => {
10023      matches!(
10024        nucleus.get_attribute("meaning").as_deref(),
10025        Some("maximum" | "minimum" | "gcd")
10026      ) || nucleus.get_content() == "Pr"
10027    },
10028    Some("OPERATOR") => nucleus
10029      .get_attribute("scriptpos")
10030      .is_some_and(|position| !position.is_empty()),
10031    _ => false,
10032  };
10033  if binds {
10034    node_subscript_variables(op, document, &mut variables);
10035  }
10036  variables
10037}
10038
10039/// The variables of every subscript on a scripted node.
10040fn node_subscript_variables(node: &XMLNode, document: &Document, variables: &mut Vec<Variable>) {
10041  let node = realize_xmnode(node, document);
10042  if node.get_name() == "XMApp"
10043    && let [script_op, base, script] = node.get_child_elements().as_slice()
10044    && is_script_node(script_op, document)
10045  {
10046    if realize_xmnode(script_op, document)
10047      .get_attribute("role")
10048      .as_deref()
10049      == Some("SUBSCRIPTOP")
10050    {
10051      node_bound_variables(script, document, false, variables);
10052    }
10053    node_subscript_variables(base, document, variables);
10054  }
10055}
10056
10057/// What a bare argument takes after its first item (`op_bare_next`): a bare item, but no OPFUNCTION —
10058/// bare, scripted, applied or postfixed — and no ellipsis, which stays inside only between two items
10059/// (57cb, user ruling 2026-09-29): `\log x\log y` is log@(x)·log@(y), `\nabla u\cdots` ∇@(u)·⋯,
10060/// `\nabla u\ldots` ∇@(u)·….
10061fn is_bare_continuation(xm: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
10062  let nucleus = script_nucleus(postfixed_operand(xm).unwrap_or(xm));
10063  is_bare_item(xm)
10064    // a partial derivative is a bare argument's first item only (`op_bare_item`, not `op_bare_next`):
10065    // `\nabla u\partial_x v` is ∇@(u)·∂_x v, as Perl (57cj review)
10066    && !is_partial_derivative(xm)
10067    && !matches!(head_category(nucleus), Some("OPFUNCTION" | "ELIDEOP"))
10068    && !is_ellipsis(nucleus, ctxt)
10069}
10070
10071/// A big operator, a limit-type or a differential operator standing alone, bare or scripted: `\sum`, `\sum_n`,
10072/// `\int_0^1`, `\bigcup`, `\lim_{n\to\infty}`, `\det`, `\sup`, `\partial_x` (SUMOP, INTOP, BIGOP, LIMITOP, DIFFOP — the
10073/// categories `is_bigop_or_scripted_bigop` reads, here of a head with no operand yet).
10074fn is_bare_big_operator(xm: &XM) -> bool {
10075  let nucleus = script_nucleus(xm);
10076  matches!(nucleus, XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..))
10077    && matches!(
10078      operator_category(nucleus),
10079      Some("SUMOP" | "INTOP" | "BIGOP" | "LIMITOP" | "DIFFOP")
10080    )
10081}
10082
10083/// What an ellipsis right after it continues or multiplies, never the last operand of an elided operation
10084/// (`infix_apply_and_elide`): a head with no argument of its own — a function or trig function (`is_bare_function_head`),
10085/// an operator (`is_operator_head`), a big, limit-type or differential operator (`is_bare_big_operator`), bare or
10086/// scripted — whose argument the ellipsis opens, or such a head's bare (unfenced) application, whose argument it goes on
10087/// or which it multiplies (`\det A\cdots` det@(A·⋯), `\sin x\cdots` sin@(x)·⋯).
10088fn reaches_a_following_ellipsis(xm: &XM) -> bool {
10089  let is_a_head =
10090    |xm: &XM| is_bare_function_head(xm) || is_operator_head(xm) || is_bare_big_operator(xm);
10091  is_a_head(xm)
10092    || matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(head), Args(args), _, meta)
10093      if meta.fenced.is_none() && args.len() == 1 && is_a_head(head))
10094}
10095
10096/// A function head with no argument of its own, bare or scripted: `\log`, `\mathbb E_y`, `\sin^2`.
10097fn is_bare_function_head(xm: &XM) -> bool {
10098  let nucleus = script_nucleus(xm);
10099  matches!(nucleus, XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..))
10100    && matches!(
10101      operator_category(nucleus),
10102      Some("OPFUNCTION" | "TRIGFUNCTION")
10103    )
10104}
10105
10106/// The last item of a bare application's argument, through trailing bare applications:
10107/// `\log p\,\log q` ends in `q`.
10108fn last_bare_leaf(application: &XM) -> &XM {
10109  match application {
10110    XM::Apply(_, args, ..) => match args.0.as_slice() {
10111      [Some(arg)] => {
10112        let last = product_end(arg, true);
10113        if is_bare_operator_application(last) {
10114          last_bare_leaf(last)
10115        } else {
10116          last
10117        }
10118      },
10119      _ => application,
10120    },
10121    _ => application,
10122  }
10123}
10124
10125/// Does `item`, ending a bare argument, take the group `right` begins with? An unknown takes its
10126/// group by divergence #18 (OXIDIZED_DESIGN_MATH; `speculative_item`: `a\log f(x)` is
10127/// a·log@(f@(x))) unless it recurs in the group (`letter_recurs_in_its_group`: `\sin x(x+1)`
10128/// sin@(x)·(x+1)); a bare function by Perl's `addEasyArgs` (MathGrammar:571-576), the group's
10129/// scripts too (divergence #351: `\log\exp(x)^2` is log@((exp@(x))²)).
10130fn takes_the_group(item: &XM, right: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
10131  let first = product_end(right, false);
10132  // A postfixed group is its group (`\log f(x)!` log@((f@(x))!), not log@(f)·(x)!; 57bw review).
10133  let first = postfixed_operand(first).unwrap_or(first);
10134  let unknown = matches!(item, XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..))
10135    && matches!(operator_category(item), Some("UNKNOWN" | "XDIFFUNK"));
10136  unknown
10137    && is_applicable_group(first)
10138    && !letter_recurs_in_its_group(item, first, ctxt)
10139    && !space_before_a_group(item, first, ctxt)
10140    || is_function_head(item) && is_function_group(script_nucleus(first))
10141}
10142
10143/// Does explicit space stand between a letter and the group after it, the group no argument list (`is_an_argument_list`)?
10144/// The letter multiplies the group then, everywhere (user ruling Q6, 2026-10-01, widening #367's trig arguments and #374's
10145/// derivative operands; divergence #18): `k\,(x-y)` k·(x−y), `\log k\,(x-y)` log(k)·(x−y), `\exp\phi\,(1-x)`
10146/// exp(φ)·(1−x), `\nabla\phi\,(1-x)` ∇(φ)·(1−x) (were k@(x−y), …; the 57cj.8 review's mine: 429 formulas in 140 of the
10147/// 3,003 A/B papers). An argument list keeps the application, an evaluation point (`u\,(x,0)=g(x)`, `u\,(x,t)`).
10148fn space_before_a_group(head: &XM, group: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
10149  is_a_one_letter_head(head, ctxt)
10150    && ends_with_space(head, ctxt.nodes)
10151    && !is_an_argument_list(group, ctxt.nodes)
10152    && !holds_an_argument_s_content(group, ctxt)
10153}
10154
10155/// Does `group` hold what is only ever an argument, never a multiplicand — a condition (`p\,(x\mid y)`), a relation
10156/// (`P\,(X\in A)`, `\mathbb 1\,(x>0)`) or a semicolon parameter list (`\phi\,(x;\theta)`)? The content's type is the evidence
10157/// (the merge review of 57cj.22's Q6; the open-categories principle): a space before such a group keeps the application
10158/// (`space_before_a_group`).
10159fn holds_an_argument_s_content(group: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
10160  let content = match group {
10161    XM::Dual(content, ..) => content.as_ref(),
10162    other => other,
10163  };
10164  let relates = |op: &XM| {
10165    matches!(operator_category(op), Some("RELOP" | "ARROW"))
10166      || realized_meaning(op, ctxt).is_some_and(|meaning| meaning == "conditional")
10167  };
10168  let applies_a_relation = |xm: &XM| matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(op), ..) if relates(op));
10169  // (the fence's items: a dual's content may be a reference to the one item the presentation holds)
10170  let inner = match group {
10171    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) => match presentation.as_ref() {
10172      XM::Wrap(items, ..) if items.len() >= 2 => &items[1..items.len() - 1],
10173      _ => &[][..],
10174    },
10175    _ => &[][..],
10176  };
10177  inner
10178    .iter()
10179    .any(|item| matches!(delimiter_role_text(item), Some((_, ";"))) || applies_a_relation(item))
10180    || applies_a_relation(content)
10181}
10182
10183/// A letter, scripted or not: one character (`k`, `\phi`, `a_i`), not a name, which a space does not part from its
10184/// argument (`\mathrm{Unif}\,[0,1]` 2605.00394, `\mathrm{sigmoid}\,(x)` 2605.01208, `{\rm Pr}\,[A]` 2605.03400, `\mathrm{diag}\ (v)`:
10185/// the km24 A/B's 50 named heads, functions applied; `space_before_a_group`).
10186fn is_a_one_letter_head(head: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
10187  let nucleus = script_nucleus(head);
10188  matches!(nucleus, XM::Lexeme(..) | XM::Token(..))
10189    && realized_value(nucleus, ctxt).is_ok_and(|value| value.chars().count() == 1)
10190}
10191
10192/// Does the bare letter `head` occur as a plain value in its own group — `x(x+1)`, `n(n-1)`,
10193/// `\lambda(\lambda I-A)`, `y(1-\sigma(y))`? Perl reads every unknown before a group as a product
10194/// (`doubtArgs`, MathGrammar:515-528); #18 applies it, except here (57bz; 2605.28300, 2605.02279,
10195/// 2605.04013, 2605.30479). A letter only (`\#(\#A)`, `\Box(\Box\phi)` stay applied; 2605.12296,
10196/// 2605.13710), unmarked or bold (a blackboard, script, fraktur or upright head is a named function:
10197/// `\mathbb E[\mathbb E[X]]`, `{\cal V}(|{\cal V}|=K)`, 2605.01849); not before an argument list,
10198/// the sign of a function Perl's `forbidArgs` flags under MaybeFunctions (MathGrammar:524-525;
10199/// default Perl multiplies every unknown) — `E(Y|X,E)`, `T(\sigma,P,T)`, `I(a;I\mid q)`; 2605.11385,
10200/// 2605.11761, 2605.01520. An occurrence is the same letter in the same font, not a head (`f(f(x))`),
10201/// not scripted or in a script (`x(1+x^2)`, `p(y_p)`), not under an accent, and not in function
10202/// position in a product: a letter before a group of its own (`\sigma(W\sigma(Wx))`), a differential
10203/// `d` before a factor (`d(x\,dy)` stays d@(x·d·y), 2605.21794); every choice of an ambiguous item
10204/// must hold it.
10205fn letter_recurs_in_its_group(head: &XM, group: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
10206  let XM::Lexeme(lex, _) = head else {
10207    return false;
10208  };
10209  if !(lex.starts_with("UNKNOWN:") || lex.starts_with("XDIFFUNK:")) || holds_arguments(group, ctxt)
10210  {
10211    return false;
10212  }
10213  let Ok(node) = lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes) else {
10214    return false;
10215  };
10216  let mark = token_font_mark(&realize_xmnode(node, ctxt.document), ctxt.document);
10217  if !matches!(mark, None | Some("bold")) {
10218    return false;
10219  }
10220  let Ok(text) = realized_value(head, ctxt) else {
10221    return false;
10222  };
10223  if text.is_empty() || !text.chars().all(is_plain_math_letter) {
10224    return false;
10225  }
10226  let body = match group {
10227    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) => presentation.as_ref(),
10228    _ => group,
10229  };
10230  occurs_as_value(body, &text, mark, ctxt)
10231}
10232
10233/// A group of arguments: parentheses or brackets around items separated by commas, semicolons or a
10234/// bar (`fence`'s lists and conditionals present `[open, item, separator, item, …, close]`), or
10235/// around one item that is such a list, relations included (Perl's `Argument`, MathGrammar:581-587).
10236/// Not an angle pair (`U\langle\mathcal{G}U,U\rangle` is U times an inner product, 2605.25149) nor a
10237/// colon pair (`\nabla x(G^{-1}\nabla x:\nabla e)`, 2605.21445).
10238fn holds_arguments(group: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
10239  let XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) = group else {
10240    return false;
10241  };
10242  let XM::Wrap(items, ..) = presentation.as_ref() else {
10243    return false;
10244  };
10245  let text = |xm: &XM| {
10246    realized_value(xm, ctxt)
10247      .map(Cow::into_owned)
10248      .unwrap_or_default()
10249  };
10250  let listed = |xm: &XM| {
10251    let content = match xm {
10252      XM::Dual(content, ..) => content.as_ref(),
10253      _ => xm,
10254    };
10255    matches!(content, XM::Apply(Operator(op), ..)
10256    if matches!(op.as_ref(), XM::Token(props, _)
10257      if matches!(
10258        props.meaning.as_deref(),
10259        Some("list" | "vector" | "formulae" | "conditional")
10260      )))
10261  };
10262  match items.as_slice() {
10263    [open, _, separator, _, .., _close] => {
10264      matches!(text(open).as_str(), "(" | "[")
10265        && matches!(
10266          text(separator).as_str(),
10267          "," | ";" | "|" | "\u{2223}" | "mid"
10268        )
10269    },
10270    [open, only, _] => matches!(text(open).as_str(), "(" | "[") && listed(only),
10271    _ => false,
10272  }
10273}
10274
10275/// A letter as the default math font sets it: Latin or Greek, or a Mathematical Alphanumeric
10276/// Symbol in bold, italic or bold italic — not a script, fraktur, double-struck, sans-serif or
10277/// monospace glyph (`{\cal V}` sets 𝒱 with no family of its own).
10278fn is_plain_math_letter(ch: char) -> bool {
10279  ch.is_ascii_alphabetic()
10280    || ('\u{0391}'..='\u{03C9}').contains(&ch) && ch.is_alphabetic()
10281    || matches!(
10282      ch,
10283      'ϑ' | 'ϕ' | 'ϖ' | 'ϱ' | 'ϵ' | 'ϰ' | 'ℓ' | 'ℎ' | 'ı' | 'ȷ'
10284    )
10285    || ('\u{1D400}'..='\u{1D49B}').contains(&ch)
10286    || ('\u{1D6A4}'..='\u{1D6A5}').contains(&ch)
10287    || ('\u{1D6A8}'..='\u{1D755}').contains(&ch)
10288}
10289
10290/// `letter_recurs_in_its_group`'s walk.
10291fn occurs_as_value(xm: &XM, text: &str, mark: Option<&str>, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
10292  match xm {
10293    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => {
10294      (lex.starts_with("UNKNOWN:") || lex.starts_with("XDIFFUNK:"))
10295        && realized_value(xm, ctxt).is_ok_and(|v| v == text)
10296        && lookup_lex_node(lex, ctxt.nodes).is_ok_and(|node| {
10297          token_font_mark(&realize_xmnode(node, ctxt.document), ctxt.document) == mark
10298        })
10299    },
10300    XM::Apply(Operator(op), Args(args), ..) => {
10301      if matches!(
10302        operator_category(op),
10303        Some("SUBSCRIPTOP" | "SUPERSCRIPTOP" | "OVERACCENT" | "UNDERACCENT")
10304      ) {
10305        return false;
10306      }
10307      let product = is_invisible_times_op(op);
10308      let args: Vec<&XM> = args.iter().flatten().collect();
10309      args.iter().enumerate().any(|(k, arg)| {
10310        // In a product a letter before a group of its own (`\sigma(W\sigma(Wx))`) and a differential
10311        // `d` before a factor (`d(x\,dy)`) are in function position; beside a visible operator a
10312        // letter is a value (`x(x-(y+z))`, `d(d-1)`).
10313        let function_position = product
10314          && args.get(k + 1).is_some_and(|next| {
10315            matches!(arg, XM::Lexeme(..)) && is_applicable_group(next) || is_differential_d(arg)
10316          });
10317        !function_position && occurs_as_value(arg, text, mark, ctxt)
10318      })
10319    },
10320    XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) => occurs_as_value(presentation, text, mark, ctxt),
10321    XM::Wrap(items, ..) | XM::Arg(items) => items
10322      .iter()
10323      .any(|item| occurs_as_value(item, text, mark, ctxt)),
10324    XM::Choices(items) => {
10325      !items.is_empty()
10326        && items
10327          .iter()
10328          .all(|item| occurs_as_value(item, text, mark, ctxt))
10329    },
10330    _ => false,
10331  }
10332}
10333
10334/// A fence whose close does not balance its open — `(0,1]`, `[a,b)`, which Perl's `factorOpenExpr`
10335/// builds (any CLOSE, MathGrammar:473-481): no function's argument, as `addEasyArgs` needs a
10336/// `balancedClose` (:571-576), so a function before it multiplies it — `\log(0,1]` is log·(0,1]
10337/// (golden tests/parse/opfunction_arguments.tex#function_before_an_unbalanced_interval_multiplies).
10338fn is_unbalanced_fence(xm: &XM) -> bool {
10339  matches!(xm, XM::Dual(.., meta) if meta.unbalanced_fence)
10340}
10341
10342/// A group a function applies to (Perl `addEasyArgs`, MathGrammar:571-576: a balanced `OPEN …
10343/// CLOSE`, `\lvert…\rvert` included) — not a bar fence (`Meta::bar_fence`), an `aBarearg` that
10344/// starts the bare argument, nor a fenced modifier `(>0)`. By the fence's own marks, so a `split`
10345/// row, whose bars read through XMRefs, reads as the inline formula.
10346fn is_function_group(xm: &XM) -> bool {
10347  matches!(xm, XM::Dual(_, presentation, _, meta)
10348    if matches!(**presentation, XM::Wrap(..)) && !meta.bar_fence)
10349    && !is_fenced_modifier_dual(xm)
10350}
10351
10352/// A fenced group an unknown applies to — what `speculative_prefix_apply` accepts: not bars
10353/// (`|x|`, `\lvert x\rvert`), which multiply, nor a fenced modifier `(>0)`, which annotates.
10354fn is_applicable_group(xm: &XM) -> bool {
10355  matches!(xm, XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) if matches!(**presentation, XM::Wrap(..)))
10356    && !is_vertbar_fenced_dual(xm)
10357    && !is_fenced_modifier_dual(xm)
10358}
10359
10360/// Does Perl's operator `head` take `right` rather than multiply it (MathGrammar:312-313): while
10361/// its nest is open a function or operator, scripted or applied (`nestOperators`, :663-671); a
10362/// parenthesized group (`nestOperators`' OPEN, `addEasyArgs`, :571-576); a bare argument
10363/// (`addOpFunArgs`, :553-558)?
10364fn operator_takes(head: &XM, right: &XM) -> bool {
10365  is_bare_item(product_end(right, false))
10366    || matches!(right, XM::Dual(_, presentation, ..) if matches!(**presentation, XM::Wrap(..)))
10367    || nest_is_open(head)
10368      && matches!(
10369        head_category(right),
10370        Some("OPERATOR" | "FUNCTION" | "OPFUNCTION" | "TRIGFUNCTION")
10371      )
10372}
10373
10374/// Extract the role of an XM operator.
10375fn get_operator_role(op: &Operator, nodes: &[libxml::tree::Node]) -> Option<String> {
10376  operator_role(&op.0, nodes)
10377}
10378
10379/// Extract the role from a lexeme ID by looking up the DOM node (through an XMRef).
10380fn get_lexeme_role(lex_id: &str, nodes: &[libxml::tree::Node]) -> Option<String> {
10381  let node = lookup_lex_node(lex_id, nodes).ok()?;
10382  crate::data::resolve_xmref(node)
10383    .unwrap_or_else(|| node.clone())
10384    .get_attribute("role")
10385}
10386
10387/// An item's role as Perl reads it, `p_getAttribute(realizeXMNode($x), 'role')`: a token's
10388/// own; a lexeme's node's, read through an XMRef, as a gathered/split row's content branch holds
10389/// them (MathParser.pm:135-150); and a decorated operator's, the role `decorate_operator` gave it
10390/// (Perl DecorateOperator, MathParser.pm:1649-1654).
10391fn operator_role(xm: &XM, nodes: &[libxml::tree::Node]) -> Option<String> {
10392  match xm {
10393    XM::Token(props, _) | XM::Apply(_, _, props, _) | XM::Ref(props) => {
10394      props.role.as_deref().map(String::from)
10395    },
10396    XM::Lexeme(lex_id, _) => get_lexeme_role(lex_id, nodes),
10397    _ => None,
10398  }
10399}
10400
10401/// Is `xm` a relation or arrow operator (Perl's `relop` pseudo-terminal, MathGrammar:704-712), bare
10402/// or decorated with scripts (`decorate_operator`)? A lexeme's role is its lexer category, read
10403/// through an XMRef when it was lexed.
10404fn is_relational_op(xm: &XM) -> bool {
10405  operator_category(xm).is_some_and(|r| r.contains("RELOP") || r.contains("ARROW"))
10406}
10407
10408/// An operator's grammatical category without the lexeme table: a lexeme's lexer category (read
10409/// through an XMRef when it was lexed), a token's role, a decorated operator's role.
10410pub(crate) fn operator_category(xm: &XM) -> Option<&str> {
10411  match xm {
10412    // an expectation or probability is an OPFUNCTION of its own lexeme category, for the grammar
10413    // (`plain_opfunction`, builder.rs)
10414    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lex.split(':').next().map(lexeme_category),
10415    XM::Token(props, _) | XM::Apply(_, _, props, _) => props.role.as_deref(),
10416    _ => None,
10417  }
10418}
10419
10420/// A lexeme's grammatical category: its first `:`-segment, an EXPECTATION's `OPFUNCTION`, an ATOM_NUMBER's
10421/// (a fraction of numbers, util.rs) `ATOM`.
10422pub(crate) fn lexeme_category(category: &str) -> &str {
10423  match category {
10424    "EXPECTATION" => "OPFUNCTION",
10425    "ATOM_NUMBER" => "ATOM",
10426    _ => category,
10427  }
10428}
10429
10430/// Perl `moreRelations` (MathGrammar Formula): a relation after a relation continues one
10431/// `multirelation` — `a < b < c`, `x\sim_p y\sim z`, `y < 2 <` — whatever the relations: bare,
10432/// a two-part `<=`, or decorated. `left` is the formula so far, `op` the next relation and
10433/// `operand` what follows it; with no relation on the left, the relation is `op(left, operand)`.
10434fn chain_relation(left: Option<XM>, op: Option<XM>, operand: Option<XM>) -> XM {
10435  match left {
10436    Some(XM::Apply(left_op, mut left_args, props, meta)) if is_multirelation(&left_op.0) => {
10437      left_args.0.push(op);
10438      left_args.0.push(operand);
10439      XM::Apply(left_op, left_args, props, meta)
10440    },
10441    Some(XM::Apply(left_op, left_args, ..))
10442      if is_relational_op(&left_op.0) && left_args.0.len() == 2 =>
10443    {
10444      let multirel_tok = XProps {
10445        meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("multirelation")),
10446        ..XProps::default()
10447      };
10448      let mut left_args = left_args.0.into_iter();
10449      let (left_1, left_2) = (left_args.next().flatten(), left_args.next().flatten());
10450      XM::Apply(
10451        multirel_tok.into(),
10452        Args(vec![left_1, Some(*left_op.0), left_2, op, operand]),
10453        XProps::default(),
10454        Meta::default(),
10455      )
10456    },
10457    left => XM::Apply(
10458      op.into(),
10459      Args(vec![left, operand]),
10460      XProps::default(),
10461      Meta::default(),
10462    ),
10463  }
10464}
10465
10466/// Is `op` the `multirelation` a chain of relations flattens into (MathParser.pm, moreRelations)?
10467fn is_multirelation(op: &XM) -> bool {
10468  matches!(op, XM::Token(props, _) if props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("multirelation"))
10469}
10470
10471fn absent() -> XM {
10472  let props = XProps {
10473    meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("absent")),
10474    ..XProps::default()
10475  };
10476  props.into()
10477}
10478
10479/// Prefix arrow: `→ expr` becomes `Apply(→, absent, expr)` — matching Perl's `AnyOp Expression`
10480/// Perl: MorphVertbar — expression VERTBAR expression treated as conditional/modifier
10481/// e.g. `x | y,z,t` → `conditional@(x, list@(y,z,t))`
10482pub fn vertbar_modifier(
10483  _rule_id: i32,
10484  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
10485  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
10486  ctxt: ActionContext,
10487) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
10488  unp!(args => left, vertbar, right);
10489  // Perl's conditional is `Term | ExpressionsNoBars` (MathGrammar:261-268), no relation on either
10490  // side; ours takes a relation (`P(A|B=b)`), not one missing an operand, which only a bar
10491  // splitting the formula makes — `\bigg|g\big|_{t=1}-h\bigg|\le C` is no (|g|)_{t=1}−h | (absent ≤ C),
10492  // `\le C|a|\,|b|_L` no (absent ≤ C·|a|) | … (2605.26054, 2605.02499, 2605.12082; repro
10493  // math-parse/conditional_bar_takes_no_bare_relation).
10494  if [&left, &right]
10495    .into_iter()
10496    .flatten()
10497    .any(|side| relation_lacks_operand(side, true) || relation_lacks_operand(side, false))
10498  {
10499    return Err("vertbar_modifier: a relation beside the bar lacks its operand".into());
10500  }
10501  // … nor the statements after it: a comma list of relations holding an ellipsis or crossing a
10502  // `\quad` (`y_i|\theta_i\sim P,\quad i=1,\ldots,n` is no conditional@(y_i, formulae@(…)); 57bv A/B:
10503  // 2605.05396, 2605.13128, 2605.19519, 2605.03152; `P(A|B=b,C=c)` stays a condition).
10504  if right.as_ref().is_some_and(|r| is_statement_list(r, &ctxt)) {
10505    return Err("vertbar_modifier: the statements after a condition are no condition".into());
10506  }
10507  // … nor a relation that is no event: it relates the whole conditional (`conditional_formula`,
10508  // 57cc, user ruling 2026-09-29) — `y|x\sim N(0,1)` is conditional@(y, x) ∼ N@(0, 1) (2605.03594,
10509  // 2605.05396); and a bar after such a relation is the right side's conditional, `x|y\sim z|w`
10510  // (x|y) ∼ (z|w), no conditional@(conditional@(x, y) ∼ z, w).
10511  if right
10512    .as_ref()
10513    .is_some_and(|r| condition_holds_a_non_event(r, &ctxt))
10514  {
10515    return Err("vertbar_modifier: a relation that is no event relates the conditional".into());
10516  }
10517  if left.as_ref().is_some_and(relates_a_conditional) {
10518    return Err(
10519      "vertbar_modifier: a relation over a conditional takes a conditional on its right".into(),
10520    );
10521  }
10522  // … and its condition reads no bar of its own (`ExpressionsNoBars` sets `$forbidVertBar`,
10523  // :267-268): `|f(x)|_0^1|+|\nabla a|_L|\nabla b|_L` is no (|f(x)|)_0^1 | (+|∇a|_L | eval(∇b, L)).
10524  if right
10525    .as_ref()
10526    .is_some_and(|r| holds_bar_reading(r, &["evaluated-at", "conditional"]))
10527  {
10528    return Err("vertbar_modifier: the condition reads a bar of its own".into());
10529  }
10530  // The bar is the source token, re-roled: Perl's `Annotate($item[2], role => 'MODIFIEROP',
10531  // meaning => 'conditional')` (MathGrammar:263) — `\mid` keeps `∣` and its name, `\big|` its size
10532  // and padding, where a token built here rendered each as a plain `|` (57bc; golden
10533  // tests/parse/bar_pairs.tex, WISDOM #94). In a split or gathered row's content branch the bar
10534  // is an `XMRef`, and `Annotate` keeps it one, `<XMRef idref role meaning/>`, as the differential
10535  // does (`diffop_apply`).
10536  let source = match vertbar {
10537    Some(XM::Lexeme(lex, _)) => match lookup_lex_node(&lex, ctxt.nodes) {
10538      Ok(node) if node.get_name() == "XMRef" => {
10539        let bar = XM::Ref(XProps {
10540          id: node.get_attribute("idref").map(Cow::Owned),
10541          xmkey: node.get_attribute("_xmkey").map(Cow::Owned),
10542          role: Some(Cow::Borrowed("MODIFIEROP")),
10543          meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("conditional")),
10544          ..XProps::default()
10545        });
10546        return Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
10547          bar.into(),
10548          Args(vec![left, right]),
10549          XProps::default(),
10550          Meta::default(),
10551        )));
10552      },
10553      Ok(node) => Some(XProps::from(node)),
10554      Err(_) => None,
10555    },
10556    Some(XM::Token(props, _)) => Some(props),
10557    _ => None,
10558  };
10559  let modop = match source {
10560    Some(bar) => XProps {
10561      meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("conditional")),
10562      role: Some(Cow::Borrowed("MODIFIEROP")),
10563      ..bar
10564    },
10565    // No source token to annotate: Perl MorphVertbar's unfonted `|`.
10566    None => XProps {
10567      meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("conditional")),
10568      role: Some(Cow::Borrowed("MODIFIEROP")),
10569      stretchy: Some(Cow::Borrowed("false")),
10570      content: Some(Cow::Borrowed("|")),
10571      font: Some(Rc::new(font::FONT_TEXT_DEFAULT.specialize("|"))),
10572      ..XProps::default()
10573    },
10574  };
10575  Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
10576    modop.into(),
10577    Args(vec![left, right]),
10578    XProps::default(),
10579    Meta::default(),
10580  )))
10581}

10583/// `expectation_letter` (M3): an expectation's or probability's lexeme read as the letter the lexer
10584/// gave its token (`util::letter_lexeme`, as `parser::type_expectation_lexemes` found it), marked
10585/// (`Meta::expectation_letter`) for the soft prune that keeps it only where no reading takes it as
10586/// an operator (`ExpectationLettersAreFallbacks`).
10587pub fn expectation_as_letter(
10588  _rule_id: i32,
10589  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
10590  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
10591  ctxt: ActionContext,
10592) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
10593  unp!(args => typed);
10594  let Some(XM::Lexeme(lex, _)) = typed else {
10595    return Err("expectation_as_letter: no expectation lexeme".into());
10596  };
10597  let node = lookup_lex_node(&lex, ctxt.nodes)
10598    .map_err(|_| "expectation_as_letter: the lexeme names no node")?;
10599  let index = lex
10600    .rsplit(':')
10601    .next()
10602    .and_then(|index| index.parse::<usize>().ok())
10603    .ok_or("expectation_as_letter: the lexeme has no index")?;
10604  let letter = crate::util::letter_lexeme(node, index);
10605  let XM::Lexeme(name, mut meta) =
10606    XM::Lexeme(Rc::from(letter.as_str()), Meta::default()).specialize(Meta::default(), pragmas)?
10607  else {
10608    unreachable!()
10609  };
10610  meta.expectation_letter = true;
10611  Ok(Some(XM::Lexeme(name, meta)))
10612}
10613
10614/// How many expectations `xm` reads as letters (`expectation_as_letter`, M3): the rank of the soft prune
10615/// `ExpectationLettersAreFallbacks` at the root and, per glade, in the ASF traverser.
10616pub(crate) fn expectation_letter_count(xm: &XM) -> usize {
10617  match xm {
10618    XM::Lexeme(_, meta) => usize::from(meta.expectation_letter),
10619    XM::Token(..) | XM::Ref(_) => 0,
10620    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) => {
10621      expectation_letter_count(op)
10622        + args
10623          .trees()
10624          .iter()
10625          .map(|arg| expectation_letter_count(arg))
10626          .sum::<usize>()
10627    },
10628    XM::Dual(content, presentation, ..) => {
10629      expectation_letter_count(content) + expectation_letter_count(presentation)
10630    },
10631    XM::Wrap(items, ..) | XM::Arg(items) | XM::Choices(items) => {
10632      items.iter().map(expectation_letter_count).sum()
10633    },
10634  }
10635}

10639fn is_expectation_operator(xm: &XM) -> bool {

10643/// `open_op_head expectation_before_a_big_operator bigop_operand`: an operator takes an expectation's
10644/// application to the big operator after it, `\nabla_\theta\mathbb{E}_x\sum_i f_i` (∇_θ)@(𝔼_x@(∑…)) (57cf;
10645/// 2605.09853): the expectation applied to the big operator, the operator to that.
10646pub fn operator_takes_an_expectation_s_big_operator(
10647  rule_id: i32,

10650  ctxt: ActionContext,

10659        document: ctxt.document,
10660      },
10661    )?;
10662    args.push(applied);
10663  }
10664  prefix_apply(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)

10667/// A relation that states an event of a condition, what is given: an undecorated equality,
10668/// inequality, order, membership or inclusion (57cc, user ruling 2026-09-29, divergence #377) —
10669/// `Y\mid X=x` (2605.03233), `T-s\mid T>s` (2605.16066), `A_0|A_t\in S`. Any other relation (`\sim`, `\approx`, `\propto`, `\equiv`, an
10670/// arrow, a decorated relation) relates the whole conditional.
10671fn is_event_relation(op: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
10672  script_base(op).is_none()
10673    && realized_meaning(op, ctxt).is_some_and(|meaning| {
10674      matches!(
10675        meaning.as_str(),
10676        "equals"
10677          | "not-equals"
10678          | "less-than"
10679          | "greater-than"
10680          | "less-than-or-equals"
10681          | "greater-than-or-equals"
10682          | "much-less-than"
10683          | "much-greater-than"
10684          | "element-of"
10685          | "not-element-of"
10686          | "contains"
10687          | "not-contains"
10688      ) || meaning.contains("subset")
10689        || meaning.contains("superset")
10690    })
10691}
10692
10693/// Does a condition hold a relation that is no event — itself, a chain of relations, or an item
10694/// of its comma list (read from the presentation, as `is_statement_list` reads it)?
10695fn condition_holds_a_non_event(xm: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
10696  match xm {
10697    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) if is_multirelation(op) => args
10698      .0
10699      .iter()
10700      .flatten()
10701      .skip(1)
10702      .step_by(2)
10703      .any(|relation| !is_event_relation(relation, ctxt)),
10704    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) if is_relational_op(op) && args.0.len() >= 2 => {
10705      !is_event_relation(op, ctxt)
10706    },
10707    XM::Dual(content, pres, ..) => match (&**content, &**pres) {
10708      (XM::Apply(op, ..), XM::Wrap(items, ..))
10709        if matches!(&*op.0, XM::Token(props, _)
10710          if matches!(props.meaning.as_deref(), Some("list" | "formulae"))) =>
10711      {
10712        items
10713          .iter()
10714          .any(|item| condition_holds_a_non_event(item, ctxt))
10715      },
10716      _ => false,
10717    },
10718    _ => false,
10719  }
10720}

10722/// `expression vertbar formula_list`: a condition list that is not all relations (`y_i\mid\mu,\sigma^2`,
10723/// `Y\mid Z,X=x`, `y|x_1=a_1,\ldots,x_n=a_n`); a list of relations only is `relation_pairs`' (`U\mid A=a,B=b`
10724/// conditional@(U, formulae@(A = a, B = b)), 2605.18724), one derivation (57cc).
10725pub fn conditional_over_a_list(
10726  rule_id: i32,
10727  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
10728  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
10729  ctxt: ActionContext,
10730) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
10731  if let [_, _, Some(XM::Dual(_, pres, ..))] = args.as_slice()
10732    && let XM::Wrap(items, ..) = &**pres
10733    && items.iter().step_by(2).all(is_relational_item)
10734  {
10735    return Err("conditional_over_a_list: a list of relations is relation_pairs'".into());
10736  }
10737  vertbar_modifier(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
10738}

10740/// A conditional, `conditional@(x, y)`.
10741fn is_conditional(xm: &XM) -> bool {
10742  matches!(xm, XM::Apply(Operator(op), ..)
10743    if matches!(&**op, XM::Token(props, _) if props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("conditional")))
10744}

10746/// A relation (or chain) whose first operand is a factor-level conditional: `conditional@(x, y) ∼ z`.
10747fn relates_a_conditional(xm: &XM) -> bool {
10748  match xm {
10749    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) if is_relational_op(op) || is_multirelation(op) => args
10750      .0
10751      .first()
10752      .is_some_and(|first| first.as_ref().is_some_and(is_conditional)),
10753    _ => false,
10754  }
10755}

10757/// `conditional_head relop expression`: a relation after a factor-level conditional relates the
10758/// whole conditional unless it is an event, which the statement-level bar keeps in the condition
10759/// (`Y\mid X=x` is conditional@(Y, X = x)); one derivation each (57cc).
10760pub fn conditional_relation(
10761  rule_id: i32,
10762  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
10763  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
10764  ctxt: ActionContext,
10765) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
10766  // (between two conditionals there is no condition to keep it: `a|b=c|d`, 2605.29001's shape)
10767  if let [_, Some(relation), right] = args.as_slice()
10768    && is_event_relation(relation, &ctxt)
10769    && !right.as_ref().is_some_and(is_conditional)
10770  {
10771    return Err("conditional_relation: an event stays in the condition".into());
10772  }
10773  infix_relation(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
10774}

10776/// Does the relation `xm` lack its first (`first`) or last operand — `absent ≤ C`, `δ ≍ absent`?
10777fn relation_lacks_operand(xm: &XM, first: bool) -> bool {
10778  match xm {
10779    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) if is_multirelation(op) || is_relational_op(op) => {
10780      let operand = if first { args.0.first() } else { args.0.last() };
10781      matches!(operand, Some(Some(operand)) if is_absent(operand)
10782        || relation_lacks_operand(operand, first))
10783    },
10784    _ => false,
10785  }
10786}

10788/// The `absent` operand a relation missing one gets (`absent()`).
10789fn is_absent(xm: &XM) -> bool {
10790  matches!(xm, XM::Token(props, _) if props.meaning.as_deref() == Some("absent"))
10791}
