10793/// VERTBAR conditional with a comma-LIST left-hand side: `a,b | c` →
10794/// `conditional(list@(a,b), c)`. The grammar rule is the explicit
10795/// `statements punct statement vertbar statements` (NOT a generalized
10796/// `statements vertbar statements`, which over-applies to abs-value `|a|`
10797/// and explodes the parse forest — see EXPECTED_ID_XMREF_DESIGN 2026-06-26p/q).
10798/// Restricting to a literal comma-before-bar shape means it fires ONLY on
10799/// genuine list-LHS conditionals, leaving abs-value/norm parsing untouched.
10800/// Composes `list_apply` (build the list LHS) + `vertbar_modifier` (condition it).
10801/// Root fix for the Class-B `\Pr(s_A,s_B|\Omega)` dangling-XMRef witness.
10802pub fn vertbar_modifier_listlhs(
10803  rule_id: i32,
10804  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
10805  prag: &[ValidationPragmatics],
10806  ctxt: ActionContext,
10807) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
10808  // args: [left_statements, punct, statement, vertbar, right_statements]
10809  if args.len() != 5 {
10810    return Err("vertbar_modifier_listlhs: expected 5 args".into());
10811  }
10812  let right = args.pop().unwrap();
10813  let vertbar = args.pop().unwrap();
10814  let mid = args.pop().unwrap();
10815  let sep = args.pop().unwrap();
10816  let left = args.pop().unwrap();
10817  // Perl binds `|` to the LAST item before the bar (Factor-level, tight), NOT the
10818  // whole comma-list: `a,b | c` → `list@(a, conditional@(b, c))` (NOT
10819  // `conditional@(list@(a,b), c)`). So condition `mid | right` FIRST, then append
10820  // that conditional as the final item of the list `left`. (`x | y,z` — no comma
10821  // before the bar — is handled by the single-LHS `statement vertbar statements`
10822  // rule, giving `conditional@(x, list@(y,z))`, also matching Perl.)
10823  let cond = {
10824    let inner = ActionContext {
10825      nodes:    ctxt.nodes,
10826      document: &mut *ctxt.document,
10827    };
10828    vertbar_modifier(rule_id, vec![mid, vertbar, right], prag, inner)?
10829  };
10830  // Append the conditional as the list's last item via `list_apply_core` (NOT
10831  // `list_apply`, whose Rule-4 would reject the bare conditional item — here it
10832  // is legitimately the last item of a bar-after-comma list). Guard the unwraps:
10833  // if either operand is absent, drop this combo (pruned).
10834  let (sep, cond) = match (sep, cond) {
10835    (Some(s), Some(c)) => (s, c),
10836    _ => return Err("vertbar_modifier_listlhs: missing separator or conditional".into()),
10837  };
10838  list_apply_core(left, sep, cond, ctxt)
10839}

10875  Ok(Some(XM::Apply(

10883/// Perl: AnyOp Expression => Apply(AnyOp, Absent(), Expression)
10884/// Leading relop with implied absent left operand (e.g. `= e + f + g` in eqnarray)
10885pub fn prefix_relop_apply(
10886  _rule_id: i32,
10887  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
10888  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
10889  _ctxt: ActionContext,
10890) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
10891  unp!(args => relop, right);
10892  // Early-action prune: when the operator is METARELOP (e.g.
10893  // `\vdash`, `:`, `\models`), the formula-level
10894  // `metarelop expression → prefix_relop_apply` rule competes with
10895  // the statement-level `metarelop formula → prefix_metarelop_apply`
10896  // rule. Legacy prefers the statement-level grouping
10897  // (`Apply(vdash, formula)`) over the formula-level chain
10898  // (`multirelation(vdash, ..., =, 0)`). Reject the formula-level
10899  // METARELOP prefix here so the parse goes through the
10900  // statement-level rule.
10901  let is_metarelop = relop.as_ref().is_some_and(|op| match op {
10902    XM::Lexeme(l, _) => l.split(':').next() == Some("METARELOP"),
10903    XM::Token(p, _) => p.role.as_deref() == Some("METARELOP"),
10904    _ => false,
10905  });
10906  if is_metarelop {
10907    return Err(
10908      "prefix_relop_apply: METARELOP prefix at formula-level — \
10909       prefer statement-level prefix_metarelop_apply"
10910        .into(),
10911    );
10912  }
10913  // For BINOP prefix usage (e.g. \mathbin{|}x), Perl produces op@(x) without absent.
10914  // For RELOP prefix (e.g. = b, < c), keep absent as first arg.
10915  let is_binop = relop.as_ref().is_some_and(|op| match op {
10916    XM::Lexeme(l, _) => l.split(':').next() == Some("BINOP"),
10917    XM::Token(p, _) => p.role.as_deref() == Some("BINOP"),
10918    _ => false,
10919  });
10920  let args = if is_binop {
10921    Args(vec![right])
10922  } else {
10923    Args(vec![Some(absent()), right])
10924  };
10925  Ok(Some(XM::Apply(
10926    relop.into(),
10927    args,
10928    XProps::default(),
10929    Meta::default(),
10930  )))
10931}

10976/// OPEN expr (without CLOSE) — e.g. \{ array → cases-like wrapping.
10977/// Perl: factorOpen handles unmatched OPEN by consuming the expression.
10978/// For { delimiter, produces XMDual: content=Apply(cases, XMRef), pres=XMWrap({, expr).
10979pub fn open_fenced(
10980  _rule_id: i32,
10981  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
10982  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
10983  ctxt: ActionContext,
10984) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
10985  unp!(args => open_opt, arg_opt);
10986  let open = open_opt.unwrap();
10987  let mut arg = arg_opt.unwrap();
10988  // Perl: Fence({, content) → XMDual(Apply(cases, XMRef(content)), XMWrap({, content))
10989  let o = realized_value(&open, &ctxt)?;
10990  if o == "{" {
10991    let op = XProps {
10992      meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("cases")),
10993      ..XProps::default()
10994    };
10995    let refs = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut arg], ctxt)?;
10996    let content = XM::Apply(
10997      Operator::from(op),
10998      Args(refs.into_iter().map(Some).collect()),
10999      XProps::default(),
11000      Meta::default(),
11001    );
11002    // Perl: XMWrap(open, content, absent_close) — absent marks missing close delimiter
11003    let absent_close = XM::Token(
11004      XProps {
11005        meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("absent")),
11006        ..XProps::default()
11007      },
11008      Meta::default(),
11009    );
11010    let pres = XM::Wrap(
11011      vec![open, arg, absent_close],
11012      XProps::default(),
11013      Meta::default(),
11014    );
11015    Ok(Some(XM::Dual(
11016      Box::new(content),
11017      Box::new(pres),
11018      XProps::default(),
11019      Meta::default(),
11020    )))
11021  } else {
11022    // Non-brace open without close — just wrap
11023    let absent_close = XM::Token(
11024      XProps {
11025        meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("absent")),
11026        ..XProps::default()
11027      },
11028      Meta::default(),
11029    );
11030    Ok(Some(XM::Wrap(
11031      vec![open, arg, absent_close],
11032      XProps::default(),
11033      Meta::default(),
11034    )))
11035  }
11036}
11037
11038/// expr CLOSE (without OPEN) — e.g. array \} → cases-like wrapping.
11039/// For } delimiter, produces XMDual: content=Apply(cases, XMRef), pres=XMWrap(expr, }).
11040pub fn close_fenced(
11041  _rule_id: i32,
11042  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
11043  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
11044  ctxt: ActionContext,
11045) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
11046  unp!(args => arg_opt, close_opt);
11047  let mut arg = arg_opt.unwrap();
11048  let close = close_opt.unwrap();
11049  // Perl: Fence(content, }) → XMDual(Apply(cases, XMRef(content)), XMWrap(content, }))
11050  let c = realized_value(&close, &ctxt)?;
11051  if c == "}" {
11052    let op = XProps {
11053      meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("cases")),
11054      ..XProps::default()
11055    };
11056    let refs = create_xmrefs(&mut [&mut arg], ctxt)?;
11057    let content = XM::Apply(
11058      Operator::from(op),
11059      Args(refs.into_iter().map(Some).collect()),
11060      XProps::default(),
11061      Meta::default(),
11062    );
11063    // Perl: XMWrap(absent_open, content, close) — absent marks missing open delimiter
11064    let absent_open = XM::Token(
11065      XProps {
11066        meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("absent")),
11067        ..XProps::default()
11068      },
11069      Meta::default(),
11070    );
11071    let pres = XM::Wrap(
11072      vec![absent_open, arg, close],
11073      XProps::default(),
11074      Meta::default(),
11075    );
11076    Ok(Some(XM::Dual(
11077      Box::new(content),
11078      Box::new(pres),
11079      XProps::default(),
11080      Meta::default(),
11081    )))
11082  } else {
11083    let absent_open = XM::Token(
11084      XProps {
11085        meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("absent")),
11086        ..XProps::default()
11087      },
11088      Meta::default(),
11089    );
11090    Ok(Some(XM::Wrap(
11091      vec![absent_open, arg, close],
11092      XProps::default(),
11093      Meta::default(),
11094    )))
11095  }
11096}

11098/// Double-fenced: <<expr>> or <<list>> — double angle brackets as a single

11123/// Perl MathGrammar L259-260, MathParser.pm L1656-1668: NewEvalAt
11124/// Handles `a|_{x=0}`, `f(x)|_{0}^{1}`, `\left.xyz\right|_{0}^{2}`
11125/// Pattern: base evalAtOp sub [sup]
11126///
11127/// Content arm:  XMApp(evaluated-at, base_ref, sub_ref?, sup_ref?)
11128/// Presentation: XMApp(SUBSCRIPTOP, XMWrap(base, bar[CLOSE]), sub_content)
11129///               optionally wrapped in XMApp(SUPERSCRIPTOP, ..., sup_content)
11130pub fn eval_at(
11131  _rule_id: i32,
11132  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
11133  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
11134  ctxt: ActionContext,
11135) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
11136  // Args: base, vertbar, sub, [sup] — 3 or 4 args depending on rule
11137  let mut base = args.remove(0).unwrap();
11138  let vertbar = args.remove(0).unwrap();
11139  // Remaining args: sub and optionally sup scripts (faux_wrap'd start_POSTSUBSCRIPT tokens)
11140  // Perl: maybeEvalAt handles SUB then SUP or SUP then SUB
11141  let (sub_script, sup_script) = if args.len() == 2 {
11142    let s1 = args.remove(0);
11143    let s2 = args.remove(0);
11144    // Determine which is sub and which is super by checking the role.
11145    // faux_wrap returns Wrap([lexeme, content]) — extract the lexeme first.
11146    let s1_is_sub = s1.as_ref().is_none_or(|xm| {
11147      let lex = match xm {
11148        XM::Lexeme(l, _) => Some(&**l),
11149        XM::Wrap(items, ..) if !items.is_empty() => {
11150          if let XM::Lexeme(ref l, _) = items[0] {
11151            Some(&**l)
11152          } else {
11153            None
11154          }
11155        },
11156        _ => None,
11157      };
11158      lex
11159        .and_then(|l| lookup_lex_node(l, ctxt.nodes).ok())
11160        .map(|n| n.get_attribute("role").unwrap_or_default().contains("SUB"))
11161        .unwrap_or(true)
11162    });
11163    if s1_is_sub { (s1, s2) } else { (s2, s1) }
11164  } else {
11165    (args.remove(0), None)
11166  };
11167
11168  // Pre-extract all values from ctxt.nodes before create_xmrefs consumes ctxt
11169  let bar_close = morph_vertbar(vertbar, "CLOSE", ctxt.nodes);
11170  let sub_content_xm = get_script_child_xm(&sub_script, ctxt.nodes);
11171  let sup_content_xm = sup_script
11172    .as_ref()
11173    .and_then(|s| get_script_child_xm(&Some(s.clone()), ctxt.nodes));
11174  let sub_content_xm2 = get_script_child_xm(&sub_script, ctxt.nodes);
11175  let sup_content_xm2 = sup_script
11176    .as_ref()
11177    .and_then(|s| get_script_child_xm(&Some(s.clone()), ctxt.nodes));
11178
11179  // Build content arm FIRST: this sets _xmkey/xml:id on base and sub/sup
11180  // so the presentation arm (built after) gets the references.
11181  let eval_tok = XM::Token(
11182    XProps {
11183      meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("evaluated-at")),
11184      ..XProps::default()
11185    },
11186    Meta::default(),
11187  );
11188
11189  let mut sub_for_ref = sub_content_xm;
11190  let mut sup_for_ref = sup_content_xm;
11191
11192  let mut content_args: Vec<&mut XM> = vec![&mut base];
11193  if let Some(ref mut sc) = sub_for_ref {
11194    content_args.push(sc);
11195  }
11196  if let Some(ref mut sc) = sup_for_ref {
11197    content_args.push(sc);
11198  }
11199  let ref_args = create_xmrefs(&mut content_args, ctxt)?;
11200
11201  let content = XM::Apply(
11202    eval_tok.into(),
11203    ref_args.into(),
11204    XProps::default(),
11205    Meta::default(),
11206  );
11207
11208  // Build presentation arm AFTER content (so base has _xmkey set)
11209  let wrap = XM::Wrap(vec![base, bar_close], XProps::default(), Meta::default());
11210
11211  let sub_op = XM::Token(
11212    XProps {
11213      role: Some(Cow::Borrowed("SUBSCRIPTOP")),
11214      scriptpos: Some(Cow::Borrowed("post1")),
11215      ..XProps::default()
11216    },
11217    Meta::default(),
11218  );
11219  let mut pres = XM::Apply(
11220    sub_op.into(),
11221    Args(vec![Some(wrap), sub_content_xm2]),
11222    XProps::default(),
11223    Meta::default(),
11224  );
11225
11226  if let Some(sup_xm) = sup_content_xm2 {
11227    let sup_op = XM::Token(
11228      XProps {
11229        role: Some(Cow::Borrowed("SUPERSCRIPTOP")),
11230        scriptpos: Some(Cow::Borrowed("post1")),
11231        ..XProps::default()
11232      },
11233      Meta::default(),
11234    );
11235    pres = XM::Apply(
11236      sup_op.into(),
11237      Args(vec![Some(pres), Some(sup_xm)]),
11238      XProps::default(),
11239      Meta::default(),
11240    );
11241  }
11242
11243  Ok(Some(XM::Dual(
11244    Box::new(content),
11245    Box::new(pres),
11246    XProps::default(),
11247    Meta::default(),
11248  )))
11249}
11250
11251/// Get the first child element of a script wrapper as an XM.
11252/// Handles both old-style Lexeme and new-style Wrap([lexeme, content]) from faux_wrap.
11253fn get_script_child_xm(script_opt: &Option<XM>, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> Option<XM> {
11254  let script = script_opt.as_ref()?;
11255  // New format: Wrap([lexeme, content]) — return the parsed content directly
11256  if let XM::Wrap(items, ..) = script
11257    && items.len() == 2
11258  {
11259    return Some(items[1].clone());
11260  }
11261  // Old format: bare Lexeme — look up from DOM
11262  if let XM::Lexeme(lex, _) = script {
11263    let node = lookup_lex_node(lex, nodes).ok()?;
11264    let children = node.get_child_elements();
11265    if let Some(first_child) = children.first() {
11266      for (i, n) in nodes.iter().enumerate() {
11267        if n == first_child {
11268          return Some(XM::Lexeme(
11269            Rc::from(format!("{}", i + 1).as_str()),
11270            Meta::default(),
11271          ));
11272        }
11273      }
11274      return Some(XM::from(first_child));
11275    }
11276  }
11277  None
11278}
11279
11280/// Dirac bra-ket notation helpers.
11281/// All produce Apply(meaning, args) wrapped in XMDual with appropriate presentation.
11282fn qm_fenced(
11283  meaning: &'static str,
11284  args_xm: Vec<Option<XM>>,
11285  stuff: Vec<XM>,
11286  ctxt: ActionContext,
11287) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
11288  // A list label holding a relation is Perl's `Formulae` (`ketExpression : Formulae`, MathGrammar:401-404;
11289  // `NewFormulae`, MathParser.pm:1439-1448), as a fenced one is (`relation_list_as_formulae`):
11290  // `|F=1,m_F=1\rangle` is ket@(formulae@(F = 1, m _ F = 1)), `|n,l\rangle` keeps ket@(list@(n, l)) (57bt;
11291  // 2605.07372). The presentation's copy of the label is renamed with the content's.
11292  let mut args_xm: Vec<Option<XM>> = args_xm
11293    .into_iter()
11294    .map(|arg| arg.map(relation_list_as_formulae))
11295    .collect();
11296  let mut stuff: Vec<XM> = stuff.into_iter().map(relation_list_as_formulae).collect();
11297  let op = XProps {
11298    meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed(meaning)),
11299    ..XProps::default()
11300  };
11301  let mut arg_refs: Vec<&mut XM> = args_xm.iter_mut().filter_map(|a| a.as_mut()).collect();
11302  let refs: Vec<Option<XM>> = create_xmrefs(arg_refs.as_mut_slice(), ctxt)?
11303    .into_iter()
11304    .map(Some)
11305    .collect();
11306  // Propagate xmkey from content args to matching presentation stuff items.
11307  // create_xmrefs sets xmkey on the args in args_xm, but stuff was cloned
11308  // before that. The presentation-side elements need _xmkey so that the
11309  // base_xmath createXMRefs handler can resolve the content-side XMRef.
11310  for arg in args_xm.iter().flatten() {
11311    let arg_xmkey = match arg {
11312      XM::Token(p, _) | XM::Apply(_, _, p, _) | XM::Dual(_, _, p, _) | XM::Wrap(_, p, _) => {
11313        p.xmkey.clone()
11314      },
11315      _ => None,
11316    };
11317    if let Some(ref key) = arg_xmkey {
11318      // Find the corresponding non-delimiter item in stuff
11319      for item in stuff.iter_mut() {
11320        match item {
11321          XM::Token(props, _)
11322          | XM::Apply(_, _, props, _)
11323          | XM::Dual(_, _, props, _)
11324          | XM::Wrap(_, props, _)
11325            if props.xmkey.is_none() && props.id.is_none() =>
11326          {
11327            props.xmkey = Some(key.clone());
11328            break;
11329          },
11330          _ => {},
11331        }
11332      }
11333    }
11334  }
11335  Ok(Some(XM::Dual(
11336    Box::new(XM::Apply(
11337      op.into(),
11338      Args(refs),
11339      XProps::default(),
11340      Meta::default(),
11341    )),
11342    Box::new(XM::Wrap(stuff, XProps::default(), Meta::default())),
11343    XProps::default(),
11344    Meta::default(),
11345  )))
11346}

11348/// `<a>` → expectation@(a) — Perl enclose1: '<@>' => 'expectation'
11349#[allow(dead_code)]
11350pub fn qm_expectation(
11351  _: i32,
11352  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
11353  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
11354  ctxt: ActionContext,

11357  unp!(args => _open, expr, _close);

11361/// A Dirac label — a bra's, ket's, inner product's or operator product's part — reads no bar outside
11362/// a nested group: Perl's `ketExpression` sets `$forbidVertBar` (MathGrammar:300-302, :401-403), which
11363/// turns off the ket, bar-pair, evaluation-bar and conditional readings inside it (:258-261, :293,
11364/// :298, :301), and its `maybeBra` reads a braket before a bra (:373-379), so a label holds no ket and
11365/// no open bra: `\langle a|b\rangle|c\rangle` inner-product@(a, b)·ket@(c), the sided ket of
11366/// `\sum_b\left\langle b\right|\psi\left|b\right\rangle_{A}|b\rangle` outside the operator product
11367/// (57bp; 2605.02840, 2605.28949). A bar pair in a middle stays (#356), and a nested group's bars are
11368/// its own (#368).
11369const DIRAC_LABEL_BARS: &str =
11370  "qm: a Dirac label reads no ket, open bra, evaluation bar or conditional";
11371
11372/// A label `DIRAC_LABEL_BARS` forbids. A list label's items are labels each: a bare list has no
11373/// delimiters of its own, so it pairs no bars of its own — a ket, an open bra, an evaluation bar or a
11374/// conditional in an item is the label's (57bt; a list presents as a Wrap, which `holds_ket` and its
11375/// kin take for a nested group).
11376fn is_forbidden_dirac_label(label: &XM) -> bool {
11377  if let Some(mut items) = bare_list_items(label) {
11378    return items.any(is_forbidden_dirac_label);
11379  }
11380  holds_ket(label)
11381    || holds_open_bra(label)
11382    || holds_bar_reading(label, &["evaluated-at", "conditional"])
11383    || holds_plain_angle_relation(label)
11384}
11385
11386/// Does `xm` hold a plain `<` or `>` relation? Perl's `ketExpression` forbids one (`$forbidLRAngle`,
11387/// MathGrammar:402, :708), as the signs that delimit a bra or ket: `\langle p_\alpha\mid\alpha<\gamma\rangle`
11388/// (2605.09161), an ordinal-indexed sequence, is no inner product (57ch review).
11389fn holds_plain_angle_relation(xm: &XM) -> bool {
11390  match xm {
11391    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => {
11392      lex.starts_with("RELOP:less-than:") || lex.starts_with("RELOP:greater-than:")
11393    },
11394    XM::Token(props, _) | XM::Ref(props) => {
11395      props.role.as_deref() == Some("RELOP")
11396        && matches!(props.meaning.as_deref(), Some("less-than" | "greater-than"))
11397    },
11398    XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) => {
11399      holds_plain_angle_relation(op) || args.0.iter().flatten().any(holds_plain_angle_relation)
11400    },
11401    XM::Dual(content, presentation, ..) => {
11402      holds_plain_angle_relation(content) || holds_plain_angle_relation(presentation)
11403    },
11404    XM::Wrap(items, ..) | XM::Arg(items) | XM::Choices(items) => {
11405      items.iter().any(holds_plain_angle_relation)
11406    },
11407  }
11408}
11409
11410/// The items of a bare list — a `list` or `formulae` Dual that presents its items alone, with no
11411/// delimiters of its own (`presents_its_items_alone`) — when `xm` is one.
11412fn bare_list_items(xm: &XM) -> Option<impl Iterator<Item = &XM>> {
11413  let XM::Dual(content, presentation, ..) = xm else {
11414    return None;
11415  };
11416  let XM::Apply(Operator(op), args, ..) = &**content else {
11417    return None;
11418  };
11419  let XM::Wrap(items, ..) = &**presentation else {
11420    return None;
11421  };
11422  let listed = matches!(&**op, XM::Token(props, _)
11423    if matches!(props.meaning.as_deref(), Some("list" | "formulae")));
11424  (listed && presents_its_items_alone(presentation, args.0.len())).then(|| items.iter().step_by(2))
11425}

11427/// `<a|` → bra@(a) — Perl enclose1: '<@|' => 'bra'
11428pub fn qm_bra(
11429  _: i32,
11430  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
11431  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
11432  ctxt: ActionContext,
11433) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
11434  let stuff: Vec<XM> = args.iter().flatten().cloned().collect();
11435  unp!(args => _open, expr, _bar);

11442/// `|b>` → ket@(b) — Perl enclose1: '|@>' => 'ket'
11443pub fn qm_ket(
11444  _: i32,
11445  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
11446  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
11447  ctxt: ActionContext,
11448) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {

11450  unp!(args => bar, expr, _close);
11451  if bar
11452    .as_ref()
11453    .zip(expr.as_ref())
11454    .is_some_and(|(bar, expr)| left_bar_pairs_an_evaluation_bar(bar, expr))
11455  {
11456    return Err("qm_ket: a `\\left|` opening pairs the item's evaluation bar".into());
11457  }
11458  if expr.as_ref().is_some_and(is_forbidden_dirac_label) {
11459    return Err(DIRAC_LABEL_BARS.into());
11460  }
11461  qm_fenced("ket", vec![expr], stuff, ctxt)

11464/// `<a|b>` → inner-product@(a, b) — Perl MathGrammar L382-386
11465pub fn qm_braket(
11466  _: i32,
11467  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
11468  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
11469  ctxt: ActionContext,
11470) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
11471  let stuff: Vec<XM> = args.iter().flatten().cloned().collect();
11472  unp!(args => _open, left, bar, right, _close);
11473  if bar
11474    .as_ref()
11475    .zip(right.as_ref())
11476    .is_some_and(|(bar, right)| left_bar_pairs_an_evaluation_bar(bar, right))
11477  {
11478    return Err("qm_braket: a `\\left|` divider pairs the item's evaluation bar".into());
11479  }
11480  if [&left, &right]
11481    .into_iter()
11482    .flatten()
11483    .any(is_forbidden_dirac_label)
11484  {
11485    return Err(DIRAC_LABEL_BARS.into());
11486  }

11488}

11490/// `<a|f|b>` → quantum-operator-product@(a, f, b) — Perl MathGrammar L387-393
11491pub fn qm_bracket(
11492  _: i32,
11493  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
11494  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
11495  ctxt: ActionContext,
11496) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
11497  let stuff: Vec<XM> = args.iter().flatten().cloned().collect();
11498  unp!(args => _open, left, _bar1, mid, bar2, right, _close);
11499  if bar2
11500    .as_ref()
11501    .zip(right.as_ref())
11502    .is_some_and(|(bar, right)| left_bar_pairs_an_evaluation_bar(bar, right))
11503  {
11504    return Err("qm_bracket: a `\\left|` opening pairs the item's evaluation bar".into());
11505  }
11506  if [&left, &mid, &right]
11507    .into_iter()
11508    .flatten()
11509    .any(is_forbidden_dirac_label)
11510  {
11511    return Err(DIRAC_LABEL_BARS.into());
11512  }
11513  qm_fenced(
11514    "quantum-operator-product",
11515    vec![left, mid, right],
11516    stuff,
11517    ctxt,
11518  )

11521/// Plain `<` and `>` are relations — `\mathrel`, mathcode "313C and "313E (plain.tex:99, :101) — which
11522/// an author also types for angle brackets: `<f,g>=1`, `S_{ij}=<a,b>`, `\lambda\cdot<a,b>`, `e_{<u,i>}`,
11523/// `\exp(<a,b>)`, `<a|H|b>` (divergence OXIDIZED_DESIGN_MATH #7). A pair of them is no angles where both
11524/// stand as relations at once: an operand ends right before the `<` and one starts right after the
11525/// `>`, or the `<` continues an inequality (`continues_an_inequality`). `c_1<c_D,c_2>c_D` is
11526/// formulae@(c_1 < c_D, c_2 > c_D), `0<x<a,\;t>0` formulae@(0 < x < a, t > 0), `0<s<1,\ t>-1`
11527/// formulae@(0 < s < 1, t > −1), `\mathbb{P}(m<S<m+\delta\mid S>m)` P@(conditional@(m < S < m + δ, S > m)),
11528/// as Perl reads the relations (57bt; 2605.04340, 2605.12157, 2605.19552, 2605.13710, 2605.17504; ~33 of
11529/// the 53 angle fences of the 57bp7 output, in 18 papers, read relations as a fence). `\lambda<x,y>`,
11530/// `0<<a,b>>1` and `\mu_{23}=<2|\vec\mu|3>` stay angles, and so does a pair a relation follows: `2<x,y>=z`
11531/// is 2·⟨x, y⟩ = z (the Rust golden `math/ambiguous_relations`; Perl joins `>` `=` into one relation,
11532/// `TwoPartRelop`, MathGrammar:711, and reads `formulae@(2 < x, y >= z)`).
11533fn angle_signs_are_relations(open: &XM, close: &XM, ctxt: &ActionContext) -> bool {
11534  match (
11535    lexeme_position(open, "RELOP:less-than:"),
11536    lexeme_position(close, "RELOP:greater-than:"),
11537  ) {
11538    (Some(open), Some(close)) => {
11539      continues_an_inequality(open, ctxt.nodes)
11540        || operand_ends_before(open, ctxt.nodes) && operand_starts_after(close, ctxt.nodes)
11541    },
11542    _ => false,
11543  }
11544}
11545
11546/// Does the plain `<` at `at` continue an inequality — an operand ends right before it, and a `<`-like
11547/// relation (`<`, `\le`, `\ll`) stands right before that operand? `m<S<m+\delta\mid S>m` (2605.17504),
11548/// `0<s<1,\ t>-1`, `d_1<\cdots<d_n,\ k_i,d_i>0`: the `<` is a relation, whatever follows its `>`. An
11549/// operand here is one letter, number or ellipsis, scripted or not.
11550fn continues_an_inequality(at: usize, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> bool {
11551  operand_start_before(at, nodes)
11552    .and_then(|start| start.checked_sub(1))
11553    .and_then(|before| nodes.get(before))
11554    .is_some_and(|node| {
11555      crate::data::get_grammatical_role(node) == "RELOP"
11556        && crate::data::get_token_meaning(node).starts_with("less-than")
11557    })
11558}
11559
11560/// The position of the one-item operand that ends right before the node at `at`: a letter, number,
11561/// atom or ellipsis — a scripted one by its base, before its first script's start marker — or a group,
11562/// with the head it is applied to (`s(X)`, `\mathbb{P}_{X\sim p}\big(m<s(X)<m+\delta\mid s(X)>m\big)`, 2605.17504).
11563fn operand_start_before(at: usize, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> Option<usize> {
11564  let before = at.checked_sub(1)?;
11565  let node = nodes.get(before)?;
11566  let role = crate::data::get_grammatical_role(node);
11567  if is_script_role(&role) {
11568    let start = nodes[..before].iter().rposition(|marker| marker == node)?;
11569    return operand_start_before(start, nodes);
11570  }
11571  if role == "CLOSE" {
11572    let mut depth = 0usize;
11573    let open = (0..=before).rev().find(|&i| {
11574      match crate::data::get_grammatical_role(&nodes[i]).as_str() {
11575        "CLOSE" => depth += 1,
11576        "OPEN" => depth = depth.saturating_sub(1),
11577        _ => {},
11578      }
11579      depth == 0
11580    })?;
11581    return Some(operand_start_before(open, nodes).unwrap_or(open));
11582  }
11583  matches!(
11584    role.as_str(),
11585    "UNKNOWN" | "ID" | "NUMBER" | "ATOM" | "ELIDEOP"
11586  )
11587  .then_some(before)
11588}
11589
11590/// The 0-based position in the parse's nodes of the lexeme `xm`, when its name starts with `prefix`
11591/// (`ROLE:text:index`, the index 1-based, `lookup_lex_node`).
11592fn lexeme_position(xm: &XM, prefix: &str) -> Option<usize> {
11593  let XM::Lexeme(lex, _) = xm else {
11594    return None;
11595  };
11596  if !lex.starts_with(prefix) {
11597    return None;
11598  }
11599  lex
11600    .rsplit(':')
11601    .next()?
11602    .parse::<usize>()
11603    .ok()?
11604    .checked_sub(1)
11605}
11606
11607/// A script's start and end markers, which carry the script's node (util.rs).
11608fn is_script_role(role: &str) -> bool {
11609  matches!(
11610    role,
11611    "POSTSUBSCRIPT" | "POSTSUPERSCRIPT" | "FLOATSUBSCRIPT" | "FLOATSUPERSCRIPT"
11612  )
11613}
11614
11615/// Does an operand end right before the node at `at` — one a relation there relates on its left? A
11616/// script's end marker stands for its base, scripted or not (`c_1<`, `x_i^2<`); a big operator's
11617/// scripts, a script's start marker (`e_{<u,i>}`), a function or operator head, another relation, a
11618/// punctuation mark or the formula's start end none.
11619fn operand_ends_before(at: usize, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> bool {
11620  let Some(before) = at.checked_sub(1) else {
11621    return false;
11622  };
11623  let Some(node) = nodes.get(before) else {
11624    return false;
11625  };
11626  let role = crate::data::get_grammatical_role(node);
11627  if is_script_role(&role) {
11628    // An end marker: its start marker, earlier, carries the same node; none before a start marker.
11629    return nodes[..before]
11630      .iter()
11631      .rposition(|marker| marker == node)
11632      .is_some_and(|start| operand_ends_before(start, nodes));
11633  }
11634  matches!(
11635    role.as_str(),
11636    "UNKNOWN"
11637      | "ID"
11638      | "NUMBER"
11639      | "ATOM"
11640      | "ARRAY"
11641      | "CLOSE"
11642      | "POSTFIX"
11643      | "SUPOP"
11644      | "ELIDEOP"
11645      | "VERTBAR"
11646      | "FUNCTION"
11647  )
11648}
11649
11650/// Does an operand start right after the node at `at` — one a relation there relates on its right?
11651/// A script marker (`e_{<u,i>}`'s end), a sign, a relation, a punctuation
11652/// mark or the formula's end starts none: `\lambda<x,y>+\mu<u,v>` keeps its angles. Nor does a
11653/// detached node — the null delimiter a retry supplies, which sits last in `nodes` whatever its place
11654/// in the stream (`balance_null_delimiters`, parser.rs), or a wide space's stand-in mark (`filter_hints`).
11655fn operand_starts_after(at: usize, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> bool {
11656  nodes.get(at + 1).is_some_and(|node| {
11657    node.get_parent().is_some()
11658      && matches!(
11659        crate::data::get_grammatical_role(node).as_str(),
11660        "UNKNOWN"
11661          | "ID"
11662          | "NUMBER"
11663          | "ATOM"
11664          | "ARRAY"
11665          | "OPEN"
11666          | "VERTBAR"
11667          | "ELIDEOP"
11668          | "FUNCTION"
11669          | "OPFUNCTION"
11670          | "TRIGFUNCTION"
11671          | "OPERATOR"
11672          | "BIGOP"
11673          | "SUMOP"
11674          | "INTOP"
11675          | "LIMITOP"
11676          | "DIFFOP"
11677      )
11678  })
11679}
11680
11681/// Refutes a reading of plain `<` … `>` as angles where they stand as relations
11682/// (`angle_signs_are_relations`); `args` open with the `<` and close with the `>`.
11683fn refute_related_angle_signs(
11684  args: &[Option<XM>],
11685  ctxt: &ActionContext,
11686) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
11687  if let (Some(Some(open)), Some(Some(close))) = (args.first(), args.last())
11688    && angle_signs_are_relations(open, close, ctxt)
11689  {
11690    return Err("plain `<` and `>` between operands are relations, no angles".into());
11691  }
11692  Ok(())
11693}
11694
11695/// Refutes a plain `<a|b>` or `<a|f|b>` Dirac reading whose `<` continues an inequality
11696/// (`continues_an_inequality`): `\mathbb{P}(m<S<m+\delta\mid S>m)` (2605.17504). A factor on either
11697/// side keeps the bracket, as Perl's: `c_m^*<m|H|n>c_n` c_m^*·⟨m|H|n⟩·c_n (57ch review).
11698fn refute_an_inequality_bracket(
11699  args: &[Option<XM>],
11700  ctxt: &ActionContext,
11701) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> {
11702  if let Some(Some(open)) = args.first()
11703    && lexeme_position(open, "RELOP:less-than:")
11704      .is_some_and(|at| continues_an_inequality(at, ctxt.nodes))
11705  {
11706    return Err("a `<` that continues an inequality is a relation, no bracket".into());
11707  }
11708  Ok(())
11709}
11710
11711/// `langle_rel term_list rangle_rel`: `<x,y>` an angle fence (`fenced`), where its signs are no
11712/// relations (`angle_signs_are_relations`, 57bt).
11713pub fn ascii_angle_fenced(
11714  rule_id: i32,
11715  args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
11716  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
11717  ctxt: ActionContext,
11718) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
11719  refute_related_angle_signs(&args, &ctxt)?;
11720  fenced(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
11721}
11722
11723/// `<a|b>` → inner-product@(a, b) (`qm_braket`), where its `<` continues no inequality
11724/// (`refute_an_inequality_bracket`, 57bt).
11725pub fn ascii_qm_braket(
11726  rule_id: i32,

11728  pragmas: &[ValidationPragmatics],
11729  ctxt: ActionContext,
11730) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
11731  refute_an_inequality_bracket(&args, &ctxt)?;
11732  qm_braket(rule_id, args, pragmas, ctxt)
11733}

11735/// `<a|f|b>` → quantum-operator-product@(a, f, b) (`qm_bracket`), where its `<` continues no
11736/// inequality (`refute_an_inequality_bracket`, 57bt).
11737pub fn ascii_qm_bracket(
11738  rule_id: i32,

11746
11747/// Perl MathGrammar L294: `|| exp ||` → norm
11748/// Merges two single vertbar `|` tokens into double `‖` and fences as norm.
11749pub fn norm_fenced(
11750  _rule_id: i32,
11751  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
11752  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
11753  ctxt: ActionContext,
11754) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
11755  // Args: |1 |2 expression |3 |4
11756  unp!(args => open1_opt, _open2_opt, arg_opt, _close1_opt, _close2_opt);
11757  let arg = arg_opt.unwrap();
11758  let evaluation_bar_inside = holds_evaluation_bar(&arg);
11759  // Merge each pair of | into ‖
11760  let open = merge_vertbar_pair(open1_opt.unwrap(), "OPEN", ctxt.nodes);
11761  let close = merge_vertbar_pair(_close1_opt.unwrap(), "CLOSE", ctxt.nodes);
11762  let op = XProps {
11763    meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("norm")),
11764    ..XProps::default()
11765  };
11766  interpret_delimited(op.into(), vec![open, arg, close], ctxt)
11767    // Two `|`s merged: Perl's `SINGLEVERTBAR SINGLEVERTBAR` norm is a Factor, no `aBarearg`
11768    // (`\log||x||^2` log·‖x‖²); a bar fence like `\|x\|` here (divergence #353).
11769    .and_then(|fence| mark_bar_fence(fence, false, evaluation_bar_inside))
11770    .map(Some)
11771}
11772
11773/// Norm with the *double-bar* token: `\|x\|` and `\Vert x\Vert` each lex to a
11774/// single `VERTBAR:||` token (the doubled bar ‖), so they form
11775/// `||₁ expression ||₂` (3 args) — distinct from the four-single-bar `||x||`
11776/// form handled by [`norm_fenced`]. Without this rule the standard norm
11777/// notation `\|x\|` / `\Vert x\Vert` (ubiquitous in analysis / ML: `\|x\|_2`,
11778/// operator norms) failed to parse → `ltx_math_unparsed`, whereas Perl parses
11779/// it to `norm@(x)`. `merge_vertbar_pair` morphs each bar to an OPEN/CLOSE ‖
11780/// delimiter (it doesn't actually require a pair — it normalizes one XM).
11781pub fn double_norm_fenced(
11782  _rule_id: i32,
11783  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
11784  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
11785  ctxt: ActionContext,
11786) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
11787  // Args: ||1 expression ||2
11788  unp!(args => open_opt, arg_opt, close_opt);
11789  let arg = arg_opt.unwrap();
11790  let open = merge_vertbar_pair(open_opt.unwrap(), "OPEN", ctxt.nodes);
11791  let close = merge_vertbar_pair(close_opt.unwrap(), "CLOSE", ctxt.nodes);
11792  let op = XProps {
11793    meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("norm")),
11794    ..XProps::default()
11795  };
11796  // `\|` is a VERTBAR (`doublevertbar`): the pair is a bar fence, an `aBarearg`.
11797  interpret_delimited(op.into(), vec![open, arg, close], ctxt)
11798    .and_then(|fence| mark_bar_fence(fence, false, false))
11799    .map(Some)
11800}
11801
11802/// True iff the XM points to a token whose underlying DOM node carries
11803/// a negative `rpadding` attribute — the prefiltered signal that an
11804/// `<XMHint width="-X.Xpt"/>` (negative `\kern`) immediately followed
11805/// this token. Used by `stretchy_triple_norm_fenced` to confirm the kerned
11806/// `\vertiii` idiom (divergence #354). Task #263.
11807fn has_negative_rpadding(xm: &XM, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> bool {
11808  let node_opt = match xm {
11809    XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lookup_lex_node(lex, nodes).ok(),
11810    _ => None,
11811  };
11812  let Some(node) = node_opt else {
11813    return false;
11814  };
11815  match node.get_attribute("rpadding") {
11816    Some(s) => crate::util::get_xmhint_spacing(&s) < 0.0,
11817    None => false,
11818  }
11819}
11820
11821/// A kerned stack's merged glyph (`merge_vertbar_pair`, `merge_vertbar_triple`) takes the padding
11822/// after the stack's `last` bar: the kerns between its bars are drawn by the glyph now, not spacing
11823/// around it (57am review round 7: every `⦀` carried the `-1.1pt` between the first two bars).
11824fn padded_as(mut merged: XM, last: &XM, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> XM {
11825  if let XM::Token(props, _) = &mut merged {
11826    props.rpadding = match last {
11827      XM::Lexeme(lex, _) => lookup_lex_node(lex, nodes)
11828        .ok()
11829        .and_then(|node| node.get_attribute("rpadding"))
11830        .map(Cow::Owned),
11831      XM::Token(last_props, _) => last_props.rpadding.clone(),
11832      _ => None,
11833    };
11834  }
11835  merged
11836}
11837
11838/// Apply `merge_vertbar_pair` semantics but emit U+2980 (⦀ TRIPLE
11839/// VERTICAL BAR DELIMITER) instead of U+2016 (‖) — used by
11840/// `stretchy_triple_norm_fenced` for the `\vertiii`/`|||·|||` idiom.
11841fn merge_vertbar_triple(xm: XM, role: &'static str, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> XM {
11842  let mut props = match xm {
11843    XM::Lexeme(ref lex, _) => match lookup_lex_node(lex, nodes) {
11844      Ok(node) => XProps::from(node),
11845      _ => XProps::default(),
11846    },
11847    XM::Token(ref p, _) => p.clone(),
11848    _ => XProps::default(),
11849  };
11850  props.role = Some(Cow::Borrowed(role));
11851  props.content = Some(Cow::Borrowed("\u{2980}")); // ⦀
11852  props.stretchy = None;
11853  XM::Token(props, Meta::default())
11854}
11855
11856/// Two `\left|` bars around two `\right|` bars → norm, Perl's `SINGLEVERTBAR SINGLEVERTBAR
11857/// absExpression SINGLEVERTBAR SINGLEVERTBAR` (MathGrammar:294): `\left|\left|x\right|\right|` is
11858/// norm@(x), kerned (`\vertii`, `\left|\kern-…\left|·\right|\kern-…\right|`) or not. The lexer
11859/// sides the bars (LEFT_/RIGHT_STRETCHY_VERTBAR), so two separate fences `\left|x\right|\left|y\right|`
11860/// never match the rule, and `Meta::abs_depth` ranks the norm (one level) above |(|x|)| (two); the
11861/// kern check this action once made (task #263) read the unkerned stack as |(|x|)|, which Perl does
11862/// not (57am review round 8). Witness arXiv:2211.13044 §S4.Ex17.
11863pub fn stretchy_norm_fenced(
11864  _rule_id: i32,
11865  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
11866  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
11867  ctxt: ActionContext,
11868) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
11869  unp!(args => open1_opt, open2_opt, arg_opt, close1_opt, close2_opt);
11870  let open1 = open1_opt.ok_or("stretchy_norm_fenced: missing open1")?;
11871  let open2 = open2_opt.ok_or("stretchy_norm_fenced: missing open2")?;
11872  let close1 = close1_opt.ok_or("stretchy_norm_fenced: missing close1")?;
11873  let close2 = close2_opt.ok_or("stretchy_norm_fenced: missing close2")?;
11874  let arg = arg_opt.ok_or("stretchy_norm_fenced: missing arg")?;
11875  let open = padded_as(
11876    merge_vertbar_pair(open1, "OPEN", ctxt.nodes),
11877    &open2,
11878    ctxt.nodes,
11879  );
11880  let close = padded_as(
11881    merge_vertbar_pair(close1, "CLOSE", ctxt.nodes),
11882    &close2,
11883    ctxt.nodes,
11884  );
11885  let op = XProps {
11886    meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("norm")),
11887    ..XProps::default()
11888  };
11889  interpret_delimited(op.into(), vec![open, arg, close], ctxt)
11890    .and_then(|fence| mark_bar_fence(fence, false, false))
11891    .map(Some)
11892}
11893
11894/// Triple-bar `\left|\kern\left|\kern\left|·\right|\kern\right|\kern\right|`
11895/// → operator-norm. Requires the kern signal on the first TWO bars of each
11896/// side (open1 + open2 kerned to their successors; symmetric on the right).
11897/// Goes beyond Perl LaTeXML (Perl produces ‖|x|‖ — partial recognition —
11898/// for the same input). Task #263.
11899pub fn stretchy_triple_norm_fenced(
11900  _rule_id: i32,
11901  mut args: Vec<Option<XM>>,
11902  _: &[ValidationPragmatics],
11903  ctxt: ActionContext,
11904) -> Result<Option<XM>, Box<dyn Error>> {
11905  unp!(
11906    args =>
11907    open1_opt, open2_opt, open3_opt,
11908    arg_opt,
11909    close1_opt, close2_opt, close3_opt
11910  );
11911  let open1 = open1_opt.ok_or("stretchy_triple_norm_fenced: missing open1")?;
11912  let open2 = open2_opt.ok_or("stretchy_triple_norm_fenced: missing open2")?;
11913  let close1 = close1_opt.ok_or("stretchy_triple_norm_fenced: missing close1")?;
11914  let close2 = close2_opt.ok_or("stretchy_triple_norm_fenced: missing close2")?;
11915  let open3 = open3_opt.ok_or("stretchy_triple_norm_fenced: missing open3")?;
11916  let close3 = close3_opt.ok_or("stretchy_triple_norm_fenced: missing close3")?;
11917  let arg = arg_opt.ok_or("stretchy_triple_norm_fenced: missing arg")?;
11918  // Two kern signals on each side (between bars 1-2 and bars 2-3).
11919  if !has_negative_rpadding(&open1, ctxt.nodes)
11920    || !has_negative_rpadding(&open2, ctxt.nodes)
11921    || !has_negative_rpadding(&close1, ctxt.nodes)
11922    || !has_negative_rpadding(&close2, ctxt.nodes)
11923  {
11924    return Err("stretchy_triple_norm_fenced: bars not triple-kern-stacked".into());
11925  }
11926  let open = padded_as(
11927    merge_vertbar_triple(open1, "OPEN", ctxt.nodes),
11928    &open3,
11929    ctxt.nodes,
11930  );
11931  let close = padded_as(
11932    merge_vertbar_triple(close1, "CLOSE", ctxt.nodes),
11933    &close3,
11934    ctxt.nodes,
11935  );
11936  let op = XProps {
11937    meaning: Some(Cow::Borrowed("operator-norm")),
11938    ..XProps::default()
11939  };
11940  interpret_delimited(op.into(), vec![open, arg, close], ctxt)
11941    .and_then(|fence| mark_bar_fence(fence, false, false))
11942    .map(Some)
11943}
11944
11945/// Merge two single `|` tokens into `‖` (U+2016) with the given role.
11946/// Perl CatSymbols: concatenates two delimiters into a combined symbol.
11947fn merge_vertbar_pair(xm: XM, role: &'static str, nodes: &[XMLNode]) -> XM {
11948  let mut props = match xm {
11949    XM::Lexeme(ref lex, _) => match lookup_lex_node(lex, nodes) {
11950      Ok(node) => XProps::from(node),
11951      _ => XProps::default(),
11952    },
11953    XM::Token(ref p, _) => p.clone(),
11954    _ => XProps::default(),
11955  };
11956  props.role = Some(Cow::Borrowed(role));
11957  props.content = Some(Cow::Borrowed("\u{2016}")); // ‖
11958  props.stretchy = None; // remove stretchy=false from individual |
11959  XM::Token(props, Meta::default())
11960}
